role: CNC Machine Operator Trainee - Weekend Night Shift
location: 180 Trans Tech Drive, Athens, GA, USA
description: The CNC Machine Operator Trainee is an entry-level position designed to provide hands-on training in operating and maintaining CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machining centers. The trainee will work closely with experienced operators and supervisors to learn setup, operation, inspection, and basic troubleshooting of CNC machines. Essential Functions To accomplish this job, an individual must be able to perform each essential function. Reasonable accommodations may be made to help enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. • Sets up and operates automated CNC Vertical and horizontal machines • Accurately locates/identifies the X, Y, Z axis on Vertical and Horizontal machines • Performs daily point checks on assigned machines and reports concerns to supervisor; may initiate maintenance requests if appropriate • Meets departmental/company goals and objectives promptly (i.e., efficiencies, scrap control, time motion, and setup time reductions) • Accurately interprets product blueprints, drawings, sketches, setup sheets, and other work instructions • Uses scales, calipers, micrometers, and height gauges to determine that the part is being machined to the proper specifications • Removes and replaces dull cutting tools, following designated safety protocol and instructions • Mounts, installs, aligns, and secures tools, attachments, fixtures, and workpieces on machines, using hand tools and precision measuring instruments • Listens to machines during operation to detect irregular sounds (i.e., dull cutting tools or excessive vibration); adjusts machines to compensate for problems and notifies lead or supervisory personnel as appropriate • Adjusts machine feed and speed, changes cutting tools, or adjusts machine controls when automatic programming is faulty or if machines malfunction • Stops machines to remove finished workpieces or to change tooling, setup, or workpiece placement according to required machining sequences • Lifts workpieces to machines manually or with hoists or cranes • Enters command instructions into the machine control units to start operation • Monitors and adjusts/controls coolant systems as needed • Transfers commands from servers to computer numerical control (CNC) modules, using computer network links • Sets up future jobs, performs inspections or part checks, cleans the work area, or performs other duties while the machines are operating • May deburr machined parts as required for work in process • Follows all safety policies and procedures; consistently utilizes all required personal protective equipment (PPE) • Communicates verbally (English) and follows verbal and written instructions • Performs other tasks and/or assignments as required • Regular attendance on-site at the workplace is required Required Education and Work Experience • High School diploma or GED equivalent is required ​Other Required Skills and Abilities • Strong mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn • Demonstrated basic math skills (add, subtract, multiply, divide, fraction conversions) • A history of consistent employment without unexplained or significant gaps or frequent job changes is expected • Completion of assigned internal training for Level I , II , or III Operators, and periodic retraining or recertification is required • Experience using mics, calipers, height gauges, and other precision measuring equipment is preferred • Experience reading & accurately interpreting shop blueprints, sketches, and other technical information/instructions is preferred • Experience using cranes, forklifts, and similar heavy & oversized material handling equipment is preferred Training and Advancement • This position is part of a structured training program lasting approximately 90 days, conducted on day shift, Monday through Friday • Upon successful completion, the trainee will be assigned to a CNC Machine Operator Level I, Level II, or Level III based on skills, performance, and company needs • Full-time assignments after training may be scheduled on day, night, or weekend shifts Physical Demands and Work Environment To perform the essential functions of the role, employees must be able to perform the following activities with or without reasonable accommodations: • Regularly stand and walk throughout the facility, stand for long periods to perform job duties • Regularly lift, carry (short distances), and push/pull up to 100 pounds using peer assistance and/or other lifting & material-handling equipment • Occasionally reaches overhead and reaches out or down to perform duties • Frequently climb steps, stairs, or ladders • Occasionally bend, crawl, stoop, squat, or kneel • Frequently uses hand or fingers to manually inspect parts, tighten hardware & fixtures, and operate machine and material handling controls • Accurately distinguish colors to respond to sensors, indicators, and color-variable dashboards • Visual acuity to interpret readings on gauges and other measuring devices ​Working Conditions Work is performed in a manufacturing shop environment where working conditions may vary significantly; the employee will be exposed to: • Excessive noise (hearing protection required) • Dust, smoke, mist, fumes/vapors (regularly) • Extreme temperatures (occasionally) • Hazardous equipment including forklifts, hand tools, cranes or other lifting devices, and other equipment used in a machine shop environment (continually) We appreciate your interest in Accurus Aerospace; however, only those applicants selected for interviews will be contacted. **A World-Changing Company** Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. ### The Role We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption. You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimized, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three. Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems. ### Technologies We Use - Java, Scala, Rust, and Python - Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution - Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability - Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage - Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here. ### What We Value - Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimizers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing - A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does - Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack - A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition - Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback - Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software ### What We Require - Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience - Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Rust, Scala, C++, or C - Strong foundations in algorithms, data structures, and concurrency - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems - Contributions to open-source projects - Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.

We are a premier, fast-growing third-party logistics (3PL) provider committed to delivering multi-modal transportation solutions across North America. In this role, you will be the initial touchpoint for prospective shippers across diverse industries, identifying key decision-makers and generating new business opportunities. Responsibilities Conduct targeted outbound prospecting via cold calling, email campaigns, and LinkedIn networking to identify potential commercial shippers. Qualify inbound and outbound leads by understanding their freight volumes, shipping lanes, pain points, and current carrier setups. Schedule qualified discovery calls and meetings for senior sales executives and account managers. Energetic, resilient, and confident communicator with a natural curiosity and strong interpersonal skills. Comfortable making cold calls, overcoming initial objections, and staying persistent. Willingness to work in a collaborative, high-energy, on-site office setting. Compensation Base salary: $55,000 per year Work arrangement: Full-time, in-office

Patreon is a media and community platform where over 300,000 creators give their biggest fans access to exclusive work and experiences. We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases. Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with: - $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception - 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and - 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today. We're continuing to invest in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for **Software Engineering Interns** to support our mission. *This role is based in **San Francisco or New York** and open to those who are able to be in-office 3 days per week on a hybrid work model.* Our summer internship is a 12-week program running **May–August or June–September 2027**. This internship is designed for students graduating between **December 2027 and June 2028**. ## About the Role What you will do: - **Make an impact.** You’ll build and ship a feature that directly supports the creator economy and helps your favorite creators turn their passions into sustainable careers. - **Collaborate with the best.** You’ll be embedded within a world-class engineering team, working closely with engineers, product managers, designers, and data scientists to bring your project to life. - **Learn and grow.** With guidance from an experienced engineer mentor, you’ll tackle technical challenges, gain hands-on experience, and grow your skills throughout the internship. - **Have fun!** Beyond building great products, you’ll participate in team activities and events. ## About You - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field (i.e. Mathematics, Physics). - Strong foundation in Computer Science fundamentals and data structures. - Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Python, Swift, Kotlin, or TypeScript. - Eagerness to learn, adapt, and grow through feedback. - Genuine passion for Patreon’s mission and supporting the creator economy. ## About Patreon Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts: - **Put Creators First |** *They’re the reason we’re here. When creators win, we win.* - **Build with Craft |** *We sign our name to every deliverable, just like the creators we serve.* - **Make it Happen |** *We don’t quit. We learn and deliver.* - **Win Together |** *We grow as individuals. We win as a team.* We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you. *Patreon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the interview process, please let us know via email at* [*accomodations@patreon.com*](mailto:accomodations@patreon.com)*.* *Patreon operates under a hybrid work model, where engineering interns are expected to come into the office three days per week, excluding sick time and leave. The goal of this policy is to be intentional about the in-person time we spend together to strengthen the feeling of community at Patreon.* *At Patreon, we believe in fair and transparent pay. In compliance with New York and California pay transparency laws, we are sharing the expected salary range for this role.* *The posted salary range is dependent on the location and the level. This range may encompass multiple levels within the role’s job family. The final offer will be based on candidate’s experience, skills, competencies, and geographic location, aligning with the appropriate job level within Patreon’s leveling framework.* *Patreon reserves the right to modify or update compensation and benefits at any time.*

**About AZX** Our mission is to accelerate positive impact in critical industries through AI transformation. We specialize in physics-informed ML and enterprise AI solutions that directly address climate and sustainability challenges. We’re growing quickly and already work with category-leaders in real estate (CBRE), energy (LevelTen Energy), logistics (Flexe) and utilities. We bootstrapped profitably for our first year and are now backed by leading investors focused on AI, climate and energy. We work on challenges in clean energy, decarbonization, climate risk, energy systems, and global economics. We’re building our company for long-term success and aim to create the ultimate place to work for those passionate about AI and making a positive impact. **About the Role** We are seeking a **Solutions Engagement Manager** — a technical, outcomes-driven individual sitting at the intersection of client delivery and engineering. You will be someone who can embed with clients, deeply understand the problems they’re trying to solve, and partner hands-on with our engineering team to build and ship technical solutions that deliver real value. Based on your qualifications, experience and technical and industry expertise, you will be considered for the role of SEM or Senior SEM. **Responsibilities** - Partner directly with clients to understand their desired outcomes — not just their stated requests — and translate that understanding into clear, actionable direction for the engineering team. - Lead engineers and act as the technical product manager for your accounts: define what should be built, why it matters, and how success will be measured. This includes reviewing system architecture, evaluating data pipeline designs, assessing API integrations, and/or doing technical requirements analysis before handing work to engineers. - Push back constructively on unclear or low-value requests. You are not an order taker — you’re expected to dig into the “why” behind a client ask before it becomes engineering work. - Hold the development team accountable to commitments and quality, while working as a partner to engineering rather than a manager of it — this is not an Engineering Manager role, and you won’t be expected to carry that accountability alone. - Run the core blocking-and-tackling of project delivery: planning, coordination, budget tracking, forecasting, and keeping every workstream honest against its deliverables. - Keep the broader strategic picture in mind even though strategy work is not the current focus of this role — know how your projects ladder up to client and company goals. - Use and help refine the project management processes, tooling, and automation that our operations function is building out, and give feedback on where the basics are still breaking down. **Core Qualifications** - 2-4+ years of project, program, and/or product management experience leading technology initiatives with mid- to large-size customers. - Hands-on experience working with, deploying or supporting AI, machine learning, or advanced analytics solutions, with the ability to translate between technical users and business stakeholders. - Strong technical literacy — able to engage deeply with engineers on system architecture, APIs, data pipelines, and ML model deployment, while maintaining strategic oversight. - Proven track record delivering custom-built software and data solutions — not just SaaS deployments — with measurable business impact. - Domain proficiency/expertise in one or more of our critical industries (energy, utilities, real estate, logistics, climate, or infrastructure), with an understanding of their unique data, regulatory, and operational challenges. - Demonstrated success supporting or managing complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives in environments of ambiguity and rapid change. - Familiarity with cloud-native environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure), CI/CD pipelines, and modern software development practices. - A tenacious problem solver — someone who gets energized by ambiguous, technical problems and doesn’t stop at the first surface-level answer. - A bias toward outcomes over tasks: you ask “what is this client actually trying to achieve” before you ask “what did they ask us to build.” - A growth-oriented learner who actively seeks out feedback and acts on it, and who adapts quickly when new information, **Why AZX!** - Be part of a fast-growing, profitable, mission-driven company with industry-leading clients tackling the massive opportunity of AI transformation in critical industries. - Equity - Fully remote culture with a cluster of teammates in Seattle **Additional Information:** - Must be able to travel 2x/year for company summits and occasional client visits - **Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.** - role: Garage Door Install Apprentice, Minneapolis MN
description: We are looking for high performers to join us. The **Installer** job is physically demanding. Stamina and enthusiasm are required! You don’t need to have experience with garage doors. Our team will train you on everything you need to know (including the customer experience, the key to our success), so you can thrive in your very own market. **You Should Apply If:** - 🎓You love to learn as much as you love to win - 🗣️You’re a master of organization. You work methodically and cleanly - 💡You like to help people and you take pride from a job well done - ‍⚙️Your peers describe you as handy, reliable, and trustworthy - ‍‍⚡You move fast, you’re always busy, and no task is too small or too big - ‍📈 You’re self-motivated and enjoy working autonomously - 🛠️ **You should DEFINITELY apply if you have worked in similar industries, performing installation or assembly. (Windows & doors, flooring, carpentry, kitchen installation, furniture/fixtures/bike assembly etc.)** **You Shouldn’t Apply If:** - You prefer working where there are no customers to talk to - You think that manual labor is for other people - You’re not weather resistant (hot/cold depending on geography) - You’re not likely to follow what you were taught in class and apply it with gusto **The Job:** - Install new garage doors for residential customers - Remove existing door and mechanical parts - Replace worn or broken door parts using tools - Assemble mechanical parts - Install springs, sections, slats, and hardware - Run wiring to connect equipment - Lubricate and test mechanical parts for proper functioning - Educate customers on upgraded parts and services and ensure satisfaction - Document activities related to installations **Basic Requirements:** - Be nice! I know, we shouldn’t have to say that, but we mean it - 21 years old min - Able to bend, climb, kneel and stand for long periods - Physically able to lift 75lbs, lift garage door panels above head - Able to stand on ladder - Knowledge of hand tools (Power drill, hammer, saw etc.) - Valid driver’s license for at least 3 years with a clean driving record - Knowledge of basic software such as navigation apps, Google etc. as well as tablet and computer use - GED or HS diploma not required, however reading skills as well as basic math skills (measurements, payments) are required - Professional & approachable appearance - Employment requires current eligibility to legally work in the United States **The Journey of an Installer:** - Our apprenticeship is a 4 week training program at the A1 Training Academy in Phoenix, AZ. - We cover flights and accommodations for the duration of your training in Phoenix. *(All apprenticeship/training weeks are paid) You will typically work 45-50 hours a week while an apprentice and qualify for overtime for hours over 40 in a week.)* - Once you complete training, you will receive a one thousand dollar bonus, and graduate to a junior installer. You will perform your duties in and around your market. Boom! **Pay, benefits, other cool stuff:** - Get your very own GDD wrapped van or truck with a gas card. - Tools provided! - Steady job flow to keep you busy - Medical, dental, vision, 401K - Starting pay $36.75/hour (Piece Rate) + commission on additional sales/services - Weekly pay - One thousand dollar bonus at completion of Training Academy in Phoenix (in addition to weekly pay) **Interview Process:** Our interview process is not long, but it’s thorough. We want to make sure that each person who joins the team is the right fit. And that we are the right fit for you! 1. After we review your application, you will be contacted for an interview with a recruiter if we want to know more. Plan on up to 30 minutes. 2. Next step is an interview with the Area manager. Plan on approximately 60 minutes. 3. Next step is when the fun begins: you will be invited to ride along with one of our technicians so you can see what life at A1 is really like. Plan on a full day. **Benefits and other cool stuff:** · Medical, dental, vision, 401K · Paid Time Off · Weekly Pay · Internal Promotion opportunities · Company swag *A1 Garage Door (and affiliate companies) provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.*

role: Nu AI Core Summer PhD Research Internship
description: # **About Nu** Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services. Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Visit our [Institutional Page](https://www.nu.com/2026-en) ## **About the Program** The Nu AI Core Summer Internship Program is a research-focused internship for PhD students working at the frontier of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Over about 12 weeks, interns collaborate with engineers, applied scientists, and researchers on complex AI challenges. Each intern leads an end-to-end research or applied AI project that combines research methods with large-scale production environments. The program builds long-term relationships between industry and academia and with emerging AI research talent. # **Program Structure** - **Duration:** ~12 weeks - **Start dates:** May–June, aligned with US university calendars - **Location model**: Remote, with one in-person week at Nu's Palo Alto office in Silicon Valley, fully covered by us. **What you get** - Dedicated research mentor - Ownership of a scoped AI research project - Access to large-scale datasets and compute infrastructure - Research talks and technical seminars - Final research presentation to leadership and AI teams # **Research Areas** Interns may work on projects related to: - **Machine learning and deep learning** - **Large language models and generative AI** - **Recommender systems and ranking models** - **AI infrastructure and model optimization** - **Responsible AI and model evaluation** Projects typically combine **research experimentation with applied system development**, including model design, experimentation, and large-scale evaluation. # **Candidate Profile** This program targets **PhD students conducting research in AI and machine learning** who are interested in applying their work to real-world systems. Applicants are typically pursuing a PhD in fields such as: - Computer Science - Machine Learning - Artificial Intelligence - Statistics - Mathematics - Computational Linguistics - Electrical Engineering - or related quantitative disciplines. # **Basic Qualifications (Application/ Screening Filters)** - Currently enrolled in a PhD program - Research focus in machine learning, AI, statistics or related areas - Strong programming skills in Python or similar languages - Experience working with machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) - Experience designing experiments and evaluating models - Experience working with large datasets or training ML models # **Preferred Qualifications** Strong candidates may also demonstrate: - Publications at top AI/ML conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, KDD, RecSys, CVPR, CIKM or equivalent-conferences for related fields) - Experience working with large-scale ML systems or distributed training - Experience with LLMs, generative AI, or foundation models - Open-source contributions in AI or ML - Experience collaborating in interdisciplinary research environments # **What We Value** We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate: - Strong research rigor and experimental methodology - Ability to translate research ideas into practical systems - Track record of identifying novel research directions or reframing existing problems - Intellectual curiosity and independent problem solving - Collaboration with engineers and cross-functional teams - Interest in deploying AI systems with real-world impact # **Benefits** - Top Tier Medical Insurance - Top Tier Dental and Vision Insurance - Life Insurance and AD&D - Extended maternity and paternity leaves - Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses - NuLanguage - Our language learning program - NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program - 401K - Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account # **Location for this opportunity** Remote, but only for USA PhD students ## Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers. To maintain a consistent and fair process for every candidate, Nu does not provide individualized technical feedback. See how our policy works [here](https://script.google.com/a/macros/nubank.com.br/s/AKfycbwvrewE58oGSbRWIVv8CyCWN68GLxpPVsfYYXv-ZHg94QFsTJmi82rF1x0yt-OTs2W0DQ/exec)

role: Student Life Coordinator at KU Hillel
description: # Student Life Coordinator ## University of Kansas Hillel ## Role Overview Make your mark on Jewish student life by joining KU Hillel as our next Engagement Associate. You will build one-on-one relationships with students, plan and execute engaging events and programs around campus, and help inspire students to make a commitment to Jewish life. KU Hillel proudly serves more than 1,000 Jewish Jayhawks with a dynamic professional team and strong community partnerships. KU Hillel is a student-centric and data-informed team that is committed to dreaming big, entrepreneurial thinking, and always creating new and exciting opportunities to build student leadership, provide pre-professional training, and build a sense of belonging on campus. This is a relationship-focused, student-facing role, perfect for folks who love meeting new faces, building authentic relationships over coffee, and connecting students with opportunities. This role is ideal for an early-career professional (even right out of college!), especially someone with experience in Jewish summer camps, youth group leadership, athletics, or experiential education, who is energized by working directly with students, building belonging through shared experiences, and reaching students who may not initially see themselves in traditional Hillel spaces. This is so much more than your average 9-to-5. And, most importantly, you’ll be excited to support and be supported by a community that sees KU as home. After all, you are in Kansas! ## What You’ll Do - Be the first face and warm welcome to KU students, and help foster a community of belonging amongst Jewish students on campus. - Take a leading role in representing KU Hillel on campus through visible and head-turning opportunities in order to ensure every student on campus has the opportunity to discover who we are. - Contribute to team planning, reflection and assessment - and embrace new responsibilities as you grow with us. - Work with our first-year student community, students in Greek life, and students from multifaith families. - Supervise, mentor, and empower student leaders and volunteers to take ownership of Jewish programming and outreach. - Meet yet-to-be-engaged students wherever they are— be that in the on-campus dining hall, their favorite downtown coffee shop, or grilling kosher hot dogs on Greek Row. - Plan and engage with students to facilitate regular Shabbat and Holiday experiences, as well as social programming. If you enjoy Challah baking or experimenting with recipes in the kitchen, we’ve got an extra apron for you, too! - Assist the KU Hillel team with other on-campus activities, including recruitment for Birthright Israel trips and cohort-based learning opportunities. ## What You’ve Accomplished - You thrive on meeting new people, understanding their interests, and forging meaningful connections. - You have experience in Jewish summer camps, youth groups, or experiential leadership strongly preferred. - You enjoy working collaboratively with a team to solve problems and explore new initiatives. - You see yourself as a creative person who takes initiative and a proactive approach to problem-solving - You’ve demonstrated interest in student engagement, leadership development, and Jewish life. - You have the ability to work collaboratively while also taking ownership of projects and relationships. - You’re comfortable with working a flexible schedule that includes evenings, weekends, and Jewish holidays. ## What You’ll Bring to the Job - Recent college graduates or graduating seniors with 0-2 years experience. People with relevant internship and leadership experience are encouraged to apply. - Bachelor's degree - This is an in-person role located in Lawrence, KS; remote work is not available for this position. Staff frequently choose to live in nearby Kansas City (about a short podcast’s drive away). - A deep passion for Jewishness, Judaism, the Jewish people, and Israel. - An entrepreneurial spirit — you’re excited to take smart risks, try new ideas, and learn when something doesn’t go as planned. - Confidence in initiating, brainstorming, and running programs — both independently and collaboratively. - Familiarity with Google Suite, Canva, and social media platforms is a plus. - A willingness to work nights and occasional weekends when students are available — and to take time off to recharge. The pace of work follows the academic calendar year. ## What You’ll Receive - The salary range for this role is **$46,000 - $49,000.** - Monthly cell phone stipend. - A comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plan, Life, AD&D, and Long Term Disability (LTD) insurances, Flexible Spending accounts, generous vacation/sick time, and parental leave. - High-level professional development to help develop core skills and gain expertise from changemakers, engagers, and Jewish life experts. - Mentoring and career coaching to help you during and after your position - A network of terrific colleagues from across the Hillel movement. - Travel opportunities, both domestically and internationally, multiple times per year. ## About **KU & Lawrence, Kansas City, and Our Community** KU Hillel proudly serves more than 1,000 Jewish Jayhawks with a dynamic professional team and strong community partnerships. KU Hillel is a student-centric, data-informed team committed to dreaming big, entrepreneurial thinking, and creating new and exciting opportunities to build student leadership, provide pre-professional training, and build a sense of belonging on campus. Kansas City and Lawrence are incredible places to live: - Kansas City is a major metropolitan area with a population of over 2.2 million, while Lawrence offers a true college-town atmosphere with about 100,000 residents, blending cultural energy with a more relaxed pace of life. - Both Kansas City and Lawrence are highly livable communities, featuring all the cultural amenities of a big city, with the midwestern hospitality that makes you feel at home. - Kansas City is a cultural hub for the arts and museums, and home of the very best barbecue in the world. Kansas Citians are passionate about our hometown teams, the beloved Chiefs and Royals, and KC is considered the Soccer Capital of the USA. - Lawrence is home to the University of Kansas, where we “bleed crimson and blue” every day. The place where basketball was born, you can travel the world in Jayhawks gear, and be proudly greeted with “Rock Chalk Jayhawk,” a welcome sign that you’re in good company. *\*\*Interested candidates willing to relocate to Kansas are encouraged to use* [*Jewish Federation’s See KC program*](https://www.jewishkansascity.org/jewishkc/seekc) *as a resource to learn more about living in Kansas City and our incredible Jewish community. Kansas City boasts a thriving Jewish community of more than 20,000, including an* [*incredible group*](https://www.jewishkansascity.org/yad) *of young professionals living in and around the KC Metro Area.\*\** The University of Kansas (KU) is centered in Lawrence, Kansas. Today, Lawrence remains a crossroads of culture, celebrating the artists and innovators that populate its history and create an unmistakable identity. So, too is the spirit of the Jayhawks that powers KU. KU is the state’s flagship institution, home to innovative research and the constant pursuit of knowledge. KU Hillel is affiliated with Hillel International. Hillel International enriches the lives of Jewish students so they may enrich the Jewish people and the world, and envisions a world where every student is inspired to make an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning and Israel. ## **About Hillel International** In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. **Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.**

role: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Research, VLM Harnesses for AV Planning
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. The mission of the Waymo AI Foundations team is to develop machine learning solutions addressing open problems in autonomous driving, towards the goal of safely operating Waymo vehicles in dozens of cities and under all driving conditions. As part of our work, we also initiate and foster collaborations with other research teams in Alphabet. AI Foundations areas that we are currently focusing on include reinforcement learning, learning from demonstration, generative modeling, Bayesian inference, hierarchical learning, and robust evaluation. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in. Hourly PhD Pay $85—$85 USD

Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks run on a single data pipeline, from the local network to the data center. Most of the networking industry treats hardware as a commodity–we don’t. Build the hardware right, and everything above it gets better. Meter designs its own Firewalls, Switches, Wireless Access Points, PDUs, and Gateways because customers subscribe to the network instead of buying individual boxes; we're accountable for how the hardware performs for years. We sweat details most people never see, like the logo stamped inside the enclosure and the sound spec on our fans. Great hardware takes more than designing circuits and shipping products: It means thinking hard about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and the full product lifecycle. We’re hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to solve real technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. Over 12 weeks, you’ll own a well-scoped project picked to fit your interests, your experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter: - Next-generation power adapters: Prototype compact, efficient power supplies that could ship in future Meter products. - Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Figure out how Meter hardware can be refurbished, reused, or recycled, and what it takes to extend its life. - Installer tooling: Build tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks faster to install and troubleshoot. - Acoustics and thermal systems: Design quiet, efficient cooling for future high-performance networking and data center products. - Supply chain intelligence: Use component and supplier data to spot risks and bottlenecks before they hit a hardware build. ## **What success looks like** You’ll take a meaningful hardware problem from an open question to a recommendation backed by evidence, and leave behind something the hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, or tools. Your day-to-day will depend on your project, but you may: - Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products - Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers - Write test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, and other system-level behavior - Work with our manufacturing partners in Taiwan to understand their capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability - Present your findings and recommendations to the hardware team at the end of the internship ## **Who you are** You’re curious, hands-on, and you learn by building. You’re a good fit if: - You’re pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field - You like taking an ambiguous technical problem and breaking it into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation - You’ve built, tested, debugged, or taken apart hardware on a design team, in a lab, or at home, or you’re eager to start - You’re comfortable working with physical systems: PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples - You can explain technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations others can act on Experience with PCB design, CAD, embedded systems, thermal design, or data analysis is a plus, but none of it is required. Above all, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built. ## **Why Meter?** The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make and every video call you join is packets moving through networks. But those networks haven’t changed in decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up for a business. We started Meter to build better networks, and that meant building everything ourselves: our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations. Today we deploy those networks at scale. Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, and the San Antonio Spurs rely on Meter to keep thousands of employees and locations online. Our bet is simple: Everyone will use the internet more than they do today. Meter is building the networking stack that makes connectivity as easy and reliable as water or electricity. ## **Compensation** - The estimated pay for this role is $40–$50 per hour. This role is also eligible for a relocation and housing stipend. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE TEAM** The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments. **ABOUT THE ROLE** This is an intern role open to engineers finishing a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it. You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one. You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise. **WHAT YOU'LL DO:** - Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted - Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design - Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on - Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components - Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate - Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data - Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. - Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:** - Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes - Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++ - Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo - Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team - Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review - Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. X-Patch, SENTRi, and McMoM2D are government codes and we do not expect you to have used them - Coursework or project experience with composites, additive manufacturing, casting, or injection molding - Experience with laboratory RF measurement: network analyzers, anechoic chambers, or antenna pattern measurement - Experience reducing, visualizing, and sanity-checking measured data sets - A prior internship or co-op in aerospace, defense, or another hardware-heavy environment US Hourly Range $34—$50 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. **About the Team:** The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch. **About the Role:** - Own Forming operations within the work center, being responsible for delivery of all formed products and improving both roll forming and press brake process - Bring online a press brake work center and lead the development effort for the company to be capable of forming up to 20’ sheets of material for our rocket primary structure - Create work instructions, specifications, and best practices across multiple high-fidelity processes - Help standardize processes across the manufacturing team - Support the shop floor through live issue resolution and provide upstream feedback as we innovate the next generation of manufacturing technology - Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to structures teams during the development phase and through the first prototype and flight builds **About You:** - Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline - 1+ years progressive and related experience required, including internship experience - A history of improving manufacturing processes and the ability to independently identify and lead development projects needed to meet processing requirements - Strong engineering fundamentals in process improvement, forming, metallic processing, mechanics of materials - Deep knowledge of common metallic manufacturing processes, tools, inspection methods and GD&T - Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability - Strong 3D & 2D design/drafting skills per ASME Y14.5M (NX preferred) **Nice to have, but not required:** - Direct experience with roll forming and press brake forming aluminum alloys - New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success - Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! role: AI Research Intern: Wireless Foundation Models
description: At Bosch Research in Pittsburgh, we are looking for an enthusiastic research intern to advance the state of the art in foundation models for wireless sensing and perception. The intern will explore how large-scale self-supervised and multimodal learning can enable generalizable representations of human activities and environments from radio-frequency (RF) signals and wireless channel measurements. The research will focus on developing foundation models that learn reusable representations from diverse wireless sensing data and transfer across sensing tasks, environments, devices, and users. Potential applications include human presence detection, activity recognition, motion understanding, and fine-grained behavioral and contextual understanding. The intern will work closely with Bosch researchers on the following responsibilities: Develop novel foundation-model architectures and representation-learning methods for RF signals and wireless channel measurements. Investigate self-supervised, contrastive, generative, and multimodal learning approaches for large-scale wireless sensing data. Study model generalization and adaptation across environments, users, devices, and downstream perception tasks. Develop and evaluate methods for fine-tuning, few-shot learning, or zero-shot transfer to downstream wireless perception applications. Conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches. Develop a proof-of-concept demonstration of the proposed technology. Summarize research findings and contribute to a high-quality research publication and/or patent application. Required Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, or representation learning. Experience working with wireless sensing or RF signal data, including channel measurements or related time-series signals. Strong understanding of modern deep-learning architectures and training techniques. 2+ years of programming experience in Python and strong proficiency with PyTorch. Ability to independently design, implement, and evaluate research ideas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience with self-supervised learning, foundation models, transformers, contrastive learning, or generative models. Experience with wireless sensing for applications such as presence detection, activity recognition, localization, or smart-home sensing. Experience collecting and processing wireless channel measurements, complex I/Q samples, signal-strength data, or related RF sensing data. Experience with RF data-acquisition pipelines, wireless signal preprocessing, or time-series feature extraction. Experience with multimodal learning involving wireless signals, language, vision, audio, or other sensor modalities. Experience with large-scale model training, distributed training, or GPU-based experimentation. Strong publication record in leading machine learning, sensing, mobile computing, or robotics venues such as ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, SenSys, IPSN, MobiSys, MobiCom, IMWUT/UbiComp, or IROS. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry. **Position Overview:** As a Vehicle Software Engineering Intern at Inversion, you will help develop the software systems that enable our next-generation reentry vehicles to operate reliably, both in space and on the ground. role: 2028 Point72 Academy Investment Analyst Summer Internship Program - US
description: **2028 Point72 Academy Summer Internship — U.S.** Are you a student interested in pursuing a career in investing? If you are graduating between December 2028 and July 2029, we invite you to apply for our 8-week summer internship, taking place from June to August 2028. Launch your investing career in the Point72 Academy, an investment analyst training program designed to prepare you for a potential career on our fundamental equities teams. Since 2015, the Academy has graduated more than 250 analysts onto our platform as of August 2026; some are portfolio managers today. The Point72 Academy Summer Internship combines structured training with real investing experience, including hands-on research on our investment teams. You’ll build the core skills used by public-markets investors and experience firsthand what it’s like to work as an Analyst at Point72. The internship can be your starting point into the full-time Point72 Academy Associate Program. **During the internship, you will:** - Build a foundation in company research, financial analysis, and the skills needed to contribute as an investment analyst - Receive training in accounting, modeling, presenting, and compliance. - Work directly on an investment team, gaining exposure to researching companies and industries alongside our analysts and portfolio managers - Learn how investment ideas are developed, debated, and refined in a live market environment - Receive feedback from Academy coaches as you dive deeper into data analysis and prepare a final investment pitch Explore efficient ways to harness AI in your investment processes and workflows in collaboration with Compliance, Information Security, and the Office of the Co-CIO **About Point72** Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry’s brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people’s long-term growth. We’re a firm that thrives on ideas, and we’ve found that the Point72 Academy has provided us with diverse viewpoints and perspectives, and we are able to offer support in their growth and development as analysts and portfolio managers. **Who we’re looking for**: We welcome students from all academic disciplines. Your field of study or major is not a determining factor; we're looking for intellectual curiosity, integrity, strong judgment, and an interest in understanding businesses and markets. We want you to apply if you are: - A current student who will graduate from university between December 2028 and July 2029. - Fascinated by research, problem-solving, and analyzing how businesses work across different industries - A clear communicator who can develop a point of view and explain your thinking - Committed to continued success in your academic and professional career with the highest levels of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. - Committed to the highest ethical standards. - Highly self-driven and motivated to explore a career in finance. What to expect: - Your online application, essays, and resume will serve as an introduction to who you are as a candidate. Once you complete the online application, we will begin reviewing your profile. - Selected candidates will then receive an email invitation to participate in a case study, allowing you to showcase your experiences and demonstrate your business acumen. - Following submission and review of your case study, the next step would be an online assessment and virtual one on one interviews with various members of the Academy team, if selected. There is no set application deadline for this position. Candidates are considered as they apply, until the program is at capacity. We strongly encourage you to apply and fulfill all requirements as soon as you feel ready to begin the hiring process. Please note, you may only submit one application to the Academy internship program globally, so only apply to the region you are most interested in. Don't miss this opportunity to kickstart your career in the world of investing with the Point72 Academy. *The annual base salary is $120,000 - $140,000 (USD) which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.* *Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.* *Please note that any use of GenAI is strictly prohibited when completing this application.*

description: Applied Machine Learning and AI Engineering Intern Come Create at Ricoh If you are seeking a team driven by passion and purpose, come create with us at Ricoh. We are a team of information seekers and customer-obsessed collaborators who aspire to deliver the services, solutions, and technologies that empower business success. Position Profile Ricoh is seeking a highly motivated summer intern to help build an AI-powered globalization platform that translates our product documentation and software into eleven languages. Our translation process has already moved from fully manual to hybrid automation, and the next step is to bring translation fully in-house: an automated, AI-driven pipeline that reduces turnaround from weeks to a single day while raising translation quality and consistency. The intern will join this project during its validation and pilot phases, working on the machine learning and engineering problems that determine whether an automated translation can be trusted enough to ship to customers. This is applied work on a system with real users, measurable cost impact, and a clear path to production. Examples of summer projects: Build and run evaluation methods that measure machine translation quality across multiple languages, and help define what “good enough to ship” means for customer-facing content. Develop a terminology checker that enforces Ricoh product terminology and brand language consistently across every supported language. Implement delta translation—detecting and translating only changed content—to cut token cost and processing time on document updates. Work with large language models to improve translation accuracy on structured technical content, including XML-based documentation, tagging, and formatting preservation. Help automate the end-to-end pipeline that receives translation packages from development teams, processes them, and checks completed translations back into source control. Analyze and refine AI outputs to improve accuracy and usability, and present findings to cross-functional development, documentation, and localization teams. Job Duties and Responsibilities Contribute working code to an active engineering project alongside full-time engineers. Design and execute experiments to evaluate model and pipeline performance, and document the results. Collaborate with cross-functional teams across documentation, software development, and infrastructure. Present progress and final results to technical stakeholders and department leadership. Qualifications (Education, Experience, and Certifications) Working towards an M.S. or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Linguistics/Computational Linguistics, or a related field Student must be currently enrolled in an accredited graduate program, or completing an undergraduate degree and enrolled to continue their education in an accredited graduate program Students must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher Students are to successfully complete all required screenings prior to hire Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required Skills Excellent programming skills in Python, with a good understanding of data structures, software design principles, and algorithms Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, natural language processing, and data processing Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to design a fair evaluation of a system’s output Ability to work independently and collaborate with a team Interest in language technology, AI-driven automation, and process optimization Preferred Skills Hands-on experience working with large language models or generative AI APIs, including prompt design and output evaluation Experience using Claude and AI-assisted development workflows in Visual Studio Code, or comparable AI developer tooling Experience with machine translation, internationalization/localization, or multilingual datasets Familiarity with structured document formats (XML, DITA, JSON, YAML) and text parsing Experience with cloud services (AWS) and building or consuming REST APIs Working knowledge of Git and standard software development workflows Reading or speaking proficiency in a second language, particularly Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, or Korean Skilled in explaining and presenting analyses and machine learning concepts to a broad technical audience The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. Overview FIRE’s 10-week, paid Summer Internship Program gives undergraduate students a hands-on opportunity to defend civil liberties and advance free speech. FIRE interns do meaningful work alongside our staff, receive mentorship, participate in weekly seminars with leading experts on freedom of expression, and help execute some of FIRE’s most important student programs of the year. Interns work full-time at FIRE’s Philadelphia office. The 2027 program will run from Tuesday, June 1 through Friday, August 6, 2027. Interns receive a $6,400 stipend and will receive additional compensation for their work as counselors during FIRE’s Free Speech Forum. The program is highly competitive. FIRE typically selects just 8–12 interns from a pool of hundreds of applicants each year. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and students are encouraged to apply early. Applications open October 19, 2026 and close Sunday, January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Qualifications and Responsibilities FIRE is seeking passionate, team-oriented, and driven undergraduate students with a strong interest in free speech and civil liberties. The internship is open to rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors attending colleges or universities in the United States. All interns are expected to demonstrate excellent research, writing, and communication skills. Strong candidates are responsible, organized, eager to take initiative, and are willing to engage with ideas and viewpoints they may agree with. The ability to work under pressure and a sense of humor are also important. Because interns spend the summer working together closely as a cohort, we also look for candidates who are collaborative, open to feedback, and excited to contribute to a team. FIRE interns: Work closely with our student development, defense, policy reform, legislation, development, and media teams to assist with research and administrative projects. Assist with the planning and execution of the FIRE Student Network Summer Conference , taking place in July 2027 in Philadelphia, and lead educational and interactive sessions for conference attendees. Serve as a residential counselor during the Free Speech Forum, providing supervision, mentorship, and facilitation of educational activities centered on free speech. Have the opportunity to contribute to FIRE’s Newsdesk . Learn the foundational arguments for protecting core rights in our free society through reading and discussion in weekly seminars with FIRE’s staff and other experts on civil liberties. Written responses are evaluated not only on answers given, but also on clarity, style, and quality. We encourage applicants to thoughtfully prepare their responses to the questions. Applications open Monday, October 19, 2026, and close Sunday, January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET. The selection process consists of two virtual interview rounds followed by an in-person finalist interview in Florida. Finalists will interview with FIRE staff and participate in FIRE’s Student Development Conference. FIRE covers travel and lodging for candidates invited to the final interview. 2027 Selection Timeline October 19, 2026: Applications open January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET: Applications close By January 20, 2027: Finalists invited to the in-person interview round February 25–27, 2027: Final interviews and Student Development Conference in Florida Beginning March 5, 2027: Offers extended Questions about FIRE’s Summer Internship Program can be sent to . Frequently Asked Questions 1. What does an average day in the life of a FIRE intern look like? Interns typically start the day by catching up on and discussing recent news. Throughout the day, interns collaborate with various FIRE staffers in helping to support FIRE’s response to breaking news and our ongoing defense of free speech. Interns work both individually and in teams, and are involved in a variety of functions. This includes everything from development and conference planning to education and outreach. Interns also take part in educational sessions with FIRE’s staff and free speech experts. 2. Is the FIRE internship open to high school students, graduate students, law students, or international students? No. At this time, the internship is open only to undergraduate students who will be rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors and who attend colleges or universities in the United States. For information about other opportunities at FIRE, please visit our jobs page. 3. Will FIRE provide housing? No. Housing and transportation during the internship are the responsibility of individual interns. FIRE’s office is centrally located in Philadelphia, with a variety of housing and public transportation options nearby. Past interns have found summer housing through university housing programs, sublets, and local housing groups. 4. Can I complete the internship remotely or in a hybrid format? No. The Summer Internship Program is fully in person at FIRE’s Philadelphia office. 5. What are the required hours? The internship requires a full-time commitment of 40 hours per week. FIRE’s regular office hours are Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Interns must be available for the entire 10-week program, from June 1 through August 6, 2027. 6. Are the start and end dates flexible? No. Interns must participate for the full 10-week term, and we cannot accommodate adjustments to the program’s start or end dates. The cohort experience is an important part of the internship and we want all interns to begin and complete the program together. The summer has a full calendar of speakers, seminars, conferences, and professional development opportunities.For those reasons, interns should not plan vacations or other extended time away during the program. 7. Is previous camp counselor experience required? No. Previous camp counselor experience is not required. Because FIRE interns serve as counselors during the Free Speech Forum, prior experience as a camp counselor, resident adviser, teacher, coach, mentor, or in a similar supervisory role can strengthen an application. However, we encourage qualified students to apply regardless of whether they have held a counselor position before. 8. What does the interview process look like? The interview process consists of two virtual interview rounds followed by an in-person finalist interview in Florida. Finalists will be invited to Florida to interview with FIRE staff and participate in FIRE’s Student Development Conference. FIRE covers travel and lodging associated with the trip. Additional details will be provided to applicants who advance to the final round. Students who are studying abroad during the final round will have the option to participate virtually via Google Meet. 9. What makes a strong application and FIRE intern? Strong applicants demonstrate excellent writing and communication skills, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and an interest in free speech and civil liberties. We also look for candidates who enjoy working with a team, and are receptive to feedback. Successful interns are self-starters who seek out ways to contribute and are just as willing to handle a small task as they are to lead a major project.

Headquartered in Akron, Ohio, FirstEnergy includes one of the nation's largest investor-owned electric systems, more than 24,500 miles of transmission lines that connect the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, and a regulated generating fleet with a total capacity of 3,780 megawatts. About the Opportunity This is an open position with FirstEnergy Service Co. a subsidiary of FirstEnergy Corp. [SC00] Work location is Akron, OH with the opportunity to work remote on either Monday or Friday each week per company policy. The Summer 2027 session will take place from May 17 th , 2027 – August 20 th , 2027. As a participant in the Co-op/Intern Professional Development Program, you will be cultivating professional skills and perform professional level work at FirstEnergy. Each participant will receive on-the-job training, mentoring, experiential learning and challenging assignments to refine skills and round out competencies. As a Supply Chain Operational Buyer Intern at FirstEnergy, you will gain hands-on experience supporting the day-to-day procurement of materials and services needed across the organization. Working alongside Operational Buyers and other Supply Chain professionals, you will help process purchasing requests, coordinate with suppliers and internal stakeholders, resolve procurement issues, and support timely and accurate purchasing activities. In addition to core operational buying responsibilities, you will have opportunities to gain exposure to strategic sourcing, category management, contract management, data analytics, and supply chain process improvement. As a Supply Chain Operational Buyer Intern you may participate in the following functions Supporting the procurement of materials and services by reviewing purchase requests, validating required information, and helping ensure requests are processed accurately and efficiently. Creating and maintaining purchase orders, including supporting PO issuance, change orders, cancellations, and other purchasing transactions in accordance with established processes and policies. Working directly with suppliers and internal business partners to obtain information, clarify requirements, resolve purchasing issues, and support the timely delivery of materials and services. Supporting high-volume procurement activities while developing an understanding of purchasing policies, approval requirements, documentation standards, and procurement best practices. Assisting with supplier-related issues involving purchase orders, pricing, delivery requirements, documentation, invoicing, and other transactional discrepancies. Utilizing procurement and enterprise systems to process purchasing activities, research transactions, maintain accurate records, and support day-to-day Operational Buying activities. Reviewing purchasing data and reports to identify open items, exceptions, trends, and opportunities to improve procurement efficiency. Helping identify opportunities to utilize existing contracts and preferred suppliers when fulfilling business requirements, supporting compliance and procurement efficiency. Supporting process improvement initiatives focused on simplifying purchasing activities, improving data quality, reducing manual work, strengthening compliance, and improving the internal stakeholder experience. Gaining exposure to sourcing and category management activities, including competitive bidding, supplier evaluations, bid analysis, market research, and supplier strategy. Supporting Contract Lifecycle Management activities, including contract administration, documentation management, and compliance tracking. Conducting business research and data analysis and developing reports, presentations, and recommendations for Supply Chain team members and leadership. Collaborating across Supply Chain and other business functions to better understand how procurement supports business operations and organizational objectives. Internship Experience: Throughout the internship, you will gain practical experience in the day-to-day responsibilities of an Operational Buyer while developing a broader understanding of FirstEnergy's Supply Chain organization. You will have opportunities to work with experienced procurement professionals, business stakeholders, and suppliers while building skills in purchasing, supplier management, procurement technology, analytics, problem-solving, communication, and process improvement. The internship will also provide exposure to adjacent Supply Chain functions, including strategic sourcing, category management, and contract management, helping you understand how tactical procurement activities connect to broader Supply Chain strategies. Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s program in Supply Chain Management or related field at an accredited institution. Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. Must have a graduation date not earlier than May 2028 Authorization to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship. Strong organizational skills and the ability to follow detailed processes while identifying and resolving issues. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint); experience with data analysis or procurement systems is a plus. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; exposure to data analysis, ERP, or procurement systems is a plus but not required. A proactive and curious mindset with a willingness to learn, ask questions, solve problems, and build professional relationships. Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with team members, business partners, and suppliers. Ability to gather, organize, and analyze information and communicate findings clearly to others. Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, follow established processes, and maintain strong attention to detail. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills. Strong teamwork orientation with a commitment to workplace safety.

Learn advanced data optimization techniques.
