role: Investment Banking Associate (Current MBA Student - Remote)
description: Investment Banking Associate — Current MBA Student (Part-Time / Remote) Fireclay Partners offers a remote investment banking experience for current MBA students interested in M&A and private markets advisory. This role combines substantive research, financial analysis, and transaction support with the flexibility to contribute alongside an MBA program. Associates work within our existing development program and collaborate with senior team members and analysts on defined projects. Role Structure • Part-time during the academic year, targeting 10–15 hours per week around your MBA schedule. • Remote work from within the United States. • Current MBA enrollment is required; this is not restricted to a single graduating class. Start timing and availability will be discussed during the process. • Work is self-directed, with clear deliverables, regular communication, and review of completed work. Key Responsibilities • Prepare and review company, industry, and competitive research for business development and transaction execution. • Develop financial analyses and valuations using public comparables, precedent transactions, and discounted cash flow methods. • Contribute to pitch materials, information memoranda, buyer and acquisition-target lists, and data room content. • Assess strategic fit and synthesize research into concise recommendations for senior team members. • Support outreach preparation, coverage tracking, and internal reporting for private equity and strategic acquirer relationships. • Help coordinate analyst research, review work for accuracy, and support timely delivery of project assignments. Ideal Candidate Qualifications • Current enrollment in an MBA program with strong academic performance. • Prior professional experience demonstrating analytical judgment, ownership of deliverables, and dependable execution; finance, consulting, accounting, corporate development, or operating experience is valuable. • A clear interest in investment banking, M&A, private equity, or corporate finance, with a working foundation in accounting and valuation. • Strong Excel and PowerPoint skills, professional writing, and clear communication. • Ability to work independently, meet agreed deadlines, respond promptly, and contribute consistently within a remote team. • Capacity to commit approximately 10–15 hours each week during the academic year. Working with AI at Fireclay AI is part of how we work. We use approved AI tools to support research, organize and synthesize information, develop and refine written materials, assist with analysis, and improve repeatable tasks. Team members are expected to combine these capabilities with financial knowledge and professional judgment to produce accurate, useful work efficiently. We expect practical proficiency with AI tools and the ability to apply them responsibly to research and analytical work. You should be able to structure a task, supply useful context, refine prompts and outputs, and explain how you checked the resulting work. Be prepared to discuss examples from professional, academic, or independent projects using public or non-confidential information, and continue developing these skills as tools evolve. You remain accountable for every deliverable. Verify facts, sources, calculations, and assumptions; recognize unsupported or misleading outputs; and know when independent analysis or human review is required. Use only firm-approved tools and follow confidentiality and data-handling requirements. Never enter client, deal, personal, or proprietary information into an AI system without authorization. AI proficiency complements sound accounting, valuation, writing, and analytical skills. Why Fireclay Gain practical exposure to M&A research, financial analysis, and advisory work while contributing to a small, entrepreneurial team. The role builds on Fireclay’s existing development program and offers opportunities to take responsibility for increasingly complex assignments. How to Apply Submit your résumé with your MBA institution, expected graduation month and year, current work location, relevant experience, and weekly availability. Fireclay Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an inclusive workplace.

Investment Banking Analyst (Part-Time / During Academic Year) Fireclay Partners is building a technology-native investment bank. This remote, academic-year role gives exceptional students direct exposure to live M&A execution, financial analysis, and business development while asking them to think like both financiers and builders. We expect our bankers to use AI, programming, automation, structured data, and proprietary technology to improve the quality and speed of their work. What You Will Do Support pitch materials, information memoranda, buyer lists, data rooms, and other workstreams for live and prospective transactions. Conduct market, company, and competitive research and translate findings into clear, decision-useful analysis. Build financial analyses and valuations using precedent transactions, public comparables, and discounted cash flow methods. Support outreach to private equity firms, strategic acquirers, and other market participants. Identify repetitive work and build or improve technology-enabled solutions using AI, automation, code, or structured data. Maintain rigorous internal tracking and reporting systems while contributing reusable knowledge for future teams. Who Thrives Here High-performing students in finance, accounting, economics, computer science, engineering, applied mathematics, statistics, data science, or a related field. Genuine interest in investment banking, M&A, private markets, and the use of technology in professional services. Strong analytical judgment, writing, communication, and attention to detail. Working proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, plus curiosity about modern AI and data tools. A builder mentality: you look for better ways to solve recurring problems instead of accepting manual work as inevitable. Evidence that you have built, automated, or programmed something useful. This may be a script, model, application, data workflow, research tool, or other project; sophistication matters less than initiative and clear thinking. Ability to work independently in a remote environment, meet deadlines, and handle confidential information with discretion. This internship is structured around the academic calendar and offers meaningful responsibility, mentorship, and a differentiated view of how investment banking is evolving.

Relocation from Germany is supported. ### Location On-site in San Francisco, California, United States.

role: AI Intern - Office of CEO & Head of Product
description: **Location:** In-Person (New York, NY) **Compensation:** $18.00 – $20.00 / hour **Commitment:** 15-20 hours/week --- ### **Position Overview** At Eulerity, we are building the future of AI-driven marketing automation. To scale our technology, we need to scale our team with top-tier talent. We are looking for a highly analytical, deeply curious intern with a true **builder mentality** to join us in our New York office. This is not a traditional internship. This role is designed as a training ground for future Product Managers. You will treat our recruiting pipeline and internal operations like a product—analyzing the data, identifying bottlenecks, testing solutions, and optimizing the "user" (candidate) experience. You will work closely with leadership to recruit the best talent while learning how to build, ship, and scale processes from the ground up. ### **What You Will Build & Manage** #### **1. Talent Sourcing & Recruiting Pipeline** - **Hunt for Talent:** Proactively source passive candidates across technical and business roles using LinkedIn Recruiter and alternative networks. - **Manage the "User Journey":** Treat the candidate experience like a product flow. Coordinate interviews, manage our Applicant Tracking System (ATS), and ensure every touchpoint is seamless and reflects Eulerity's brand. #### **2. Analytics & Process Optimization** - **Funnel Analysis:** Track key recruiting metrics (time-to-hire, drop-off rates, source effectiveness) to figure out where our hiring process is succeeding or failing. - **Data-Driven Solutions:** Build dashboards and reports to present to leadership, using data to advocate for changes in how we evaluate, interview, and close candidates. - **Market Intelligence:** Conduct competitive research on compensation, benefits, and market trends to ensure our offers remain highly competitive. ### **Who You Are** - **The Builder Mentality:** You do not wait to be told what to do. You see broken processes and immediately want to design a system to fix them. - **Future Product Manager:** You have a deep interest in technology, product development, and business strategy. role: Policy and Government Affairs Spring 2027 Undergraduate Intern
description: World Wildlife Fund (WWF), one of the world’s leading conservation organization, seeks an Undergraduate Policy and Government Affairs Spring 2027 Intern. The Policy and Government Affairs department of the World Wildlife Fund is seeking part-time to full-time interns for policy research, analysis, and outreach. Given the diversity of issues that the Policy and Government Affairs (PGA) staff covers, research and analysis may entail working with legislation, regulations, and potentially court cases. By contrast, research, analysis, and support may include assessment of government agencies' roles, policies, and positions on issues relating to WWF's mission, or writing of brief materials about U.S. government agencies. Outreach may entail covering congressional hearings and markups, and preparing and attending congressional, administration, and/or NGO coalition briefings. Subject matter will cover many of the issues in which WWF is involved, including biodiversity conservation (e.g., endangered species and habitat protection), natural resource management (e.g., fisheries, forestry, and agriculture), environment and security, climate change, and energy. Internship Description: Research, writing & analysis on various topics which may include grasslands, wildlife conservation, food and water security, marine and fisheries issues, species/wildlife trafficking, and national security. Legislative tracking and research. Attend Congressional hearings and briefings, as well as NGO coalition meetings. Outreach to Capitol Hill and the Administration on legislation and rulemaking. Minimum Requirements: Only enrolled students are eligible for this internship as you must be able to receive academic credit from your current academic institution. Able to work either part-time or full-time, depending on class schedule and availability. Please note : This internship is for Spring 2027, located in Washington, D.C. Desired Skills and Qualities: Undergraduate student: Must be an actively enrolled student and not received degree at time of internship start date (January 2027). Interest in conservation and international development issues with a concentration in International Relations, Public Policy, American Government, or Political Science. Those studying outside these areas are still highly encouraged to apply. Interest and willingness to learn about Capitol Hill, the Administration (specifically U.S. Department of Interior, U.S. Department of Agriculture, and U.S. State Department) and non-governmental organizations. Excellent written and verbal communications skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, collaboratively and independently. Strong interpersonal skills crucial for developing working relationships, internally and externally. Strong organizational skills. Attention to detail. Cover Letter: Applicants who wish to be considered for this role must include a cover letter as part of their application. In your cover letter, please indicate the number of hours per week you will be available for this internship, your location for the Spring 2027 semester, and the number of hours you will be able to work from WWF’s DC Office. This is a hybrid internship based in Washington, DC. Location: Washington, DC Compensation: Unpaid. For all unpaid internships, applicants must be enrolled in school and be able to obtain academic course credit from their university. Applications will be accepted until October 30, 2026. Please note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. WWF does not provide VISA sponsorship to interns. Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. role: Adjunct Lecturer, Technology Integration in Project Management  (On-Campus, Spring 2027 & Future Semesters)
description: Columbia University School of Professional Studies seeks industry professionals for the role of adjunct Lecturer to teach Technology Integration in Project Management , a core course in the school’s M.S. in Project Management program. The course of Technology Integration in Project Management explores the integration of technology into modern project management, equipping students with the skills to navigate digital transformation and technology adoption in complex project environments. Students will gain hands-on experience with project management information systems (PMIS) and enterprise platforms such as MS Project, Asana, Trello, SAP, and Oracle Primavera, while also learning to leverage AI, automation, and data analytics tools like Power BI to enhance decision-making and performance monitoring. The course emphasizes the use of agile and hybrid methodologies supported by tech-enabled tools, preparing students to lead projects with efficiency, adaptability, and innovation in digitally driven organizations. Responsibilities Lead in-person class lectures, instructional activities, and classroom discussions Evaluate student work and grade assignments Monitor student concerns and inquiries, and be the first point of contact for student questions Hold weekly office hours Prepare, maintain, and enhance the course in Canvas, Columbia University’s learning management system for onsite and online courses Part‐time Lecturers who are new to SPS must complete Canvas training (online learning management system) Attend Project Management faculty meetings If assigned to design the course, responsibilities also include: Develop course objectives that align with program-wide learning outcomes Create activity maps tying course activities to objectives, ensuring industry relevance Draft a detailed syllabus (course description, schedule, grading rubric, and assessments) for review and approval by the Program Curriculum Committee and the Committee on Instruction (COI). Collaborate with Instructional Design to develop course materials through a consultative process. This includes partnering on course development (aligning objectives, materials, and assessments), creating dynamic instructional media (videos, infographics, and interactive resources), maintaining established courses with updates and troubleshooting, and receiving just-in-time assistance for targeted needs. Serving as an adjunct Lecturer provides an outstanding opportunity to educate and mentor students in the field of project management as well as to form a rewarding professional relationship with Columbia University’s world-class faculty. Columbia University SPS operates under a scholar-practitioner faculty model, which enables students to learn from faculty that have outstanding academic training as well as a record of accomplishment as practitioners in an applied professional setting. Requirements A master’s degree in engineering (e.g., civil, mechanical, or industrial), construction management, project management, operations research, technology management, business analytics, or data science (with a project management focus) At least 8 years of experience in roles such as IT Project Manager, Technology Consultant, Digital Transformation Lead, or Systems Engineer Hands-on experience with software selection, implementation, and integration in a project setting Experience in cross-functional technology deployment across sectors (e.g., construction, manufacturing, tech, services) PMP or equivalent certifications preferred A passion for teaching, strong interpersonal and communication skills, and the ability to connect academic material to contemporary industry practices. Preferred Skills & Experience A terminal degree in one of the above mentioned disciplines 2+ years graduate-level university teaching experience Compensation Range - $10,000 - $15,000 per semester-length course. Review of applications begins immediately and will continue until positions are filled. All applicants, please provide: A resume/CV inclusive of university teaching experience -- highlight teaching at the graduate level A cover letter Evidence of teaching effectiveness (e.g., student evaluations of teaching, teaching observation summaries, etc.) All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Columbia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer / Disability / Veteran Columbia University has been a leader in higher education in the nation and around the world for more than 250 years. At the core of our wide range of academic inquiry is the commitment to attract and engage the best minds in pursuit of greater human understanding, pioneering new discoveries, and service to society. The School of Professional Studies at Columbia University offers innovative and rigorous programs that integrate knowledge across disciplinary boundaries, combine theory with practice, leverage the expertise of our students and faculty, and connect global constituencies. Through nineteen professional master's degrees, courses for advancement and graduate school preparation, certificate programs, summer courses, high school programs, and a program for learning English as a second language, the School of Professional Studies transforms knowledge and understanding in service of the greater good.

### **About the Role** The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. ### Past Research Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes: - [Speculative Speculative Decoding](https://openreview.net/forum?id=aL1Wnml9Ef) (ICLR 2026) - [When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06932) (ICML 2026) - [Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13841) (MLSys 2026) ### **Responsibilities** - Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures - Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses. - Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads - Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team - Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production ### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals - Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP) - Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention ### Preferred Qualifications - Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning - Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys) - Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning - Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) - Contributions to open-source machine learning projects ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. ### **Internship Program Details** Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span January 4th to April 9th. ### **Compensation** We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. Our hourly rates are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. ### **Equal Opportunity** Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more. Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production ### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning - Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys) - Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning - Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) - Contributions to open-source machine learning projects ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **RETHINK MANUFACTURING** The only way to ignite change is to build the best team. At Bright Machines, we’re innovators and experts in our craft who have joined together to manufacture the AI and data center infrastructure at the edge. We believe unifying software, intelligent automation, and data is the answer to delivering quality and flexibility at scale. We deliver products to meet the demands of today while continuously investing in our Bright Factory model to take advantage of what comes next. Working with us means you’ll have the opportunity to make lasting, impactful changes for our company and our customers. If you’re ready to apply your exceptional skills to a brighter way of manufacturing AI infrastructure, we’d love to speak with you. ### ABOUT THE ROLE As a Strategic Finance Intern, you’ll work closely with Bright Machines’ finance team and senior leaders to turn financial and market data into decisions that support the company’s growth. You’ll contribute to investment analysis, forecasting, performance reporting, and investor relations while exploring practical ways to use AI to improve finance workflows. This is a hands-on opportunity to take on meaningful strategic projects and see how finance helps guide a fast-growing manufacturing business. ### WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING - Investment & ROI analysis. Build the business cases behind major spend decisions — capex, new initiatives, and resourcing bets — quantifying the returns and trade-offs so leadership can decide with confidence. - Competitive & market analysis. Size the market, track competitors and comparable companies, and translate the findings into sharper pricing and a more compelling story for investors and leadership. - AI-driven finance innovation. Use AI to make our finance, strategic finance, and investor relations processes faster and better — building apps, skills, and workflows that the whole team can use. - Cash forecasting. Partner with key stakeholders and department heads across the business — including the head of operations and senior leadership — to manage capex inflows and outflows and understand the project timelines that drive our cash position. - Management reporting & insights. Help leadership decide which KPIs matter most to track, then dig into those results — along with revenue, margins, and spend — and present the findings and recommendations directly. - Investor relations. Help refine and maintain our investor financial model and shape the investor story — proving out our growth, margin trajectory, and unit economics with the numbers. Contribute to investor-facing materials and support ongoing investor communications. - Strategic projects. Identify where the business needs help and propose the projects to go after it, working with senior leadership and partnering cross-functionally across the company to drive real improvements. ### WHAT YOU WILL GAIN - Hands-on experience at a company at a pivotal growth stage - Direct work with senior leadership and partnership with stakeholders across the company - Practical experience applying AI to real finance and investor relations work - Experience working inside a next-generation manufacturing company shaping AI infrastructure ### WHAT WE WANT TO SEE - Currently pursuing an MBA - A background in FP&A, investment banking, or consulting - Strong financial modeling instincts ### BE EMPOWERED TO CHANGE AN INDUSTRY Bright Machines is a next-generation, AI-enabled manufacturer focused on data center infrastructure production. Bright Machines uses its proprietary AI-based robotics and software to assemble AI infrastructure hardware products (i.e., data center servers) for hyperscalers, neoclouds, and leading Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to reduce their time to revenue. With its Bright Factory model, Bright Machines builds higher quality data center infrastructure at scale, addresses increasing market demands for computing power due to the surge of AI, and answers the call to the U.S. national mandate to reshore manufacturing. Bright Machines is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, and has an integration center in Guadalajara, Mexico. The company has been recognized as one of Forbes’ AI 50, awarded “Best AI-based Solution for Manufacturing” by AI Breakthrough, named a “Technology Pioneer” by the World Economic Forum, and highlighted by several other leading technology and innovation organizations.

We are looking for a driven Operations Intern with a basic understanding of supply chain, logistics, and business operations principles who is ready for an immersive, real-world experience. Under the supervision of our staff, the Operations Intern can expect to track and analyze operational data, support inventory and order fulfillment workflows, coordinate with cross-functional teams and partners, document and improve processes, and assist the Operations staff with other day-to-day activities. If you are a motivated team player who can maintain efficiency and accuracy when multitasking, we encourage you to apply! This internship offers a year-long hybrid work schedule in Lehi, Utah. During the summer months the role is full-time, but will transition to part-time during the academic year. ### What does a typical day look like for an Operations intern? - Working side by side with the Operations Business Intelligence Analyst on reporting and analysis requests, and shadowing other members of the Operations department to see how their work connects to the data - Pulling, cleaning, and validating operational data from multiple sources (spreadsheets, internal systems, and marketplace and fulfillment partner data), and maintaining accurate and complete operational records - Building and refreshing weekly and monthly reports, dashboards, and spreadsheets that track key metrics such as inventory levels, order status, shipment timeliness, and fulfillment accuracy - Monitoring inventory, orders, and shipments across marketplaces and fulfillment partners, spotting anomalies and trends in the data, and flagging issues to the right owners for follow-up - Digging into ad hoc questions from Operations team members (for example, "why did on-time shipments dip last week?") and presenting what you find in a clear, concise summary - Documenting reporting logic, data definitions, and processes so that others can understand and reuse your work, and identifying opportunities to automate manual tasks and improve efficiency and accuracy - Owning a small project or analysis during your internship and sharing your findings and recommendations with the Operations team - Taking on additional tasks or projects to learn more about ecommerce operations, business intelligence, and supply chain management ### What will I need to thrive in this role? - Currently pursuing a degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business, Logistics, Industrial Engineering, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field - Possess an understanding of operations, supply chain, and business principles and a positive attitude - Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets, including comfort with formulas, pivot tables, and lookups, and an ease working with large data sets - Familiarity with SQL or BI and data visualization tools is a plus; a strong interest in learning them is a must - Natural curiosity and an analytical mindset: you ask "why" when numbers look off, and you check your work before you share it - Strong attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accuracy when working with large volumes of data - Demonstrate collaboration, trustworthiness, receptiveness to feedback, and eagerness to learn - Demonstrate strong organization and communication skills, including the ability to explain data and findings clearly to non-technical teammates, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines - Handle sensitive or confidential information with honesty and integrity - Learn to work as part of the Operations team to compile and analyze data, track information, and support the company or client. ### What does high performance look like? - You follow through with all assignments in a timely manner - You give 100% to all tasks and projects assigned to you - You take full ownership of your projects and follow through to completion - You spot issues early and bring forward solutions, not just problems - Your data and reports are accurate, well documented, and trusted by the people who rely on them - You go beyond the numbers: you tell the story behind the data and recommend a clear next step - You proactively look for ways to automate or simplify recurring reports and manual work - You ask thoughtful questions, seek out feedback, and apply it quickly ### What is my potential for career growth? - This role will provide opportunities for mentorship and networking. You will build hands-on experience in business intelligence, data analysis, and ecommerce operations that translates directly to careers in operations, analytics, and supply chain. Additionally, outstanding performance during the internship could potentially lead to a full-time position within the company. ### What is the team like? You will report directly to the Supply Chain Manager, who will serve as your manager and mentor, meeting with you regularly to set priorities, review your work, discuss your performance, and provide guidance. You will also collaborate closely with full-time Operations team members and leaders, whom you will partner with on the reports and analyses that help them run their day-to-day work. This data-driven and results-oriented team values collaboration, encouraging all members to contribute ideas and insights to implement actionable solutions effectively

About the role We are looking for a detail-oriented, organized, and motivated Junior Graphic Designer to join our growing creative team at Manhead. The Junior Graphic Designer will be responsible for executing and preparing merchandise artwork across Tour, E-commerce, Retail, and Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) platforms for our extensive roster of artists and brands. Working closely with our Graphic Design, Apparel Design, and Production teams, this role will focus on executing established creative direction, preparing artwork for production, creating product mockups, building presentations, and ensuring all artwork meets Manhead's standards for quality, accuracy, and consistency. A significant part of this role involves supporting production workflows, managing time-sensitive artwork setups, reviewing print proofs, and maintaining an accurate, organized artwork catalog across our artist roster. Attention to detail, organization, collaboration, and flawless execution are at the core of this position. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, can confidently manage multiple priorities, and understands the importance of delivering accurate work within tight deadlines. A strong foundation in apparel graphic design and production processes is essential , along with a working knowledge of garment decoration techniques and the technical requirements needed to take artwork from approved design to finished product. What you'll do Artwork Execution & Design Support Execute artwork based on established creative direction, approved designs, and artist brand guidelines. Create accurate product mockups for apparel, accessories, and merchandise across Tour, E-commerce, Retail, and D2C channels. Build polished presentation decks and visual layouts for internal and client reviews. Make artwork revisions, adjustments, and updates based on feedback from the creative and account management teams. Resize, reformat, and adapt existing artwork for various products, garment styles, and production requirements. Ensure all artwork maintains brand consistency, accuracy, and the highest level of attention to detail. Production Coordination & Artwork Preparation Work closely with the Production team to prepare and deliver time-sensitive artwork setups, ensuring all files meet production specifications and deadlines. Prepare accurate, production-ready artwork for screen printing, embroidery, specialty inks, and other garment decoration methods. Review print proofs for accuracy, including artwork placement, sizing, color, spelling, and overall execution, ensuring all details align with approved designs. Coordinate with Production to address artwork revisions, resolve technical challenges, and maintain efficient communication throughout the production process. Prioritize urgent artwork requests and proof approvals to support tight production schedules and avoid unnecessary delays. Ensure final artwork files are properly formatted, organized, and ready for production. Artwork Catalog Management Maintain and regularly update Manhead's artwork catalog across our extensive artist roster. Ensure all artwork, revisions, approvals, and final production files are accurately organized, labeled, and easily accessible. Maintain consistency in file naming, version control, and artwork documentation. Ensure approved designs and final production artwork are properly archived for future reference, reorders, and ongoing merchandise programs. Work with internal teams to ensure the artwork catalog remains current, accurate, and complete. Collaboration & Project Management Collaborate closely with the Graphic Design, Apparel Design, Production, and Account Management teams to ensure artwork and production needs are met. Serve as a reliable resource for cross-functional teams, responding efficiently to artwork requests and production-related needs. Manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining accuracy, organization, and established deadlines. Communicate proactively regarding project status, outstanding artwork needs, potential challenges, and timelines. Maintain a positive, collaborative attitude and contribute to an efficient, solutions-oriented team environment. Qualifications Previous experience working with graphics specifically for apparel and merchandise. Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, particularly Illustrator and Photoshop. Strong understanding of typography, composition, color accuracy, and graphic layout. Working knowledge of apparel production processes, including screen printing, embroidery, and various decoration techniques. Experience preparing production-ready artwork and reviewing print proofs. Experience creating apparel mockups and presentation layouts. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to quality control. Strong organizational skills with the ability to maintain detailed artwork libraries, file structures, and version control. Ability to follow established creative direction and execute revisions accurately and efficiently. Ability to prioritize competing deadlines and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Strong communication skills and a collaborative, team-first mindset. A positive attitude, strong work ethic, and willingness to learn and grow. An interest in music, fashion, and the merchandise industry. A portfolio demonstrating apparel graphics, production knowledge, and technical execution. What We're Looking For We're looking for someone who is highly organized, detail-driven, dependable, and takes genuine pride in their work. Someone who understands that even the smallest details matter, whether it's preparing a time-sensitive print file, catching an error on a proof, building an accurate product mockup, or keeping our artwork catalog organized and current. The ideal candidate is comfortable working within established creative direction, takes feedback well, and knows how to balance quality with efficiency. Above all, we're looking for a team player who is proactive, adaptable, and eager to support the creative and production teams in delivering exceptional merchandise. At Manhead, great design starts with a strong vision, but exceptional execution is what brings it to life. About Manhead LLC Manhead is a worldwide, full service, merchandise and experiential company c reating the global intersection of music, fashion and culture through branded experiences that strengthen the bond between artists and fans. For over thirteen years, Manhead has succeeded as one of the leading, independently owned music/entertainment merchandise companies, specializing in touring, e-commerce, creative, retail, licensing, collaborations, and pop-up shops.

**PhD Internship 2027: Boston Research** Boston, US | Full-time | Fixed-term| Hybrid Salary: $55.70 per hour, DOE **About us** Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in materials and climate science to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent, and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. **About the role** Delivering practical quantum error correction requires tightly integrated quantum and classical systems. The quantum hardware connectivity, its physical error rates, circuit compilation, and compatible QEC codes all affect performance. On the classical side, decoding algorithms must process large volumes of error data within demanding latency, bandwidth, compute, and power constraints. As a Research Intern, you will investigate simulating, running, and decoding QEC experiments. Along with your supervisor, you will frame a research project. Your project will sit at the intersection of quantum error correction, computer simulations, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design. Depending on the project, you could study noise models for quantum hardware, work on efficient simulations for QEC experiments, explore efficient QEC decoding or predecoding methods, model the classical resources required by fault-tolerant quantum programs, or investigate how decoding workloads can be distributed across different levels of a computing system. You will work alongside Riverlane’s quantum scientists and engineers in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with support from a dedicated supervisor. Your work will contribute to our understanding of how QEC systems can meet the performance requirements of increasingly large quantum computers. **What you will do** - Develop algorithms, simulations or architectural models to evaluate potential approaches - Investigate methods for reducing the compute, communication, memory, latency or power requirements associated with QEC - Explore trade-offs between decoding performance, logical error suppression and classical resource requirements - Collaborate with quantum scientists and engineers working across QEC theory, decoding, software and hardware - Analyse results and communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports - Produce clear, reproducible research code and supporting documentation **What we need** - You must be currently pursuing a PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another related technical field - Research experience in at least one of the following areas: - Running quantum circuits on quantum hardware - Decoding algorithms or quantum error-correcting codes - Experience developing computational models, simulations or research software - Proficiency in Python, C, C++ or another relevant programming language - A strong understanding of computer systems and architecture - Computer architecture or quantum-classical systems - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills - The ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly - The ability to take initiative and work effectively with researchers and engineers from different disciplines - Authorization to work in the United States for the duration of the internship **Even better if…** - You have experience researching qLDPC or surface codes - You are familiar with QEC decoding or predecoding techniques - You have explored the classical resource requirements of fault-tolerant quantum computing - You have experience with scientific computing, quantum circuit simulation or QEC simulation tools - You have contributed to academic publications, open-source software or collaborative research projects - You have experience with hardware-software or compiler-hardware co-design - You understand the latency, bandwidth or power constraints affecting quantum control and decoding systems **Important notes** - You must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the internship - If you intend to work under Curricular Practical Training (CPT), Optional Practical Training (OPT) or another form of student employment authorization, you are responsible for obtaining the necessary approval before your start date - Any offer of employment will be contingent upon verification of your identity and authorization to work in the United States, as required by law - You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks - You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane - This internship is based at our US office in Cambridge, Massachusetts **How to apply** Please upload your CV and a cover letter. Your CV should include details of your education, research experience and relevant technical skills. Your cover letter should explain why you are applying for the internship and the skills and experience you would bring to the role. **Deadline** Please submit your application by November 6, 2026. **Pay and Expenses** We will reimburse reasonable expenses incurred as part of your role, such as approved travel to meetings or conferences. We are unable to cover the cost of travelling to Cambridge, Massachusetts at the beginning or end of the internship or accommodation during the internship. **What you can expect from us** You can expect a diverse and collaborative working environment that brings together experts in software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics, mathematics and other technical fields. Our global team represents more than 20 nationalities. We also provide free snacks and refreshments and organize regular social and cultural events. If you have any questions, please contact [jobs@riverlane.com](mailto:jobs@riverlane.com). *Riverlane is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome qualified applicants and consider them for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.* *We know that strong candidates may not meet every requirement listed. If you are interested in the opportunity and believe your experience could be relevant, we encourage you to apply.* *Riverlane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you require an accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know. We will be happy to help.*

description: Role Description The Greenager Program is a San Francisco Recreation and Park Department and Port of San Francisco Youth Stewardship and Leadership program. The program was created and designed to offer teens a chance to play an important role in the community by improving the City’s green spaces, raising awareness, creating place-based projects and/or projects based on issues or themes that participants value and are interested in. The program is for 9th to 11th graders who live in or attend a school in the Tenderloin, Northeast, or Southeast neighborhoods. Greenagers are trained and provided with multiple leadership opportunities. They lead public volunteer service projects, participate in community events, go on fun team excursions, and more. With this belief, San Francisco became the first city in the United States for which 100% of its residents live within a ten-minute walk of a park. The Recreation and Park Department’s goal is to close the gaps and improve equity and access to quality parks and open space, and recreation activities for historically marginalized communities. We envision a department that proactively infuses racial and social equity in its internal operations. Amid a dynamic and ever-evolving urban landscape, the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department stewards one of the premier urban park systems in America. In 2017, San Francisco became the first city in the nation where all residents have access to a park within a 10-minute walk, a direct result of the Department’s commitment to increasing and improving parkland in the city Learn More . Considered by San Franciscans to be one of the City’s most popular and effective public agencies, our Department currently manages more than 230 parks, playgrounds and open spaces throughout San Francisco, including two outside city limits—Sharp Park in Pacifica and Camp Mather in the High Sierras. The system includes full-complex recreation centers, swimming pools, golf courses, sports fields and numerous small-to-medium-sized clubhouses that offer a variety of sports- and arts-related recreation programs for people of all ages. Included in the Department’s responsibilities are Golden Gate Park, Coit Tower, the Marina Yacht Harbor, the San Francisco Zoo and Lake Merced. More than 2,000 talented individuals are part of our team, from gardeners, foresters, and recreation leaders to park rangers, custodians, electricians, painters and more. Our core mission, as it has been throughout our history, is to provide opportunities for San Francisco residents and visitors alike to gather, play, learn, relax, and enjoy nature in the city.

description: **Build your civil engineering career in site design.** You'll work on real land development projects, design real sites, and grow through hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship from engineers who want to see you succeed. **About the Role** Bohler’s West Palm Beach, FL office is seeking an Entry Level Civil Engineer (Land Development) who is eager to learn, grow, and make a positive impact. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, designers, and project managers to bring exciting land development projects to life, including site planning, grading, utilities, and stormwater management. The opportunity to take ownership of your career with an unsurpassed focus on career development and mentorship - A Learning & Development department that facilitates ongoing technical and professional growth, including individualized AutoCAD Civil 3D training - Complete visibility and exposure to all aspects of land development projects - The chance to immerse yourself in the design process while working side-by-side with talented teammates - Open and transparent communication with senior leadership and local office management - Team-building activities, office events, and a collaborative, high-energy environment **What You’ll Bring** - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field - 0–1+ years of residential, commercial, or industrial site design and permitting experience - Familiarity with AutoCAD Civil 3D (preferred; training provided if not yet proficient) - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to teamwork - Motivation to take initiative and contribute to shared goals - EIT certification is helpful but not required **Get hands-on experience contributing to real projects, and see how your work helps shape communities and your career.** #LI-Onsite

description: **This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Machine Learning Engineer, New Grad – Quora based in the United States.** Launch your machine learning career by helping build AI-powered systems that improve content quality and safety across a global knowledge-sharing platform. In this role, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to design, develop, evaluate, and deploy large language model (LLM)-powered agents that identify harmful content, detect abuse, and automate complex moderation tasks. You will work on challenging machine learning problems at scale, with opportunities to experiment with emerging AI technologies and contribute to systems serving millions of users. As part of a small, collaborative engineering team, you will take ownership of meaningful projects and follow them from early development through production deployment. You will evaluate model performance, investigate failure cases, and continuously improve the accuracy, reliability, and efficiency of AI-driven solutions. This remote opportunity is ideal for a recent graduate or emerging engineer with a strong technical foundation, a curiosity for AI innovation, and a passion for building safer online experiences. ### Accountabilities - Design, build, and deploy LLM-powered agents that detect and address spam, harassment, and other policy-violating content across a large-scale online platform. - Develop agentic workflows that automate complex content moderation and user safety tasks, improving the efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness of existing systems. - Build and enhance machine learning models and AI-powered systems that adapt to evolving abuse patterns, emerging threats, and changing content safety challenges. - Evaluate model and agent performance through offline testing, online experiments, and production monitoring, balancing accuracy, reliability, latency, and computational costs. - Investigate model failures, analyze edge cases, conduct experiments, and refine technical approaches to improve system quality and overall performance. - Identify new opportunities to apply machine learning, large language models, and emerging AI techniques to content quality, platform integrity, and user safety. - Collaborate closely with experienced machine learning engineers and cross-functional colleagues to develop practical solutions to complex technical challenges. - Take ownership of projects throughout the engineering lifecycle, from problem identification and experimentation to implementation, deployment, and ongoing optimization. - Contribute to a culture of continuous learning, technical experimentation, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving. - Help develop scalable, reliable, and cost-effective AI systems that support a positive user experience and protect the integrity of a global knowledge-sharing community. ## Requirements - A bachelor's, master's, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, either completed or currently in progress. - Strong understanding of the mathematical foundations underlying machine learning algorithms and their practical applications. - Coursework, research, or project experience involving large language model applications, transformer architectures, or related AI technologies. - Strong programming skills in Python and the ability to develop, test, and maintain reliable code. - Genuine enthusiasm for learning, experimenting with new technologies, and continuously improving both individual and team performance. - Availability to begin full-time employment in early 2027. - Ability to participate in meetings and spontaneous collaboration during the team's coordination hours, Monday through Friday, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time. - Previous software engineering experience through an internship, professional role, open-source contribution, or coding competition is preferred. - Practical experience building, implementing, or evaluating LLM-powered agents through academic projects, research, internships, or production systems is an advantage. - Familiarity with AI-assisted coding tools, such as Claude Code or Codex, preferably through regular hands-on use. - Coursework, research, or project experience in natural language processing (NLP) is beneficial. - Familiarity with machine learning frameworks and infrastructure, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Spark, or Kubernetes, is an advantage. - A genuine interest in content safety, online community quality, and the responsible application of artificial intelligence. - Strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate technical issues and develop evidence-based solutions. - A collaborative mindset and willingness to learn from experienced colleagues, share ideas, and contribute to a high-performing engineering team. - An interest in supporting a mission centered on expanding access to knowledge and creating positive online experiences. - Candidates from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply, including those who may not meet every preferred qualification but demonstrate strong technical potential and a passion for machine learning. ## Benefits - **Competitive U.S. salary:** Annual base compensation ranging from $107,360 to $152,900 USD, depending on experience, education, location, and business needs. - **Equity compensation:** Eligibility for equity awards and refreshers, with a flexible equity program available in eligible countries that may allow a portion of equity compensation to be received as cash. - **Comprehensive healthcare:** Medical, dental, and vision coverage. - **Remote-first work environment:** Flexibility to work remotely from eligible locations within the United States. - **Remote work reimbursement:** Financial support to help cover eligible remote-working expenses. - **Paid time off:** Time away from work to support rest, personal commitments, and work-life balance. - **Employee assistance programs:** Resources designed to support employee well-being. - **Professional development:** Opportunities to learn from experienced machine learning engineers and contribute to challenging, real-world AI projects. - **Hands-on AI innovation:** Exposure to large language models, agentic workflows, production machine learning systems, and modern engineering tools. - **Meaningful technical impact:** The opportunity to develop AI systems that improve content quality, detect harmful behavior, and help create safer online communities. - **Inclusive culture:** A collaborative environment that values diverse perspectives, experimentation, transparency, and continuous learning.

Responsibilities Personally monitors either visually, electronically or audibly a variety of assigned areas, or grounds by working in a variety of assignments including but not limited to roving inside the facilities, roving in a vehicle, other locations deemed appropriate. Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth. With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection. **Overview** As a **Mechanical Engineering Co-op**, you will be an embedded member of our Spacecraft Mechanical and Thermal team and contribute directly to the tools, systems, and hardware that enable spacecraft production and integration. This is a six-month, full-time co-op intended for students who have already developed hands-on mechanical engineering experience through a prior internship, co-op, research role, or similarly rigorous engineering project. You will take ownership of meaningful engineering work spanning design, manufacturing, validation, and implementation. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a fast-paced startup environment and see your work contribute to spacecraft production and integration. **What You'll Do** - Own the design and development of mechanical hardware supporting spacecraft manufacturing, integration, and test activities. - Partner with engineering, manufacturing, and operations teams to define requirements and develop practical design solutions. - Create detailed CAD models, manufacturing drawings, and engineering documentation. - Perform engineering analyses to validate structural, mechanical, and packaging performance. - Coordinate fabrication, procurement, assembly, and integration of designed hardware. - Support integration, testing, verification, and continuous improvement efforts. - Participate in design reviews and cross-functional engineering discussions. - Communicate technical progress, tradeoffs, risks, and final results to engineering leadership. **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Expected graduation between December 2026 and May 2028. - Completed at least one prior internship or co-op in a mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, or closely related hardware-engineering role. - Demonstrated experience designing, building, testing, or supporting mechanical hardware beyond coursework alone. - Proficiency with SolidWorks or similar 3D CAD software. - Ability to create or interpret mechanical drawings and basic engineering documentation. - Working knowledge of mechanical design fundamentals, including material selection, fastening, tolerancing, load paths, and design tradeoffs. - Ability to commit to a full-time, six-month co-op. - Comfortable working in both office and hands-on laboratory/manufacturing environments. - Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills. - Ability to work on-site in Burlingame throughout the co-op. **Preferred Qualifications** - Experience designing and releasing hardware for fabrication, including drawings, GD&T, tolerance analysis, and/or bills of materials. - Familiarity with DFM/DFA principles and common manufacturing processes such as machining, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, composites, or assembly processes. - Hands-on experience with mechanical assembly, integration, test, troubleshooting, or validation. - Experience with structural analysis, hand calculations, FEA, or test-data analysis. - Experience in a fast-paced hardware environment, such as robotics, CubeSat teams, Formula SAE, aerospace, research laboratories, or manufacturing. - Interest in spacecraft, aerospace, and high-reliability hardware development. **Why You'll Love This Co-op** - Take ownership of engineering work that directly supports spacecraft production. - Work through the full hardware-development cycle: requirements, design, fabrication, integration, test, and deployment. - Gain six months of immersive experience alongside experienced aerospace engineers. - See your projects progress from concept through operational deployment. - Work in a highly collaborative environment with meaningful technical ownership. - Build practical, career-relevant experience in spacecraft and high-reliability hardware development. - Help develop technology redefining the future of global navigation. **For U.S. Roles:** To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). **For U.K. Roles:** To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC). **For Canada Roles:** Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

role: Research Intern (Academic Credit) - Department of Neurology - Per Diem (On-site)
description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The Research Internship program provides students and trainees an opportunity to develop basic research skills. Interns in this program are provided the opportunity to experience and observe many different aspects of basic, translational and/or clinical research. This program offers interns a unique experience, which is intended to provide a wealth of knowledge about the numerous options for a career in healthcare research. Typically lasting not more than a twelve-month period, this internship will expose participants to a diverse spectrum of clinical and non-clinical based research investigations. Under direct supervision from the assigned Postdoctoral Scientist, senior-level Research Associate and/or Principal Investigator, the intern will be provided with basic research instruction, will be oriented to the Institutional Review Board and other Human Subjects courses, and will be introduced to new and innovative research practices and techniques. Overview of Department & Mentor The Goldrich Center for Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders clinic occupies 15,000 square feet on the 6th floor of the Cedars-Sinai the Advanced Health Sciences Pavilion (AHSP) building, which contains 100,000 square feet of state-of-the-art wet lab and supporting space for neuroscience and neurology related research. The Center oversees the care of over 500 patients per year, has two fellowship-trained behavioral neurology and neuropsychiatry specialists, one fellowship trained geriatric medicine specialist, one fellowship trained geriatric psychiatrist, three memory disorders nurse practitioners, one behavioral neurology and neuropsychiatry fellow, two neuropsychologists specializing in memory disorders, and one dedicated social worker. Center research personnel include one research manager and one memory disorders clinical research coordinator. Dr. Mitzi Gonzales is an Associate Professor of the Department of Neurology and the Director of Translational Research for the Goldrich Center for Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. She is a board-certified clinical neuropsychologist and clinician scientist, who has led and collaborated on large-scale research efforts evaluating plasma proteins, sensory-motor functioning, and broader aging phenotypes as biomarkers for neurodegenerative disease risk. Dr. Sarah Kremen is an Associate Professor of the Department of Neurology, where she serves as the Director of the Neurobehavior Program in the Department of Neurology and the Goldrich Alzheimer’s and Memory Disorders Center. She is a board-certified neurologist with subspecialty training in Neurobehavior and Neuropsychiatry. Dr. Kremen’s research focuses on clinicopathological correlation in neurodegenerative diseases, Alzheimer’s disease clinical trials, and the lived impact of implementation of new diagnostics and therapies. Dr. Gonzales and Dr. Kremen co-lead for the Goldrich Observational ADRD Longitudinal studies, which the visiting scholar will partake in. Role Activities & Timeline January 15th - January 31st: Human subjects training; research ethics, fundamentals of the informed consent process February 1st – February 14th: Clinical research study design review; discussion of observational research projects; protocol review February 15th – March 14th: Overview community-engaged research, introduction to neurodegenerative diseases; observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; introduction to data coding, REDCap; research literature review March 15th – April 14th: Introduction to cognitive assessments; hands on administration practice; observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; data quality assurance and management; research hypothesis generation April 15th – May 15th: Observations of observational clinical research procedures; attendance at outreach events; attend consensus reviews and team meetings; research hypothesis testing and basic statistics, research abstract writing All weeks: mentorship in clinical trial design, implementation, data management, statistics, and abstract writing Systems Access: N/A Role Summary & Objectives The Research Intern will have the opportunity to work with an interdisciplinary team of neuropsychologists, neurologists, geriatricians, and clinical researchers with expertise in aging and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). The Research Intern will be immersed in the clinical research process, gaining experience on study design and implementation. The Research Intern will be able to partake in two clinical research studies. The first, the GOAL Study, is an internally funded project that aims to establish a longitudinal cohort of individuals of across the ADRD continuum. The second is the RAPID study, which deploys brief cognitive testing and questionnaires relevant to ADRD. The Research Intern will learn fundamental skills relevant to clinical research in aging and ADRD including best practices for the informed consent process, human subjects' protection, clinical cohort study design, and community-based participatory research engagement. The overarching goal is to provide foundational clinical research skills that the successful candidate can utilize to develop independent research projects in the future. In addition, the Research Intern will learn data management skills using REDCap, basic statistical analyses, hypothesis development, and abstract writing. The successful candidate will develop and implement a clinical research project that can be completed utilizing existing datasets and will produce an abstract that can be submitted to a local or national research conference. Required Education & Experience Must be 18 years of age or older. Must have a HS Diploma or GED. Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship.

communicates information (for example, facts, ideas, or messages) in a succinct and organized manner; produces written information, which may include technical material that is appropriate for the intended audience ***Desired:*** - A strong sense of mission in supporting national security initiatives - An impeccable work ethic, integrity, and a positive, can-do attitude This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. role: Global Supply Chain Rotational Program, Volume Buyer I, New College Grad- Bachelor's (Gloucester, MA)
description: **Who We Are** Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. **What We Offer** Salary: $60,000.00 - $73,500.00 Location: Gloucester,MA You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our [benefits](https://hrportal.ehr.com/applied/). As a Buyer, you’ll be responsible for purchasing the materials, supplies, machinery, and services that equip our state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities. You’ll collaborate across teams and showcase your organization and strategic planning skills to monitor inventory, manage delivery scheduling, negotiate with suppliers, and procure essential items that transform possibilities into realities for our customers and teams. **Program Overview** Through the 30-month Supply Chain Undergraduate Rotational Development Program, you will rotate through positions in Purchasing/Sourcing, Project/Program Management, and Supplier Account Management over the course of 18 months, then apply your learnings to a “Final Placement” role for an additional 12 months. Assignment of Final Placement roles will be based on business need, role availability, and the individual assessments of candidates’ performance and skills displayed during their rotations. In the program, participants develop and refine the technical and business skills required to be successful in the Supply Chain organization. You will experience a blended learning environment which includes mentorship, job shadowing, and expanded networking opportunities with leaders and within our Employee Resource Groups, such as the Young Professionals Network (YPN). Participants will have the opportunity to gain high level visibility and create significant impact within a global manufacturing organization. **Position Details** During a series of rotations, participants will take on full-time responsibility of their functional role, which may include: - Issuing RFQs, analyzing proposals, negotiating prices, executing orders, and ensuring delivery in support of volume manufacturing requirements. - Developing strategies to procure components at the lowest cost consistent with consideration of quality, reliability of source, and urgency of need. - Assisting with development, alignment, and implementation of commodity strategies across Applied Business Units. - Driving resolution to systematic supply chain issues affecting quality, cost, delivery or lead-time. - Assisting in developing and presenting high-level cost reduction opportunities. - Presenting sourcing, cost, lead time reduction, capacity initiatives to key stakeholders. - Forecasting and communicating engineering, materials, and manufacturing requirements to suppliers. - Providing critical input to outsourcing decisions by performing Make vs. Buy analysis. **Requirements** - This is a 30-month rotational program. Candidates should be prepared to complete the full program. - Graduating with a Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Distribution, Industrial Engineering, Management Information Systems, Business Analytics or related field - Good academic standing with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or above on a 4.0 scale - Proficiency in developing effective executive reports and presentations - Proficiency in Microsoft office tools - Excellent listening, writing, quantitative, qualitative and oral communication skills - Ability to handle multiple assignments concurrently - Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to interact cross-organizationally - Ability to problem-solve creatively and analytically - Commitment to quality and customer satisfaction - Detail-oriented; ability to multi-task; deadline-oriented - Flexible and adaptable mindset - Thrive in a results-driven culture - Nice to have technical skills: Statistics, Machine Learning, Data Analytics, R, SAS, SQL, Python Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
