role: Mechatronic Apprentice I, Amazon Fulfillment RME, SDF8 RME
description: This permanent, full-time position is located in Jeffersonville, IN. Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. Key job responsibilities Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals. • You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells. • You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components. • You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc. • You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head Program Requirements: • Flexible to relocate after completion of the program • Able to enroll in and attend a 9-week training at one of four designated training providers (Location to be determined post-interview) • Meet the minimum qualifying score on a Mechanical Aptitude Test Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment.

role: Program Manager II, NAST GoCarts Management , Scheduling Transfers And Reusables
description: Come build the version of GoCarts logistics that schedules itself. Every day, our network moves tens of thousands of GoCarts between fulfillment, sortation, and repair sites, and every one of those moves is a promise, that the right GoCarts show up at the right site before it runs short. When that promise is at risk, the GoCarts scheduling team is the one that catches it. We're good at catching. We need a Program Manager to help us build for the day we don't have to. GoCarts scheduling is the layer that keeps the network solvent in reusable assets. We own the proactive planning that places GoCarts before sites feel the gap, the reactive intervention that resolves shortages in real time, and — this is the part that matters — the mechanisms that make those interventions unnecessary. Our hardest problems aren't scheduling problems. They're throughput, visibility, and signal problems, and we're moving the whole program from reactive execution to proactive, data-driven decision-making. In this role you will: Own outcomes, not status decks. Build mechanisms, not workarounds. Automate what you touch. Turn bottlenecks into asks leadership can act on. Key job responsibilities - Own the end-to-end health of the GoCarts scheduling program across proactive and reactive tracks, and the metrics that define it: asset solvency, defective-asset rate, trailer dwell, and fill rate. - Drive peak-season readiness, including solvency targets, defective-asset reduction, injection plans, and contingency strategy, and manage the tradeoffs between them. - Diagnose true network constraints, separating the real bottleneck (for example, repair throughput) from the symptom (scheduling), and build the data and business case to resolve it with the right owners. - Manage cross-functional dependencies with repair and capacity partners, holding partner commitments to committed dates and escalating risk clearly and early. - Close data-visibility gaps with partner data teams, improving scan compliance and site-level inventory signals so scheduling runs on actuals rather than assumption. - Partner with science and automation teams to advance the roadmap toward continuous demand-versus-inventory detection, alerting, and model-driven resolution. - Author crisp, data-backed narratives for senior leadership that frame risk, ownership, the ask, and the plan forward. - Develop and own KPI reporting across the program portfolio, with clear visibility into milestones and performance.

role: Program Manager II, NAST GoCarts Management , Scheduling Transfers And Reusables
description: Come build the version of GoCarts logistics that schedules itself. Every day, our network moves tens of thousands of GoCarts between fulfillment, sortation, and repair sites, and every one of those moves is a promise, that the right GoCarts show up at the right site before it runs short. When that promise is at risk, the GoCarts scheduling team is the one that catches it. We're good at catching. We need a Program Manager to help us build for the day we don't have to. GoCarts scheduling is the layer that keeps the network solvent in reusable assets. We own the proactive planning that places GoCarts before sites feel the gap, the reactive intervention that resolves shortages in real time, and — this is the part that matters — the mechanisms that make those interventions unnecessary. Our hardest problems aren't scheduling problems. They're throughput, visibility, and signal problems, and we're moving the whole program from reactive execution to proactive, data-driven decision-making. In this role you will: Own outcomes, not status decks. Build mechanisms, not workarounds. Automate what you touch. Turn bottlenecks into asks leadership can act on. Key job responsibilities - Own the end-to-end health of the GoCarts scheduling program across proactive and reactive tracks, and the metrics that define it: asset solvency, defective-asset rate, trailer dwell, and fill rate. - Drive peak-season readiness, including solvency targets, defective-asset reduction, injection plans, and contingency strategy, and manage the tradeoffs between them. - Diagnose true network constraints, separating the real bottleneck (for example, repair throughput) from the symptom (scheduling), and build the data and business case to resolve it with the right owners. - Manage cross-functional dependencies with repair and capacity partners, holding partner commitments to committed dates and escalating risk clearly and early. - Close data-visibility gaps with partner data teams, improving scan compliance and site-level inventory signals so scheduling runs on actuals rather than assumption. - Partner with science and automation teams to advance the roadmap toward continuous demand-versus-inventory detection, alerting, and model-driven resolution. - Author crisp, data-backed narratives for senior leadership that frame risk, ownership, the ask, and the plan forward. - Develop and own KPI reporting across the program portfolio, with clear visibility into milestones and performance.

role: Visiting Graduate Student (Academic Credit) - Simpkins Lab - Department of Neurology - Per Diem (On-site)
description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. Dr. Alexis Simpkins invites you to consider this great opportunity to join her dynamic team! We can only consider applicants who will be able to commute to our Los Angeles location a few times per week. You must reside in the commutable area. Overview of Department & Mentor The Neurology Department provides clinical care, quality improvement, and research focused on stroke and cerebrovascular disease. Under the mentorship of Dr. Alexis Simpkins, the graduate intern will support quality-improvement initiatives that strengthen physician staffing processes and patient care coordination across the stroke clinic and related services. Activities may include reviewing staffing and coverage workflows, analyzing appointment and referral data, mapping handoffs among neurology, primary care, rehabilitation, and other services, and finding opportunities to improve timely follow-up and continuity of care. The role is educational and administrative/operational; it does not replace a staff position or involve independent clinical decision-making. Role Activities & Timeline: Role Activities and curriculum (skills to be learned) over the course of 1 year: Literature review 1 month Chart view and redcap entry 7 months Manuscript writing last 3 months Presentation development 1 month Career Development mentorship throughout: CV building Pre-residency neurology prep lectures Presentation skills Basics of project development and critical thinking for research project development Systems Access: N/A Role Summary & Objectives: This internship is designed for a student enrolled in a master’s program in health administration. The intern will learn how healthcare operations, workforce planning, and care-coordination processes affect access, quality, and patient experience in a stroke-care setting. Working with the mentor and relevant clinic leaders, the intern will define a quality-improvement question, collect and organize de-identified or minimum-necessary operational data, conduct workflow and root-cause analyses, and help develop and evaluate practical interventions related to physician staffing and patient care coordination. Objectives are to: Assess physician staffing, scheduling, coverage, and workload patterns; Identify barriers to timely referrals, follow-up, and communication across care teams; Develop process maps, dashboards, and recommendations; Learn quality-improvement methods such as PDSA, Lean, process mapping, and run-chart interpretation; and (5) present findings to collaborators in a concise report or presentation. All work will follow institutional privacy, compliance, and quality-improvement/IRB requirements, and the intern will not make independent clinical, staffing, or privileging decisions. Required Education & Experience Must be 18 years of age or older. Must have a HS Diploma or GED. Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship. VISITORS: Must be receiving funding from an eligible sponsoring institution (employer, educator, funder, etc.). Preferred Education, Experience, and Skills: Graduate student currently enrolled in a graduate school (Master’s program, PhD, or Medical School).

role: Research Intern - Efficient AI Software Systems
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Researchers in artificial intelligence (AI) are building systems that can reason, plan and act on behalf of the people who use them, from writing software to automating complex, multistep tasks. As these systems become more capable and more widely used, making them efficient matters more and more. That means getting the most value from the compute they use, choosing the right capabilities for each task, and adapting to the needs of the people and environments they serve. Microsoft's deep investments in the field are advancing the state of the art in efficient and agentic AI. Its researchers combine machine learning, systems research and rigorous empirical evaluation to understand how intelligent systems can balance quality, speed and cost, and how they can improve with experience. The research, tools and services that result are woven into existing and new products and, at the same time, made open and accessible to the broader community in a bid to accelerate innovation, democratize AI and help developers and organizations do more with the resources they have. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a relevant field. #### **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### #### Preferred Qualifications - 1+ year(s) of experience (classroom or work-related) in one or more of the following areas: machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, AI agents, or machine learning systems. - 1+ completed courses in probability and statistics, machine learning, or optimization. - Experience conducting research on the efficiency, cost, or performance of machine learning models or systems (e.g., inference optimization, model selection, model compression, or adaptive computation). - Experience building or evaluating applications or agents that use large language models. - Experience designing benchmarks or experiments to evaluate machine learning systems, and analyzing quantitative results. - Experience comparing alternative methods, prototypes, or analytical approaches to address a research or applied problem. - Experience collaborating with researchers or engineering teams on a research or applied project. - Prior research experience evidenced by publications, preprints, or open-source research projects. - Experience communicating research findings through a presentation, poster, report, or publication. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. This is a fully remote position ideal for individuals who are organized, responsive, and enjoy working in a structured, client-focused environment. ### Key Responsibilities - Assist with coordinating bookings, reservations, and scheduling requests - Gather and organize client information and preferences - Review reservation details to ensure accuracy and completeness - Communicate confirmations, updates, and follow-ups in a timely manner - Maintain organized records of bookings and client interactions - Support a smooth and efficient coordination process from start to finish ### Requirements - Strong organizational and multitasking skills - Clear and professional communication abilities - Ability to work independently in a remote environment - Detail-oriented with strong follow-through - Comfortable using email, online systems, and scheduling tools ### **Preferred (Not Required)** - Experience in customer service, administrative support, or coordination roles - Interest in travel, hospitality, or event-related services ### What We Offer - Flexible remote work environment - Structured onboarding and ongoing guidance - Opportunities for growth based on performance - Supportive and collaborative team setting ### **Work Environment** This is a remote role requiring a reliable internet connection and the ability to stay organized and productive in a virtual workspace.

We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation. Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet. **Location & Team Gatherings** Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016. We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON. We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture. **About this role** As a Campus Project Director on Intersect's Construction team, you'll oversee the complete execution and delivery of multi-facility clean energy campuses designed to power Google data centers. You will lead complex, multi-technology buildouts encompassing utility-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and high-voltage substation and transmission infrastructure, serving as the single point of accountability for site performance, vendor integration, and executive reporting. You will collaborate closely with internal engineering, procurement, asset management, and executive leadership, as well as external EPC partners and hyperscale client stakeholders. By deploying modern construction management platforms and leveraging clear, strategic communication, you'll drive operational excellence while ensuring safety and quality standards across all sites. **Team overview** This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Construction team partners across development, engineering, procurement, and operations to build resilient, gigawatt-scale power infrastructure that energizes critical digital infrastructure. Joining this team means directing high-impact energy campuses from earthworks to commercial operation, shaping how clean energy powers the future of computing while growing alongside a dedicated group of industry leaders. **What you'll do** Direct Multi-Technology Campus Execution - Lead end-to-end site delivery for multi-facility energy campuses combining solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage transmission scope. - Manage and mentor Campus Project Managers, serving as their primary escalation point and holding overall accountability for the success of the campus as a whole. - Establish site governance, schedule baselines, and budget oversight across simultaneous project builds powering Google data center infrastructure. - Incorporate advanced field management tools, including Terabase Construct and AI Clearing, to track site progress, optimize craft sequencing, and ensure quality. Drive High-Voltage Integration and Technical Compliance - Oversee the seamless integration of high-voltage substations, interconnection facilities, and generation assets into active grid and off-grid interconnections. - Troubleshoot complex engineering, procurement, and field bottlenecks alongside technical experts to maintain strict commercial operation timelines. - Evaluate natural gas power integration options where applicable to enhance campus resilience and microgrid performance. Lead Executive Communication and Strategic Stakeholder Alignment - Synthesize high-density technical, financial, and schedule data into executive-ready slide decks for leadership and key off-taker stakeholders. - Deliver regular strategic briefings to executive leadership detailing campus health, risk contingencies, and critical path milestones. - Maintain strong working relationships with EPC firms, key equipment vendors, utilities, and local regulatory authorities. Strengthen Safety, Cost, and Operational Culture - Enforce rigorous safety programs across all campus sites, cultivating an environment that prioritizes total personnel well-being. - Manage financial workflows using Stampli and internal financial tools to control capital expenditure, change orders, and contract compliance. - Utilize generative AI platforms such as Claude and Gemini to streamline reporting workflows, executive briefing prep, and team documentation. **What you'll bring** - Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil/Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. - 10+ years of project management experience in power generation, with 3+ years specifically as a Project Director leading utility-scale clean energy projects. - Proven track record delivering complex campus-scale builds featuring solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage (HV) scope; natural gas experience is a plus. - Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex technical challenges and produce executive-level presentation decks for C-suite leadership and external client stakeholders. - Proficiency with modern construction, workflow, and AI tools including Terabase Construct, AI Clearing, Stampli, Lucidchart, G Suite, Claude, and Gemini. - Willingness to travel up to 50% to active campus sites with a minimum once-a-month onsite footprint. - Strong team builder and strategic thinker with an adaptable leadership style focused on cross-functional alignment and field enablement. - Deep commitment to long-term value, safety, and authentic leadership, fully aligned with Intersect's core values: Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

## **About Abridge** Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients. Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems. We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh. ## **The Role** We're looking for Software Engineering Interns to join Abridge's Engineering team for a 3-month internship program in Fall 2026, Spring 2027, or Summer 2027 with the possibility of extension. You'll collaborate with our engineering team to build and ship real-world features that translate cutting-edge language model capabilities into dependable clinical systems. With mentorship and guidance, you'll gain hands-on experience designing, coding, and releasing AI-powered software that makes a meaningful impact on clinicians' workflows. **What You'll Do** - Design and build end-to-end features, enhancing our existing systems and contributing to agentic LLM workflows (retrieval pipelines, structured tool use, chained LLM calls) - Fix user-facing bugs and issues, and make quality-of-life improvements across our backend and frontend systems - Get hands-on with evaluation frameworks that measure accuracy, robustness, and clinical reliability - Help prototype with new models, prompting techniques, and open-source orchestration tools (LangChain, LlamaIndex, etc.) - Develop a strong user-centric mindset, building empathy for Abridge's clinicians and the challenges they face - Collaborate across cross-functional product teams — design, product, machine learning, and infrastructure — to ship features to our customers - Receive guidance from an experienced software engineering mentor, and collaborate one-on-one with teammates within your pod **What You'll Bring** - A strong interest in pursuing a full-time software engineering role in 2027 or 2028 — high-performing interns are eligible to receive a return offer - AI tooling is already part of how you work — you use it to write, debug, and learn faster, and you know when to trust it vs. verify - Passion for and understanding of Abridge's mission - A curious, adaptable, and proactive mindset, with a desire to learn and grow in a fast-paced startup environment - A collaborative, low-ego mindset — we move fast, and we need team players who are eager to contribute wherever needed **Base Salary:** $40/hr Must be willing to work from our San Francisco (Potrero) office 5x per week. This internship is based in our San Francisco office. Relocation to SF will be supported through reimbursements. ## **Why Work at Abridge?** At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month. Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business. Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients. We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life. If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you. ## **How we take care of Abridgers:** - **Generous Time Off**: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees - **Comprehensive Health Plans**: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families. - **Generous HSA Contribution**: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA. - **Paid Parental Leave**: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees. - **Family Forming Benefits:** Resources and financial support to help you build your family. - **401(k) Matching**: Contribution matching to help invest in your future. - **Personal Device Allowance**: Tax free funds for personal device usage. - **Pre-tax Benefits:** Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits. - **Lifestyle Wallet**: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more. - **Mental Health Support**: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals. - **Sabbatical Leave**: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment. - **Compensation and Equity**: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees. - ... and much more! ## **Equal Opportunity Employer** Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability. We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process. ## **Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud** We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @[](http://abridge.com) email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to [this article](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/05/scammers-are-hijacking-job-ads-heres-how-spot-fakes). Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

## **About Cowboy Space** **Mission:** Cowboy Space Corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. We are tackling one of humanity’s most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth. **Background**: Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport. Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases. Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. Inspired by his father’s work with NASA Langley Research Center, Baiju earned his B.S. in Physics and M.S. in Mathematics at Stanford before co-founding Robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million Americans access the financial system. Cowboy Space Corporation has raised ~$365 million from Index Ventures, Interlagos, Construct Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and others. This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Cowboy Space Corporation’s team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA, and is based in San Carlos, CA. If you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you. ## **About the Role**: As the Stage 1 Lead, you will be the Responsible Engineer for the reusable first stage of Cowboy Space's launch vehicle, owning its entire lifecycle: from architecture and design through assembly, integrated test, launch, recovery, and refurbishment. You will serve as chief engineer, program manager, and lead systems engineer for the stage. You will lead an integrated product team of propulsion, structures, mechanical, fluids, avionics, GNC, software, and test engineers to deliver a flight-proven, rapidly reusable first stage. You will work closely with the engine, upper stage, manufacturing, test, and launch operations teams as the stage integrates with the rest of the launch system. You must be ready to stay focused, move fast, self-direct, and learn on the fly. This role reports to the Head of Launch & Propulsion. **What You’ll Do** ● Own the Stage 1 program from architecture and design through flight, recovery, and reflight ● Define Stage 1 architecture, conceptual design, and stage-level requirements in coordination with the owners of the engine, upper stage, ground systems, and other launch system elements ● Define and manage subsystem requirements and interfaces (propulsion, structures, fluids, avionics, GNC, and recovery) with subsystem owners, including the engine-to-stage interface ● Track stage technical performance, mass, margins, and risk throughout the design cycle; manage changes to requirements and interfaces and mediate technical disagreements between subsystems ● Define and manage schedule and budget for the Stage 1 program ● Lead stage assembly, integration, and integrated test campaigns (cryogenic proof, static fire) with support from manufacturing and test engineers ● Define the verification and qualification plan for stage and subsystem requirements and manage its execution ● Develop stage operating procedures and operational limits in coordination with engine, test stand, and launch operations teams ● Participate in test and launch operations to make real-time engineering decisions on technical risks ● Drive design-for-reuse decisions: recovery loads and environments, inspection intervals, life-limited parts, refurbishment procedures, and acceptance criteria for reflown stages ● Own the stage upgrade plan for improved reliability, rapid turnaround, and faster production rate; derive upgrade scope and timelines to achieve these goals **Basic Qualifications:** ● 10+ years of experience in the design, build, integration, or test of launch vehicles, rocket stages, or similarly complex aerospace flight systems ● Demonstrated experience on one or more development programs through a significant portion of the lifecycle (concept through development, qualification, flight, or sustained operations) ● Demonstrated ability to lead and integrate a team of technical contributors spanning propulsion, structures, mechanical, fluids, avionics, GNC, and software disciplines ● Strong knowledge of systems engineering fundamentals (requirements, interfaces, verification, and risk and margin management) applied practically in a fast-paced development program ● Exceptional command of fundamentals: structures and loads, fluid systems, thermodynamics, cryogenics, flight dynamics, and control systems ● Experience with integrated stage- or vehicle-level testing (pressure/proof testing, cryogenic loading, static fire, or equivalent) ● Strong data analysis and data reduction skills (test and flight data to vehicle health and performance) ● Hands-on experience with fabrication, assembly, and integration of flight hardware ● Ability to lead; AECOM is seeking an Intern Geologist for the Arlington, Virginia office. This position is expected to begin ASAP. Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. We are seeking a Junior Scheduler / Project Controls Consultant to support our growing project advisory and construction consulting practice. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional with hands-on experience developing and maintaining construction schedules who is looking to expand their capabilities in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory. The successful candidate will ideally have approximately two years of experience working with a general contractor, construction manager, specialty contractor, or similar construction organization, with direct exposure to developing, updating, and managing construction schedules. The role will support projects across the building and infrastructure sectors and will work closely with senior schedulers, project controls professionals, project managers, and technical experts. Key Responsibilities Assist in the development, review, and maintenance of detailed construction project schedules. Develop and update Critical Path Method (CPM) schedules based on project scope, construction sequencing, and contractor work plans. Support preparation of baseline schedules, schedule updates, recovery schedules, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Review contractor schedule submissions for completeness, logic, sequencing, durations, and compliance with project requirements. Monitor project progress and incorporate actual progress into schedule updates. Identify critical and near-critical activities, schedule constraints, and potential impacts to project milestones. Assist with analysis of schedule variances and changes to the critical path. Work with project teams to collect schedule information, progress data, and supporting documentation. Assist in preparing schedule narratives, progress reports, schedule graphics, and management presentations. Support schedule impact assessments and preliminary delay analyses under the direction of senior scheduling and claims professionals. Assist with evaluating change orders and potential time impacts. Review project documentation, including drawings, specifications, contracts, progress reports, RFIs, submittals, and change documentation, to understand project sequencing and schedule impacts. Participate in project meetings and schedule review meetings with clients, contractors, designers, and other project stakeholders. Support broader project controls activities, including progress measurement, reporting, cost and schedule integration, and project performance analysis. Maintain clear and organized documentation supporting schedule updates and analyses. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or a related field. Approximately 2 or more years of relevant construction industry experience, preferably working for a general contractor, construction manager, or specialty contractor. Practical experience developing or maintaining construction schedules. Understanding of construction sequencing, project milestones, and the relationship between design, procurement, and construction activities. Basic understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to organize and analyze project information and communicate findings clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Preferred Experience using Oracle Primavera P6. Experience with Microsoft Project or other scheduling/project controls software. Experience working on commercial buildings, healthcare, higher education, transportation, infrastructure, or other complex construction projects. Exposure to schedule review, delay analysis, change-order evaluation, or construction claims. Familiarity with construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation. Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional certification is a plus. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has started their career working directly within the construction industry and understands how projects are actually planned and built. They have had hands-on exposure to construction scheduling and are interested in developing deeper expertise in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory . This position is particularly well suited to someone who has spent the first few years of their career with a contractor or construction manager and is interested in transitioning into a consulting environment where they can work across multiple projects, clients, and construction sectors. What You Will Develop In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop expertise in: Advanced CPM scheduling Primavera P6 Construction schedule review and analysis Project controls and performance reporting Schedule risk and critical path analysis Change and delay analysis Construction claims and dispute support Project advisory and owner representation You will work alongside experienced construction, engineering, scheduling, and project controls professionals and gain exposure to complex projects from both the contractor and owner perspectives. For more information, please visit Job Type: Full Time (4 days a week in office with one hybrid/ remote day) The position may be based in our Atlanta, New York, or Boston office. Some travel to project sites and client offices may be required depending on project assignments. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. role: Associate Consultant - Entry-Level Clinical Data Technology Consulting
description: Veeva’s Consultant Development Program (CDP) is an accelerated pathway that transforms early-career professionals into high-impact consultants who deliver cloud and AI solutions, helping global Life Sciences companies bring life-changing therapies to patients. ### The Role You’ll work hands-on with innovative Clinical Data Management technology, collaborating directly with internal teams and external customers to design, configure, and implement our clinical data software. In this role, you’ll learn our industry-leading clinical trial cloud platforms and work with cutting-edge AI solutions to transform how life sciences companies manage clinical trial data. Empowered from day one by a team-first culture, you will accelerate your career growth as a technical consultant who thrives in an environment where we work hard for our customers and each other. ### The Program As part of the Consultant Development Program, you will: - **Ramp up quickly:** Your journey begins with an intensive, team-based onboarding program that combines hands-on learning, transparent feedback, and active collaboration to develop the consulting skills and industry knowledge to make an impact right away. - **Learn by doing:** You won't be watching from the sidelines. You will take on real responsibility and work directly with customers to solve clinical data management problems within your first three months. - **Thrive together:** Grow alongside a supportive team of seasoned leaders and peers who actively champion your development through open communication and actionable feedback. - **Build your future:** Advance from Associate to Consultant in less than 2 years. More importantly, you’ll develop the foundation for a successful, long-term career where you can continually expand your technical expertise, lead complex projects, and evolve with our global and diverse team. ### What You'll Do As part of our Professional Services team, you are a strategic partner guiding clinical operations and data management teams through implementation. We will teach you how our CDMS software works, and you will use that knowledge to design, configure, and deliver solutions that drive real business value]. Your day-to-day will involve: - **Designing & tailoring the software:** You will lead the configuration of our Vault CDMS platform to fit each customer's unique clinical trial requirements—setting up study workflows, structuring clinical data models, and aligning system capabilities to study protocols. - **Conducting discovery workshops:** You will lead interactive discovery workshops with customer stakeholders (e.g., Clinical Data Managers, CRCs, CRAs) to gather business requirements, map out existing data management workflows, and translate their vision into actionable technical specifications. - .**Managing project scope & execution:** You will take ownership of core implementation deliverables by scoping study requirements, building timeline estimates, and keeping project milestones on track from study design through go-live. - **Guiding the customer as an expert:** You will lead the customer with best practices to ensure their clinical data collection and study management processes are optimized for maximum long-term value. ### What We Are Looking For | We are open to graduates of a variety of backgrounds and look for a specific mindset: **Education & Preferred Background** A Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative or life science field is preferred, such as: - Biomedical Engineering, Health Informatics, Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering - Clinical Research, Public Health, Biology, Pharmacology **Desired Experience** Prior experience (internships, co-ops, academic projects, or entry-level roles) in one or more of the following areas is highly valued: - Data entry or management in a healthcare/research setting, or experience at a CRO, as a Clinical Research Associate (CRA), or Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) - Clinical trial operations, monitoring, or clinical data management - Data analysis using statistical software (SAS, SPSS, Python, R) - Design training, UX Design, or Human Factors Studies - Business or technical consulting - Speech and Debate or Manufacturing **Technical Skills & Mindset** - **Technical Familiarity:** Basic familiarity with database concepts. For example, SQL for querying relational databases and Python or R for data manipulation and analysis - **Drive:** You thrive in a challenging, intense environment that rewards initiative and rapid learning - **Curiosity:** You have a genuine desire to be hands-on with software and master new technologies - **Communication:** You are fluent in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills - **Analytical Mindset:** You are a strong critical thinker with a proven track record of analytical performance - **Integrity:** Veeva is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees - **Work Ethic:** A commitment to excellence and passion for working hard to achieve results - **Travel:** Willingness to travel as needed (up to 20-30% of the time) - **Experience:** Open to recent graduates of Bachelor's or Master's programs (up to 2 years postgraduate experience maximum) ### How We Hire | Our process is different from most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps: - **Apply:** Submit your resume, a short cover letter, and take a quick personality test. - **Fast Response:** We will notify you of your next step typically within one week. - **Interview & Case:** Interview with a Veeva leader. If successful, we will give you a real-world scenario (with 3 days to prepare) to present to our team. - **Offer:** We make decisions quickly—usually within a week of your final presentation. ### Perks & Benefits - Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance - Flexible PTO and company paid holidays - Retirement programs - 1% charitable giving program ### Compensation - Starting Salary: $80,000 USD - Perform well, and in one year you’ll receive a compensation increase and participate in our bonus program

role: Avionics Embedded Software Engineer - Summer Internship 2027
description: **Advanced Reentry Technologies** **Who We Are:** Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions. The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry. **Position Overview:** As an Avionics Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development, integration, verification, and debugging of embedded software for Inversion’s next-generation reentry vehicles. You will sit within the Avionics team and work closely with embedded software, electrical, RF, GNC, test, and vehicle engineers to develop software that interfaces directly with flight hardware. You will gain hands-on experience developing and debugging firmware and embedded software, bringing up new hardware, integrating sensors and communications interfaces, and validating software in laboratory and hardware-in-the-loop environments. This is a practical, systems-focused internship for students interested in embedded systems, real-time software, flight computers, hardware/software integration, and aerospace applications. **Key Responsibilities:** - Work closely with embedded software and avionics engineers to develop, integrate, test, and debug flight software and firmware. - Develop software for microcontrollers, processors, sensors, communications interfaces, and other avionics hardware. - Support board bring-up and hardware/software integration, including debugging interfaces between embedded software and electrical hardware. - Implement and debug drivers and interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, GPIO, ADCs, and other embedded interfaces. - Develop and execute software tests using laboratory hardware, engineering test fixtures, and hardware-in-the-loop systems. - Support real-time software development using an RTOS or similar embedded software framework. - Debug software and hardware issues using tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers, serial consoles, and software instrumentation. - Develop test scripts and analysis tools using Python or similar languages to automate validation and characterize system behavior. - Support integration of sensors, flight computers, RF systems, power electronics, and other avionics subsystems. - Analyze failures and anomalies, identify root causes, and work with multidisciplinary teams to implement and verify corrective actions. - Document software behavior, test results, interfaces, and technical findings to support flight hardware development and verification. **Required Qualifications:** - Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline. - GPA of 3.0 or above. - 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable). - Coursework or project experience in embedded systems, computer architecture, operating systems, real-time systems, or related disciplines. - Experience programming in C or C++. - Experience developing software for a microcontroller, embedded processor, FPGA-based system, robotics platform, or similar hardware. - Strong problem-solving, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical results clearly to multidisciplinary teams. **Desired Qualifications:** - Hands-on experience with an RTOS such as Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or similar. - Experience with embedded Linux or low-level software development. - Experience developing device drivers or low-level hardware interfaces. - Familiarity with SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, GPIO, ADCs, or similar embedded interfaces. - Experience debugging embedded systems using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD debuggers, or similar tools. - Experience with board bring-up and hardware/software integration. - Experience developing automated software tests or hardware-in-the-loop test systems. - Experience with Python for test automation, data analysis, or development tooling. - Familiarity with real-time concepts such as interrupts, scheduling, concurrency, synchronization, timing constraints, and memory management. - Experience developing embedded systems through Formula SAE, student rocketry, CubeSat, robotics, or similar engineering projects. - Previous internship experience at a space, aerospace, or hardware startup. - Familiarity with Git, CI/CD, software configuration management, and collaborative software development practices. **Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in-office presence.** *The California annual base hourly rate for this role is currently $38-$41. Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual pay will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and internal equity.* **ITAR Compliance:** To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. role: AUSTIN - Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer
location: 101 W Louis Henna Blvd, Suite 400, Austin, Texas 78728
description: Your future begins here! BGE, Inc**.** is a nationwide civil engineering consulting firm offering diverse career opportunities in a wide range of disciplines for public and private infrastructure projects. Our employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes outstanding health care, generous 401(k) match, professional career resources, and highly competitive work-life balance programs, including personal-time allowances, dependent care, and flexible Fridays. In addition, BGE provides unlimited sick leave, floating holidays, and robust career growth guidance, including organization-wide leadership and mentorship programs to help you build connections and shape your career. BGE goes beyond competitive benefits to attract and retain the best in an environment that inspires excellence. **Summary** The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer is an entry level engineer who supports the delivery of instrumentation, control, and automation solutions for the energy services sector. This role assists on projects involving field instrumentation, process measurement, control narratives, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA and telemetry, safety instrumented systems, metering, control panels, and industrial networks. The Junior Instrumentation and Controls Engineer works under the direction of senior technical staff on assigned project tasks, prepares calculations and drawings for review, supports project teams and client deliverables, builds knowledge through mentorship and training, and helps deliver safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective energy solutions. **Job Responsibilities** · Assist with instrumentation and controls design and production of deliverables for energy services projects, including field instrumentation, control panels, PLC and DCS systems, SCADA, telemetry, metering, and site automation. · Prepare, under the direction of a senior engineer, instrumentation and controls design documents, including instrument index, instrument datasheets, loop diagrams, P&ID markups, wiring and termination details, panel layouts, I/O lists, and cable and conduit schedules. · Support instrument sizing and selection calculations, including flow element sizing, control valve sizing, level, pressure and temperature sizing and range setting; loop power and signal calculations, for senior review. · Learn and apply control system architecture and communication requirements, and gather information needed for protocol selection such as HART, Modbus, Profibus, Foundation Fieldbus, Ethernet/IP, and OPC, along with network layouts and remote I/O or RTU interfaces. · Draft control narratives, functional descriptions, technical reports, specifications, cost estimate backup, equipment selections, construction documents, and other project deliverables for senior engineer review. · Perform self-checks on assigned work before submittal, assist with quality control reviews at project milestones, and help verify that deliverables are complete and follow applicable ISA, NEC, NFPA, and client standards as well as project scope. · Help resolve routine design and construction-phase issues, draft responses to RFIs, review vendor submittals and instrument data for conformance with the design, and escalate unusual or complex items to a senior engineer. · Support factory acceptance testing, loop checks, point to point verification, calibration records, commissioning, and startup under supervision, including punch list tracking and as-built markups. · Communicate with internal project teams, instrument and control system vendors, and contractors on assigned tasks, and participate in client, operations, and vendor meetings alongside a senior engineer, including taking notes and tracking action items. · Build technical knowledge through mentorship, formal training, self-learning, and hands-on project and field work, ask questions when direction is unclear, and share lessons learned with peers. · Support business development and proposal efforts by compiling background information and past project data, and contribute ideas for continuous improvement of design standards, workflows, tools, templates, and checklists. **Job Requirements** · Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Control Systems Engineering from an accredited university required. · Must have passed or be eligible to sit for the FE exam by the time of graduation. · 0 to 2 years of instrumentation and controls engineering experience. Internships, co-ops, undergraduate research, or capstone work related to process control, automation, energy services, oil and gas, power systems, or engineering consulting preferred. · Coursework-level knowledge of process measurement for flow, level, pressure, temperature, and analytical variables, along with final control elements, control loop fundamentals, and PID control. · Exposure to PLC, DCS, SCADA, HMI, safety instrumented systems, custody transfer or allocation metering, control panels, or industrial networks through coursework, internships, or student projects preferred. · Awareness of applicable codes and standards, including NFPA, IEEE, ANSI, ISA, with a willingness to learn to apply them under supervision. · Exposure to instrument sizing calculations, hazardous area classification, intrinsic safety, cause and effect development, or alarm rationalization through coursework or internships preferred. · Familiarity with design and configuration tools such as AutoCAD, AutoCAD Electrical, Revit, SmartPlant Instrumentation, MATLAB, or Python preferred. · Demonstrated ability to follow technical direction, organize assigned work, manage deadlines on multiple tasks, and communicate clearly in writing and in person with team members, vendors, and project stakeholders, including in plant and field environments. · Strong analytical, problem-solving, attention to detail, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills, with a commitment to accuracy and to learning quickly. Some of our Benefits: - 401k Match: 100% up to 4% of your contributions with immediate vesting + 3% Safe Harbor Contribution with immediate vesting - Merit-Based Bonus Compensation - Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance; BGE contributes to HSA on eligible plans - 9 paid Holidays, including 3 Floating holidays - Personal Time Allowances - 2 to 4 weeks of Vacation, depending on experience-level. Unused vacation carries over to the next year. - "Unlimited" Sick Days. - Mentorship Program – Provides you with the opportunity to learn and receive guidance from seasoned professionals. - Employee Referral Program that pays you for bringing great people into the BGE family BGE is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We prohibit discrimination and all employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, Vietnam Era Veteran Status, Disabled Veteran Status, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local laws. NO SPONSORSHIP NO AGENCIES

### How Your Role Will Shape Our Success Start your engineering career by learning how structures perform in the real world. As a Structural Restoration Engineer, you’ll work alongside experienced engineers to investigate existing structures, understand the causes of deterioration or distress, and help develop practical repair and restoration solutions. You’ll gain experience both in the field and in the office, giving you the opportunity to see projects from initial investigation through design and construction. Along the way, you’ll build the technical knowledge, problem-solving skills, and project experience that will help you grow as a structural engineer. **New to restoration? That’s okay.** We’re looking for someone with a strong engineering foundation, curiosity, and a desire to learn. You’ll have the opportunity to develop your restoration knowledge through hands-on project experience and mentorship. #### What You’ll Do - Participate in field investigations of existing buildings and structures - Help evaluate structural conditions, deterioration, and damage - Perform structural analysis and engineering calculations with guidance from experienced engineers - Assist in developing repair and restoration designs - Prepare drawings, details, reports, and other project documentation - Visit active project sites and gain exposure to construction and repair methods - Collaborate with engineers, architects, contractors, and clients - Take on increasing responsibility as your technical and project experience grows #### What You’ll Bring - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or a related field - Interest in structural engineering, restoration, existing buildings, and hands-on problem-solving - Strong analytical and communication skills - Curiosity and a willingness to learn - Ability to work collaboratively as part of a project team - Interest in pursuing professional engineering licensure ### We offer a robust total compensation and rewards package designed to support our employees’ well-being, growth, and diverse needs, including: - Annual discretionary bonus program - Opportunity to purchase Walker stock – Walker is 100% employee-owned! - Medical, dental, vision, company-paid life insurance - Mental wellness benefits - Health Savings Account with company contribution - 401(k) with company match - Flexible Spending Accounts and Commuter Spending Accounts - 529 college savings plan - A minimum of 3 weeks of Paid Time Off per year - 9 paid holidays per year, including 3 paid floating holidays - 5 days of bereavement leave and PTO Donation Bank to help during difficult times - 100% compensation replacement during short-term disability leaves - Paid parental leave that allows an additional week of paid time alongside short-term disability leave and/or applicable state paid leave programs - Paid community involvement hours - Tuition and licensure reimbursement and sponsorship of professional memberships - Internal conferences and professional development opportunities - Employee Resource Groups and Affinity Groups

Description Are you interested in building a career in facilities maintenance, building operations, or the skilled trades? Public Service Credit Union is seeking a motivated and hands-on Facilities Apprentice to join our team. This is an excellent opportunity to gain real-world experience, learn from experienced professionals, and build practical skills in facility maintenance, safety, vendor coordination, and building operations. Working alongside our Facilities Manager, you'll receive structured on-the-job training while helping maintain safe, functional, and welcoming environments for our employees and members. **What You'll Do** - Assist with routine inspections of credit union buildings, grounds, and common areas. - Report maintenance, safety, and building concerns to the Facilities Manager. - Learn how facility services are coordinated, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, janitorial, landscaping, and pest control. - Participate in hands-on training and learning opportunities focused on facilities operations and preventative maintenance. - Perform basic maintenance tasks such as changing light bulbs, replacing filters, assembling furniture, and completing minor repairs. - Support preventative maintenance activities by preparing equipment, gathering supplies, and documenting completed work. - Assist with vendor, contractor, and service provider visits by preparing workspaces and restoring areas after work is completed. - Help coordinate seasonal facility needs, including landscaping and snow/ice preparation. - Move and set up furniture, equipment, and supplies as needed. - Maintain facilities inventory, including supplies, equipment, keys, and access badges. - Track maintenance requests and accurately document completed work. - Follow established workplace safety, security, and emergency response procedures. - Maintain professionalism and confidentiality while working in employee and member areas. Requirements - High school diploma or GED. - Valid driver's license with a clean driving record. - Interest in facilities maintenance, building operations, or a skilled trade. - Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills. - Ability to travel between branch locations. - Basic computer proficiency, including Microsoft 365 applications. - Ability to work independently and as part of a team. - Basic maintenance experience or knowledge of building systems is a plus. **Why This Role?** - Gain valuable hands-on experience in facilities management. - Work alongside experienced facilities professionals. - Develop practical skills that can lead to long-term career opportunities. - Contribute to maintaining safe, functional, and welcoming environments for employees and members. - Be part of a team-oriented organization committed to supporting employee growth and development. **Physical Requirements:** Position may require lifting, moving furniture and equipment, standing, walking, climbing ladders, and performing other physical activities associated with facility maintenance. **What we offer** - Competitive wages - Career Growth / Robust Training Program - Work Life Balance - Top quality health insurance (Full Time) - Paid Time Off (accrued and available for use immediately) - Paid holidays - Banking hours / Closed on Sunday’s - Tuition Reimbursement - Employer Provided Retirement Benefits - 401(K) Plan - Dental & Vision Insurance (Full Time) - Short & Long-Term Disability (Full Time) - Life Insurance (Full Time) **Why join us?** *At PSCU, we are dedicated to our mission of educating, equipping, and empowering both our team and the communities we serve. By joining us, you’ll be part of a culture that listens to your ideas, supports your growth, elevates and celebrates your achievements, cares for your well-being, and serves with purpose. Together, we create a meaningful impact, and we invite you to be a part of our journey!* **To apply, please complete the online application and attach an up-to-date resume.**

description: [DLR Group](http://www.dlrgroup.com/) is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place. #### DLR Group's Mid-Atlantic Region has an opening for a [**Mechanical Engineering**](https://www.dlrgroup.com/services/engineering/#jason-majerus) **Summer Intern**. This role could be based in the following studios: - Charlotte, NC - Durham, NC *We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.* ### [About EPX at DLR Group](https://www.dlrgroup.com/emerging-professional-experience/) As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry. Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession. The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals. ### Position Summary As a **Mechanical Engineering Intern** at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of mechanical systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside mechanical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration. Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running **May 18 through August 6, 2027**, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design. ### What you will do - Work with a licensed engineer designing mechanical systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects - Attend design team meetings with a mechanical engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team - Assist a mechanical engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit - Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects) - Develop HVAC, plumbing, and fire protection designs from concept through completion ### Required Qualifications: - Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Mechanical Engineering or Architectural Engineering program - Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow ### Preferred Qualifications: - Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam - Interest in architectural building design - A third-year student in an accredited engineering program *Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.* #LI- [DLR Group](http://www.dlrgroup.com/) is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects. We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment. Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together. DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.
