ScorePlay is the AI-powered media infrastructure for sports, built to automate the content operations behind the world's biggest sports organizations. We work with **300+ leagues, competitions, teams and broadcasters** – including Ligue 1 and Premier League clubs, NBA and NFL teams, the Tour de France, the Australian Open, and leading bodies like UEFA and FIBA – helping them turn every moment on and off the field **into high-value, structured content**. Our platform brings all their media into one place and makes it effortless to find, edit and share in seconds. **Founded in 2021**, we’re a **50-person** team based between **New York** and **Paris**, growing **2x year over year** with 98% retention. We’ve raised **$20M+** from top investors including Alexis Ohanian and Harry Stebbing’s 20VC and elite athletes like Kevin Durant, Raphaël Varane, Mario Götze, Nico Rosberg and Giannis Antetokounmpo. If you’re **passionate about sports** and thrive in **fast-paced environments** - and you want to help shape how the next generation of fans experience sports, you’re in the right place. We’re on track to become the **global leader in sports media**, and this is definitely the **best time to join our adventure**. **💡 Overview** ScorePlay is moving from lighter deployments to highly structured rollouts that meet the technical demands of the largest sports and broadcast organizations in the world. Our Deployment team sits between the product and the client, and makes complex implementations feel simple. We’re opening an internship in New York to reinforce that team. You’ll work on real client environments from week one, alongside the engineers running our biggest North American rollouts. It’s a hands-on role for someone technical enough to read code, understand an API and debug a workflow, but there is no need to be a full fledged software engineer. This role is for people who like to work directly with clients as much as they love solving complex technical issues. We’re hiring this internship with the intention of converting the right person into a full-time Deployment Engineer in New York. **🧠 What you’ll work on** **Fixing things for clients** - Investigate and resolve technical issues raised by clients during and after onboarding: failed imports, metadata mismatches, integration errors, permission and access problems. - Dig into logs, API responses and existing scripts to find the actual root cause rather than patching the symptom. - Be a reliable point of contact for client technical teams, and escalate to Engineering with a clear diagnosis when something needs a product fix. **Taking part in complex rollouts** - Join large deployments alongside senior engineers: archive migrations, platform setups, bulk operations, backfills. - Own the repeatable parts of a rollout yourself: environment prep, configuration, data checks, validation before go-live. - Follow our deployment playbook, and improve it with what you learn in the field. **Building so the team scales** This part grows as you do. Once you know our deployments well enough to see what keeps coming back, you’ll have room to build. - Turn recurring issues into something that stops them recurring: scripts, internal tools, AI agents. - Automate parts of our delivery work that are still manual today, and package what works so the rest of the team can reuse it. - Help the Deployment team get better at using AI day to day. **🧩 What we’re looking for** - Final year of an engineering program OR a master’s degree in Business with at least one experience working on technical topics - Solid understanding of APIs, able to read and understand code (Python, JavaScript, Bash or similar) and modify an existing script. You don’t need to be a software engineer. - A genuine power user of AI tools. You use them every day, you know what they’re good at and where they fall apart. - Comfortable with ambiguity. A lot of what you’ll touch has no existing solution yet. - At ease talking to clients, including technical teams at large organizations. - Fluent English, written and spoken. French is a plus. **🏆 Why ScorePlay** A few signs you might love it here: - You want to be hands-on with real systems: media, archives, integrations, large scale migrations. - You’d rather own a result than close a ticket. - You like turning messy, loosely defined problems into something repeatable that others can run. - You want to build the tooling a team runs on, at the point where it’s still being invented. - You’re motivated by seeing world-class sports organizations actually use what you helped deploy. **📍 Practical details** - Based in our New York office (we provide the VISA) - 6 month internship, starting Q1 or Q2 2027 - Compensation: $3,500/month *We know many people hesitate to apply if they don’t meet every single requirement on a job description. If you’re interested in ScorePlay but not sure you tick all the boxes, we’d still love to hear from you, this could be the start of a great long-term collaboration.*

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. Maritime Digital Production is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. That includes Serapis, our program building components for the Virginia-class submarine. We operate at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology, incubating solutions close to the production line, validating them with real operators, hardening them for reliability and security, and scaling them across sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship. We are scaling from a founding team to more than 70 engineers across multiple U.S. sites. As an intern you join early, on a problem that matters to production, with a defined project and a named engineer you work with every day. We have built a computational geometry engine that takes a 3D CAD assembly and works out the orders in which it can physically come apart, and therefore the orders in which it can be built. It finds where parts touch, builds directional blocking graphs from that contact geometry, searches for collision-free removal directions, and produces the precedence constraints our production scheduling system plans against. It works on small and mid-sized assemblies. It needs to work on the assemblies we actually build, which have hundreds to thousands of parts. Your job is to close that gap. This is algorithms engineering with a research flavor. You will profile the engine on real assemblies, find where the time and memory go, and attack it: search ordering, pruning, memorization, incremental updates, subassembly decomposition, and parallelism. The goal is a measurably faster engine rather than a paper, and every result is held to one rule: a faster answer that is a different answer is a bug. **WHAT YOU’LL DO** - Profiling a C++ computational geometry pipeline on real assemblies and reporting where time and memory go - Designing and implementing algorithmic improvements to a disassembly sequence search: candidate ordering, pruning, memoization, and incremental graph updates - Decomposing large assemblies into subassemblies that can be solved independently - Parallelizing expensive geometric tests across cores without losing determinism - Building a benchmark corpus and harness that run in continuous integration and catch regressions - Gating every optimization on output equivalence against a reference set - Writing up results and presenting them to the engineering team **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. - Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person co-op in Santa Ana, CA, in winter 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Strong modern C++, C++17 or later. You have written and debugged performance-sensitive C++ in a codebase you did not write yourself, not only coursework. - Solid algorithms and data structures, including graph algorithms such as strongly connected components and topological ordering, combinatorial search and pruning, and complexity analysis. - Computational geometry fundamentals: triangle meshes, bounding volume hierarchies and other spatial indexes, intersection and collision tests, and reasoning about directions on the sphere. - Experience profiling and optimizing code. You have used a profiler and made something measurably faster. - Research or coursework in assembly sequence planning, disassembly planning, or motion planning. If you know what a non-directional blocking graph is, or have read Wilson and Latombe or the STAAT work by Romney and colleagues, we want to talk to you. - Publications at ICRA, IROS, RSS, SoCG, or Solid and Physical Modeling, or in the Computer-Aided Design journal. - Experience with Eigen, OpenCASCADE, OpenVDB, CGAL, or a collision or bounding volume hierarchy library. - Parallel programming in C++ with Intel TBB, OpenMP, or standard threads, with attention to determinism. - Familiarity with CAD data: boundary representations versus tessellated meshes, and formats such as STEP and JT. - Experience with CMake, GoogleTest, and reproducible builds. Nix is a plus. - Python for tooling and analysis, e.g. NumPy and trimesh. - Familiarity with infinitesimal motion analysis or rotational motions in assembly planning. The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines. On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Atlanta, GA office . This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities. AECOM’s Atlanta office is seeking a Transportation Planning Intern to support planning and public engagement efforts for transit, rail, roadway, and multimodal transportation projects. This position provides hands-on experience working alongside senior planners, engineers, and project managers on projects for local, state, and federal clients. The internship is ideal for students interested in transportation planning, public policy, urban planning, or related fields who want exposure to professional consulting, federal and state transportation programs, and community-focused planning. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to: Support transportation planning studies, including transit, multimodal, corridor, and long-range planning efforts. Assist with data collection, analysis, and visualization (e.g., demographic data, travel patterns, GIS mapping). Help prepare technical memoranda, reports, presentations, and graphics. Support public engagement activities, including developing meeting materials, surveys, and outreach content and attending public meetings in communities across Georgia. Assist with grant-related research and documentation (e.g., FTA, FHWA, FRA programs). Participate in project team meetings and coordination activities. Participate in client meetings and coordination activities. Perform general planning and research tasks under the supervision of senior staff. What You’ll Gain Exposure to nationally and regionally significant transportation projects. Mentorship from experienced transportation planners and project managers. Experience working with public-sector clients and multidisciplinary teams. Professional development through AECOM’s learning and networking opportunities. Minimum Requirements Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Transportation Planning, Urban/Regional Planning, Civil Engineering, Public Policy, Geography, or a related field and must have completed at least 1 year of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s degree and plan to continue with the Master’s degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship. Preferred Qualifications Coursework or experience in transportation or transit planning. Familiarity with GIS (ArcGIS or similar). Experience with data analysis or visualization tools. Interest in public engagement and community-based planning. Knowledge of federal, state, or local transportation programs. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. This position requires a hybrid work schedule which includes in office work in Atlanta, GA. The selected candidate must be available to work in Atlanta, GA on a scheduled basis. Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. About AECOM AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options , well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan. client base not assigned - Manage and prioritize workload towards weekly goals in a results-oriented team environment - Consult with clients regarding plan operation, design, and upgrading platforms - Follow-up by phone with clients about missing items - Assist firm-wide clients via the phone, video conference, or email with census submission issues, submitting Forms 5500, simple 401(k) questions, resetting passwords, troubleshooting web access, etc. - Collaborate with account managers and others to ensure a positive client experience - Document all client interactions in our workflow management system - Assist with other assigned tasks to balance workloads and receive well-rounded training - Perform work according to Nova policies and procedures - Complete assigned training - Work towards obtaining an industry designation **Qualifications:** - Bachelor’s degree - Customer service experience a plus - Excellent written communication skills and ability to compose a professional email - Excellent verbal communication skills and knowledge of phone etiquette - Excellent time management, organizational skills, and ability to multi-task - Experience with Microsoft Office and comfortable using a computer - Knowledge of VOIP phone systems a plus - Help desk experience a plus - Committed to lifelong learning and coachable **Salary and benefits:** - Base Salary $55,000 - $60,000 - Salaried, non-exempt position - Medical, dental, disability, and life insurance - Paid time off - 401(k) plan with employer match **Work Location/Hours:** - Hybrid role - Must work in the Houston, TX office 4 days per week; 40 hours per week - You may choose a start time between 7:30 am and 8:30 am CST Nova 401(k) Associates is an energetic and thriving national third-party administrator for retirement plans. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. Sitting between Industrial Design and Mechanical Engineering, this role is perfect for those who love to sketch, build, test, and iterate—with the consumer always top of mind. You’ll collaborate with cross-functional teams to imagine what’s next for Shark, transforming insights into elegant, viable, and exciting product solutions. If you’re a creative thinker, curious builder, and motivated problem solver who enjoys translating real-world challenges into tangible design opportunities, we want to hear from you! **Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:** - Generate new product concepts with a user-centered approach, focusing on ergonomics, aesthetics, and functional innovation. - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to define solutions that meet functional requirements while enhancing the user experience. - Lead and participate in design studies to solve technical and user-experience challenges. - Build and test quick turnaround, low fidelity prototypes, and be able to build key findings on user testing with them. - Approach everyday design challenges with curiosity and resilience, driven to rethink and innovate **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - **Education:** Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s program or has graduated from such a program within the past year - Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedulewith 5 days per week onsite in Needham, MA - Strong communicator who can convey ideas, concepts, and solutions effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. - Strong intuition for mechanical engineering and physics principles, with an emphasis on applying this in product design, ergonomics, and human-centered engineering. - Analytical and detail-oriented, with a creative approach to identifying and addressing potential issues. - Demonstrates intellectual curiosity, a hands-on attitude, and commitment to developing elegant, innovative solutions that balance technical and user-focused design principles. - Skilled at juggling multiple projects, with flexibility to pivot as needed while keeping sight of broader design objectives. - Enthusiastic about user-centered product design, form, and function. - Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, Creo, or Rhino) and basic prototyping tools (3D printing, shop competency). - Hands-on experience building physical prototypes in various materials (e.g., plastic, metal) and familiarity with machine shop equipment. - Basic understanding of electronics and components commonly used in small appliances (motors, sensors, PCBAs) is desirable. - Experience with rapid prototyping tools like Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or other developer kits is a plus. **Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. Our team appreciates your patience!** **Salary and Other Compensation:** The hourly salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more. Hourly Pay Range $27—$40 USD **Our Culture** At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. **Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset** drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home. **What We Offer** We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. **We empower your personal and professional growth** with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. **When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community.** Together, we won’t just launch products—**we’ll disrupt entire markets.** At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA. description: Franklin University, a private, independent, accredited, nonprofit university located in Columbus, Ohio, invites applications for the position of Director, Student Wellbeing & Access. Founded in 1902, Franklin University has built its reputation on removing barriers to higher education for ambitious adults balancing educational goals with work, family, and other commitments. Accredited and nonprofit, Franklin is recognized as an innovator in online education and serves students through applied undergraduate, master's, and doctoral programs designed to support career advancement and lifelong learning. More than 50,000 Franklin alumni live and work around the world, making meaningful contributions to their professions and communities. Position Summary The Director, Student Wellbeing & Access will provide strategic and operational leadership for initiatives that promote student wellbeing, accessibility, accountability, persistence, and success at Franklin University. Reporting to the Dean of Students, this role oversees Accessibility Services, Student Wellbeing, and Community Standards, while serving as the University's ADA/Section 504 Coordinator and Title IX Coordinator. The Director will lead efforts to identify and address barriers that may interfere with student engagement and academic progress, developing innovative, scalable approaches to student support that meet the needs of Franklin's diverse and geographically dispersed student population. This includes advancing disability access and accommodations, strengthening student wellbeing resources, and providing oversight for complex student matters and institutional compliance responsibilities. As a key member of the Dean of Students leadership team, the Director will foster collaboration across the University, leverage data and technology to improve student services, and promote a culture of accountability, compassion, continuous improvement, and student-centered support. Key Responsibilities The Director provides strategic and operational leadership for Accessibility Services, Student Wellbeing, and Community Standards, ensuring these functions support student engagement, persistence, and success. The Director serves as the University's ADA/Section 504 Coordinator and Title IX Coordinator, overseeing disability accommodations, institutional accessibility, regulatory compliance, and related policies and procedures. This role leads the development of proactive, scalable, and virtual-first student wellbeing initiatives designed to address nonacademic barriers to student success, including oversight of the Student Emergency Fund and partnerships that expand access to student resources and support. The Director also provides leadership for student conduct, grievances, appeals, and other complex student matters, ensuring fair, consistent, and timely resolution. Responsibilities include coordinating responses to concerns submitted through the University's anonymous reporting system and participating on the Franklin Intervention & Awareness Team (FIAT). The Director supervises and develops professional staff, collaborates with University leaders to strengthen student support and institutional practices, and leverages data, technology, and process improvements to enhance service delivery and operational effectiveness. As a member of the Dean of Students leadership team, the Director promotes a culture of accountability, compassion, innovation, and continuous improvement while exercising sound judgment and discretion in sensitive matters. Minimum Qualifications A master's degree in higher education, student affairs, counseling, rehabilitation counseling, education, law, public administration, social work, or a related field is required, along with a minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in higher education. Candidates must have meaningful experience in postsecondary disability or accessibility services, including demonstrated knowledge of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504, the interactive accommodation process, and related regulatory requirements. The successful candidate will have supervisory experience, a broad understanding of Student Affairs practices, and experience supporting students with complex needs or circumstances affecting their success. Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply institutional policies and regulatory requirements, including student conduct, grievances, investigations, or related resolution processes, is essential. Knowledge of Title IX requirements, strong leadership and communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage sensitive and confidential matters with discretion, neutrality, and compassion are also required. Additional Information This position follows an on-site hybrid work schedule and requires flexibility to meet departmental and university needs. Occasional evening and weekend availability may be required to address sensitive or time-sensitive student matters, and some travel may be expected. Franklin offers a competitive benefits package, incentive program, and free parking. In addition, Franklin provides free undergraduate tuition for employees and eligible family members, graduate tuition assistance for full-time employees and eligible family members, and a discount on doctoral tuition for employees. Franklin University is committed to creating a respectful and inclusive educational and workplace environment. Franklin does not discriminate on the basis of age, religion, race, ethnicity, color, national origin, ancestry, immigration status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or familial status, disability, or veteran or military status.

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE TEAM:** Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** As part of the operations team, you will work to scale our footprint and run business operations for AIS. In this role, you will partner with teams from across the business, from our software and hardware teams to our Finance and G&A teams to our core internal operations teams, to unpack ambiguous problems and build lasting, scalable solutions. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact and specialized projects, all in the mission of growing one of our newest Business Units at Anduril. The role will have four primary responsibilities: 1. We're expanding our footprint globally. The Operations team is the glue across cross-functional teams at Anduril to execute our site expansions flawlessly and with speed. You will be responsible for ensuring each site is progressing, will serve as the key touchpoint across these teams, and burn down issues as they arise. This person wakes up every day thinking about our sites globally. 2. Standing up the operational processes for our Program Execution team. We work with the Program Execution team to ensure we are enabling world-class program managers to execute against contracts with ease, whether it's unlocking headcount, running analysis on our IRAD spend, to working with finance to ensure we're running profitable programs. 3. Serve as a key partner to the Revenue Operations teams. You will partner with Sales teams and Revenue Operations to monitor pipeline health and identify material changes to forecast and help drive the business planning processes for AIS. 4. Lead various special projects. You will be critical to supporting all of these responsibilities. While the Intelligence Systems team will be your team, you will often be working across the business, working cross-functionally with leaders and teams throughout the organization to solve messy problems, set up new processes, capture data, action upon it, and enable others to do the same. The day-to-day could look like: - Own operational projects end-to-end, from Definition, Solution, to Implementation. You will often be handed ambiguous problems with little prescription on how to solve them. - Execute analyses on short-timelines to get answers quickly, while also owning more scalable solutions that will make Intelligence Systems successful in the long term. - Project manage across many stakeholders. If you don't like being the person leading meetings with large groups of people or managing large comms channels to wrangle stakeholders towards a solution, this may not be the role for you. - Work across functions and learn Anduril's business top-to-bottom. You will interact with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Finance, Engineering, HR, Recruiting, Growth, and more. The Operations team is one of the most cross-functional teams at Anduril. - Set up structures and processes that enable the Division to scale our people and physical footprint, while ensuring mature programs are operating at peak efficiency and impact. **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Up to 2 years of previous experience (including internships) in management consulting, internal strategy & operations, or a business analyst role, to include internships, and able to start full time in 2027. - Strong analytical skills with comfort translating operational problems into data-driven solutions. - Excellent communication skills, including experience presenting to senior leadership or large cross-functional groups. - A desire to work on operations that have real-world impact on national security. - **Must be a U.S. Person who with the ability to obtain and hold a US Top Secret clearance** **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Already have obtained a U.S. Top Secret security clearance - Have a bias for action. If you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it. - Be naturally curious about the technologies and tools you use. - Low-ego, high ownership, and mission oriented. **Who we are** Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress. Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that. Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive. This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale. We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life. If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us. **What we’re looking for** **Actively pursuing a Bachelor/Master in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field** - Graduating in Summer/Fall/Winter 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028. - 3.7 GPA Minimum - Must have completed an introductory Computer Science course - Have advanced programming experience in one or more application or systems languages (Go, Python, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, C/C++, etc.) - A problem-solver who thrives in tackling diverse technical challenges and demonstrates a clear track record of growth and learning - A take-charge individual who exhibits ownership and takes pride in writing clean, maintainable, and fun code - An engineer who can dive deep into open source software, find issues, and fix them. **What you’ll do** As an engineering intern at Atoms, you'll be an integral part of building out the state-of-the-art intelligent machine for the food industry. Your role will encompass a diverse range of responsibilities, including: - You will build foundational software systems to enable globally scaled kitchen infrastructure and real estate innovations - You test software development methodology in an agile environment - You provide ongoing maintenance, support, and enhancements in existing systems and platforms - You work alongside other engineers to elevate technology and improve systems overall - You write, debug, maintain and test code - You design scalable, fault tolerant architectural systems - You develop information systems by designing, developing, and installing software solutions - You drive innovation within the team and support Atoms’ technological advancements **Why join us** At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. **What else you need to know** This role can be based in **New York, Seattle, Los Angeles, Mountain View or San Francisco**. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. The base starting rate for this role is **$70.00 per hour.** Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. **Program Dates:** January - April, our Winter Internship cohort runs from early January through late April. **Application Timeline:** Getting a head start on your job search? So are we! We’re building our candidate pipeline now for our upcoming internship positions. Feel free to submit your resume today, we’ll be reviewing applications over the coming weeks and will reach out directly if your background is a match when interviews begin in the Fall.

This role is central to planning and executing Fanatics College's annual event calendar — spanning CALS, SBJ/NFF, Tailgate, CFP, Final Four, CLC Seminar, NACDA/ICLA, and Fanatics Fest — and building the operational infrastructure that enables Partner Development and College GM teams to maximize event impact. role: Systems Intern - Validation, Software, Design, Architecture & Packaging (USA)
location: Austin, Texas, United States; Santa Clara, California, United States
description: Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities. **Overview:** A chip isn't a product until it's a working system. These teams cover both ends of that: getting silicon to boot and validate correctly,building the board, power, mechanical, thermal, packaging and IO around it. You submit one application, you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best. - **Systems & Silicon Validation:** Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs. - **System Software:** Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware. - **System Design:** The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint. - **System Architecture:** Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals. - **Packaging:** A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. This role is on-site, based out of Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA. **Who You Are** - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering - Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog). - Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical. - Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs). **What We Need** - **Systems & Silicon Validation:** Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications. - **System Software:** Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware. - **System Design & Architecture:** Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs. - **Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design:** Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis **What You Will Learn** - Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips. - Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal. - Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages. - Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch. **USA Hiring Timelines** This internship opportunity is available throughout our 3 terms with the following corresponding recruitment cycles: - Winter Term: Jan–Apr work term, Sept–Dec recruit. - Summer Term: May–Aug work term, Oct–Apr recruit. - Fall Term: Sept–Dec work term, Jan–Aug recruit. *Please note these timelines are for reference only. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.* *Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.* *This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. Experience in DOE and data interpretation. Preferred qualifications Research experience in environmental fracture of aluminum such as stress corrosion cracking, corrosion fatigue, and hydrogen embrittlement. Knowledge of various corrosion methods including setup, instrumentation, and interpretation of results. Specific experience related to aluminum products would be a distinct advantage. *Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. description: Suncast Corporation is the leading US-based designer, manufacturer, and distributor of high-quality resin products for the home and industrial markets. Everything we do is supported by the strength and ingenuity of American workers and we are committed to helping families across the country make the most of their unique spaces. We utilize state-of-the-art machinery and innovative manufacturing techniques to consistently engineer products of the highest possible quality. Suncast is the market leader in the manufacture of plastic injection and blow molded home and garden items, which are sold by large retailers worldwide. Establish a challenging, rewarding, lifetime career in manufacturing! The Apprentice is responsible for participating in a structured apprenticeship program that combines full-time employment, hands-on training, mentorship, and classroom instruction. Apprentices will develop technical skills in Metals, Automation, Setup, Equipment Maintenance, or Process while working alongside experienced professionals. The program is designed to prepare individuals for a successful long-term career in manufacturing through practical experience, technical education, and continuous skill development. Upon successful completion of the apprenticeship program and degree requirements, the Apprentice will transition to an off-shift position and be assigned to a specific department based on business needs and demonstrated competencies. Complete your education with no student debt and an established career in manufacturing! Responsibilities: • Participate in on-the-job training and rotational assignments within the assigned apprenticeship track. • Learn and apply safe work practices while maintaining compliance with company safety policies and procedures. • Assist with equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, setups, and process improvements under the guidance of experienced mentors. • Develop knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, automation, and manufacturing systems as applicable to the assigned area. • Operate hand tools, power tools, testing equipment, and manufacturing machinery safely and effectively. • Support preventive maintenance activities to ensure equipment reliability and production efficiency. • Demonstrate problem-solving skills to identify and assist in resolving equipment and process issues. • Complete all required apprenticeship coursework and maintain satisfactory academic performance. • Attend classes at an approved educational institution to obtain an Associate Degree. • Maintain accurate records of training progress, coursework, and apprenticeship requirements. • Communicate effectively with team members, trainers, supervisors, and cross-functional departments. • Demonstrate professionalism, dependability, and a willingness to learn new skills and technologies. • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives and support operational excellence objectives. • Successfully complete all apprenticeship program requirements within the established timeframe. • Support and comply with all Suncast safety policies, quality standards, and housekeeping practices. • Perform additional duties as required. Qualifications: • High school diploma or equivalent required. • Ability and willingness to enroll in and complete a company-sponsored apprenticeship education program. • Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and interest in working with tools, equipment, and machinery. • Strong desire to learn technical skills and manufacturing processes. • Ability to identify problems and develop effective solutions. • Strong organizational and time management skills. • Self-motivated and capable of working independently as well as part of a team. • Effective verbal and written communication skills. • Basic computer skills and willingness to learn new technology. • Ability to follow instructions, procedures, and safety guidelines. • Interest in pursuing a challenging and rewarding career in manufacturing. • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and perform repetitive movements for extended periods. • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and push or pull materials and equipment up to 100 lbs. as required. • Ability to safely work around manufacturing and wear required safety equipment. We will: • Provide full-time employment starting at $21.50/hour. • Pay your tuition, books and fees at one of several local community colleges for the duration of the program, when you enroll in their Industrial Maintenance apprenticeship programs. • Give you hands-on, on-the-job training, development and mentoring in your area of interest. • Offer you great benefits. Suncast offers a comprehensive benefits package including: • Medical, Dental, Prescription Drugs, Vision insurance, Telehealth benefits • Group Term Life insurance • 401K with employer match • Paid vacation time off • Paid holidays • Short- and long-term disability coverage • Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) & Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) for health • Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity) • Tuition Reimbursement • For more information, contact Guadalupe Arriola at All qualified applicants will be given equal consideration regardless of race, age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, color, religion, protected veteran status or national origin.

About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride: In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut. The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons. In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win. The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year. In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando. In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League. GMEA LLC | Full-Time | Nationwide Travel Required $65,000–$75,000 Annually | No Experience Required | Bachelor’s Degree Required | Paid Training About the Position Start your career helping manage large-scale construction projects across the United States — no previous experience required! GMEA LLC is a rapidly growing nationwide commercial and industrial electrical contractor seeking motivated, organized, and ambitious college graduates to join our team as Entry-Level Traveling Project Managers. This is an exciting opportunity to earn a competitive salary, travel throughout the country, gain hands-on experience on major construction projects, and develop valuable leadership and management skills early in your career. No previous construction, electrical, or project management experience is required. We provide the training, mentorship, and support necessary to succeed. We’re looking for individuals who are dependable, detail-oriented, eager to learn, and comfortable taking responsibility. Unlike traditional office positions, this role puts you directly in the field, working alongside experienced construction professionals, interacting with customers, and helping oversee projects from start to finish. This is an excellent opportunity for a recent college graduate who enjoys traveling, working with people, solving problems, and wants to build a long-term career in project management. Compensation & Benefits This position offers a competitive starting salary of $65,000–$75,000 annually , based on qualifications, with opportunities for performance-based bonuses and salary increases as experience and responsibilities grow. GMEA offers: Company-paid business travel, including flights, accommodations, and transportation. Daily meal per diem while traveling, in accordance with company policy. Company-paid health, dental, and vision insurance. Paid time off. 401(k) retirement plan. Paid training and mentorship from experienced construction professionals. Opportunities for career advancement into senior project management and operations leadership positions. We believe in rewarding employees who demonstrate initiative, develop their skills, and take on increasing responsibility. Travel & Work Schedule Requirements — Please Read Carefully Extensive nationwide travel is a mandatory requirement of this position. Must be willing and able to travel frequently by air throughout the United States. Project assignments may last several weeks to multiple months. Must be comfortable spending extended periods away from home. Must be physically present onsite each day that assigned construction activities are taking place, unless otherwise directed by management. Must be comfortable working in active construction environments, including warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and other commercial and industrial settings. Work schedules are determined by project needs and construction activities. Hours may exceed 40 per week and may include early mornings, evenings, or weekends. GMEA provides company-paid travel accommodations and opportunities for trips home in accordance with company travel policies. This is a field-based position, not a remote, hybrid, or traditional office role. Applicants must be genuinely interested in extensive travel and spending the majority of their working time at active construction sites. What a Typical Day Looks Like As an Entry-Level Project Manager, you’ll spend most of your day at an active construction site, helping ensure work progresses safely, efficiently, and according to plan. Your day might include: Walking the project with field supervisors to review installation progress. Taking photos and preparing daily reports for management. Attending coordination meetings with customers, general contractors, and other project stakeholders. Reviewing project schedules and identifying potential delays or concerns. Checking that employees have the materials, tools, and equipment needed to complete their work. Conducting routine safety walks and verifying proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Ensuring tools, materials, and equipment are properly organized, stored, and secured. Communicating project updates, questions, and concerns to company leadership. You’ll work closely with experienced electricians, field supervisors, and project managers who will help you understand the construction process. You will not be expected to know how to manage a construction project on your first day. We will teach you the technical aspects of the job. Your responsibility is to show up prepared, stay organized, communicate clearly, follow established procedures, and be willing to learn. Key Responsibilities Project Oversight & Reporting Monitor daily installation progress and help ensure work follows established project schedules, installation plans, and management instructions. Document construction progress through photographs, daily reports, and regular project updates. Identify potential delays, installation concerns, and missing materials, and communicate them promptly to management. Customer & Team Communication Attend onsite meetings with customers, general contractors, and project stakeholders. Communicate professionally with customers, field supervisors, electricians, and company leadership. Coordinate with field personnel to track progress, address concerns, and support project execution. Field Safety & Site Organization Spend significant time in the field observing installations and conducting routine site walks. Monitor compliance with company safety procedures, site requirements, and proper PPE usage, escalating concerns to the appropriate supervisor. Help ensure company tools, materials, and equipment are properly tracked, stored, secured, and maintained. Monitor material deliveries, identify shortages, and help maintain an organized and professional jobsite. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required. Bachelor’s degree must be fully completed at the time of application. Current students who have not yet graduated are not eligible. No previous construction, electrical, or project management experience required. Must be willing and able to travel extensively throughout the United States, including assignments lasting several weeks or months. Must be available to work onsite daily during assigned construction activities, including occasional evenings and weekends as required. Strong communication, organizational, and time-management skills. Comfortable using computers, smartphones, and basic business software. Ability to follow instructions, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate issues promptly. Comfortable spending significant time standing, walking, and working in active construction environments. Dependable, self-motivated, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. Candidates with degrees in business, engineering, construction management, operations, supply chain management, or related fields are encouraged to apply. However, all bachelor’s degree majors will be considered. Who We’re Looking For We’re not looking for someone who already knows how to manage electrical construction projects. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, work ethic, and willingness to learn. The ideal candidate: Enjoys traveling and experiencing new places. Prefers an active work environment over sitting behind a desk all day. Is organized, observant, and pays attention to details. Enjoys interacting with people and building professional relationships. Takes initiative and follows through on responsibilities. Is comfortable asking questions and learning from experienced professionals. Can work independently while following established processes and instructions. Wants to build a long-term career with opportunities for increased responsibility. Training & Career Growth At GMEA, we believe in developing talented individuals from the ground up. New Project Managers receive hands-on training, guidance, and mentorship from experienced construction professionals while gradually taking on additional responsibilities. As you develop your skills, you’ll have opportunities to manage larger projects, lead teams, build customer relationships, and advance into senior project management or operations leadership positions. We’re looking for individuals who want to grow alongside our company and become valuable members of our long-term leadership team. If you’ve completed your bachelor’s degree, are excited about extensive nationwide travel, and want to build a rewarding career in project management, we encourage you to apply!

Applicants must be genuinely interested in extensive travel and spending the majority of their working time at active construction sites. What a Typical Day Looks Like As an Entry-Level Project Manager, you’ll spend most of your day at an active construction site, helping ensure work progresses safely, efficiently, and according to plan. Your day might include: Walking the project with field supervisors to review installation progress. Taking photos and preparing daily reports for management. Attending coordination meetings with customers, general contractors, and other project stakeholders. Reviewing project schedules and identifying potential delays or concerns. Checking that employees have the materials, tools, and equipment needed to complete their work. Conducting routine safety walks and verifying proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Ensuring tools, materials, and equipment are properly organized, stored, and secured. Communicating project updates, questions, and concerns to company leadership. You’ll work closely with experienced electricians, field supervisors, and project managers who will help you understand the construction process. You will not be expected to know how to manage a construction project on your first day. We will teach you the technical aspects of the job. Your responsibility is to show up prepared, stay organized, communicate clearly, follow established procedures, and be willing to learn. Key Responsibilities Project Oversight & Reporting Monitor daily installation progress and help ensure work follows established project schedules, installation plans, and management instructions. Document construction progress through photographs, daily reports, and regular project updates. Identify potential delays, installation concerns, and missing materials, and communicate them promptly to management. Customer & Team Communication Attend onsite meetings with customers, general contractors, and project stakeholders. Communicate professionally with customers, field supervisors, electricians, and company leadership. Coordinate with field personnel to track progress, address concerns, and support project execution. Field Safety & Site Organization Spend significant time in the field observing installations and conducting routine site walks. Monitor compliance with company safety procedures, site requirements, and proper PPE usage, escalating concerns to the appropriate supervisor. Help ensure company tools, materials, and equipment are properly tracked, stored, secured, and maintained. Monitor material deliveries, identify shortages, and help maintain an organized and professional jobsite. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required. Bachelor’s degree must be fully completed at the time of application. Current students who have not yet graduated are not eligible. No previous construction, electrical, or project management experience required. Must be willing and able to travel extensively throughout the United States, including assignments lasting several weeks or months. Must be available to work onsite daily during assigned construction activities, including occasional evenings and weekends as required. Strong communication, organizational, and time-management skills. Comfortable using computers, smartphones, and basic business software. Ability to follow instructions, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate issues promptly. Comfortable spending significant time standing, walking, and working in active construction environments. Dependable, self-motivated, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. Candidates with degrees in business, engineering, construction management, operations, supply chain management, or related fields are encouraged to apply. However, all bachelor’s degree majors will be considered. Who We’re Looking For We’re not looking for someone who already knows how to manage electrical construction projects. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, work ethic, and willingness to learn. The ideal candidate: Enjoys traveling and experiencing new places. Prefers an active work environment over sitting behind a desk all day. Is organized, observant, and pays attention to details. Enjoys interacting with people and building professional relationships. Takes initiative and follows through on responsibilities. Is comfortable asking questions and learning from experienced professionals. Can work independently while following established processes and instructions. Wants to build a long-term career with opportunities for increased responsibility. Training & Career Growth At GMEA, we believe in developing talented individuals from the ground up. New Project Managers receive hands-on training, guidance, and mentorship from experienced construction professionals while gradually taking on additional responsibilities. As you develop your skills, you’ll have opportunities to manage larger projects, lead teams, build customer relationships, and advance into senior project management or operations leadership positions. We’re looking for individuals who want to grow alongside our company and become valuable members of our long-term leadership team. If you’ve completed your bachelor’s degree, are excited about extensive nationwide travel, and want to build a rewarding career in project management, we encourage you to apply!

We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. description: Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful — keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions. Amazon North American Customer Fulfillment (NACF) is a central part of Amazon and at the heart of our supply chain processes. The Central Flow team focuses on operational execution, risk mitigation, and best practices to deliver for our customers. Are you interested in working on a fast-paced team that pioneers ways to delight customers? Do you have a passion for deep diving data and crunching numbers? Are you motivated to work in challenging situations that will provide you amazing growth opportunities? Do you have the grit required to deliver results no matter what? This is what the Central Flow team is all about – we obsess about our customers! The Central Flow team provides critical operational insights and works with leaders to develop advanced and intuitive automated flow control for Amazon operations. Central Flow is comprised of multiple business verticals each tasked with monitoring and overseeing different aspects of daily operations throughout Amazon’s fulfillment network. Central Flow Leads are responsible for monitoring and managing these workflow functions from a centralized location in Tempe, Arizona or Nashville, Tennessee. Amazon is looking for college students with high-potential. As you join our team, you will have an opportunity to work with stakeholders across North America and develop a collaborative leadership style, while utilizing the tools and processes that have helped create the most customer-centric company on Earth. Flow leads are empowered to use data to drive decisions that can positively impact their teams and customers. Central Flow Interns will bring Amazon’s customer obsession to life in an execution focused environment. You will work on a team of engaged flow leaders to deliver a best-in-class fulfillment experience for customers and stakeholders. You will play a vital role in maintaining a vibrant team culture based on customer obsession, trust, respect, continuous learning, safety, and fun. Central Flow Leads are natural leaders who are comfortable with change and are always looking for ways to improve their operation through data-driven decision making. Central Flow Leads demonstrate a strong work ethic, excellent ownership, the ability to meet deadlines, a willingness to learn new things, and a commitment to the customer and employee experience. role: Junior Design Verification Engineer, Amazon Leo
description: Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. This is a unique opportunity to define a groundbreaking wireless solution with few legacy constraints. role: Research Intern - Machine Learning and Statistics
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Machine Learning (ML) and Statistics group at Microsoft Research New England is hiring multiple Research Interns to work alongside leading researchers, applied scientists, and engineers to advance the state-of-the-art in the field. Projects include applied and theoretical machine learning research on topics including (but not limited to): generative models, transfer learning, domain adaptation, stochastic control, meta-learning, sign language modeling, statistics, approximate inference, distribution compression, weather and climate forecasting, chemistry and materials science, Monte Carlo methods, optimal transport, large language models, AI Scientists, AI for Science, causal inference, causal machine learning, ML for health, adversarial ML, learning and incentives, reinforcement learning, deep learning, supervised learning, and unsupervised learning. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. ## **About Groma** Groma is blending real estate and technology to unlock a new real estate asset class while making it easier for everyone – from institutional investors to the residents in our buildings – to participate in ownership. Our property technology platform uses AI to bring new efficiencies to the small unit count multifamily sector, enabling us to efficiently acquire, upgrade, and operate these 2-20 unit multifamily buildings and bring institutional performance to this massive but historically overlooked sector. Our investor technology platform makes owning these assets accessible to a broad array of investors, with bespoke vehicles available to institutional and family office investors and our flagship vehicle, the blockchain-powered GromaREIT, available to everyone, with a special focus on enabling ownership for the residents in our buildings. Visit to learn more about us. ## **About the Role** We are seeking highly-motivated and organized co-ops to join our property operations team. The Property Operations Co-op will play a crucial role in overseeing the day-to-day operational tasks of our residential real estate portfolio, as well as handle corporate-level administrative responsibilities. This multifaceted role requires a proactive individual with exceptional communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills. The successful candidate will collaborate across various elements of the Property Operations department, including property management, maintenance, construction, and leasing. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: **Property Management** - Field inbound calls, emails, and resident portal requests and inquiries - Perform on-site property inspections quarterly and for apartment turnovers - Perform monthly outstanding balances audit for rent collections - Perform monthly billing for completed work orders - Collaborate with maintenance on the scheduling and follow-up of maintenance tasks - Assist with the move-in and move-out processes **Leasing** - Execute apartment showings for prospective residents - Coordinate showing requests and third-party real estate agent showings - Assist with subletting and lease assignment process for current residents - Assist in reviewing rental applications for prospective renters **Corporate Development** - Assist with the onboarding of new acquisitions to the portfolio - Assist with the implementation of policies and procedures across the property operations team - Participate in property operations meetings and projects ## **Experience** - 1+ years of experience in customer service or hospitality positions (experience in the real estate, construction, or property management industries is a plus) - Strong computer and Excel skills (Google Suite experience preferred) - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, must be very comfortable talking on the phone - Ability to work independently and as part of a team - Diligent and efficient documentation, task, and schedule management skills ### ## **Work Schedule** Most individuals looking for a new place to live tend to do so outside normal working hours, and we have created coverage schedules that balance our team members' and our renters' needs. These schedules allow for a 40-hour work week for our team members, with alternating shift times to account for weeknights and weekend coverage. We’ve included a sample schedule below, but more specific details will be provided during the interview process. | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | **Week 1** (40 total hours) | **Week 2** (40 total hours) | **Week 3** (40 total hours) | **Week 4** (40 total hours) | | **Saturday** | OFF | 11-7 | OFF | 11-7 | | **Sunday** | OFF | 11-7 | OFF | 11-7 | | **Monday** | 11-7 | OFF | 11-7 | OFF | | **Tuesday** | 11-7 | OFF | 11-7 | OFF | | **Wednesday** | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | | **Thursday** | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | | **Friday** | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | 11-7 | ### ## **About our Culture** At Groma, we’re looking to build something big and are on a very fast growth trajectory. We strive to respect individuals and their needs, while also acknowledging the reality that we have a small team that is trying to accomplish some very ambitious goals in a short period of time. We are focused on maintaining our dynamic in-office culture at Groma’s headquarters in downtown Boston. We believe that in-person collaboration and spontaneous interpersonal interaction is critical to the company’s success at this stage. We understand that everyone will need to work from home or the road occasionally, but want to be transparent with this expectation. We have an ever-evolving list of values and conventions that guide how we operate as a company, but here’s a high-level overview of how we think about doing what we do: - We approach our work with pragmatic idealism that enables us to focus on our desire to make the world a better place in ways big and small while also being open to intelligent compromises that accelerate us on our path to serve our broader societal goals. - Our whole team believes strongly that the challenges we are solving require effective teams, not individual heroes. - We have complex conversations well. We sit at the intersection of housing and blockchain policy, both nuanced topics with real-world impacts. We pride ourselves on being thoughtful, seeking the best solutions to real-world challenges, and implementing them effectively in the real world. ## **Compensation** This is a 40 hour per week position and is paid at a rate of $20 per hour. ## **Job Benefits** - Fully covered commuter passes for bus, subway, boat, or commuter rail - Competitive paid time off policy, 4 company holidays within co-op cycle - In-office gym and roof deck - Comprehensive catering, snack, and beverage program Position Salary Range $20—$20 USD

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. You’ll gain exposure to end-to-end mission architecture, customer requirements, and cross-functional engineering collaboration. ### **About Groma** Groma is blending real estate and technology to unlock a new real estate asset class while making it easier for everyone – from institutional investors to the residents in our buildings – to participate in ownership.
