Answer phone calls and provide information or assistance to motorists, SCDOT personnel, or other agencies on traffic and road conditions, transfer calls to designated personnel as appropriate. Communicate via radio and/or phone with law enforcement, ambulance, fire department, and towing service staff and provide clear and accurate information regarding traffic incidents and the response required. Communicate via radio and/or phone with SCDOT personnel to provide clear and accurate information regarding incidents, traffic, road, maintenance and construction activity, and related weather conditions. Perform written documentation of activity and communication in a clear, concise, and complete manner. Minimum Requirements: High School Diploma or GED. Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time monitoring Intelligent Transportation Systems such CCTV camera displays, law enforcement radio broadcasts, answering/responding to calls and communicating to other staff or partner agencies. Ability to successfully pass post-employment 6-week SCDOT TMC training and performance program which is a condition of continued employment. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Previous experience working in a call center, customer service, 911 Operator or dispatching environment. Demonstrated ability to meet a high level of customer service expectations. Ability to work in a calm manner and professional manner in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment. Previous experience working in a position which includes heavy telephone, radio, and computer/technology usage. Effective oral and written communications skills for in-person, radio, and phone conversations. Ability to interpret and understand geographic information portrayed on a map and map-based applications. Knowledge of interstates and state routes throughout South Carolina with geographic familiarity of the freeway system and arterial roads. Working knowledge of and skill set to utilize and operate an ATMS software platform and/or web-based applications. Efficient and accurate data entry skills. Ability to solve problems and prioritize tasks, and be organized, responsible and timely. Ability to work independently and in a team environment. The successful candidate will contribute to traffic engineering studies, transportation planning and design, traffic operations analyses, and preparation of technical reports and project deliverables. This role is well suited for a recent graduate who is interested in developing a career in traffic engineering and transportation. Assist with preparation of plans, specifications, cost estimates, and other project documentation. Maintain organized project files and documentation while meeting project schedules and quality requirements. Support other transportation engineering assignments as needed. Familiarity with AutoCAD, MicroStation, ArcGIS, or other transportation design/GIS software. Knowledge of MUTCD, NCDOT standards and guidelines, AASHTO guidance, and/or ITE resources. Experience collecting and analyzing traffic data. Familiarity with North Carolina transportation practices and local/regional roadway systems. role: Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Control Systems (New Grad)
description: Vast is developing next-generation **space stations and space infrastructure** using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced **Vast Satellite**, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo. Headquartered in **Long Beach, California**, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy. Vast is looking for **Mechanical Engineer, Thermal Control Systems (New Grad)**, to help develop the systems behind our human-rated space stations. You'll use your engineering knowledge and creativity to design, build, and test novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. This will be a **full-time, exempt** position located in our **Long Beach, CA** location. ### Responsibilities: - Design and develop thermal control system components for our artificial-gravity space station, such as heat exchangers, cold plates, heaters, and heat pipes, with guidance from senior engineers. - Perform thermal and fluid analyses to size components and check that designs meet requirements. - Contribute to design trades and support systems engineering tasks such as tracking requirements and interfaces. - Help plan and run development tests, collect and interpret data, and use the results to improve designs and manufacturing processes. - Work with avionics, software, and mission operations teams to make sure your components integrate with the rest of the station. - Work hands-on with technicians and suppliers to build, test, and troubleshoot hardware. - Design with manufacturability and reliability in mind. ### Minimum Qualifications: - B.S. in mechanical, aerospace, or civil engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field. - Coursework, project, or internship experience designing and developing mechanical components or systems. - Familiarity with 3D CAD and FEA software through coursework, student project teams, or internships. - Understanding of GD&T fundamentals (ASME Y14.5). ### Preferred Skills & Experience: - Participation in hands-on engineering teams such as Formula SAE, rocketry, CubeSat, or robotics. - A portfolio or examples of designs you've taken from concept through build or test. - Coursework, project, or internship experience designing structures or components for a high-performance vehicle or spacecraft. - Familiarity with CAD tools, ideally NX, and exposure to PLM tools such as Teamcenter. - Exposure to thermal or structural analysis using Ansys, Femap/Nastran, Abaqus, or similar tools. - Working knowledge of GD&T fundamentals (ASME Y14.5). - A curious, hands-on approach to problem solving, including interest in troubleshooting and root cause analysis. - Hands-on experience building or testing hardware, whether through internships, co-ops, machine shops, or student project teams. - Awareness of aerospace design and environmental test standards such as SMC-S-016, NASA-STD-5001, or MIL-STD-810. ### Additional Requirements: - Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends to support critical mission milestones. ### Pay Ranges: - Mechanical Engineer/ Level I: $86,100.00 - $122,220.00 *We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.* **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS** Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee & onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees. **U.S. EXPORT CONTROL COMPLIANCE STATUS**The person hired will have access to information and items subject to U.S. export controls, and therefore, must either be a “U.S. person” as defined by [22 C.F.R. § 120.62](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22/section-120.62) or otherwise eligible for deemed export licensing. description: **About Us**: Founded 20 years ago and headquartered in Chicago, the DV Group of financial services firms has grown to more than 600 people operating throughout North America, Europe and Asia. Since spinning out of a large brokerage firm in 2016, DV Trading has rapidly scaled as an independent proprietary trading firm utilizing its own capital, trading strategies, and risk management methodologies to provide liquidity to worldwide financial markets and hedging opportunities to commodity producers and users. Why you are prepared for an intense, entrepreneurial, fully in-office environment. **Benefits:** - Discretionary bonus eligibility - Medical, dental, and vision insurance - HSA, FSA, and Dependent Care Options - Employer Paid Group Term Life and AD&D insurance - Voluntary LTD, Life & AD&D insurance - Flexible Vacation policy - Retirement plan with employer match **Compensation:** *Competitive base salary plus discretionary performance bonus* *DV is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms. All resumes submitted by search firms to DV via e-mail, the Internet, personal delivery, facsimile, or any other method without a valid written agreement shall be deemed the sole property of DV, and no fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by DV. Turner's award winning internship program strives to combine meaningful work as a part of a construction finance team with opportunities to learn every facet of our business as a general contractor. We seek to employ thought-provoking leaders who excel in a fast-paced, challenging, and collaborative environment. Position Description: Participate in a structured Intern Program designed to apply academic knowledge to real-world business scenarios. Build foundational knowledge in Operational Finance, including training on accounting fundamentals, project finance concepts, and financial systems. Support day-to-day financial management activities across key accounting functions including Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, General Ledger, Reconciliation, and Special Services. Contribute to data collection, reporting, and analysis efforts while assisting with process improvements related to budgeting, cost tracking, variance analysis, and operational performance metrics. Gain exposure to emerging technologies, including use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data tools in finance to support analysis, improve efficiency, and enhance reporting processes. Where applicable this assignment will support learning that applies to earning educational credits. Intern may be assigned to a single construction project on a construction job site or to an office location supporting multiple projects. This opportunity is available during summer. Essential Duties Key Responsibilities: Engage with full participation and immersion of Intern Program, take ownership to fulfill learning requirements and assigned responsibilities, while coordinating with supervisors to effectively prioritize work, manage time, and ensure successful completion of program and project deliverables. /li> Learn, understand, and apply Turner financial accounting processes, including construction accounting principles, earnings, and revenue recognition, with guidance from your supervisor. /li> Follow company and Finance policies related to financial reporting, confidentiality, and data governance. /li> Learn and develop skills related to effective communication, conflict resolution, taking direction, and teamwork. Maintain professional relationships with colleagues, clients, and business partners. /li> Participate in training sessions, meetings, project site visits, and other learning opportunities provided through Intern Program. /li> Review billing details against client contractual requirements for accuracy, review contracts and invoice backup for accurate accounts receivable. /li> Assist with validating coding of project costs and comparing invoices and expenses to project cost coding structures. /li> Support Shared Services Organization (SSO) with invoice processing tasks, verify subcontractor and vendor accounts status, including lien waivers and recoded costs to support accurate month-end work-in-place reporting. /li> Assist with analyzing budgets and reallocating costs through preparation of journal entries and in support of month-end close process. Assist with monitoring project cash flow, including billings, collections, and payments, and prepare payments held reports to support team communication and visibility. /li> Support under and overbilling analysis and participate in team meetings to support communication of project status. /li> Gain exposure to Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled tools and data analytics techniques to support financial analysis, reporting, and process efficiencies. /li> Contribute to process improvement initiatives, identify opportunities to use AI technology and automation to standardize financial workflows, templates, and reports. /li> Prepare ad hoc analyses and presentations to support financial reviews and management requests. /li> Share periodic progress updates with your supervisor and engage in feedback conversations to support learning and professional growth. /li> Other activities, duties, and responsibilities as assigned.

This permanent, full-time position is located in Phoenix, AZ. Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. Key job responsibilities Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals. • You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells. • You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components. • You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc. • You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head Program Requirements: • Flexible to relocate after completion of the program • Able to enroll in and attend a 9-week training at one of four designated training providers (Location to be determined post-interview) • Meet the minimum qualifying score on a Mechanical Aptitude Test Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment.

## About Us Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to **$200M+ in ARR**, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. - We **lean in:** ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. - We **fight for excellence:** high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. - We **grow together:** as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. **Please note, this role is 5 days/week on-site in NYC.** ## The Role As a Junior/Mid-level Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work directly with enterprise customers to understand their needs and build the software that connects Legora to their systems and workflows. You'll build integrations and contribute to Legora's core product, taking defined projects from technical scoping through implementation, testing, and production delivery. You'll learn to turn customer needs into practical engineering solutions, with support from experienced engineers on more complex architecture and delivery decisions. This is a hands-on individual contributor role within Enterprise Engineering. You'll work closely with product engineers, Legal Engineers, and Engagement Managers, building your technical judgment and customer-facing skills while taking increasing ownership of delivery. ## What You'll Be Doing - Work with enterprise customers and your team to understand workflows, clarify requirements, and translate customer needs into engineering tasks. - Build, test, and ship integrations and product changes, taking ownership of defined projects from implementation through deployment. - Explain technical decisions clearly, ask useful questions, and keep customers and teammates informed about progress and blockers. - Work with experienced engineers on design reviews and technical tradeoffs, seeking support early when requirements or risks are unclear. - Debug issues across Legora and customer systems, using logs, tests, and systematic investigation to find and resolve problems. - Bring customer feedback into product discussions and identify opportunities to make solutions and tooling reusable. ## Who You Are - **2-3+ years of software engineering experience**, with hands-on experience building and shipping production software. - Strong software engineering fundamentals. You can write, test, and debug reliable code and work effectively in an existing codebase. - A clear communicator who is comfortable talking with customers, asking questions, and explaining technical work to engineers and nontechnical stakeholders. - Experience taking a feature or defined project through implementation and delivery. You can explain what you built, the decisions you made, and the outcome. - Curious about the problem behind a request. You want to understand how people use what you build and improve it based on feedback. - Accountable for your work, receptive to feedback, and able to surface blockers early. You are ready to take on more independence as your scope grows. - Adaptable across technologies and interested in learning unfamiliar systems quickly. ## Nice to Have - Experience building B2B enterprise software in a fast-moving environment. - Experience working directly with customers or partnering with product teams to understand user needs. - Familiarity with APIs, authentication, integrations, and data flows across systems. - TypeScript experience. We use it extensively, but welcome strong engineers from other stacks. - Practical experience using AI tools to build software or improve a workflow. ## **What’s In It For You** - **Global collaboration:** Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America. - **Competitive package:** Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success. - **Meaningful work:** Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily. - **In-person environment:** Union Square office designed for ambitious builders and company provided lunch daily. - **Benefits & Perks:** We invest in our people with a comprehensive, thoughtfully designed benefits package: Medical, Dental & Vision - Multiple medical plan options through Aetna and Kaiser Permanente - HSA or Healthcare FSA (based on plan selection) - Dental plans via MetLife - Vision plans via Vision Care Family Support - Generous parental leave - Free access to Maven Clinic - Dependent Care FSA - Free One Medical membership for employees and dependents Additional Perks - Pre-tax commuter benefits - Life Insurance + STD/LTD - 401(K) with generous company match - Unlimited PTO - Robust voluntary benefits, including identity protection (via Aura), legal coverage via MetLife, pet savings programs, and more **Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer** At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

At Coolray Electrical, you’ll have the opportunity to play an important role on our Electrical team. You’ll work alongside experienced electricians and collaborate with other departments to ensure quality workmanship, accurate service, and the exceptional customer experience Coolray is known for! As an Apprentice Electrician , you’ll assist Senior Electricians with general electrical repairs, installations, and services. You’ll learn the skills needed to build a successful career in the electrical industry while ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with applicable local and national electrical codes. We’re looking for someone who is dependable, eager to learn, takes pride in their work, and is committed to delivering outstanding customer service by treating every customer with professionalism, respect, and care. Pay: $18–$20 per hour , plus industry-leading benefits, paid time off, six paid holidays per year, a paid day off for your birthday, a 401(k) with company match, and much more! Must be able to pass a pre-employment background check and drug screen. The Company Coolray Companies has been keeping homes in Atlanta comfortable since 1966. Through Coolray, Mr. Plumber, and our electrical services team, we are committed to providing prompt, reliable service, convenient scheduling, and an exceptional customer experience. With more than 500 team members and multiple service locations, we’re continuing to grow and are looking for motivated individuals to grow with us! Ongoing training and opportunities to develop your electrical skills. Support and mentorship from experienced electricians and management. A team-oriented environment focused on quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. Opportunities for career advancement within Coolray Companies. What’s In It for Me? Competitive hourly pay of $18–$20 per hour . Eligibility for bonus programs, including biweekly bonuses. Tool purchasing program. Annual boot allowance. Family-friendly schedules. Paid training and ongoing professional development. Robust paid time off (PTO) plan. Six paid holidays per year, plus a paid day off for your birthday. Health, vision, and dental insurance options for you and your family. 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage. Flexible spending account (FSA), employee assistance program (EAP), legal services, pet insurance, and identity theft protection options. Opportunities to attend Atlanta Braves and Gwinnett Stripers games through Coolray Company tickets. Opportunities to participate in charitable events through the Coolray Cares program. Continuous training and career growth supported by an experienced management team. A dynamic, collaborative, and fun work environment. Ready to build your future in the electrical trade? Join Coolray Electrical and become part of a team that values hard work, professional growth, and exceptional customer service! Responsibilities Job Responsibilities Assist Senior Electricians with troubleshooting and accurately and efficiently diagnosing electrical problems. Learn to provide written and verbal recommendations for electrical repairs and replacements. Develop strong customer service and communication skills while delivering a professional customer experience. Assist with the repair and replacement of electrical components, including: Light fixtures Switches and receptacles Circuit wiring Circuit breakers Breaker and fuse panels Electrical service and metering equipment Perform routine electrical maintenance inspections under the direction of Senior Electricians. Safely access areas of buildings being serviced, including crawl spaces, attics, and other confined or difficult-to-reach areas. Learn to proficiently use the tools and equipment necessary to complete assigned tasks, including electrical meters, power tools, hand tools, and ladders. Communicate regularly with Senior Electricians and team members in a professional, friendly, and efficient manner. Participate in on-the-job training to develop technical expertise, strengthen troubleshooting skills, and work toward becoming a Lead Electrician. Follow applicable electrical codes, company safety procedures, and established quality standards. Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by management. Qualifications Education High school diploma or General Education Development (GED) preferred. Experience Six months to one year of experience as an apprentice or helper electrician preferred. Residential and/or light commercial electrical experience is a plus. Willingness to learn, follow instructions, and develop electrical trade skills through hands-on training. Certifications and Licenses Valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record. State electrical license or certification is a plus, but not required for an apprentice position. Language Ability to communicate effectively in English with customers, team members, and management. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Basic knowledge of electrical methods, materials, tools, and equipment, or the willingness to learn. Understanding of electrical hazards and safety precautions, with a commitment to following company safety procedures and applicable electrical codes. Ability to work evenings, weekends, holidays, or participate in an on-call rotation when needed. Strong customer service, verbal and written communication, and interpersonal skills. Good time management, organization, and planning skills. Ability to follow directions, work as part of a team, and accept coaching and feedback. Dependable attendance, punctuality, and a strong work ethic. Motivation to learn the electrical trade and advance toward becoming a Lead Electrician. Computer, Software, and Equipment Skills Smartphone, iPad, or tablet proficiency. Basic computer skills. Ability to learn industry-specific software and applications. Basic email skills using Microsoft or web-based email platforms. Ability to use office equipment, including copiers, scanners, and fax machines, as needed. Work Environment and Physical Requirements This position involves working in residential and light commercial environments, including homes, offices, schools, hospitals, retail stores, and other customer locations. Employees may travel to multiple service locations throughout the workday and work both indoors and outdoors, depending on the service call. The work environment may involve exposure to electrical hazards, varying weather conditions, confined spaces, crawl spaces, attics, ladders, and other conditions common to the electrical trade. Employees must follow established safety procedures and use appropriate personal protective equipment. Physical Requirements The Apprentice Electrician must be able to perform the following physical activities, with or without reasonable accommodation: Standing and walking: Frequently throughout the workday. Sitting and reaching: Frequently, depending on job assignments. Climbing and crawling: Occasionally, including accessing ladders, crawl spaces, and attics. Squatting, kneeling, and bending: Frequently when inspecting, installing, or repairing electrical components. Lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling: Frequently handling tools, equipment, and materials weighing up to 40 pounds. Heavy lifting: Occasionally handling items weighing between 41 and 100 pounds, with assistance or appropriate equipment when necessary. role: AI Security Engineer Co-Op Intern, Winter 2027
description: # Our Mission Rebuild how the world works, to make institutions work better for the people they serve. # About Brain Co. Brain Co. builds AI-native operating systems for large, regulated institutions. Each system is built for a specific industry, powered by agents that push real workflows forward. Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model. # Why Now Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services. Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact. You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now. ## **About the Co-Op** As a **Platform Security Engineer Co-Op Intern**, you’ll work alongside experienced security, platform, and infrastructure engineers to help build security directly into how Brain Co. develops and ships software. This co-op is designed for current undergraduate students, specifically **juniors or seniors**, who want hands-on experience securing real production systems. You’ll contribute to projects across CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, containers, and Infrastructure-as-Code while receiving mentorship through code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on collaboration with the team. This is a builder-focused security role. You’ll learn how security tooling and automated guardrails can make the secure path the easy path for engineers. ## **What You’ll Work On** - Help build and improve **security controls in CI/CD pipelines**, including static analysis, secrets scanning, dependency checks, and automated policy enforcement. - Contribute to **developer-facing security tooling**, such as linting rules, reusable workflows, automation, and guardrails. - Help secure **Kubernetes and containerized workloads**, including access controls, image security, workload configuration, and deployment policies. - Contribute to security baselines in **Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code**, including IAM, networking, encryption, and secure defaults. - Work with **cloud infrastructure across AWS, GCP, or Azure** to identify misconfigurations and improve security visibility. - Help automate the detection and remediation of common security issues. - Participate in **threat modeling, code reviews, and architecture discussions** alongside experienced security and platform engineers. - Work with engineers to understand security findings and turn them into practical, actionable fixes. - Help improve documentation and tooling so security controls are easy for developers to understand and adopt. ## **You Might Be a Great Fit If You…** - Are a **current undergraduate student, specifically a junior or senior**, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field. - Have strong **software engineering fundamentals** through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects. - Have experience programming in **Python, Go, Java, C++, Bash, or a similar language**. - Have exposure to or a strong interest in **application security, platform security, cloud security, or infrastructure security**. - Are familiar with or excited to learn technologies such as **Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and AWS/GCP/Azure**. - Have an interest in how software moves from code to production, including **CI/CD, containers, cloud infrastructure, and deployment workflows**. - Enjoy thinking about how systems can fail, where trust boundaries exist, and how security controls can prevent problems without slowing engineers down. - Are curious, proactive, and excited to learn quickly in a fast-paced engineering environment. - Enjoy taking ownership of technical problems while learning from experienced engineers. ## **Bonus Points For** - Coursework, projects, or internship experience involving **cloud security, Kubernetes, or Infrastructure-as-Code**. - Familiarity with security tooling such as **OPA, Conftest, Kyverno, Trivy, Semgrep, or similar tools**. - Experience with **secrets management, IAM, or authentication and authorization systems**. - Interest in **software supply chain security**, including dependency security, image signing, SBOMs, or secure build pipelines. - Experience building developer tools or automation. ## **What You’ll Gain** - Hands-on experience building **security tooling for production AI systems**. - Practical exposure to **CI/CD security, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, containers, and Infrastructure-as-Code**. - Experience designing security controls that fit directly into real engineering workflows. - Direct mentorship from experienced security, platform, and infrastructure engineers. - Exposure to threat modeling, secure architecture, and software supply chain security. - Ownership over meaningful engineering projects that can ship into production. ## **Co-Op Details & Benefits** - **Winter / Spring Co-Op: January 11, 2027 – April 30, 2027** - Competitive co-op compensation. - Hands-on mentorship from experienced security and infrastructure engineers. - Opportunity to work on real production systems used globally. - Potential return-offer consideration for future internships or full-time roles. - Daily lunches if onsite. ## **Why Intern at Brain Co.** - Help secure AI systems deployed across governments, healthcare, and other critical industries. - Work on security as an **engineering problem**, not just a policy or compliance exercise. - Learn directly from engineers and leaders from Tesla, DeepMind, Databricks, and other top engineering organizations. - Build practical experience with the security foundations behind modern production AI systems. - Take ownership early and grow quickly through hands-on engineering. - Thrive in a culture built on speed, curiosity, and impact. If you’re a current junior or senior who wants to **build security into real systems rather than only study vulnerabilities in isolation**, Brain Co. is a place to learn, build, and make an impact.

### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ## **About the Firmware Team** The firmware team owns the embedded firmware on all of our microcontroller systems on our aircraft and delivery system. We range from the application layer to the platform and foundation it’s built on. Including bootloaders, RTOS integration, serial and ethernet communication, up to battery management and motor control. ## **The Role** Zipline aircraft depend on embedded firmware to execute critical flight and safety functions across a network of microcontrollers and embedded Linux computers. This software must perform reliably as aircraft move from manufacturing into delivery operations at field sites around the world, including locations that are difficult to access over a network. You will own C++ firmware and supporting tools that are critical to the safety and operation of these systems. While making the system more observable and easier to diagnose at scale. Working alongside electrical, mechanical, embedded Linux, and systems engineers, you will turn hardware behavior and flight data into reliable, maintainable software for deployed aircraft. ## **What You'll Do** - Design and build C++ firmware for a distributed system of aircraft microcontrollers. - Develop reliable Ethernet, serial, and other microcontroller communication interfaces. - Define platform-level interfaces and reusable firmware components that support multiple aircraft subsystems. - Own the predictable and reliable performance of our microcontroller systems and the communication buses that connect them, across startup, real-time operation, fault handling, and recovery. - Optimize real-time behavior, including CPU utilization, memory usage, scheduling latency, timing jitter, and resource contention - Develop metrics, monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities to prepare the system for field deployment at scale - Develop Rust-based tooling and software-in-the-loop simulations to test and validate firmware behavior. ## **What You'll Bring** You are a person who: - Is passionate about learning about firmware, realtime systems, Zipline’s aircraft and systems, and our mission. - Has prior internship or design team experience. - Has experience with writing C or C++. - Has excellent grades in embedded systems classes. It is expected that you will be onsite in South San Francisco 5 days / week for this internship. Rising seniors are preferred. ### **What Else You Should Know** *Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May to June/September.* *Candidates are limited to* ***three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** *The hourly rate for this internship is $54 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements* The total compensation package for each role may also include: a housing stipend; overtime pay; relocation support; paid sick time; and more. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

description: During this internship, you will conduct research and engineering in AI and machine learning, with a particular focus on Foundation Models and Data-centric AI . This includes specialized areas like Foundation Model AI tooling, spatiotemporal machine learning, time series learning, and general representation learning. Applications span Bosch's AIoT (AI+IoT) business domains such as ADAS, connected vehicles, Industry 4.0, IoT, and car multimedia. A few of your additional responsibilities will include: Implement research results to solve real-world challenges, ensuring high-quality system integration within Bosch's existing platforms. Document and disseminate research findings through high-caliber publications and/or patent submissions. Required Qualifications: Currently pursing a Master's degree with peer-reviewed publication(s) in machine learning, deep learning, or computer vision, OR a Ph.D. in Computer Science or a related discipline. Research experience, or an equivalent graduate research background, primarily in AI technologies including Foundation Models and Data-centric AI. Publications in premier machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision journals and conferences. Proficiency in one or more programming languages commonly used in machine learning (e.g., Python). Minimum GPA of 3.0 Desired Qualifications: Knowledge in machine learning and deep learning, notably in Foundation Model AI tooling, ADAS, spatiotemporal machine learning, deep graph learning, general representation learning, model distillation, and related areas. Familiar with major machine learning platforms like PyTorch. Experience in vision and multimodality foundation models (e.g., SAM, CLIP, LLaVA) and AI-based ADAS solutions is a plus. Strong background in math and statistics is a plus. Strong interpersonal, communication, and teamwork capabilities. role: Director of Student Engagement at Boston University Hillel
description: # Director of Student Engagement ## Boston University Hillel ## Role Overview Make your mark on Jewish student life by joining Boston University Hillel as its Director of Student Engagement. This is a big, exciting job for BU Hillel, working at the largest private university for Jewish students in the world. This position will work on major aspects of undergraduate student engagement, serving 4,000 Jewish undergraduate students. We welcome candidates who are thirsty for being in relationship with Jewish people – from students to alumni, parents, donors, and other partners. If you’re team-oriented, never give up, and truly believe that you must “be the change you wish to see in the world,” then this is the position for you! This position reports to the Executive Director and works closely with the CEO, Campus Rabbi, and COO. ## What You’ll Do ### **Undergraduate Student Life Work** The role brings a professional with talent, passion, and skills to Boston University to imagine and implement Jewish undergraduate student life. As the Director, you will serve as both the architect of a comprehensive, strategic, and robust undergraduate engagement plan and the primary practitioner implementing this plan with 4,000 Jewish undergraduate students. You’ll have the opportunity to impact thousands of students—Boston University is home to over 17,000 undergraduate students across 10 undergraduate schools and colleges thirsty for resources, engagement, and care from BU Hillel. This position has significant responsibility overseeing key student engagement areas for BU Hillel, including: student engagement outreach strategies, mentoring projects, advising student leaders, leading cohorts around Boston and trips to Israel, and more. You also contribute to religious activities such as Shabbat services/dinner, holiday programs, Israel events, and more. You will teach in our award-winning Jewish learning seminars with Jewish text at the center of each class. You will partner with BU Hillel’s senior rabbinic leadership on strategy and content for each of these programs, and receive guidance. You’ll receive training from BU Hillel and Hillel International professionals, and learn from Jewish leaders on how to seamlessly weave Judaism into your work as a Hillel engagement professional. Each day you will be charged with empowering students to engage in meaningful and joyous Jewish lives, weaving in Jewish values, texts, and history. ### **Student Engagement and Outreach** - Manage Hillel’s marketing and outreach to all undergraduate colleges and residence halls—working with individual college partners and student groups. - Director strategies for outreach and relationships with undergraduate students, conducting daily 1x1 initial and follow-up meetings. - Strengthen and support student leadership cohorts ranging from engagement interns, to marketing interns, and career focused fellowships. - Mentor various students in their desire to bring passion projects to campus. - Grow Hillel’s capacity to meet engagement goals through detailed management and analysis of the CRM Database. - Drive key insights on undergraduate student engagement and population for further growth of the program. - Works with Hillel’s staff and student leaders to identify micro-communities and opportunities for students to engage within those micro-communities. These include but are not limited to: class years, majors, Jewish Greek life, Jewish residence hall life, arts and culture, volunteerism, and social justice. ### **Jewish Life and Learning** - Develop, lead, and recruit 1-2 Jewish learning fellowship classes and 1-2 experience groups in Boston per semester - Weave Jewish education into social and cultural programs across campus. - Co-lead immersive travel trips to Israel or community service trips to international destinations weaving Jewish content, text, and learning into each day of travel. - Co-lead experience groups around Boston that have 3-5 parts to each group focused on fun, friendship, Jewish identity, and exploration. These cohorts attend fun events like Celtics games, fitness studios, best restaurants of Boston, musical concerts, theater shows, and more. ## On a day to day basis you will - Meeting with a group of students or individual students over coffee or a meal to understand which issues are most important to them and developing a plan of action together. - Designing and executing a strategic engagement plan for undergraduate students, including planning educational, social, cultural, holiday, or Shabbat programs across a wide variety of undergraduate schools, students, and disciplines. - Participating in a conversation with student leaders of all types of faith, ethnic, and racial backgrounds to build key relationships and partnerships. - Developing key insights through 1x1 conversations on how to create an engagement program with high levels of reach and depth. - Working Shabbat, holidays, and otherwise supporting the rest of your Hillel team—sometimes on nights and weekends. - Participating in a professional development webinar. - Teaching and facilitating Jewish learning through an undergraduate student lens. ## What You’ve Accomplished - 3–5 years of experience - Bachelor's degree required; master's or advanced degree preferred (could be rabbinic, Jewish education, business, social work, or other relevant fields to this work). - Significant computer skills, including Microsoft Office, Google Docs, CRM, and social media - Must be willing to work nights and occasional weekends - Requires discretion and independent judgement in performing all aspects of the position. - An entrepreneurial spirit, willingness to take risks and the ability to learn from efforts that don’t work out as planned ## What You’ll Bring to the Job We are most interested in someone who is organized, driven, and mission-focused. The most important experience we are looking for is the ability to be a Jewish leader, organize people and projects, and inspire commitment and action. In terms of prerequisite requirements, we are open to candidates with the following: - We are interested in people with backgrounds in PR, Communications, Marketing, Communal Engagement, For Profit Business, Customer Service **and/or** - Significant Jewish communal life experience in any of the following: Hillel, Jewish nonprofit, Jewish camping, Jewish education, or Rabbinic leadership. **and/or** - Significant experience with relationship-based work in areas such as: student engagement, community partnerships, nonprofit management, corporate social responsibility, or arts management. **and/or** - Significant experience in for-profit environments that is relatable to this work, alongside a very strong Jewish lay leadership background. ## What You’ll Receive - High-level professional development to help develop core skills and gain expertise from changemakers, engagers, and Jewish life experts. - Mentoring and career coaching to help you during and after your position. - A network of terrific colleagues from across the Hillel movement. - Travel opportunities, both domestically and internationally, multiple times per year. - A comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, Tax Deferred Retirement Plan, Life, AD&D, and Long-Term Disability insurances, Flexible Spending Plan, generous vacation/sick time, and parental leave. - A salary of $55,000–$65,000 depending on level of experience. ## About Boston University Hillel Boston University Hillel is at the hub of a world-class university, in the thriving city of Boston, right near Fenway Park. Home to 4,000 Jewish undergraduates and 2,000 Jewish graduate students, BU Hillel’s mission is to inspire, educate, and empower BU students to lead meaningful and joyous Jewish lives. We engage 4,000 students per year, 600 of whom qualify as in-depth relationships. 200 students travel with BU Hillel each year. We have 160+ student leaders and 120+ lay leaders. Boston University Hillel is affiliated with Hillel International. role: Research Intern - Document Intelligence and Content Understanding
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Documents are one of the richest forms in which human knowledge is created and communicated, combining language, visual structure, tables, images, and domain-specific conventions. Our team is developing the next generation of document intelligence systems that can perceive, understand, and reason over this complex multimodal content. As a Research Intern, you will investigate new models and learning techniques that advance the state of the art in document understanding, from fundamental research to challenging real-world scenarios. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to evaluate new ideas at scale and translate research advances into practical AI capabilities. We are seeking candidates with strong machine learning research experience and an interest in multimodal AI, computer vision, natural language processing, or related areas. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** **Required Qualifications** - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a relevant field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. **Preferred Qualifications** - Experience conducting research in document intelligence, document understanding, multimodal AI, computer vision, natural language processing, or related areas. - Experience with large language models, vision-language models, or other multimodal foundation models. - Experience developing machine learning systems using Python and modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch. - Demonstrated ability to define research questions, design experiments, establish evaluation methodologies, and analyze experimental results. - Prior research experience demonstrated through publications at peer-reviewed conferences or journals, research internships, or significant research projects. - Experience collaborating with researchers and engineers to translate research ideas into prototypes or practical AI systems. - Proficient written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting research findings through papers, technical reports, posters, or presentations. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. **About Neuralink:** We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world. **Team Description:** The Pathology Team plays a critical role in the evaluation of both macroscopic and microscopic tissue samples derived from our preclinical studies. The team encompasses specialized units focused on Anatomic Pathology, Histology, Digital Pathology, and Laboratory Operations. **Job Description and Responsibilities:** As a Histopathology Intern, you will support both routine histology workflows and the development of next-generation tissue preparation and imaging techniques. In this role, you will work closely with pathologists and histology specialists to evaluate tissue-device interactions, with a primary focus on benchmarking, optimizing, and scaling novel volumetric histology pipelines such as tissue clearing and lightsheet microscopy. You will apply foundational biological and laboratory principles in a fast-paced environment and are expected to: - Assist in the optimization and validation of next-generation histology workflows, specifically focusing on aqueous and solvent-based tissue clearing methods and lightsheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) for 3D tissue visualization - Help maintain, calibrate, and operate advanced optical hardware, lightsheet imaging systems, and automated histology equipment - Support routine tissue processing, embedding, sectioning (microtomy), slide preparation, and standard/special staining protocols - Document experimental protocols, image acquisition parameters, and data analysis pipelines in compliance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and laboratory SOPs - Work cross-functionally with Pathology, Preclinical, and Surgical Engineering teams to prepare tissue samples, acquire high-resolution datasets, and support study deliverables - Assist with laboratory upkeep, including reagent preparation, chemical and biohazardous waste disposal, and inventory management **Required Qualifications:** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, Biology, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline - Basic understanding of anatomy, neuroanatomy, and light/fluorescence microscopy principles - Familiarity with laboratory safety standards, fume hood operation, and handling biohazardous/chemical materials - Strong written and verbal communication skills with high attention to detail **Preferred Qualifications:** - 6+ months of relevant academic coursework or wet-lab experience handling biological tissues and standard histology techniques (e.g., tissue fixation, sectioning, or fluorescence imaging) - Direct hands-on experience or coursework in tissue clearing protocols and lightsheet fluorescence microscopy - Experience with 3D image analysis software or large volume rendering tools (e.g., Imaris, ImageJ/Fiji, or Python/MATLAB image processing libraries) - Exposure to medical device research and/or neuroscience applications - Proven ability to learn new laboratory equipment quickly and troubleshoot technical procedures **Additional Requirements and Competencies:** - Ability to work flexible hours, including off-hours and weekends - Comfortable working in a controlled laboratory environment with potential exposure to extreme temperatures, fumes, and biohazardous materials or chemicals, including formalin. - Ability to lift and maneuver up to 45 pounds to manage large volumes of chemical waste, reposition large animals, and perform other physically demanding tasks as required. **Pay Transparency:** The following details are for Texas individuals only. **Texas Hourly Rate:** $25/Hr USD **What We Offer:** Full-time employees are eligible for the following benefits listed below. - An opportunity to change the world and work with some of the smartest and most talented experts from different fields - Growth potential; we rapidly advance team members who have an outsized impact - Excellent medical, dental, and vision insurance through a PPO plan - Paid holidays - Commuter benefits - Meals provided - Equity (RSUs) *\*Temporary Employees & Interns excluded* - 401(k) plan *\*Interns initially excluded until they work 1,000 hours* - Parental leave *\*Temporary Employees & Interns excluded* - Flexible time off *\*Temporary Employees & Interns excluded*

Given the diversity of the work, Interns learn how to approach real estate decisions in many different contexts. - **Build a durable analytical toolkit.** Interns learn how to identify market trends, conduct research, construct financial and statistical analyses, and communicate findings through clear, polished client materials. - **Learn from experienced consultants.** Interns work directly with project managers and senior firm leadership, gaining exposure to how consulting teams approach problems, evaluate solutions, and translate analysis into recommendations. - **Establish a foundation for a career in real estate.** Strong performers may be invited to return to RCLCO to advance their careers in real estate consulting. role: RBT Recruiting Manager, Campus & University Partnerships
description: **Location:** Remote (US) | **Reports to:** Strategy & Ops, Senior Manager | **Compensation:** 60,000–100,000 base + eligible for bonus ## **About the role** A child's ABA therapy can't start until a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) is hired. Behavior technicians are the scarcest resource in ABA, and families wait for them. Alpaca Health recruits RBTs for the ABA clinics we work with. Most of our candidates today come from inbound applicants and direct outreach. Nobody has had time to build the channels that bring in new behavior technicians steadily. That is this role. You will build our campus and partnership recruiting from scratch. No program, playbook or event calendar exists yet. You decide which schools to target, make the first contact, and show up in person. Then you report honestly on what produced hires. ## **What you'll do** - Build and run campus recruiting at colleges and universities, focusing on psychology, education, speech/OT, social work and pre-health programs - Plan and staff job fairs and career events, on campus and in the community - Set up standing partnerships with career centers, faculty, student organizations and RBT training programs - Create internship, practicum and student-to-RBT pathways, including helping students without certification complete the 40-hour training and credentialing - Track which schools and events produce hires, at what cost, and decide where to spend next - Lead the offshore RBT recruiters day to day: set weekly targets, review their pipeline reports, coach them on outreach and follow-up, and keep their work consistent. You are the day-to-day manager, and you work alongside Strategy & Ops team on priorities and hiring targets ## **What we're looking for** **Must have** - Experience recruiting high-volume hourly or entry-level roles - Experience recruiting behavior technicians or RBTs, or in comparable high-volume healthcare, education or childcare hiring - Comfort cold-contacting career offices and building relationships with people who owe us nothing - Willingness to travel to campuses and events periodically, as-needed basis - Experience leading or coordinating recruiters, ideally a remote or offshore team, and clear, organized reporting on pipeline and cost per hire **Nice to have** - Existing relationships with ABA, psychology or special education programs - Experience building a campus or early-career program from zero - Familiarity with RBT certification requirements ## **What success looks like in your first 90 days** - A ranked target list of schools and programs, with reasons for the ranking - First-contact conversations opened with 10+ career centers or departments - At least 1 events or job fairs scheduled or attended - A first student-to-RBT pathway designed and ready to pilot with one partner - A simple tracker showing sources, candidates and hires, so we can decide where to invest

**About Nominal** Nominal is building the connected test and operations platform powering the world's most advanced hardware systems, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense programs. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software. We serve top-tier commercial and defense customers, from autonomy leaders like Anduril and Shield AI to next-generation aerospace teams like Hermeus and REGENT, and performance engineering teams like Pratt Miller Motorsports, alongside mission partners within the U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force on programs where failure isn’t an option. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. **The role** We’re looking for students with solid engineering fundamentals on track to graduate in Summer 2027 or sooner. As a Mission Ops Engineer, you'll be the person on the ground helping customers deploy Nominal's platform into their test and operations environments — propulsion test stands, satellite mission ops, flight test, and similar high-stakes settings. You'll train users, troubleshoot issues in real time, and build the relationships that turn a deployment into a long-term partnership. ### ### ### **🚀 What you’ll do** - Write code to ingest and normalize customer data from test stands, DAQs, telemetry streams, and other hardware sources - Build custom apps, dashboards, and workflows on Nominal's platform for each customer's specific needs - Own outcomes for a set of customer accounts: run discovery to understand their test problems, then deliver solutions that stick - Build trusted relationships with engineers and operators, and train their teams as they bring Nominal into daily use - Debug issues across the stack in real time, and know when to solve something yourself versus pull in the broader team - Turn patterns you see across customers into clear input for the product and engineering teams ### ### ### **🎯 Reach out if…** - You're graduating in Summer 2027 or sooner and are interested in a full-time position - You have hands-on experience with hardware systems — test stands, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or similar — through internships, personal projects, research, or coursework - You can write code (Python or similar) to work with real-world data, whether that's parsing sensor logs, building data pipelines, or automating analysis - You communicate clearly and can explain technical ideas to people who aren't engineers - You're comfortable working through open-ended problems in unfamiliar environments - You're willing to travel occasionally to be on-site with customers - You have a genuine interest in hardware testing and the industries Nominal serves ### **⚡ Bonus** - Experience with data acquisition or hardware tools (DAQs, LabVIEW, MATLAB/Simulink) or data tools (SQL, Python, Pandas, Grafana) - Prior customer-facing, account management, or technical support experience ### ### ### ✨ Benefits/Perks - 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance - Unlimited PTO and sick leave - Free lunch, snacks, and coffee - Professional Development Stipend - 401k Plan - In-office hardware lab with a $250 project stipend - Annual company retreat *All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.* ITAR Requirements *To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. role: CNC Machine Operator Trainee - Weekend Dayshift - Aerospace
location: 12716 East Pine Street, Tulsa, OK, USA
description: The CNC Machine Operator Trainee is an entry-level position designed to provide hands-on training in operating and maintaining CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machining centers. The trainee will work closely with experienced operators and supervisors to learn setup, operation, inspection, and basic troubleshooting of CNC machines This role is identified as requiring ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations) compliance; therefore, qualified candidates must meet the definition of a U.S. Person (per EAR Part 772 and ITAR 120.15): • An individual who is granted U.S. citizenship, or • An individual who is granted U.S. permanent residence (i.e., a "Green Card" holder), or • An individual who is granted status as a "protected person" Essential Functions To accomplish this job, an individual must be able to perform each essential function. Reasonable accommodations may be made to help enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions • Sets up and operates automated CNC Vertical and horizontal machines • Meets departmental/company goals and objectives promptly (i.e., efficiencies, scrap control, time motion, and setup time reductions • Accurately interprets product blueprints, drawings, sketches, setup sheets, and other work instructions • Uses calipers, micrometers, and height gauges to determine that the part is being machined to the proper specifications • Removes and replaces dull cutting tools, following designated safety protocol and instructions • Listens to machines during operation to detect irregular sounds (i.e., dull cutting tools or excessive vibration); adjusts machines to compensate for problems and notifies lead or supervisory personnel as appropriate • Stops machines to remove finished workpieces or to change tooling, setup, or workpiece placement according to required machining sequences • Lifts workpieces to machines manually or with hoists or cranes • Enters command instructions into the machine control units to start operation • Transfers commands from servers to computer numerical control (CNC) modules, using computer network links • Sets up future jobs, performs inspections or part checks, cleans the work area, or performs other duties while the machines are operating • May deburr machined parts as required for work in process • Follows all safety policies and procedures; consistently utilizes all required personal protective equipment (PPE) • Communicates verbally (English) and follows verbal and written instructions • Performs other tasks and/or assignments as required • Regular attendance on-site at the workplace is required Required Education and Work Experience • High School diploma or GED equivalent is required Other Skills and Abilities • Strong mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn required • Demonstrated basic math skills (add, subtract, multiply, divide, fraction conversions) required • Timely completion of assigned internal training is required • Experience using mics, calipers, height gauges, and other precision measuring equipment is preferred • Experience reading & accurately interpreting shop blueprints, sketches, and other technical information/instructions is preferred • Experience using cranes, forklifts, and similar heavy & oversized material handling equipment is preferred Training and Advancement • This position is part of a structured training program lasting approximately 90 days, typically conducted on day shift, Monday through Friday • Upon successful completion, the trainee will be assigned to a CNC Machine Operator Level I based on skills, performance, and company needs • Full-time assignments after training may be scheduled on day, night, or weekend shifts Physical Demands and Work Environment To perform the essential functions of the role, employees must be able to perform the following activities with or without reasonable accommodations: • Regularly stand and walk throughout the facility, stand for long periods to perform job duties • Regularly lift, carry (short distances), and push/pull up to 100 pounds using peer assistance and/or other lifting & material-handling equipment • Occasionally reaches overhead and reaches out or down to perform duties • Frequently climb steps, stairs, or ladders • Occasionally bend, crawl, stoop, squat, or kneel • Frequently uses hand or fingers to manually inspect parts, tighten hardware & fixtures, and operate machine and material handling controls • Accurately distinguish colors to respond to sensors, indicators, and color-variable dashboards • Visual acuity to interpret readings on gauges and other measuring devices Working Conditions Work is performed in a manufacturing shop environment where working conditions may vary significantly; the employee will be exposed to: • Excessive noise (hearing protection required) • Dust, smoke, mist, fumes/vapors (regularly) • Extreme temperatures (occasionally) • Hazardous equipment including forklifts, hand tools, cranes or other lifting devices, and other equipment used in a machine shop environment (continually) We appreciate your interest in Accurus Aerospace; however, only those applicants selected for interviews will be contacted.
