role: Utilities Plant Operator - Wastewater Utilities Plant Operator-Trainee (Various Locations)
description: Job Overview Utilities Plant Operator performs certified and skilled work or directs and oversees the performance of certified and skilled work in the operation of Advanced Water Reclamation, Potable Water supply, distribution systems, and solids management to provide high quality treatment of water and wastewater in compliance with Florida Administrative Codes and local rules and regulations. Hiring Range (annual) $37,752.00 *Internal rates may vary based on the selected candidate’s current grade. Ideal candidate has finished or is working towards the educational requirements to obtain a Class C Florida Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator’s License. The candidate would have some prior experience in a position with duties and responsibilities that would support skill sets that are complementary to the duties of a Utilities Plant Operator. The ideal candidate would also have good analytical and troubleshooting skills, with an ability to make sound and logical corrective actions. Some chemistry background would be advantageous. The candidate should be able to communicate effectively with others via written, oral, email, and other methods, as well as maintain detailed records and logs of duties and logistical data. Candidates should be able to safely and comfortably work with various industrial and laboratory chemicals. Candidates must be able and willing to respond to emergency situations to provide for public health and safety. Candidates will be required to work independently, rotating shifts, including nights, weekends and holidays as well as cover overtime as needed. Candidates should have computer skills with standard software such as Excel, Word, Outlook, etc. Incumbents hired at the “trainee” skill level will serve a minimum of one year probationary period. Benefits Click HERE to view our Benefits at a glance Generous PTO & Holiday Plan Health Plans Health Savings Account Dental & Vision Plans Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Healthcare Flexible Spending Account Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account Tuition Reimbursement Cafeteria Benefit Life Insurance Short & Long-Term Disability Insurance Core Competencies Customer Commitment - Proactively seeks to understand the needs of the customers and provide the highest standards of service. Dedication to Professionalism and Integrity - Demonstrates and promotes fair, honest, professional and ethical behaviors that establishes trust throughout the organization and with the public we serve. Organizational Excellence - Takes ownership for excellence through one's personal effectiveness and dedication to the continuous improvement of our operations. Success through Teamwork - Collaborates and builds partnerships through trust and the open exchange of diverse ideas and perspectives to achieve organizational goals. Job Distinctions This tier serves as a trainee level. Successful completion of the training program requires obtaining a Water or Wastewater Plant Operator “C” Certificate of License. Duties and Responsibilities Note: The following duties are illustrative and not exhaustive. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position. Depending on assigned area of responsibility, incumbents in the position may perform one or more of the activities described below: Responds to emergency situations such as floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, and other natural and/or unnatural crisis to provide for public health and safety. Prepares and maintains accurate, detailed operations reports and maintenance records. Collects, organizes and evaluates water/wastewater operational data, and develop logical conclusions for operational adjustments. Oversees and/or performs inspections of facility equipment and machinery to determine that all systems are operating properly. Oversees and/or performs routine and non-routine adjustments to controls in conformance with operating instructions, Florida Administrative Code, and prescribed standards. Notifies manager and/or other appropriate staff of needs for non-routine adjustments and/or malfunctioning of equipment. Performs and assists with plant maintenance work as required. Operates, calibrates, and maintains all department equipment, vehicles, and test equipment to ensure safe and efficient operations. Maintains current knowledge of Florida Administrative Code and regulatory requirements. Researches and responds to information requests in conformance with department procedures. Performs laboratory analysis on collected samples, interprets test results, and makes routine process changes following established guidelines. May function as a lead worker when working with new operators or trainees. Implements OSHA lock-out/tag-out procedures to safely isolate equipment and remove it from service. Responds to customer inquiries and complaints to include determination of water quality issues and resolution, provides requested information within established guidelines and capabilities or redirects call to appropriate person to ensure good customer relations. Accepts documentation from chemical delivery drivers, signs to verify amounts of delivered for payment, and submits the tickets to the facility supervisor or office assistant for payment. Uses appropriate personal protective equipment and follows material safety data sheets recommendations for handling toxic, corrosive, and flammable materials. May direct the work of other staff by scheduling, assigning and reviewing work, providing training and counseling to include assisting with the training of personnel in emergency response plans and safety programs in conformance with local, state, and federal regulations. May establish and implement operating protocols for one or more water/wastewater treatment facilities which includes reclaimed water systems according to local, state, and federal regulations to ensure permit compliance. Assists and advises operators at all levels in the resolution of difficult process problems. Works closely with environmental laboratory personnel to develop and implement sampling and testing procedures in compliance with local, state, and federal regulations. Coordinates with Reclaimed Water staff to ensure uninterrupted service to all reclaimed water customers. Performs related work as directed Job Specifications Knowledge of operating principles and practices applicable to advanced treatment facilities and distribution systems. Knowledge of written, oral, computer communication, and analytical skills are required. Knowledge of department procedure and guidelines. Knowledge of chemistry and biology related to the operation of water/wastewater treatment facilities. Knowledge of all regulations governing water/wastewater treatment and operator responsibility. Ability to perform assigned duties with considerable independence. Ability to work in a team environment. Ability to communicate effectively with others. Ability to prepare and maintain accurate, detailed operations, and maintenance records and reports. Ability to understand and interpret, utilize, and adjust automation/instrumentation devices and systems to meet facility operational requirements. Ability and willingness to respond to emergency situations such as floods, hurricanes, tornadoes and other natural and/or unnatural crises to provide for public health and safety. Ability and willingness to work overtime, rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Ability to use a computer and related software. Physical Requirements The work is performed in an environment where various types of chemicals are used Required to work in outside in all types of weather. Required to work in confined spaces while wearing a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA). Required to lift to 50 lbs. and climb up to 35 Feet. Work Category Medium Work - Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Minimum Qualifications Required Graduation from high school or possession of a GED Certificate; AND Possession of a valid Florida Driver's License. NOTE: Incumbents hired as “Trainees” will serve a one-year probationary period. They are required to complete all educational requirements to acquire a valid State of Florida Water or Wastewater Plant Operator "C" Certificate of License within one year of position assignment and obtain the license within eighteen (18) months. Upon completion of training, to include obtaining a valid State of Florida Water or Wastewater Plant Operator "C" Certificate of License, incumbents will be promoted to Plant Operator Tier 2. The training period may be extended by the Agency to which the position is assigned. Emergency Management Responsibilities In the event of an emergency or disaster, an employee may be required to respond promptly to duties and responsibilities as assigned by the employee’s department, the County’s Office of Emergency Management, or County Administration. Such assignments may be for before, during or after the emergency/disaster. Career Progression Employees in this broadband classification that acquire the competencies and minimum qualifications for the next tier will automatically advance to the new tier upon submission of appropriate documentation of qualifications. Additionally, employees in tier 1 trainee positions will be required to complete their initial probationary period successfully in order to advance to the next tier.

role: Software Development Engineer (Embedded Systems) Intern, Amazon Leo - Summer 2027 (USA)
description: Shape what comes next | Discover careers in Tech At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you. What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus. Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide? At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands. Our SDE interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years. At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As a SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers. We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth. ________________________ By applying to this position, your application will be considered for Summer 2027 internship roles. Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. Apprentices must successfully complete all required coursework and training, demonstrate application of classroom learning on the job, and maintain a minimum C grade average throughout the program. **What You’ll Learn and Do** Throughout the apprenticeship, you will progressively develop the skills needed to: - Safely operate manufacturing and production equipment. - Learn equipment start-up, shutdown, adjustment, and changeover procedures. - Develop structured troubleshooting and diagnostic skills to identify equipment and production issues. - Perform routine equipment adjustments and basic repairs as capabilities develop. - Conduct equipment inspections and identify potential mechanical or operational concerns. - Perform basic equipment maintenance, including cleaning, inspection, lubrication, and adjustment. - Support preventative maintenance, equipment overhauls, modifications, and installations. - Build an understanding of equipment reliability and how maintenance practices impact production performance. - Monitor equipment and production processes to support quality, productivity, and minimize downtime. - Apply problem-solving and root-cause thinking to equipment and production challenges. - Support continuous improvement efforts focused on safety, quality, reliability, effectiveness, and cost. - Perform sanitation activities and follow established sanitation standards. - Complete applicable quality checks, including GMP, HACCP, weights, and other plant-specific requirements. - Follow Kraft Heinz safety, environmental, food safety, and quality standards. - Identify and report situations that could impact employee safety, food safety, product quality, or equipment performance. - Apply concepts learned through classroom instruction to hands-on manufacturing assignments. - Complete required training, assessments, coursework, and program milestones. - Perform other duties and training assignments as needed. As technical capabilities develop, apprentices may be assigned increasing levels of responsibility and may perform work more independently. **What You’ll Build** Tech U is designed to develop foundational and practical technical capabilities in areas such as: - Mechanical and equipment fundamentals - Troubleshooting and diagnostics - Preventative and precision maintenance - Equipment inspection - Basic equipment repair - Equipment reliability - Production line start-ups and shutdowns - Equipment changeovers - Root-cause problem solving - Food safety and quality - Sanitation - Continuous improvement - Manufacturing safety Specific training may vary based on the Kraft Heinz location, production equipment, education partner, and operational needs. **Training Experience** Tech U combines classroom instruction with hands-on manufacturing experience. Apprentices will divide their training between the Kraft Heinz facility and the designated education partner. **Education Partner:** MTS Training will primarily occur on [Primary Shift]; however, schedule flexibility is required. Training may occur on alternate shifts to provide exposure to production line shutdowns, sanitation, start-ups, equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, and changeovers. Apprentices are expected to report to both Kraft Heinz and the designated education partner at the required times and locations. Applicable Kraft Heinz attendance, conduct, safety, and program expectations must be maintained throughout the apprenticeship. **Recipe for Success** Candidates must: - Be at least 18 years of age. - Have a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent. - Meet all academic prerequisites and enrollment requirements established by the designated education partner. - Successfully enroll in the required apprenticeship coursework. - Successfully complete applicable Kraft Heinz apprenticeship selection steps and assessments. - Demonstrate an interest in developing mechanical, technical, and manufacturing skills. - Demonstrate a willingness to learn, solve problems, and develop new technical capabilities. - Be willing and able to complete both classroom and hands-on training. - Maintain a minimum C grade average throughout the program. - Demonstrate reliable attendance and punctuality. - Be willing to work a flexible schedule based on training and operational requirements. - Follow all Kraft Heinz safety, food safety, quality, attendance, and workplace requirements. **Experience That Can Help You Succeed** Previous Line Tech experience is not required. Candidates with transferable skills or experience in the following areas are encouraged to apply: - Manufacturing or production - Mechanical or maintenance work - Automotive - Construction - Warehousing or distribution - Military technical occupations - Technical or vocational education - Skilled trades - Experience working with tools, machinery, or mechanical equipment Candidates who demonstrate mechanical aptitude, curiosity, problem-solving ability, and an interest in understanding how equipment works are encouraged to apply. **Physical and Work Environment Requirements** This position operates within a manufacturing environment. Specific requirements may vary by plant, department, and production area. Employees may be required to: - Lift and move materials weighing up to 50 pounds. - Stand and walk for extended periods. - Bend, reach, climb, push, pull, and perform other physical activities associated with manufacturing work. - Safely work around manufacturing equipment and machinery. - Use required tools and personal protective equipment. - Work in environments that may be hot, cold, wet, noisy, or temperature controlled. - Work overtime, weekends, alternate shifts, or other schedules based on training and production needs. Additional requirements may apply based on the participating Kraft Heinz location. **Selection Process** Candidates may be required to successfully complete multiple steps as part of the Tech U selection process, including: - Application and eligibility review - Talent Acquisition screening - Technical or mechanical aptitude assessment - Interview - Education partner prerequisite and enrollment requirements - Applicable pre-employment requirements Candidates must successfully complete applicable selection requirements to participate in the program. **Completing Tech U and Your Career Path** The goal of Tech U is to develop skilled technical talent with the knowledge and hands-on capabilities needed to support safe, reliable, and effective manufacturing operations. Successful completion of the 12-month apprenticeship requires participants to meet established academic, attendance, safety, performance, and technical competency expectations. By the end of the program, successful apprentices are expected to demonstrate increased technical proficiency and the ability to apply structured troubleshooting, diagnostics, maintenance, and problem-solving practices in a manufacturing environment. Upon successful completion, apprentices may be eligible to pursue available Line Tech or other applicable skilled technical opportunities based on position availability, plant needs, applicable posting or bidding processes, and collective bargaining requirements where applicable. Position, department, and shift availability following completion of the program will be based on business and operational needs. **Benefits** Kraft Heinz offers benefit programs designed to support employees and their eligible dependents. Eligibility and coverage are subject to applicable plans, governing documents, employment status, location, union status, and other applicable requirements. Programs may include: **Physical Wellbeing:** Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, and health screenings. **Social Wellbeing:** Paid time off, company holidays, leave programs, recognition, training, and development opportunities. **Emotional Wellbeing:** Employee Assistance Programs, wellbeing resources, and family support programs. **Financial Wellbeing:** Retirement savings programs, life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment coverage, and disability benefits. Specific benefits and eligibility will be communicated based on the participating Kraft Heinz location and employment classification. **Benefits:** Coverage for employees (and their eligible dependents) through affordable access to healthcare, protection, and saving for the future, we offer plans tailored to meet you and your family’s needs. Coverage for benefits will be in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and associated governing plan documents. **Wellbeing:** We offer events, resources, and learning opportunities that inspire a physical, social, emotional, and financial well-being lifestyle for our employees and their families. You’ll be able to participate in a variety of benefits and wellbeing programs that may vary by role, country, region, union status, and other employment status factors, for example: - Physical - Medical, Prescription Drug, Dental, Vision, Screenings/Assessments - Social - Paid Time Off, Company Holidays, Leave of Absence, Recognition, Training - Emotional – Employee Assistance Program , Wellbeing Programs, Family Support Programs - Financial – 401k, Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, Disability **Location(s)** Kendallville Plant **Kraft Heinz is an Equal Opportunity Employer that prohibits discrimination or harassment of any type. role: KIP Spring 2027 - North America Programs Intern - Foundation for Economic Education
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **About FEE** [The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)](https://fee.org/) is a leading nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the economic, ethical, and legal principles of a free society. For 80 years, FEE has been committed to inspiring and educating individuals on the values of personal freedom, entrepreneurship, and sound economic thinking. Through various programs, publications, and events, FEE empowers individuals to understand the economic principles that drive prosperity and fosters a society rooted in individual rights and limited government. **About FEE’s Student Engagement Team** FEE’s Student Engagement team inspires and awakens students by delivering the world-class learning experiences at the heart of FEE’s mission, introducing high school and college students to the ideas of a free society through in-person programs, webinars, and campus-based programs. The Student Engagement team runs single- and multi-day programs across North America and Latin America. Its summer campus programs bring students together for several days of learning about economics, entrepreneurship, and personal freedom. Behind every program is a detailed operational effort: venues and vendors, speakers and faculty, travel, materials, participant recruitment, and day-of execution. The team takes pride in getting those details correct so that every participant leaves with a world-class experience that inspires & awakens. **About This Internship** The North America Programs Intern will support FEE’s Senior Associate, North America Programs and the broader Programs team, with a primary focus on the logistics and operations behind FEE’s programming in the Washington, DC office. This is an opportunity for a highly organized, detail-oriented student or recent graduate to gain hands-on experience in event logistics, participant communication, and program operations within a mission-driven organization. In addition to supporting DC programming, the intern will contribute to key work evolving FEE’s summer campus programming, helping research, plan, and document improvements to how these programs are recruited for, organized, and delivered. The Investment Planning Intern will focus on developing a comprehensive financial model tailored to renewable energy projects. You will create a model capable of running various sensitivity analyses to assess project viability under different scenarios and generate detailed financial statements. Additionally, you will gain hands-on experience with the financial structuring and analysis required for utility-scale solar projects. \*Paid 12-week internship opportunity starting in May/June 2027. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** - Design and build detailed financial models that incorporate project-specific data and will forecast cash flows, internal rates of return (IRR), and net present values (NPV) to evaluate the financial feasibility of solar and storage projects. - Conduct sensitivity analyses within the financial models, testing different variables like energy prices, financing terms, tax incentives, and operational efficiencies. - Support the generation of key financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements. - Assist in evaluating various financing options for solar projects, including debt and equity structures, tax equity financing, and other renewable energy-specific financial mechanisms. - Collaborate with senior finance professionals during the due diligence process for project financing by compiling and analyzing financial documentation, researching market conditions, and ensuring financial assumptions align with current industry benchmarks. - Collaborate with individual department, as well as cross-functionally with other departments within the organization. - Maintain organizational excellence in terms of project timelines and deliverables. - Demonstrates the Clēnera Core Values of Caring, Committed, and Courageous. - Other duties as assigned. **MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS** - Education: Undergraduate or graduate student, preferably entering their final year, pursuing a degree in finance, economics, or accounting. - Technology: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, and an ability to learn company-specific software programs, tools, processes, and machines. - Skills/Attributes: - Intermediate Excel skills like formulas and functions (i.e. Sum, Lookup, If, IRR, NPV) including the ability to apply across complex modeling. - Ability to take complex financial information and effectively develop PowerPoint decks for internal and external stakeholders. - Understanding and interpretation of time value of money and financial statements. - Ability to adapt quickly to changing factors and bring solutions. - Critical thinking and analytical mindset. - Self-motivated to work through complex problems and competing priorities, including a high level of detail and organization. - ## **About us** At Roadrunner, we’re replacing the broken CPQ software that Sales teams have complained about, worked around, and given up on for years. Not improving it - replacing it. We’re building a new agentic stack called PQA - Prompt, Quote, Approve, designed for the enterprise, on a data model built for how pricing actually works today. We’re Kleiner Perkins’ first incubation since Glean, led by second-time founders with successful exits, and a team of engineers from Snowflake, Databricks, Citadel, Meta, Robinhood, Brex, and so on. We’re in-person in San Francisco, and we’re just getting started. ## **What you'll do** - **Embed with our customers.** You'll sit with the RevOps and Sales leaders who live inside Roadrunner every day, turn their hardest pricing and approval problems into shipped features, and stay on the hook until they're actually solved - not just handed off to support. - **Own delivery end-to-end, in production.** From technical discovery through go-live, you're the engineer who scopes it, builds it, and keeps it running. - **Turn one-off solutions into product.** Every customer-specific integration or workflow you build feeds back into Roadrunner's core platform. The pattern you build for customer #1 is the feature customer #10 gets out of the box. - **Ship AI agents in the field.** Deploy and tune proactive agents - quoting recommendations, deal modeling, multi-step approval workflows - against real customer data and real deal pressure, then iterate on what actually breaks. - **Be the fastest feedback loop in the company.** You're often the first to see where the product breaks under real enterprise complexity. You carry that back to the core team the same day, not next sprint. ## **What you'll bring** - **Strong engineering fundamentals** - from coursework, internships, or projects. You don't need a track record of shipping to production yet; you need to be able to build fast without cutting the corners that matter. - **Real curiosity.** You want to know why something broke, not just that it broke - and you'll dig through an unfamiliar codebase or a customer's system until you find the actual answer. - **Ambition.** You want real ownership fast, not a backlog of tickets, and you're ready to earn it. - **Comfort with ambiguity** - from a hackathon, a research project, or an internship where nobody handed you a spec. - **Clear, direct communication** - with engineers and with the non-technical people you'll be sitting across from. - **Willingness to travel occasionally** to be onsite with customers when it matters. - **Based in SF or excited to relocate** - we're an in-person team. ## **Bonus points if…** - You've interned somewhere and shipped code that real users touched. - You've built something on your own - an app, a tool, a research project - because you wanted it to exist, not because a class required it. - You've spent time close to customers or end users, even outside of engineering (support, tutoring, ops), and know what it's like to translate someone's problem into something you build. - You've picked up a new language, framework, or domain fast because a project needed it. - You have a side project. Tell us what it is and why you built it. ## **What we offer** - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family. - Lunch and dinner, as well as snacks and coffee to keep you energized. - Take what you need vacation policy. ## **Equal opportunity** We value our differences, and we encourage all to apply — especially those whose identities are traditionally underrepresented in tech organizations. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected by law. Roadrunner is an equal opportunity employer.

Strong performance creates a pathway to a return offer for a Summer or Fall 2027 internship and full-time consideration upon graduation, based on business needs. You'll work directly with our Manager, Value Engineering, and the broader GTM org. This includes Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and senior leadership — on live enterprise deals. ## **About the Team** The Value Engineering team exists to close two critical gaps: leadership isn't always in touch with the factory floor, and new technology doesn't always translate into operational impact. We bridge both by quantifying Relay's value proposition, building investment-grade business cases, and acting as a forcing function for customer ROI. Our work shapes the enterprise sales motion, customer relationships, product roadmap, and company strategy. ## **Responsibilities** - Support the development of executive-level business cases that translate frontline operational data into P&L-level ROI. - Map prospect workflows and analyze operational metrics to identify Relay's highest-impact use cases. - Build financial models that quantify the value Relay delivers across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, and healthcare. - Partner with AEs and CSMs on pilot strategies and account planning for key enterprise opportunities. - Conduct research on industry operations and competitive benchmarks to strengthen Relay's value narratives. - Assist in developing internal tools, ROI frameworks, and proofs-of-concept that scale across the sales org. - Synthesize customer and field insights to support product roadmap and pricing strategy conversations. - Contribute to the company's wildly well-attended intern showcase — presenting your work to Relay's full team at summer's end. ## **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field. - Expected graduation between December 2027 and May 2029. - Minimum GPA of 3.7 - No employer work authorization sponsorship available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship, now or in the future. - Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building models and working with data. - Excellent written and verbal communication — ability to synthesize complexity into a clear, executive-ready narrative. - Available to work onsite at Relay's Raleigh HQ (near the Lenovo Center) for both the Spring engagement and the full-time Summer program. ## **Preferred Qualifications** - Coursework or project experience in operations research, systems engineering, supply chain, or financial analysis. - Exposure to manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, or hospitality environments through coursework, co-op, or personal experience. - Familiarity with data analysis tools (Excel, Python, SQL) and/or data visualization. - A genuine curiosity about how physical-world businesses operate and where technology creates real impact. ## **What success and impact look like in this role** By the end of the Spring engagement, you've shipped at least one analysis or framework that's been used in a live enterprise deal. By mid-summer, you're running financial models and contributing to business cases with real ownership — not just support. By the final showcase, you've presented work that a senior leader would put in front of a Fortune 500 prospect. Top performers earn a return Summer or Fall 2027 internship offer and are on the radar for full-time consideration upon graduation. ## **What Makes This Internship Different** - **Executive exposure:** Regular touchpoints with Relay's senior leadership team, including Q&A sessions, Breakfast with the CEO, and working sessions. - **Real ownership:** You'll own a project from kickoff to final presentation — not a shadow assignment. - **Cross-functional cohort:** Work alongside interns from across the business, not just your team. - **Structured learning:** Skill-building sessions covering financial modeling, operations strategy, sales craft, and professional development. - **Intern showcase:** Present your work to the full company at the end of the summer. - **Raleigh HQ experience:** Team lunches, volunteer Intern Impact Day, social events, and a front-row seat to how a scaling tech company operates. - **Pathway that matters:** This isn't a résumé builder for its own sake. Strong performers get return offers and full-time pipeline consideration. ## **Why Join Relay?** Our culture hinges on Relayers getting LIT up in an environment that fosters Learning, Impact, and Teamwork, where we CHASE the best work of our lives. BWIML - Best Work In My Life. **The future of frontline work is being built here. Come build it with us. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Economics Olympiad Intern - Foundation for Economic Education
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **About FEE** [The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)](https://fee.org/) is a leading nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the economic, ethical, and legal principles of a free society. For 80 years, FEE has been committed to inspiring and educating individuals on the values of personal freedom, entrepreneurship, and sound economic thinking. Through various programs, publications, and events, FEE empowers individuals to understand the economic principles that drive prosperity and fosters a society rooted in individual rights and limited government. **About FEE’s Student Engagement Team** The Student Engagement department leads FEE's student-facing events. Through a mix of in-person and virtual programs, FEE partners with schools, educators, and organizations to introduce students to the principles of a free society, fostering deeper understanding and thoughtful discussions. From outreach and relationship-building to event logistics and execution, the Student Engagement team works to create engaging, high-impact experiences that challenge and inspire the next generation. Domestically, FEE's programs have reached students in nearly all 50 states. Internationally, FEE has a growing footprint in Latin America. **About This Internship** This role will assist with FEE’s new initiative, the Economics Olympiad (EO). EO is FEE's international student competition, running students through a School Round and a National Round on their way to an International Final Round. In Canada and the USA, the program is scaling to reach students at schools across both countries during the School Round, before bringing top performers together for an in-person National Round in Washington, DC. Behind the scenes, a small team of staff and partners keeps teachers, students, and parents informed and supported at every stage, helping turn the National Round into a well-run, memorable event. The Economics Olympiad Intern will be the front line of that experience — helping students, teachers, and parents get clear, timely answers as they move through the School and National Rounds, while also supporting the planning of the National Round event in DC. This is an opportunity for the ideal candidate to combine a love for the ideas of a free society with a passion for clear communication and flawless event execution. ### Responsibilities: - Draft, send, and track communications to registered teachers and students throughout registration, testing, and the National Round — reminders, deadlines, logistics updates, and FAQs. - Monitor inboxes and shared communication channels to ensure inquiries are answered promptly and accurately. - Support planning and execution of the National Round in Washington, DC, including venue coordination, vendor and catering logistics, AV needs, schedules, and day-of logistics packets. - Help maintain registration and communication records (e.g., in Salesforce) so participant status and outreach history stay accurate and up to date. - Assist with creating participant-facing materials such as logistics packets, FAQs, itineraries, and confirmation emails. - Work closely with your intern supervisor on new projects, ideas, and initiatives related to the Economic Olympiad. - Track and report relevant KPIs (e.g., response times, registration follow-through, inquiry volume). ### Skills: - Business, Economics, Project Management or other related majors desired, but not required. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills and strong customer service skills. - Ability juggling multiple priorities while keeping everything on track and maintaining careful attention to detail. - The ability to work independently and take initiative with minimal supervision. - A proactive, entrepreneurial spirit to improve existing programs. - A collaborative personality; unafraid of challenge. - An unwavering commitment to the mission and principles of FEE.

description: **Our Vision**: To make New York City the global model for inclusive innovation and economic growth, fueled by the City’s diverse people and businesses. **Our Mission**: Creating a vibrant, inclusive, and globally competitive economy for all New Yorkers. **The Asset Management Property Operations Department** is responsible for protecting and enhancing the value of City-owned real estate assets and supporting the operational needs of tenant businesses. This position will work closely with NYCEDC Asset Management leadership, on-site field staff, tenants, contractors, and other internal and external stakeholders to ensure that the campus is safe, well-maintained, operationally effective, and responsive to tenant and property needs. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Policy/Research Intern - Competitive Enterprise Institute
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **About Competitive Enterprise Institute:** The [Competitive Enterprise Institute](https://cei.org/) is a nonprofit think tank based in Washington which focuses on critical economic and regulatory policy issues. CEI’s [internship program](https://cei.org/about/internships/) provides interested students and recent graduates the opportunity to learn about and promote the principles of limited government, free enterprise, and individual liberty. A CEI internship gives applicants the opportunity to work alongside some of the most prominent regulatory affairs scholars and policy specialists. CEI offers a number of internships across the various [policy areas](https://cei.org/issue-areas/) we work on, as well as internships in communications and marketing. Generally, CEI’s policy interns are assigned to work with a specific CEI expert for the duration of their internship; and our communications and marketing interns work with the CEI staff of each respective team. CEI’s internship program is an invaluable educational experience. We work with interns to help them grow professionally, hone their skills, and cultivate lasting relationships. Ultimately, our goal is to give interns work that will help them further their careers. Interns are encouraged to be proactive, and exceptional interns are often given the freedom to shape their experience with us and the possibility to explore other opportunities at CEI. Past CEI interns have gone on to work in the executive and legislative branches, federal regulatory agencies, academia, and at prominent research institutions and think tanks. A number of current CEI staff are former CEI interns. You can find out more about CEI [here](https://cei.org/about/) and learn about our history [here](https://cei.org/about/history/). You can see our team of experts here and see some of our work [here](https://cei.org/news-room/) and [here](https://cei.org/publications/). ***Policy/Research Intern:*** Policy/Research Interns are assigned to work with one or more CEI policy experts for the duration of their internship. Interns have the opportunity to research important policy issues which include, but are not limited to; regulatory reform, banking and finance, energy and environment, technology and telecommunications, antitrust, trade, labor, transportation, healthcare, and asset forfeiture. **Qualifications:** Applicants must have a strong interest in policy and politics, capitalism and economics, and libertarian/conservative principles. Applicants must have strong research, writing, and organizational skills. Applicants must possess a professional demeanor and the ability to handle confidential and private information. Applicants should be able to work independently, effectively, and efficiently. A basic understanding of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook is a must. CEI also seeks interns to work on communications, marketing - and from time to time, philanthropy/fundraising, government affairs, events, litigation, and IT. During the interview, we would be more than happy to discuss these other opportunities if they are available and of interest to you! **This role is in person, in Washington, D.C.**

role: Member of Technical Staff Intern - US
description: ## **DRYFT** Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for. Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world. We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads. What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century. Dryft is building the intelligence layer that will power the next. ​ ## **THE ROLE** As a **Member of Technical Staff Intern**, you'll build the system that decides how some of the largest manufacturers in the world operate. That means combining agent-based reasoning with mathematical optimization and simulation on large-scale industrial data. - **Build agents people trust** – when an agent runs a factory's week, the largest industrial companies in the world have to trust it with their critical processes and understand every decision it makes; you build the routing, orchestration and guardrails behind that - **Ship features end-to-end** – you understand the user need, and you get the freedom to build it across the LLM pipeline, infrastructure, backend and frontend, in production in your first weeks - **Work close to the users** – sit with the planners who use it, see what would make their work 10x faster, and build it You'll own your own features from day one, and what you ship decides what a plant does next week. ​ ## **YOU** - **Full-stack shipper** – you've shipped production code end-to-end, you build scalable backend and infra that handles massive amounts of structured and unstructured data, and you build the interface that makes it usable - **Highly technical** – you've built something technically hard, and you can walk us through every decision behind it - **Product sense** – you spot the feature hiding in a user's complaint, and you've deleted your own favorite one because nobody used it - **You care about getting it right** – you know when it has to be 100% and when to keep it simple, and when it matters, you're still chasing the root cause at 2am - **Sense of urgency** – you'd rather ship it tonight than sleep on an open PR - **Relocation** – you're ready to work onsite in San Francisco (we support visa) ​ ## **TECH STACK** - **FE (TypeScript):** React, Chakra UI v3, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, Vite - **BE (Python):** FastAPI with Pydantic v2, Temporal, Postgres with pgvector, dagster - **AI:** Pydantic AI, Langfuse

description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **Organization Overview** [The Foundation Against Intolerance & Racism (FAIR)](https://www.fairforall.org/) is a nonpartisan, 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2021 to advance civil rights and liberties for all people. Rooted in the classical civil rights tradition and the principle that individuals should be treated without regard to race, gender, or other group identity, FAIR works to counter the spread of identity-based ideology across American institutions and to promote a common culture built on fairness, understanding, and humanity. FAIR pursues this mission through a dual strategy: identifying & supporting precedent-setting litigation that ensures diversity and inclusion efforts remain non-discriminatory, and grassroots, cultural, medical and educational programming that shifts hearts and minds at the community level. FAIR's network includes more than 50 chapters across the United States and Canada, along with professional networks of educators, clinicians, artists, and legal advocates. **Program Areas** FAIR in Medicine: A nonpartisan professional network dedicated to advancing the highest ethical standards in medical practice. FAIR in Medicine raises awareness of unethical and politicized practices in healthcare, promotes scientific debate and inquiry free from ideological pressure, and builds a common medical culture grounded in critical thinking and evidence-based care. FAIR in the Arts: A professional network championing freedom of expression and excellence in arts, entertainment, and media. FAIR in the Arts provides grants and funding for artists, curates events and mentorship opportunities, and builds a network of advisors, institutions, and enterprises that support artists facing intolerance for their work or viewpoints. FAIR in Education: FAIR in Education equips teachers, administrators, and school communities with pro-human learning resources and support to build healthy school environments. Its flagship offering is the Many Stories, One Nation (MSON) curriculum an academically rigorous alternative to "liberated" ethnic studies models that gives students a comprehensive view of the contributions of all Americans, paired with the FAIR Pro-Human Learning Standards, literature guides, and the Educators Alliance professional community. FAIR Legal Network: The FAIR Legal Network identifies and publicizes precedent-setting litigation on behalf of individuals denied equal protection, advises schools and employers on bringing policies into compliance with civil rights law, and equips FAIR members with the tools to challenge discriminatory practices in their own communities. Chapter Network & Communications: FAIR's grassroots Chapter Network spans more than 50 chapters that host discussions, outreach events, and educational campaigns locally. This work is supported by FAIR's communications, social media, and Substack newsletter operations, which extend FAIR's programs and message to a national audience. **About the Role** FAIR for All is seeking motivated, mission-aligned interns to support its programs in 2027. This general internship placement allows students to gain hands-on experience across one or more of FAIR's core program areas: Medicine, the Arts, Education, and Legal as well as organizational operations, working in close coordination with the CFO/COO. Specific project assignments will be tailored to the intern's interests, skills, and department needs. Key Responsibilities • Support day-to-day administrative and project needs of assigned FAIR program area(s) • Conduct research on relevant policy, cultural, legal, or educational developments • Assist with drafting internal memos, briefing documents, and correspondence • Help prepare materials for events, webinars, and chapter or member communications • Participate in team meetings and contribute ideas for program improvement • Complete special projects as assigned by the CFO/COO Qualifications • Strong written and verbal communication skills • Interest in civil liberties, education, healthcare, the arts, or nonprofit operations • Detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple tasks • Alignment with FAIR's mission of viewpoint diversity and nonpartisan civil rights advocacy • Proficiency with Google Workspace; additional skills a plus What You'll Gain • Direct exposure to nonprofit operations and leadership decision-making • Mentorship from the CFO/COO, program directors and Chapter Leaders • Networking opportunities across FAIR's national professional communities

description: ## Hillel International ## Role Overview Hillel International is seeking a dynamic marketing and fundraising professional to serve as a project-based Campus Marketing and Development Manager. This is an exciting opportunity to join an in-house consulting agency that provides expert digital and direct fundraising and marketing services to about 60 Hillel campus clients nationwide. This temporary position on our growing team will let you make an immediate impact on the lives of thousands of Jewish college students over a 6-month contract. The Campus Marketing and Development Manager will support the grassroots fundraising and marketing efforts of a portfolio of campus Hillels. Top candidates will have a strong background in digital marketing and/or fundraising, with an emphasis on excellent writing, strong graphic design skills, and developing impactful campaigns using data-driven strategies to achieve positive results. We welcome applications from candidates across the U.S., with fully remote options and hybrid options available in Washington, D.C., and New York City. ## What You’ll Do - Create, write, design, and distribute digital and direct response fundraising campaigns across platforms (email, direct mail, texting, social media, and web). - Develop annual fundraising and marketing campaign calendars incorporating stewardship touchpoints, appeals, renewal messaging, and email newsletters. - Optimize campaigns at an advanced level using data-driven strategies, including A/B testing, personalization, audience targeting, and nonprofit industry trends. - Provide in-depth analysis of campaign performance to meet or exceed goals, use CRMs for audience segmentation, and provide web support related to fundraising. - Lead audience acquisition efforts (parents, alumni, donors) and lead key initiatives such as Giving Days and text campaigns. - Serve as a strategic partner to campus staff to ensure brand cohesion, powerful storytelling, and top-notch client service. - Successfully manage multiple timelines and concurrent projects across campus clients. ## What You’ll Bring to the Job - 3–5 years of experience in marketing, digital advertising, and/or fundraising within the non-profit space (deep understanding of Hillel is a plus). - Proven success planning and executing digital and multichannel campaigns. - Excellent written communication skills for crafting compelling fundraising messaging, paired with exceptional graphic design skills (Canva, Adobe Suite, etc.). - Mastery of data analysis and audience segmentation, along with experience using CRMs/databases and email marketing platforms (MailChimp, Constant Contact, etc.). - Superior organizational skills, acute attention to detail, and a client-service mindset to manage multiple stakeholders effectively. - Passion for entrepreneurship, innovation, and Jewish life ## What You’ll Receive - Competitive salary in the nonprofit marketplace. The salary range for this position is $60,000-$65,000 per year, prorated for the 6-month period of employment. - Anticipated contract period: December 2026-June 2027 - Temporary employees are eligible to enroll in our Tax Deferred 403(b) Retirement Plan and are eligible for our benefits program - Professional development, mentoring, and skill-building opportunities. #LI-REMOTE #LI-REMOTE ## **About Hillel International** In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. **Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.**

Role Summary At Overland AI, we believe the hardest problems demand exceptional teams. We're excited to offer software engineering internship opportunities for the Summer of 2027. As an intern, you will tackle real, open-ended problems that directly contribute to our mission of building autonomous systems for the most challenging environments. Working closely with a mentor and our engineering team, you will apply your knowledge and grow your skills through high-impact projects. You must be ready to stay focused, move fast, self-direct, and learn on the fly. Software internships are available across the company within different teams such as Mission Autonomy, Perception & Machine Learning, Platforms, Behaviors and Planning, C2 and Interfaces. Please note: these roles require you to work onsite at our Seattle location. Minimum Qualifications Pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, or a similar STEM field Project-level experience with Python, C++, or Rust Exceptional command of engineering fundamentals Hands-on engineering experience through internships, personal projects, work, or teams Ability to manage a complex technical project and take it through execution Ability to learn and apply state-of-the-art techniques to technical projects Excellent written and verbal communication Able to work full-time, onsite for a minimum of 10–14 consecutive weeks Various Teams: Mission Autonomy - Builds the core autonomous mission execution capabilities that enable ground vehicles to independently navigate, adapt, and complete objectives in complex off-road environments without direct operator control. Perception/ML - Develops the machine learning models and sensor processing pipelines that allow vehicles to understand and interpret terrain, obstacles, and their surroundings in real time. Platforms - Owns the foundational software infrastructure, developer tooling, and systems that power the OverDrive autonomy stack and enable other engineering teams to build and deploy reliably. Behaviors and Planning - Designs the decision-making and path planning algorithms that determine how vehicles navigate terrain, react to dynamic conditions, and execute tactical maneuvers. C2 and Interfaces - Creates the intuitive OverWatch command-and-control interface that gives operators and commanders real-time situational awareness and precise coordination of autonomous vehicles. Internship Term Windows Spring (January – April) Application Window: May – July Summer (May – August) Application Window: September – November Fall (September – December) Application Window: January – March Benefits & Compensation Direct ownership and impact Mentorship from industry-leading engineers Complimentary snacks & refreshments available on-site Company events with Leadership team Pay Range(s) Freshman/Sophomore: $28.00/hour Junior/Senior: $33.00/hour Completed Bachelor's: $35.00/hour Completed Master's: $40.00/hour Your pay will be determined by academic level. You may also be eligible for relocation support. Overland AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, protected veteran or military status, or any other status protected by applicable law. This position may involve access to export-controlled technology. Employment is contingent on the ability to comply with U.S. export control laws. Overland AI provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans during the application process. Please contact to request an accommodation. About Overland AI Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, Overland AI is transforming land operations for modern defense. The company leverages over a decade of advanced research in robotics and machine learning, as well as a field-test forward ethos, to deliver combined capabilities for unit commanders. Our OverDrive autonomy stack enables ground vehicles to navigate and operate off-road in any terrain without GPS or direct operator control. Our intuitive OverWatch C2 interface provides commanders with precise coordination capabilities essential for mission success. Overland AI has secured funding from prominent defense tech investors including 8VC and Point 72, and built trusted partnerships with DARPA, the U.S. Army, Marine Corps, and Special Operations Command. Backed by eight-figure contracts across the Department of Defense, we are strengthening national security by iterating closely with end users engaged in tactical operations.

**Controls Engineer Intern** **- Position Description –** **Position Overview:** The Controls Engineering Intern learns and applies foundational automation skills while supporting internal and customer projects under close supervision. The intern works closely with other interns and the Controls team to complete tasks in PLC/HMI/robotics, documentation, and basic commissioning while building good engineering habits in safety, standards, and communication. **Rotational Development Path:** - Rotation 1 – Foundations: Gain familiarity with electrical schematics, PLC coding basics, HMI structure, standards, and documentation. Contribute to Axis internal projects and update documentation for existing customer programs. - Rotation 2 – Expansion: Tackle more advanced internal projects; begin supporting customer projects (electrical design tasks and code edits). Intro to robot programming and simulation. - Rotation 3 – Application: Provide hands-on support to customer projects: schematics updates, programming, commissioning, debug, and runoffs with supervision. **Key Responsibilities:** - Completes structured training/checklists; seeks feedback; applies lessons on subsequent tasks. - Performs small, scoped PLC ladder edits, basic structured-text tweaks, HMI tag routing and simple screens within established architecture and standards. - Reads and updates prints with redlines; maintains I/O lists, tag maps, device tagging, and device databases under review. - Assists I/O checkout, device bring-up, and online debug; follows test procedures; supports FAT/SAT with supervision. - Runs provided simulations; adjusts simple parameters; safely jogs/teaches points with guidance. - Keeps backups, change logs, and manuals current; practices disciplined version control. - Works constructively with Mechanical, Electrical, Build, and PM; communicates status/risks early. - Gathers accurate technical details and relays them to the project lead. - Follows LOTO/site rules; maintains organized benches, panels, and work areas. - Learns and practices our Operating Principles daily; asks for feedback; shows timeliness, accountability, and safe execution on small tasks. **Qualifications:** - **Education:** Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a university program in Electrical/Controls/Mechatronics (or related field). - **Technical Skills:** - PLC/HMI: Basic ladder logic, simple ST edits, tag creation and implementation, simple screens/alarms. - Robotics: Safe jogging, point teaching, basic tool/frame setup. - Electrical Basics: Reads schematics/wire lists; verifies wiring against prints. - Networks & Devices: Basic device/IP setup and commissioning. - Documentation/Tools: Uses templates, checklists, and version control per team process. - **Communication:** Clear, timely communicator with project teams and other interns; asks clarifying questions early; provides crisp status and thorough hand-offs. - **Problem-Solving:** Demonstrates critical thinking and a structured troubleshoot-verify-document approach; knows when to escalate with clear context. - **Teamwork:** Collaborative, coachable, and respectful; supports peers during busy phases and shares what they learn. - **Reliability:** Punctual, meets commitments, follows procedures/standards, and keeps documentation current. - **Travel:** Occasional supervised visits to customer sites or supplier facilities as assigned

The Role The Guest Experience Specialist will create an exceptional first impression for every guest who walks through our doors. This role embodies the warmth, hospitality, and storytelling that define the Frank & Eileen brand by welcoming customers and ensuring every customer feels seen. The ideal candidate will create a warm environment and seamlessly connect customers with the right member of our team. This is a seasonal position with full time hours. Responsibilities Warmly greet customers upon entry, creating an inviting and approachable atmosphere. Share Frank & Eileen’s story, from our Irish heritage to welcoming customers to our flagship NYC store, helping connect emotionally with the brand. Assess customer needs quickly and direct them to the appropriate stylist or sales associate for personalized service. Support an organized and smooth experience during high-traffic periods by maintaining awareness of store flow and wait times. Collaborate with the sales and support teams to ensure every customer receives attentive service, including offering services and following up with clients as needed. Maintain an upbeat, professional presence that reflects Frank & Eileen’s values of kindness, craftsmanship, and community. Genuine enthusiasm for people and creating memorable experiences. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Comfort with storytelling and brand education. Ability to remain poised and upbeat in a fast-paced, high-traffic environment. Availability on weekends, holidays, and key store events. Compensation Hourly Rate from $20-$24 This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the contractor. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice. The Company Founded in 2009 by Audrey McLoghlin, Frank & Eileen set out to reinvent the women's button-up using the finest Italian fabrics often reserved for menswear. Named in honor of Audrey's beloved Irish grandparents, the brand has grown slowly and intentionally into a woman-owned, woman-led leader in sustainability and slow fashion. After seventeen years of steady growth through wholesale partnerships and direct-to-consumer e-commerce, Frank & Eileen recently opened its first US flagship store—an Irish country house on Madison Avenue, NYC. This new chapter continues the brand's legacy of using entrepreneurship as a force for good while delivering generationless style to its beloved community of customers—all from our HQ in sunny California.

| | | --- | | **About Mammoth Brands** Mammoth Brands (formerly Harry’s Inc.) is the modern CPG company behind brands Harry’s, Flamingo, Lume, Mando, and Coterie. We’re building a new model—and home—brands, founders, and talent looking to solve unmet needs, improve peoples’ lives, and ultimately challenge the status quo. Our mission is to “Create Things People Like More.” Simply put: everything we do should be better than what already exists. If it’s not, we don’t do it. This guides everything we do, from developing the best product experiences, to making Mammoth Brands a great place to work, to exploring innovative ways to give back to our community. We got our start in 2013 when our co-founders created Harry's. They built the brand differently—online first, prioritizing direct relationships with customers—and in the process learned they’d created something bigger: a playbook and platform that could help other brands grow and scale to their full potential, and a vision to reimagine consumer packaged goods. Today, Mammoth Brands is a growing portfolio of brands and the largest CPG company built in the last 20 years. Even as we grow, we take extra care to maintain the small, scrappy, entrepreneurial culture that helped to get us where we are today: to create a company that people like more, that better serves its customers, employees, and community. As a company, we’re also committed to making a positive impact and have donated over $20 million through our network of nonprofit partners to date. We build brands that move fast and think big — and we hire people who are curious about AI, willing to experiment with it in their day-to-day work, and excited to accelerate what's possible. We prioritize giving our team the tools, training, and space to build real fluency, so you grow alongside the technology and help shape how we use it. | ## About the Role We're looking for a hungry, curious Junior Creative Strategist to work as a close partner to our Head of Creative/Growth Director. This role exists to multiply great creative thinking — owning the full creative planning cycle from performance analysis through to brief. You'll run monthly brainstorming and planning sessions, translate insights into structured plans with clear territory and style splits, and build high-level briefs that editors and production can move against with confidence. You'll lead monthly Creative Insight Analytics sessions, help pilot AI creative tools, and serve as the creative anchor the team comes to for direction. You'll also be a connector: between creative and performance, between strategy and execution, and between our growth team and the social commerce and TikTok ecosystem teams we work closely with. ## ## What You'll Do - Own the full monthly creative planning cycle — run brainstorming and planning sessions, bring the data, drive the ideas, and leave with a plan the team can execute against. - Translate performance insights into a structured monthly plan with clear territory and style splits. - Build high-level briefs for editors and production — clear enough that the team can move with confidence and without hand-holding. - Lead monthly Creative Insight Analytics sessions: what worked, what didn't, and what to chase next. Partner closely with the growth and creative leadership teams on this. - Act as a strong cross-functional partner to our social commerce and TikTok teams — syncing on creative needs, feeding insights upstream, and helping ensure creative output is built for the right platforms and moments. - Study competitor creative, read customer reviews and comments, and stay in the communities we're trying to reach. Every brief should start from a genuine customer insight, not just a creative instinct. - Pick up new tools quickly — AI creative platforms, performance analytics, scripting tools — and build light workflows that speed up concepting and briefing. - Support Trybe with creative briefs and strategic direction. ## ## Who You Are - Genuinely creative, with taste, opinions, and ideas you can defend. You think in hooks, territories, and angles — not just executions. - A natural cross-functional partner. You communicate clearly, keep people informed, and know how to work across teams with different priorities and rhythms. - Obsessed with the customer. You think about who you're talking to before you think about what you want to say. - A "whatever it takes" operator who doesn't wait to be told what to do and finds a way to get things done. - Fast. You move quickly without sacrificing quality, and you know the difference. - Energized by AI and new tools. Not intimidated by new platforms — excited to figure them out. - Comfortable with ambiguity. You can start from a rough idea, a data pattern, or a half-formed brief and run with it. - A clear, clean communicator. Your briefs are easy to read and your handoffs don't require follow-ups. ## ## What You Bring - 1–3 years of experience in creative strategy, performance creative, brand or growth marketing, or a related discipline. - Fluency in Meta Ads Manager or similar performance platforms. You can read the data and draw clear conclusions from it. - Exposure to direct-response or performance advertising. You understand what makes an ad convert, not just look good. - Familiarity with short-form video formats and an instinct for what works on platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels — you don't need to be a TikTok expert, but you should be a fluent consumer of the format. - Familiarity with AI creative tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar). You don't need to have used all of them, but you should be the kind of person who will try them. - Basic editing literacy (CapCut, Premiere, or similar) is a plus — being able to mock up a rough cut can help unblock a concept. ## ## Why This Role You'll get a front-row seat to how performance creative strategy gets made — with direct access to senior creative and growth leadership. If you want to grow quickly, take on real creative ownership early, flex across formats and channels, and work on brands that millions of people love, this is the role for you. **Benefits and perks** - **Medical, dental, and vision coverage** - **401k match** - **Equity in Mammoth Brands** - **Flexible time off and working hours** - **L&D stipend** - **4 weeks sabbatical after 5 years, 6 weeks after 10 years, and 8 weeks after 15 years** - **20 fully paid weeks off for parents who give birth, or 16 fully paid weeks off for all other paths to parenthood** - **Fun IRL and virtual events including happy hours, team building events, and parties on our rooftop** - **Free products from our family of brands** *The Mammoth Brands' working model is in-office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Our beautiful* [*70,000 square foot SoHo office*](https://www.wallpaper.com/lifestyle/shaving-brand-harrys-new-york-city-office-design) *is decked out with bagels on Wednesdays and lunch on Thursdays, and fully stocked kitchens with snacks, coffee, and drinks everyday. Can’t forget the free products and the opportunity to have some meetings without Zoom!* We can’t quantify all of the intangible things we think you’ll love about working at Mammoth Brands, like the exciting challenges we tackle, the smart and humble team you’ll get to work with, and our supportive and inclusive culture. That said, our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total rewards package, which also includes a comprehensive set of [benefits](https://www.harrys.com/en/us/careers) and our equity program.
