Position Purpose: Under the direction of the Operations Supervisor, Operations Lead Personnel and in coordination of fellow Operations Personnel the incumbent will perform a variety of basic tasks relevant to the day-to-day operation of the wastewater treatment plant facilities, processes and equipment, including process and equipment rounds, recording operations data and information, making observations and reporting on variations in operating conditions, maintaining logs and other required reports and forms, and provides input for corrective actions and implements corrective actions as directed. Assist Operations in efforts to maintain efficient and cost-effective facility operations while maintaining compliance with all Corporate and Regulatory environmental, health and safety rules and requirements. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Works a scheduled shift and will be subject to required emergency call in or shift coverage as Operational needs demand. Under the direct Supervision of Shift Supervisor or Lead person may be required to perform some of the following tasks depending on the station assigned for that shift: Record and Read meters for (pumps, gauges, motors etc.…) in accordance with all regulatory requirements. Record tank levels, sludge blanket levels. Operate equipment pertinent to assigned workstation (GBT, BFP, overhead lifting jib crane, pumps) Open, close and adjust valves for tanks & pumps. Observe their process areas (pumps, motors, valves, sewage color, odor, flow) record their findings. Collect samples for laboratory analysis. Receive chemicals in bulk, drum and tote form. Adjust / bleed pumps as directed. Keep the workstation and surrounding area safe and clear of debris. Inspect equipment for proper functionality and refer to Maintenance for any necessary repairs. Maintain a logbook for the station they are operating. Create work requests for equipment found to be malfunctioning or broken. Make adjustments to equipment to optimize the operation (GBT & Dewatering). Troubleshoot operational issues and get approval of operations supervisor before executing. Work Environment: Work is performed both inside and outside with exposure to all kinds of weather conditions. Incumbents may be occasionally exposed to some noise, silica, dust, fumes, smoke, gasses, greases, oils, electrical energy, solvents and vibration. Incumbents may work on slippery/uneven surfaces, around machinery with moving parts, moving objects/vehicles, ladder/scaffolding, below ground and may be exposed to water or other liquid materials. Maintain a high level of focus on health, safety and environment, ensuring safety within all activities. Education/Experience/Background: High School Diploma or GED, associate degree (or equivalent experience) in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology/Laboratory or related fields preferred. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Requires good reading, math, writing, and verbal communication skills. Ability to read, and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles, and other equipment. Ability to understand/execute written and oral instructions, read/understand technical instructions. Ability to interpret data and information from technical service manuals and drawings. Knowledge of Windows, Google Workspace, MS Office Suite, and other computer-based systems. Knowledge of basic laboratory sampling, testing and documentation. Ability to adjust chemical feeds and processing equipment as directed to maintain compliance. Basic knowledge of wastewater treatment equipment and processes. Must have the ability to maintain effective working relations w/management, supervisors, and staff. Must be able to work as a team in a teamwork-oriented environment. Must be safety conscious and able to work independently with little or no supervision. Must have a general understanding of how the treatment plant works and the SPDES limits associated to the station being operated. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Valid NYS Driver’s license and the ability to meet risk management guidelines. Ability to attend classes required for obtaining valid NY State Wastewater Treatment license and obtain license within 24 months. Pay Rate: $22.91 per hour. Benefits: Our employees are covered by comprehensive benefits packages including paid time off policies; health, dental, vision, and life insurance; retirement plans, savings accounts; tuition reimbursement; paid volunteering and more. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law. description: **Who We Are** Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides. Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles. With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected. Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors. #### **About the Role** Product Engineering at Nuro spans the teams that build the software our vehicles, operators, and partners depend on every day, from the on-road experience of the fleet itself to the routing engine that decides where it goes. - The **On-Road Experience** team builds the internal tools and platform systems that Nuro's operations, engineering, and partner teams rely on to manage, monitor, and maintain our autonomous vehicle fleet. This is hands-on product engineering work at the intersection of fleet operations and software infrastructure. The systems you build directly impact user-facing features and how reliably & efficiently Nuro operates vehicles on public roads. - The **Routing** team builds the critical services that determine the routes our robots take to reach their destinations safely and efficiently, along with the simulation tools that shape the company's strategy for robot deployment and business expansion. The team is constantly working towards computing more efficient routes and providing more accurate ETAs. As a Product Engineer, you'll join one of these teams and help build the products, tools, and services that turn Nuro's autonomy technology into a system people can operate, trust, and rely on. #### **About the Work** **On-Road Experience** - You will design, build, and ship full-stack applications using React, TypeScript, and modern web development practices. - You will develop backend services and APIs that integrate with onboard vehicle systems, cloud infrastructure, and external partner platforms. - You will build tools that enable fleet monitoring, vehicle health tracking, maintenance workflows, and operational decision-making. - You will contribute to frontend architecture decisions, component libraries, and shared platform patterns used across the org. **Routing** - You will build and scale backend systems for the Routing team, including designing microservices, optimizing routing algorithms, and understanding road network graphs. - You will build software modules written in C++ that operate onboard the vehicle to generate routes, receive live map updates, and interface with motion planning. - You will build monitoring and analytics infrastructure that supports routing performance and ETA accuracy. - You will work on scalable traffic management and simulation tools that shape the company's strategy for robot deployment and business expansion. **Both Teams** - You will work closely with Product, UX, Operations, and cross-functional stakeholders to define requirements and deliver new user experiences. - You will own features end-to-end: scoping, implementation, testing, deployment, and iteration based on user feedback. #### **About You** - Technical excellence. - You have a strong foundation in software fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, and either web fundamentals (HTML, CSS, browser APIs) or server-side programming (Go, Java, Python, or C++). - You have experience (through coursework, internships, or personal projects) building applications with React and TypeScript, or building real-time, server-side systems. - You understand how to build and consume RESTful or gRPC APIs. - You are familiar with relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) and have some exposure to cloud infrastructure (GCP or AWS). - You are comfortable working across the stack, and eager to grow into whichever end of it your team needs most. - You have a wide range of technical interests, you love learning new technologies, and you're a quick learner. - You have a passion for making lives easier for the people who rely on your work, whether that's an operator troubleshooting a vehicle or a rider waiting on an accurate ETA. - You have the instinct for making the right tradeoffs. You know when it makes sense to move quick-and-dirty versus build the scalable approach, and you're eager to develop that judgment further. - You care about users. You like working closely with product and design to build the best experience for the people who depend on your work. - You are a great communicator, and you're excited to collaborate with PMs, UX researchers, other engineers, and cross-functional stakeholders on product requirements and designs. - You are impact-driven. You care deeply that your work makes a significant impact on the lives of millions of people. #### **Bonus Points** - Familiarity with real-time data systems: WebSockets, Pub/Sub, streaming pipelines. - Experience with Protocol Buffers and gRPC, or RPC frameworks like Thrift. - Exposure to Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, or infrastructure-as-code. - Experience with routing algorithms, map data, or graph data structures. - Background or coursework in the autonomous vehicle, robotics, logistics, or automotive industry. - Experience working with partner or third-party API integrations. - Interest in frontend platform work: design systems, shared component libraries, and developer tooling. #### **Minimum Qualifications** - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, completed or in progress (new grad / early-career candidates welcome, no professional experience required). At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $132,300 and $198,450 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package. *At Nuro, we celebrate differences and are committed to a diverse workplace that fosters inclusion and psychological safety for all employees. As long as you have the raw ingredients, we can teach the rest. Sales Academy is a 3-month program where you'll learn from proven sales leaders and all-star sellers, and you'll be selling a product customers love. The world's best engineering teams rely on [](http://incident.io) when things go wrong, so you'll start your career with something worth talking about. # **What that looks like day to day** You'll start in January 2027 alongside a cohort of people who, like you, have never done this job before. You get to be bad at it in front of people who are also bad at it, and get good fast. **Part one: training.** You'll get intensive training and support from our sales leaders and tenured sellers. It covers researching prospects, cold calling, writing outreach people want to answer, and handling objections. You'll also learn how [](http://incident.io) works, who we sell to, and why they buy. There's daily practice, homework, and plenty of coaching from people who want to see you succeed. **Part two: doing the job.** For the rest of the academy, you'll work as a Business Development Rep (BDR) on live accounts. You'll make calls and send outreach, and the meetings you book will feed our pipeline. By the end, you'll be able to hold your own on a cold call with a CTO. # **What you get out of it** **It all starts here.** BDRs are the bench for the rest of our go-to-market team. People in this seat go on to become Account Executives, Account Managers, and Customer Success Managers. The goal is for everyone who finishes the academy to convert to a permanent BDR, launching a long, high-trajectory career here at [](http://incident.io). Alongside sales training, you'll get professional development and networking opportunities across the wider business. We want you to feel like part of our culture from day one, not someone passing through. **If you don't convert,** you'll still have had three months of paid, on-the-job training. You'll leave with tested, marketable hard skills and a clearer sense of your strengths and where you'd do your best work. We'll do our best to help you with your next move. # **Who you are** - **You've never been a BDR before.** You might be a new grad, someone switching careers (teaching, the military, sport, performing), or someone from traditional sales like retail, door-to-door, events, or fundraising. We care about what you're capable of, not what's on your resume. - **You really want this.** You're not drifting into tech sales. You've decided, and you can tell us why. - **You're seriously curious.** About people, about what's keeping a VP of Engineering up at night, and about why one call landed when another didn't. - **You've had to be resilient already.** You've held a room, or heard "no" over and over without taking it personally. - **You like being coached.** Someone has told you the honest version of how you're doing, and you got better for it. - **The phone doesn't scare you.** You may never have made a cold call, but talking to strangers all day sounds fun rather than horrifying. - **You want the cohort.** Learning alongside other people, being measured against them, and wanting them to do well too sounds good to you, not stressful. # **Interview process at a glance** - **Stage 1: Video application & aptitude assessment.** Send us your LinkedIn profile, your contact details, and a quick video on why you'd be great at this. From there, we'll email a link to complete a 25-minute aptitude assessment. - **Stage 2: On-site interview.** A half day in our San Francisco office with the sales team. - **Stage 3: Offer.** # **Good to know** - **This role is based in our San Francisco office.** You're welcome to apply from outside the Bay Area, but you'll need to be in the office from day one, working five days per week in office. - **We don't provide relocation assistance for this role.** - **This is a 3-month temporary role**, and the goal is to convert you to a permanent employee when the academy ends. - **Benefits start when you convert to a permanent role.** You won't be eligible for our employee benefit plans during the 3-month academy. - **Our first cohort starts in January 2027.** Applications for this cohort close on December 1st. We'll begin hiring for our April 2027 cohort January 4th.

Overview The Science and Technology Policy Institute (STPI) is a congressionally chartered, Federally Funded Research and Development Center operated by the Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA). STPI provides independent analytical support to the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), the National Science Foundation (NSF), the National Institutes of Health (NIH), and other federal departments and agencies on science and technology (S&T) policy issues. The STPI Science Policy Fellowship Program provides recent bachelor’s or master’s degree recipients a unique opportunity to use their critical thinking and analytic skills to work on a diverse set of challenges in S&T policy areas, including space sciences, innovation and competitiveness, energy, health and life sciences, national security, biotechnology, information technologies, and STEM education. Responsibilities Fellows will work with teams of researchers to support a wide variety of S&T policy-related tasks. Duties may include conducting survey-based and interview-based research, database development, use of data visualization tools, use of statistical techniques, and other qualitative and quantitative methods to perform project-driven policy analysis. Over the course of the two-year program, experiences will include: Participation in analyses that support tasking from Federal Government policymakers Interaction with OSTP and other Federal science agency personnel Involvement in workshops and discussions on relevant topics Mentorship from members of the STPI research staff Training on specific analytical methods and tools Attendance and presentation at select professional society meetings Qualifications This is a full-time position and is only open to recent recipients of a bachelor’s or master’s degree. Candidates with degrees higher than a master’s degree will not be considered. Candidates must have at least a bachelor’s degree conferred between May 2025 and July 2027. Candidates with MA/MS degrees should apply if their bachelor’s degrees were conferred between May 2024 and July 2026. Candidates with degrees in engineering, life sciences, physical sciences, social and behavioral sciences, computer science, mathematical sciences, statistics, and learning sciences are encouraged to apply. Candidates should possess a strong interest in science and technology policy, although previous policy experience is not required. Candidates must demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills. Ideal candidates are able to contribute to and support team efforts. Application Materials To be considered for this fellowship opportunity, interested candidates must follow a two-step process: Apply using the link on IDA's careers page. Submit via email to the following documents: Personal Statement—explain in 500 words or fewer why you want to work in the area of science and technology policy and how your background/experience will contribute to STPI’s work Writing Sample—2,500-word maximum. Applicants must be the sole author to be eligible for consideration. Transcripts—unofficial transcripts are acceptable for consideration Finalists will be asked to solicit two Letters of Academic Recommendation—letters must be signed by the individual rendering the reference and delivered as PDF files. Letters must also be sent directly to by the recommender. Ensure the application and supporting materials are submitted no later than January 4, 2027. Why Work at IDA? Competitive salary and benefits, including diverse health insurance options, generous 10% contribution to retirement, 6 weeks 100% paid parental leave, 20 days paid time off, and relocation reimbursement. Eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSFL) due to IDA’s non-profit status. Organization-wide commitment to diversity in the workplace and providing a working environment free from discrimination, by fostering a culture of active citizenship and implementing data-driven processes of continuous feedback and learning. Professional development, including tuition reimbursement, internal and external trainings, and funding for researcher-pitched projects and publications. A strong employee and corporate culture of work-life balance, including commitment to average 40- hour work weeks through flex time, telework options, and expectation of communication only during core business hours. Easy access to local dining and shopping. Employer contributes $300/month (the IRS maximum) to commuter benefits. Compensation We support transparency, equity, and fairness in our compensation program. The stipend for this fellowship is based on data-driven market analysis. Failure to obtain/maintain required certifications will result in disqualification for this position and could result in termination. Candidate must exhibit a professional behavior that promotes teamwork, fosters cooperation and enhances productivity in the workplace. Must be well organized with the ability to coordinate, prioritize, and execute multiple tasks simultaneously. Candidate must have the ability to communicate verbally and in writing to work effectively with various external customers including government, military, and contractor personnel at all levels. Candidate must be able to communicate effectively with individuals at all levels of the company. For office environments, grooming and dress are typically business casual but are dependent on the client’s standards. JOB DESCRIPTION: The Utah Senate invites applications for the position of Senate Minority (Democratic) Policy Intern for the 2027 General Session. This intern will support the Senate Democratic Caucus by monitoring legislation, tracking bill progress, and assisting with members’ policy priorities. A significant portion of the role involves updating and maintaining tracking spreadsheets. This position is ideal for students or recent graduates interested in state government, public policy, and public service. RESPONSIBILITIES: ●This intern will work closely with the Minority Caucus Administrator by assisting with research and preparation on substantive policy issues. ●Strong ability to organize, code, and manage data using Google Sheets. ●Highly organized, accurate, and detail-oriented in research and reporting. ●Strong research, writing, and analytical skills. ●Ability to synthesize complex information clearly and concisely. ●Receptive to feedback and able to respond effectively to suggestions. ●Maintains confidentiality and professionalism when working with multiple senators and staff. ●Excellent command of grammar, spelling, and punctuation. ●Demonstrated interest in public policy, government, or legislative affairs. ●Work independently for long periods of time.

Packaging Engineer Intern Job Description: The packaging engineering group of MACOM supports the design, development, and implementation of packaging solutions for RF semiconductor devices. Interns may assist in package design work and in creating / reviewing assembly drawings using CAD software. They may collect data directly or coordinate work with external labs, using metrology and failure analysis tools and techniques. They may help design experiments and analyze results using statistical techniques and process improvement methodology. Interns may also, depending on skill level, run thermal and mechanical simulations with FEA software packages to characterize new materials and device designs. Interns will periodically need to put together reports of work and present to other engineers and management.

GaN RF Power Amplifier Intern Job Description: The engineering intern will be working at the Morgan Hill CA Design Center alongside a highly knowledgeable team of RF engineers and will initially be tasked with device characterization of MACOM’s high power GaN transistor products geared towards Base Station market. As an intern you will learn to operate the RF test bench software and Digital Predistortion testers, handling RF devices, biasing devices, capturing accurate RF data, and performing a limited amount of data processing. This device characterization activity will be in support of current product development and R D activities. A follow-on activity will task the intern to design an impedance matching network for a GaN device, using either MWO or ADS design software, in order to match the device to a 50 ohm environment. The intern will be expected to layout the impedance matching network in AutoCAD, have it fabricated and will be tasked to assemble, solder components, and tune the circuit on the RF bench. During the 12 weeks each Intern will: > Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals > Gain hands on experience > Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision > Be invited to attend an intern webinar series > Attend networking/social events > Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls > Receive formal, written feedback

description: JOB DESCRIPTION: This is a temporary internship for the 2027 General Legislative Session. RF Power Application Intern Role Overview: The RF Power Application Intern will design, assemble, and test RF Power application circuits in support of our RF power amplifier product line. The intern will learn to utilize RF models and measured data to drive circuit level designs. This will include learning to utilize RF test equipment and test software to perform RF measurements, such as s-parameters and circuit level characterization. This role will also utilize AWR to model and analyze RF device performance. ## **Compound Management Specialist (Part-time Internship)** **Time Commitment:** 1-2 days per week **Location:** Boston, MA ### **About Proxima** Proxima is a frontier AI and data generation company discovering the next generation of proximity therapeutics by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round with an elite group of VCs including DCVC, NVIDIA’s NVentures, AIX, Yosemite among others. Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time. In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. We’re building the tech and the team to make that happen. Come join us! ### **What you'll do** - Manage daily chemical repository routines, encompassing the receipt, registration, and intake logging of novel materials into Mosaic - Process assay-ready samples, including mass measurement, preparation of DMSO stocks, serial dilutions, microplate reformatting, and liquid handling automation configuration - Ensure repository data accuracy through periodic audits, reconciling physical chemical assets with database records while managing cold-chain storage organization - Uphold chemical safety protocols, regulatory guidelines, and hazardous material handling procedures while driving continuous enhancement of operational workflows ### **Your skills** - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program in chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or a related scientific discipline (junior or senior standing) - Practical bench experience acquired via academic laboratory coursework, undergraduate research, or industry internships, including gravimetric analysis and micro-pipetting - Meticulous documentation practices and precision in experimental record-keeping - Proficiency in computational spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets), with prior exposure to laboratory information management systems (LIMS) being advantageous - Understanding of standard laboratory safety regulations and hazardous reagent management - Strong organizational capability, reliability in executing written experimental SOPs, and proactive judgment - Strong communication skills and ability to operate within a dynamic environment ### **Desirable Qualifications** - Experience operating robotic liquid handling platforms, high-throughput microplate screening, or complex dilution series

role: Run Perception Graduate Internship, R&D - Winter 2027
description: **Who We Are:** At Brooks, we believe movement is the key to feeling more alive. That’s why we’re driven to create gear and experiences that take people to the place that makes them feel more alive — whether it’s a headspace, a feeling, or a finish line. Everyone who works at Brooks is propelled by a company culture that sparks excitement, fuels collaboration, inspires creativity, and ignites innovation. Our brand values help bond us together and drive our success: - ***Runner First*** - *We act in the best interest of the runner* - ***Word is Bond*** - *We do what we say we’ll do* - ***Champion Heart*** - *We give our all in everything we do* - ***There is no “I” in Run*** - *We stay generous with our humanity* - ***Keep Moving*** - *We find ways to move every day, because joy is kinetic!* We welcome everyone from every walk of life looking to inspire others through the power of movement - because we’re *all* moving towards something. Let’s run there. #### Brooks Internship Program: Brooks Running hosts internships at our Seattle HQ offices to provide hands-on, meaningful work experience to further enhance your education and professional aptitude. Our interns gain exposure to real work, and projects while working side by side with Brooks employees and leadership. If chosen for this role, you will embark on 6 months of learning, professional development, and exposure to the Brooks brand and culture. #### Internship Details: Duration: 6 months Internship Target Start: January 12, 2026 Compensation: $33.00/hr Location: Seattle, HQ Schedule: 40 hours / week Please apply if you can commit to the duration, salary and location for this opportunity. #### Your Opportunity: Our Run Perception Team is seeking a master’s graduate intern to work at our Seattle HQ offices. As the Run Perception Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in product research at the leading running brand – Brooks Sports, Inc. Your primary responsibilities will be to assist Run Perception Researchers as they collect information from product testers across the nation to contribute key perceptual information regarding fit, performance, and design. This information is critical for our multi-departmental infrastructure, including Development, Design, and Merchandising, to ensure that performance integrity of our product meets the needs of our end consumers. You will also gain knowledge on how perceptual feedback influences design and development of athletic products at Brooks. With the Run Perception Team being part of our Development team, you will learn how to work closely with the Developers on building product based off insights collected not only from the Run Perception Team, but also from other collaborators across the company. #### Your Impact (Responsibilities): - Understand athletic product design features and components, and how they influence fit, feel, and ride. - Conduct internal and external perception testing data collections for inline footwear and the sourcing team. This entails targeted participant recruitment based on the product goals and consumer base, creation of perception surveys that test the hypotheses at hand, analysis of qualitative results, and synthesis of data into a clear point of view highlighting how the product is performing. - Compile and present scientific reports via PowerPoint, summarizing findings based on runner feedback that are delivered to product teams for use in product improvement. - Use your graduate-level research skills to conduct Run Perception studies that lead to innovative testing procedures and optimization of product for all who run. - Use your advanced data analytics skills to mine data in our Tableau historical dashboards containing over 3 million words of perception testing feedback for product over the last six years to recommend product improvements based on identified opportunities. - Use AI-powered tools to help analyze and summarize wear test feedback at both the individual and historical dataset level, uncovering meaningful patterns and insights that strengthen product storytelling and recommendations. - Develop loyal, engaging relationships with our product testers and the Brooks community. - Assist with the management of Brooks perception testing community social media account on Facebook with timely and accurate responses to participants and the creation of engaging content for the group. Other duties as assigned. #### Project: As a part of your experience as a graduate intern at Brooks, you will have the opportunity to complete a project under the support and supervision of your manager. Details of your project will be finalized once you arrive at Brooks based on your interests and the needs of the business. role: Run Performance Graduate Internship, Run Research Team - Winter 2027
description: **Who We Are:** At Brooks, we believe movement is the key to feeling more alive. That’s why we’re driven to create gear and experiences that take people to the place that makes them feel more alive — whether it’s a headspace, a feeling, or a finish line. Everyone who works at Brooks is propelled by a company culture that sparks excitement, fuels collaboration, inspires creativity, and ignites innovation. Our brand values help bond us together and drive our success: - ***Runner First*** - *We act in the best interest of the runner* - ***Word is Bond*** - *We do what we say we’ll do* - ***Champion Heart*** - *We give our all in everything we do* - ***There is no “I” in Run*** - *We stay generous with our humanity* - ***Keep Moving*** - *We find ways to move every day, because joy is kinetic!* We welcome everyone from every walk of life looking to inspire others through the power of movement - because we’re *all* moving towards something. Let’s run there. #### Brooks Internship Program Brooks Running hosts internships at our Seattle HQ offices to provide hands-on, meaningful work experience to further enhance your education and professional aptitude. Our interns gain exposure to real work, and projects while working side by side with Brooks employees and leadership. If chosen for this role, you will embark on 6 months of learning, professional development, and exposure to the Brooks brand and culture. #### Internship Details Duration: 6 months Internship Target Start: Jan 4, Jan 11, or Jan 18. Compensation: $ 33.00/hr. Location: Seattle, HQ Schedule: 40 hours / week Please apply if you can commit to the duration, salary, and location for this opportunity. #### Your Opportunity The mission of the Brooks Run Research Lab is to create and leverage novel, scientific concepts and runner-driven product performance insights to create amazing products to help everyone run their path. Our Run Research Lab is seeking a Master's graduate intern to work at our Seattle HQ offices. As a Run Research performance Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in product research at the leading running brand – Brooks Sports, Inc. Your primary responsibilities will be to assist in biomechanical data collection and processing for Run Research that will be used to inform product design, materials, and development. The protocols will include but are not limited to motion capture, material mechanical properties, and metabolic testing. This information is critical for our multi-departmental infrastructure, including Development, Design, and Merchandising, to ensure that the performance integrity of our product meets the needs of our end consumers. You will also gain knowledge on how the human movement influences the design and development of athletic products at Brooks. #### Your Impact (Responsibilities) - Understand athletic product design features and components and how they influence human movement. - Collection and processing of human subject data using Motion Analysis 3D motion capture. - Write code to analyze mechanical and biomechanical data in Python or Visual 3D. - Perform mechanical testing on material samples and full shoes (Instron). - Write scientific reports in PowerPoint and Microsoft Word. Summarize human movement and mechanical property findings for Brooks product and competitors that are delivered to product teams for use in product improvement. - Use your graduate-level research skills to conduct human movement studies that lead to innovative testing procedures and optimization of products for all who run. - Use your advanced data analytics skills to mine data in our historical dashboards to recommend product improvements based on identified opportunities. - Develop loyal, engaging relationships with our customers and the Brooks community. - Other duties as assigned #### Project: - As a part of your experience as a graduate intern at Brooks, you will have the opportunity to complete a project under the support and supervision of your manager. Details of your project will be finalized once you arrive at Brooks based on your skills and the needs of the business. You will use your ever-growing analytical skillset as a graduate student to prepare a thoughtful and elevated project. During the course of this project, you will weave your learnings from your graduate courses into your work to challenge yourself, and benefit Brooks. You will present your work and findings to senior leadership at Brooks at the end of your internship, to hone in on your research, recommendation, and presentation skills. ### Qualifications: - Master's degree with a background in biomechanics, kinesiology, and/or exercise science or an equivalent analytical field. - Willing to commit to the intern position for six months onsite in Seattle, WA - Willingness to learn and gain hands-on experience. - Able to commit to up to 40 hours a week to be physically present at HQ. - Strong verbal and written communication skills, demonstrating effective listening through concise, clear verbal and written communication. - Hands-on experience in a biomechanics lab or a lab that involved data collection on human subjects using 3D motion capture. - Hands-on experience with materials testing and familiarity with stress/strain testing protocols. - Well-developed quantitative skills with an aptitude for report-building, data mining, and interpretation. - Hands-on experience with writing code (Python [preferred], MATLAB, etc.) and creating kinematic and kinetic models for human motion capture (Visual 3D). - Experience with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. - Strong organizational skills. - Detail-oriented with an emphasis on quality work products. Always looking to improve our products and processes while also displaying a willingness to dive into the details and help wherever necessary. - Must be able to collaborate in a team-oriented environment. - Embrace Brooks values!

description: **Who We Are** Hi! We’re The Heist, the motion design, live action, and post production studio within Thinkingbox, the Brief-to-Built agency. We bring together directors, designers, animators, editors, and technologists to create work that moves. From brand films to broadcast spots to social campaigns and experiential content, our team blends craft and curiosity to push ideas further. We’re looking for someone who’s hungry to learn and ready to jump into real projects. This role is ideal for someone early in their creative career who is passionate about animation, design systems, digital storytelling, and motion-driven craft. You’ll work alongside experienced designers and directors while building hands-on experience across 2D and 3D pipelines. This is not a coffee run internship. You’ll be making things. ### What You’ll Be Doing - Support the motion design team across 2D and 3D projects for commercial, social, and digital campaigns - Assist in animating assets for short-form video, branded content, and broadcast work - Help prepare project files, exports, and deliverables across multiple platforms - Organize assets and maintain clean project workflows - Participate in creative reviews, brainstorms, and internal critiques - Take feedback constructively and apply revisions efficiently - Stay curious about trends in motion, culture, design, and emerging tools ### What You'll Bring - Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a Motion Design, Animation, Design, or related program - Foundational proficiency in Adobe After Effects - Familiarity with Premiere Pro, Photoshop, and Illustrator - Exposure to 3D tools – ideally Cinema 4D and/or Houdini - An understanding of basic animation principles including timing, easing, and composition - Strong attention to detail and eagerness to grow - Ability to manage time and collaborate in a team environment - Ability to effectively communicate in written and verbal formats ### What You'll Gain - Real studio experience across client projects - Exposure to professional production and post workflows - Mentorship from senior designers and creative leaders - A deeper understanding of how motion fits within broader brand systems and campaigns ### Bonus Points! - Knowledge of basic 3D workflows, lighting, and rendering - Curiosity around AI assisted workflows and emerging creative tools - A portfolio that shows personality, taste, and an eye for motion - Rive, Cavalry, Figma, or other creative platform experience ### Additional Info - Monday - Thursday in office (Fridays are remote optional) - Flexible time off, including paid vacation and sick days - Consistent culture and team-building events - Employee recognition and incentive programs - Seasonal celebrations and gatherings throughout the year - Office lunches - Branded company swag - Access to industry events, learning opportunities, and non-profit outreaches - Dog-friendly offices - Unlimited coffee, drinks, and snacks - Flex work and travel options - Comprehensive extended health benefits - 401k matching

# **Why Harvey** At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. # **Role Overview** The Software Engineer, New Grad joins Harvey's Engineering team, working alongside experienced engineers to build the AI-powered systems that serve the world's leading law firms and enterprises. The team's mission is to deliver secure, intuitive, and high-performance application-layer experiences that turn frontier AI capabilities into real customer value. This role offers an accelerated path to ownership, contributing production code to features spanning retrieval, document intelligence, and workflow automation from day one. It is an opportunity to develop rapidly at the intersection of AI and professional services, with direct exposure to how engineers shape a category-defining product. We're currently hiring new grads to start in 2027 across multiple teams and roles, including Frontend, Backend, Full-Stack, Infrastructure, and Applied AI roles. Your interests & experience will be factored into our team matching process, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn about teams across Harvey including Agents, Applied AI, Assistant, Enterprise, Infrastructure, Mobile, Vault and many others. # **What You'll Do** - Design, implement, and ship production-level code across the stack while maintaining high quality, reliability, and security standards. You'll use AI-assisted development tools daily, and you’ll own the quality of everything you ship—AI-generated or not. - Collaborate with cross-functional teams including AI Research, Legal Engineering, Product, and Design to translate problem statements into compelling product experiences. - Collaborate with your team through code reviews, technical design discussions, and engineering best-practice development alongside senior and staff engineers. - Experiment with and evaluate cutting-edge LLMs and AI systems, contributing to how Harvey's platform evolves. - Depending on your team, you could work on retrieval over large document collections, interfaces for collaborating with AI systems, multi-region compute infrastructure, enterprise agents, or secure systems for sensitive client data. # **What You Have** - Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, graduated either in Winter 2026 - Spring 2027. - Able to work from our New York or San Francisco office starting in January 2027 and beyond, based on your graduation schedule. Relocation support is available. - Previous internship experience is required. - **Technical foundation.** Strong proficiency in one or more languages (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, or similar) and solid general computer science knowledge. - **Decisiveness.** You have a bias toward action. You've built something start to finish in coursework, a personal project, or a past internship, and you know the difference between a decision you should make yourself and one worth getting feedback on. You'd rather move and correct course than stall. - **Simplicity.** You can explain a complex technical idea in plain language, whether or not the person you're explaining it to is an engineer. You look for the simplest solution that works, and you know when added complexity is worth it. - **Job's Not Finished.** You aren't satisfied when something merely works. You proactively seek out feedback, act on it, and keep pushing after the assignment is technically complete. Past internship experience at an early-stage startup is a plus. - **AI Forward.** Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and curious about building LLMs into your own coding workflow. # **Compensation** $165,000-$181,500 ### **Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices** [**here**](https://harveyai.notion.site/Harvey-Candidate-Privacy-Notices-319ac3fcdd7a803bb807d5094f249922?pvs=74)**.** #LI-LW1 *Harvey is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.* We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made by emailing [accommodations@harvey.ai](mailto:accommodations@harvey.ai)

Job Summary: This position is located in the Dean of Students Office, reporting to the Senior Resident Dean, who is in charge of the Student Support Team (SST). The Student Support Team is convened by the Senior Resident Dean to review complex student cases; it brings together representatives from Residential Life, DAO, Secretary of the College, HUHS and others on a weekly basis. The Student Support Coordinator will work closely with the Senior Resident Dean to coordinate for students dealing with complex issues that impact their time at the College, including hospitalizations, emergency travel coordination for student and family members, and/or leaves of absence. The Student Support Coordinator interfaces often with the Student Support Team and residential staff, including the Allston Burr Resident Deans, the Resident Deans of First-Year Students, as well as the Dean of Students Office, staff from HUHS/CAMHS, Disability Access Office (DAO), and Housing Office. Job-Specific Responsibilities: Student Support and Coordination Support individual students around complex health or academic issues. This includes: Serve as an immediate point of contact for the hospital social worker and care coordination team (if applicable), the student, the parents, CAMHS, HUHS, Title IX, Housing Office, DAO, and other stakeholders Coordinate re-entry with HUHS, CAMHS, DAO and the hospital social worker and Care Coordination team as necessary. Attend return meetings at CAMHS/HUHS if requested. In coordination with the Senior Resident Dean, convey information about policies and student situations to case/social workers in hospital and to notification group. Communicate regularly with residential staff and other offices to provide updates on a student’s status and facilitate connections to other resources as appropriate. Work with residential staff to arrange move-out of student belongings and/or access to room. Work with the respective FYE/House Administrator and Academic Coordinator to make sure the student is properly checked out of our student systems. Outreach to student treatment teams each term in specific cases. Administration Maintain Student Support Team records and contribute to student files as appropriate. Attend weekly Student Support Team Meetings and update SST records as appropriate. Collect and summarize relevant information from stakeholders and residential staff to present to the College Student Support Team. Work with Harvard College student information systems (SST, my.harvard, AppXtender, and StarRez) and be conversant with the College policies around hospitalizations, clearance for return, and leaves of absence, as well as the resources available to students and staff at the College. Must be aware of and comply with Harvard’s policies for handling confidential student information safely and securely. Financial Administration Work with the Financial Aid Office and the Senior Resident Dean regarding financial and logistical aspects of student support such as tuition and term bill implications, emergency travel and accommodation support and coordination, shipping costs, etc. Upon request of the Senior Resident Dean, reimburse student and family expenses using Buy2Pay (B2P), When necessary, facilitate registration by the student and/or family members for payments through vendor setup in B2P. Upon request of the Senior Resident Dean, arrange emergency travel for the student and/or family members, using Egencia, Harvard’s travel vendor. Make purchases with the appropriate University-issued credit card, maintaining receipts and processing payments in Concur. Be familiar with and comply with University financial policies and best practices. Working Conditions: Office Setting- The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs and objectives and consistent with College Policy, which requires 5 days on-site in Cambridge, MA during term time (first day of classes through commencement), with the exception of winter break in December, spring break in March, and the summer months when students are away from campus, where staff is expected be on campus two days a week. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts . Additional details about the College policy will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment. Travel Requirements: Local – accompanying the Resident Dean/College representative Physical Requirements: Able to lift file boxes, manage records, regular typing/computer work. Basic Qualifications: 3 to 5 years of student support experience in higher education. Additional Qualifications and Skills: Experience with crisis management in higher ed preferred. Appointment End Date: Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week Compensation Range/Rate (including Shift Differential if applicable): Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Criminal Other Information: Support Preparation of Training Materials and documentation workflow. description: We are seeking a graduate-level intern to join our Talent Acquisition (TA) team as a Talent Acquisition Data Engineering & Analytics Intern. This role is designed for a highly motivated individual who wants hands-on experience building and analyzing TA metrics that influence business decisions at a global scale. The intern will learn how to extract, transform, and visualize data from multiple HR and business systems while contributing to the foundation of our global TA reporting function. The Talent Acquisition Data Engineering & Analytics Intern will build the production reporting layer for Talent Acquisition. This internship is designed for a technically strong graduate student who wants to own the full path from raw recruiting data to automated, leadership-facing dashboards. The intern will establish Snowflake connectivity and automated data refresh, build a query-ready data model, and develop a complete Power BI dashboard suite covering all Talent Acquisition metrics. The intern will work directly with Talent Acquisition leadership and collaborate with the teams responsible for SmartRecruiters, Workday, Jira, ServiceNow, and Snowflake. This internship focuses on data engineering, data modeling, dashboard development, and reporting automation, rather than operational recruiting activities. Key Responsibilites Establish and validate connections between Talent Acquisition source systems and Snowflake, partnering with Data Engineering and IT. Configure Power BI connectivity and scheduled refresh so dashboards update automatically without manual data pulls. Implement data quality checks and refresh monitoring so reporting issues surface before leadership sees them. Build a query-ready dimensional data model in Snowflake supporting recruiting requisition, funnel, and hiring activity analytics. Write and optimize SQL transformations that turn raw source system data into analysis-ready tables, including historical and point-in-time reporting such as requisition status history and pipeline snapshots. Develop a full Power BI dashboard suite covering the Talent Acquisition metrics framework, including executive summary, requisition and pipeline health, funnel conversion, time-to-fill and time-in-stage, offer metrics, sourcing effectiveness, recruiter workload, and TA operational SLA metrics. Build a governed semantic model with certified DAX measures so metrics are defined once and consumed consistently across all reporting. Implement row-level security and optimize model performance at full data volume. Produce implementation-ready documentation covering pipeline architecture, data lineage, model diagrams, measure definitions, and a refresh and troubleshooting runbook. Create end-user guides and deliver enablement sessions for TA Operations and HR leadership. Partner with Talent Acquisition leadership to prioritize requirements, translate business questions into measurable metrics, and present dashboard walkthroughs and insights. Example Internship Deliverables Operational Snowflake data pipeline supporting Talent Acquisition reporting Dimensional data model deployed in Snowflake Complete Power BI dashboard suite covering the Talent Acquisition metrics framework Governed semantic model with certified, documented measures Automated refresh configuration with monitoring and data quality validation Technical documentation, refresh runbook, and end-user enablement materials Recommended roadmap for future Talent Acquisition analytics development Currently pursuing a graduate degree in Data Analytics, Data Science, Data Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Strong proficiency in SQL, including joins, aggregations, window functions, and query optimization. Hands-on experience building dashboards in Power BI, including DAX measures and data modeling. Experience with Python or R for data extraction, transformation, and analysis. Working knowledge of dimensional data modeling and dataset design principles. Familiarity with ETL/ELT concepts and building or maintaining data pipelines. Ability to translate ambiguous business questions into structured, measurable analytics requirements. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse (BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks). Experience configuring automated refresh, scheduled jobs, or orchestration tooling (dbt, Airflow, Azure Data Factory). Experience with Power BI Service administration: workspaces, gateways, deployment pipelines, or row-level security. Experience with APIs or system-to-system data integrations. Experience with large datasets in cloud environments (Azure, AWS, or GCP). Exposure to version control (Git) and analytics engineering practices. Familiarity with AI/ML techniques and interest in applying them to workforce data. Passion for HR, Talent Acquisition, or workforce analytics and how data informs business strategy. AECOM is actively seeking a creative, highly talented High School Intern for immediate employment in the Virginia Beach, VA office. Internship Purpose: The proposed internship would provide a high school student with meaningful experience in multidisciplinary building design, with primary emphasis on electrical engineering and Revit. The high school student must be a senior in high school. The internship would begin in November 2026 and continue through May 31, 2027. The high school student will complete at least 140 documented hours which is a typical requirement through the EBA academy program with the Virginia Beach Public School system (VBCPS) and would typically work approximately 6 to 8 hours per week, with additional hours when his or her academic schedule, office workload, and available supervision allows. The student will be available to work at the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and/or Thursday and will work with their supervisor to determine the appropriate weekly work schedule. We move at pace, tackle genuinely complex problems, and foster a high-accountability culture that stays genuinely human. If you are looking for room to build and meaningful scope, you belong here. Learn more at[](http://www.teads.com). ## **About the Opportunity & Team** This role sits within **Teads Studio**, our creative center of excellence. At Teads Studio, we empower global brands to redefine digital advertising by combining data-driven insights with creative innovation. We are looking for a **Junior Designer**—a creative talent who can carry concepts from initial visual design through to working, production-ready, interactive ad units. Strong on design craft and comfortable enough in code to build, prototype, and ship end-to-end, you will serve as a vital bridge between design vision and technical execution on our team. ## **About the Role** - **Core Mission:** Support the creation and build of high-performing, interactive video and display ad experiences across web and mobile ecosystems. - **Team Alignment:** Work closely with cross-functional Studio teams, strategists, and developers to bring brand and campaign visions to life. - **Scope of Ownership:** Deliver custom interactive creatives—from initial layout and motion design to light coding, prototyping, QA, and launch. - **Impact Metric:** Success in this role means executing pixel-perfect, production-ready ad formats on tight deadlines while maintaining high QA standards across all target platforms. ## **What You’ll Do** ### **Design Craft & Motion** - **Translate** brand guidelines and campaign concepts into engaging visual designs optimized for in-feed environments. - **Craft** sleek visual layouts applying core UI/UX fundamentals—composition, typography, color theory, and visual hierarchy. - **Design** fluid motion sequences, establishing precise timing, easing, and choreography for interactive creative assets. ### **Creative Development & Prototyping** - **Build** responsive HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript (ES6+) layouts from existing templates and patterns without relying on heavy frameworks (React/Angular) to adhere strictly to publisher lightweight specs. - **Repurpose & Analyze** existing codebase patterns to quickly integrate, adjust, or tweak snippets for custom builds. - **Prototype** and ship simpler display and video experiences end-to-end, reducing handoffs. ### **Technical Standards & Quality Assurance** - **Configure** campaign builds under the hood—managing scaffolding, assets, parameters, and tag structures. - **Understand** AdTech standards, including IAB specifications, VAST/VPAID video tags, and 3rd-party tracking pixels (1x1s, click tags). - **Execute** thorough QA testing across browsers, devices, and publisher environments to catch and fix technical issues before campaign go-live. ### **Innovation & AI Workflow** - **Leverage** generative AI tools into daily workflows for both visual exploration and code assistance. - **Bridge** design and dev perspectives across the team, growing your technical skills while delivering polished creative work. ## **What Will You Bring to the Team?** ### **Must-Haves (The Baseline Bar)** - **Core Experience:** Foundational background in digital graphic design, UI/UX, or digital media. - **Design Toolkit:** Proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Photoshop and After Effects). - **Front-End Development:** Solid grasp of HTML5, CSS3 (animations/transitions), and vanilla JavaScript (ES6+). - **Format & Tech Literacy:** Understanding of display vs. video formats, basic IAB standards, VAST/VPAID tags, and third-party tracking setup. - **QA & Execution:** Strong detail orientation with an eager mindset to test, troubleshoot, and optimize work across browsers and devices. ### **Nice-to-Haves (The Performance Multiplier)** - Prior exposure to ad platforms, dynamic creative tools, or demo environments (e.g., Teads Studio). - Curiosity and hands-on familiarity using Generative AI tools (Midjourney, ChatGPT, Copilot, etc.) inside design and coding processes. ## **What You’ll Get** At Teads, your scope is bigger than your title. Here is what you can count on in return: - **Meaningful scope & real ownership** — work with global strategic impact and trusted autonomy. - **Global exposure and genuinely complex challenges** at real scale — 2.2Bn users / month and 18Bn ad opportunities / day. - **Smart, ambitious peers** across 30+ markets in a collaborative setup. - **A genuinely human culture** — high care alongside high accountability. - **Real investment in your growth** — structured mentorship, coaching, courses, workshops, certifications, and leadership development programs. At Teads, your impact travels ***further***. *The pay for this position is USD $60,000 annually including on target earnings. The actual amount offered may be higher or lower, based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, job-related knowledge, skills, and abilities. In addition to salary, you may be eligible for our competitive benefits and perks to support you and your family as part of Teads’ total rewards package.* *Teads utilizes or may utilize artificial intelligence to assist in the screening and selection process to ensure an efficient and fair evaluation of candidates.* #LI-Hybrid **Life at Teads** At Teads, we don’t just offer jobs. We blend creativity, technology, and cutting-edge data to shape the future of media. As a Teadster, you’ll work alongside smart humans, collaborate with meaningful brands, and leverage advanced AI and automation to redefine how advertising works in a transparent, privacy-first world. We are builders, innovators, and future-thinkers. If you are excited by the evolution of technology and ready to embrace the future of AI-driven media, you belong here. **Why Join Us?** - **A New Era of Media:** We’ve merged two open internet category leaders, Outbrain and Teads to create a unified omnichannel platform. Together, we drive results from branding to performance across CTV, mobile, and web. - **AI-Powered Innovation:** We actively embrace AI and next-gen technology to solve complex industry challenges. We look for curious minds who aren't afraid to experiment, adapt, and lead the charge into the future of digital advertising. - **Growth & High Performance:** Our culture is dynamic, global, and built on excellence. We are committed to your success, offering the modern tools, mentorship, and development opportunities you need to thrive. - **Belonging & Impact:** We foster a welcoming, diverse environment where approachable, resourceful, and passionate people excel. Through our employee-ledEmployee Resource Groups (ERGs), you can actively drive change in areas like sustainability, women’s empowerment, charitable initiatives, and DE&I. **Equal Opportunity Employer** Teads is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion at all stages of recruitment and employment. We celebrate unique perspectives and are dedicated to building a team that reflects the global communities we serve.

# **Why Harvey** At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. # **Role Overview** As a Software Engineer, Intern (Summer 2027) on the Engineering team at Harvey, you’ll work alongside experienced engineers on projects that power our AI products. You’ll collaborate with our Product, AI, Legal, and GTM teams to help build secure, intuitive systems that deliver real value to our customers. This 12 or 16 week internship is ideal for students who are curious, motivated, and excited to learn how modern application-layer and GenAI products are built. You’ll gain hands-on experience across the stack, contribute to real features, and see how your work impacts users in production. We're currently hiring Winter 2027 interns in Toronto and Summer 2027 interns in New York and San Francisco across multiple teams and roles, including Frontend, Backend, Full-Stack, Infrastructure, and Applied AI intern roles. Your interests & experience will be factored into our team matching process, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn about teams across Harvey including Agents, Applied AI, Assistant, Enterprise, Infrastructure, Mobile, Vault and many others. # **What You'll Do** You will: - Own a project end-to-end from coding and testing to deploying it to production, and presenting your work to peers and leaders across the company. - Write clean, maintainable code that meets our team's standards. You'll use AI-assisted development tools daily, and you’ll own the quality of everything you ship—AI-generated or not. - Build real knowledge of the systems you support and the users they serve, bringing that perspective into product discussions. - Debug problems in your area, follow escalation procedures, and treat quality as urgent. Our users are lawyers doing high-stakes work. - Collaborate with your team through code review, pair programming, design reviews and technical documentation. - Depending on your team, you could work on retrieval over large document collections, interfaces for collaborating with AI systems, multi-region compute infrastructure, enterprise agents, or secure systems for sensitive client data. You'll also evaluate frontier models alongside senior engineers. # **What You Have** - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in computer science, engineering, or a related field with a graduation date of December 2027 or later. - Able to work from our New York or San Francisco offices during our summer cohort, based on your academic schedule. Relocation support is available. - Previous internship experience is required. - **Technical foundation.** Strong proficiency in one or more languages (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, or similar) and solid general computer science knowledge. - **Decisiveness.** You have a bias toward action. You've built something start to finish in coursework, a personal project, or in a past internship, and you know the difference between a decision you should make yourself and one worth getting feedback on. You'd rather move and correct course than stall. - **Simplicity.** You can explain a complex technical idea in plain language, whether or not the person you're explaining it to is an engineer. You look for the simplest solution that works, and you know when added complexity is worth it. - **Job's Not Finished.** You aren't satisfied when something merely works. You proactively seek out feedback, act on it, and keep pushing after the assignment is technically complete. Internship experience specifically at an early-stage startup is a plus. - **AI Forward.** Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and curious about building LLMs into your own coding workflow. *Our interview process includes AI-assisted coding sessions; you'll be expected to work with AI tools the way you would on the job.* # **Compensation** - **Pay:** $62/hr-$72/hr in San Francisco and New York ### **Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices [**[**here**](https://www.notion.so/harveyai/Harvey-Candidate-Privacy-Policies-319ac3fcdd7a803bb807d5094f249922)**].** #LI-LW1 *Harvey is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.* We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made by emailing [accommodations@harvey.ai](mailto:accommodations@harvey.ai)

About the Role: The Special Projects Group of KPFF is growing and looking for an ambitious and initiative-driven Junior, Senior or Graduate School level Structural Engineering student for a summer internship in the Tacoma Office of our Special Projects Group. The Structural Engineering Summer Internship being offered is approximately 40 hours a week for up to 90 days depending on candidate’s availability. Job responsibilities will vary depending on the project and individual intern. Our work leans toward heavy civil, transportation and highways, structural, industrial and waterfront infrastructure throughout the US with a focus on the West Coast and Pacific Northwest regions. We frequently function as prime consultants and are tasked with solving unusual, multi-discipline challenges that require an innovative and team-oriented approach. We often work closely with contractors on alternative delivery projects, including design-build contracts. What You’ll Be Doing: Assist a structural engineer with various tasks associated with the project design, including calculations, member sizing and detailing, documentation, plan production and review, and cost estimating. Assist with project site visits. The applicant may be required to navigate through a jobsite and must comply with all Company and Site safety requirements in the office and on the jobsite. Who We’re Looking For: Ability to work collaboratively with project team members and clients on a variety of projects Detail oriented and desire for continued learning Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in civil engineering. Willingness to work on a variety of projects Structural analysis coursework, including moment and shear diagrams, load calculations, load paths, and mechanics of materials. Concrete, steel, foundation engineering, and/or timber coursework is a plus. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Programs Excellent teamwork, communication, and interpersonal skills. Interest in pursuing a career as a structural engineer after college. Example of Projects: Ports, harbors and light industrial related projects on the waterfront for a variety of public and private clients Highway and roadway structures engineering, including bridges, retaining walls, and draining structures Container terminal infrastructure design Marinas & Ferry terminals Rail infrastructure Work done by other disciplines and supported by structures, including: Fisheries Engineering; hatchery building and pond design, diversion and intake structures; Fish passage replacement Stormwater conveyance and treatment and design Environmental cleanup and habitat restoration Waterway dredging Physical Demands and Work Environment: Duties are primarily conducted in a standard office setting, requiring prolonged periods of sitting at a desk or computer table. Occasionally may be required to lift objects weighing up to 15 lbs. Occasionally visiting project locations and performing field inspections which may involve walking, standing, kneeling, or navigating uneven terrain. Culture and Benefits: Join KPFF for a career adventure that celebrates your expertise and fuels your development. Here, autonomy and innovation converge, empowering you to tackle complex challenges and blossom into a consulting trailblazer. Our culture fosters teamwork, ownership, and common values, ensuring that your accomplishments are celebrated, and your career trajectory is in your hands. At KPFF, we're not just coworkers; we're a vibrant community fueled by collaborative creativity, offering you the chance to leave a lasting mark on pioneering projects. Compensation: The salary for this role is competitive and will be determined based on the candidate's experience, education, and skills. The expected range for a qualified candidate is $27-$32 per hour. About Us KPFF Special Projects Group Since 1996, KPFF's Special Projects Group has been at the forefront of addressing specialized challenges in project development. With over 150+ team members in three offices strategically located in Long Beach, CA, Tacoma, WA, and Seattle, WA, our approach combines dedicated project managers, a skilled technical team, and a commitment to innovation. We offer a comprehensive range of services including civil, structural, and mechanical engineering, machinery design, construction and project management, and planning services. Join us at KPFF Special Projects Group and be part of a dynamic team driving innovation and excellence in project delivery. Our 1,500+ professionals in 36 offices nationwide thrive in a decentralized structure, offering abundant flexibility and numerous opportunities for professional growth. At KPFF, join a legacy of excellence where every team member has the opportunity to contribute to innovative solutions and impactful projects. description: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. Anduril is seeking Industrial Engineering Interns to join our summer internship program. As an IE intern, you will work alongside a team of Industrial Engineers who will provide guidance and mentorship while you work to optimize Anduril’s manufacturing operations for best-in-class quality, reliability, speed, and asset utilization.
