*Full-time Co-op (≥6 months) · In person · Boston, MA (Seaport)* **About Kernal Biologics, Inc.** Kernal Bio is a venture-backed therapeutics company engineering cells inside the body using AI-designed, selective mRNA and targeted LNP technology. By developing in vivo CAR-T therapies, Kernal Bio is advancing precision treatments for autoimmune diseases and blood cancers. The company was founded by experts from MIT, Harvard, Merck, and BMS, and its leadership team brings a track record of three FDA-approved therapies and over 120 patents. With support from leading investors, including Hummingbird Ventures, Amgen Ventures, Y Combinator, and HBM, Kernal Bio is transforming the future of cell therapy design and delivery. **Job Summary** We are seeking a highly motivated researcher to fill a Co-op position on our Synthetic Biology team, supporting the design, production, and in vitro testing of mRNA therapeutics. This is a hands-on, bench-based role: you will work with mammalian cell lines every day, transfect and test mRNAs, and support DNA template and mRNA production, while learning cutting-edge mRNA and synthetic biology technologies as an integral member of the team. You will perform experimental research, document it, and present your results. **Key Responsibilities** - Maintain human and murine cell lines: sterile technique, passaging, cell counting and viability, cryopreservation - Transfect IVT mRNAs and LNP-formulated mRNAs into mammalian cells and quantify expression by flow cytometry - Support DNA template design and construction (primer design, PCR, DNA assembly, plasmid prep and QC) - Support internal mRNA production and quality analysis (IVT, purification, Nanodrop/Bioanalyzer) - Execute, document (electronic lab notebook), and present experiments; learn to work with minimal supervision and generate decision-making data **Qualifications** - B.S. or M.S. student in Biology, Biological Engineering, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or a related field - **Required:** hands-on mammalian cell culture experience at the bench (sterile technique, passaging, transfection, viability assays), not coursework alone - ≥6 months of previous laboratory experience strongly preferred - Experience with molecular biology techniques (PCR, cloning, gel electrophoresis) and/or assays such as flow cytometry is a plus - Reliable, detail-oriented, and able to work full-time (35-40 hours/week) on site in Boston's Seaport throughout the ≥6-month Co-op - Eagerness to grow and develop as a scientist **Benefits** - Compensation: $20-25/hour based on experience - Free monthly subway pass - Free Bluebikes membership - Gym membership support - On-site cafeteria **Equal Employment Opportunity** Kernal is dedicated to providing a diverse work environment and is committed to equal employment opportunity for all its employees and qualified applicants. We do not discriminate in employment practices for reasons of race, color, national origin, age, gender, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, religion, disability, or any other legally protected status. Kernal will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

description: Position Summary Acuren is currently recruiting for a Junior Cathodic Protection Tech for our Salt Lake City, UT and Magnolia,TX location. The Intermediate CP Technician is responsible for planning and performing technical duties that support assigned projects. Job tasks include but are not limited to: testing, evaluating, remediation and installation of cathodic protection systems. The Intermediate CP Technician works independently with moderate supervision or as part of a project team and follows procedures and specifications applicable to the job scope. Responsibilities Follow applicable procedures and standards to diagnose and troubleshoot cathodic protection and AC mitigation system deficiencies, conduct various types of field surveys and assessments, and complete installations Maintain detailed field notes and provide field level assessment to inspection results and recommendations Sketch various CP system components and electrical schematics Provide technical assistance to other divisions within the company Conduct and/or supervise various field tests (ex. structure potential, CIPS, AC, DCVG, ACVG, ACCA, line locating, soil resistivity, current requirements, etc.) under minimal support from senior team member Organize and review data gathered, prepare charts and tables Field test equipment, software and testing procedures; log results and communicate to development team(s); provide issue resolution recommendations to development team(s) Contribute to internal initiatives as required Provide training and mentorship to junior staff Contribute to the continual improvement quality process Conform to corporate, client, and government operating and safety procedures Develop trusted business relationships with existing and prospective clients Additional duties as assigned Requirements 2+ years in pipeline integrity or oil and gas industry1+ years in cathodic protection or AC mitigation NACE CP2 certification Rectifier training or experience Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat Benefits Competitive salary Medical, dental, vision, and supplemental insurance 401K Plan Paid Holidays Paid Time Off Company Overview Acuren is a trusted, single source provider of technology-enabled asset protection solutions used to evaluate the structural integrity of critical energy, industrial and public infrastructures. Committed to delivering a Higher Level of Reliability , Acuren provides an unrivaled spectrum of capabilities including inspection, traditional and advanced NDE/NDT, failure analysis, rope access, materials engineering, field engineering, reliability engineering, drones, robotics, V-Deck and condition-based monitoring services. Our work is critical to the integrity and safety of industrial firms, including petroleum refinery, pipeline, power generation, pulp & paper, mining, pharmaceutical, aerospace and automotive industries. Acuren employs over 4,000 dedicated professionals supporting the mechanical integrity and inspection programs of the world’s largest industrial segments. Acuren is a market leader. Our formula for success is straightforward: be capable locally, with certified and well-equipped personnel supported by trained, experienced leaders. Continuing to build on a strong heritage of safety, quality and professionalism, Acuren strives to maintain incident free work environments, pursues advanced technical developments, and supports reliability programs that are valued by clients and employees. #LI-MC1

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality. ## About the Role As a Robot Software Engineer Intern, you'll work on the software foundation that keeps our robots running. You'll own real projects on the software platform stack: ranging from on-robot software, networking and communication infrastructure, data collection pipelines, telemetry, teleoperation, inference infra, developer tooling etc., and see your impact run on physical robots by the end of your internship. You'll sit with the engineers who build our robots and ship code that the team depends on every day. ## What You'll Do - Contribute to the networking and communication infrastructure connecting onboard robot systems to each other, to the cloud, and to teleoperation and monitoring systems - Help build data collection pipelines that capture sensor, telemetry, and behavioral data from the robot and upload it reliably to cloud storage for model training - Work on telemetry and observability systems that give the team real-time visibility into robot health and field performance - Build internal tooling that accelerates robot software development: deployment pipelines, logging, debugging tools, and field testing utilities - Support bring-up and field testing on live hardware, debugging issues across the onboard software stack - Collaborate with ML, perception, and control engineers to keep onboard systems reliable and training data high quality - Automate internal workflows to improve execution efficiency of the Rhoda teams ## What We're Looking For - Assist in the development of student athletes in alignment with the mission, vision, and values of Creighton University and the Creighton University Athletic Department. Meet individually with student-athletes to help them develop learning strategies, goal setting, communication skills, and time management skills. Communicate and collaborate with support staff members (sports medicine, strength and conditioning, nutrition, and counseling) and coaching staffs to identify any potential issues and ensure student athlete is provided appropriate resources and support for academic and athletic success. Utilize the University online course platform to monitor at-risk student athletes, and provide appropriate interventions (study hall, tutoring, meetings, etc.) to address any academic issues. Create and distribute missed class travel letters for assigned teams. Provide appropriate advocacy for student athletes by communicating and following up with University faculty and administration. Generate and distribute weekly academic reports to coaches that include the tracking of weekly study hall hours, academic updates, and any current or potential issues with student athletes. Communicate all important information regarding student athlete support services to student athletes, coaches, and other athletic department staff members. Additional duties including but not limited to: Serves as a resource for coaches, prospective student-athletes, and parents during the recruitment process by creating and providing academic-specific recruiting materials, meeting with recruits and families during campus visits, and advising on AP and dual enrollment courses to take prior to enrollment at Creighton. Identify and promote athletic tutors to serve in elevated positions including but not limited to walk-in tutors, study group leaders, virtual paper editors, and peer mentors. role: Vice President, General Manager & Campus Lead, Devens
description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. **Position Summary** The General Manager, Devens is the senior leader accountable for the end-to-end performance, compliance, and strategic direction of BMS’s large-scale commercial biologics Global Business Unit (GBU) operations at Devens, and serves as the Campus Lead for the full Devens site, spanning both the GBU Biologics organization and the Cell Therapy business unit. This role oversees all GBU Biologics site operations at Devens – from cell culture and manufacturing sciences & technology (MS&T) to large-scale commercial drug substance production – with full accountability for talent development, safety, quality, regulatory compliance, supply reliability, and cost management across the Biologics organization. As Campus Lead, the General Manager also owns end-to-end site services and shared infrastructure – Site Engineering, Environmental Health & Safety, Security, and Facilities – that support both the GBU Biologics and Cell Therapy business units operating on the Devens campus, ensuring both organizations have the capacity, capabilities, and infrastructure to deliver on their respective missions. A defining focus of this role over the next several years is leading the transformation and integration of the GBU Biologics and Cell Therapy business units at Devens – building a single, unified campus operating model, governance structure, and culture that harmonizes site services, talent, and ways of working across both modalities. This includes championing innovative, digitally enabled and AI-driven transformation – advanced analytics, automation, digital twins, and other Industry 4.0 capabilities – to reimagine site processes, accelerate integration, and establish Devens as a “smart campus” that delivers sustainable competitive advantage. The General Manager also serves as the primary representative of the Devens campus both within the global manufacturing network (driving adoption of world-class standards and sharing best practices across BMS’s network of manufacturing sites) and externally (engaging with regulatory authorities, government officials, industry partners, and the local community to uphold the Company’s reputation and advance strategic initiatives). This position is pivotal in ensuring that the Devens campus remains a world-class, innovative biologics and cell therapy manufacturing hub that reliably delivers life-saving medicines to patients while successfully transforming into a single, integrated, future-ready campus. **Key Responsibilities** In this role, the General Manager will provide strategic, technical, and operational leadership across a broad range of functional domains and both business units at Devens. Key responsibilities include: - **Strategic & Enterprise Leadership:** Develop and execute Devens’ long-range strategy in alignment with BMS’s global manufacturing network, GBU pipeline plans, and Cell Therapy growth objectives. Ensure the site’s capabilities evolve in step with enterprise needs, including readiness for new biologics modalities and Cell Therapy platform expansion. Represent Devens in Product Development and Supply (PDS) and Cell Therapy governance forums, and in enterprise-wide manufacturing network forums (e.g., Factory Level Optimized Work (FLOW), best practice standardization). Anticipate industry trends and build site-level strategies and contingency plans that maintain a competitive edge for both business units. - **Biologics Manufacturing Operations & Technical Excellence:** Oversee all GBU Biologics drug substance manufacturing operations at Devens, ensuring reliable supply of high-quality biologics to meet commercial demand and clinical pipeline needs. Maintain rigorous standards for safety, quality, and efficiency across cell culture, purification, and manufacturing sciences & technology (MS&T) operations. Drive effective technology transfer and scale-up of new processes, enabling rapid industrialization of new biologic therapies while minimizing risk and optimizing time-to-market. - **Campus Leadership & Cross-Business Unit Governance:** Serve as the Campus Lead for the full Devens site, with end-to-end accountability for shared infrastructure and services – Site Engineering, EHS, Security, and Facilities – that enable both the GBU Biologics and Cell Therapy business units to operate safely, reliably, and efficiently. Establish and chair a unified campus governance model and leadership forum that brings GBU Biologics and Cell Therapy leadership together to align priorities, resolve cross-business unit resource and capacity trade-offs, and represent one Devens voice to the enterprise. - **Site Transformation & Business Unit Integration:** Lead the multi-year transformation and integration of the GBU Biologics and Cell Therapy business units at Devens into a single, unified campus operating model. Design and execute the integration roadmap – covering organizational structure, ways of working, shared services, talent, and culture – in close partnership with GBU and Cell Therapy senior leadership. Serve as the primary change agent for the transformation, building momentum, managing risk, and ensuring business continuity for both business units throughout the integration period. - **Quality, EHS & Regulatory Compliance:** Champion a world-class safety and quality culture across the full Devens campus. Ensure full compliance with global GMP standards, EHS regulations, and all regulatory requirements across biologics and cell therapy manufacturing processes. Serve as the site’s executive sponsor during regulatory inspections and audits, maintaining a state of constant inspection readiness. Model and enforce behaviors that prioritize patient safety, product quality, and a safe working environment, aiming for zero safety incidents and the highest levels of regulatory confidence. - **Digital Transformation & AI-Driven Innovation:** Lead Devens’ journey toward becoming a smart, digitally enabled campus. Drive the adoption of AI/ML, predictive analytics, automation, robotics, and other Industry 4.0 technologies to improve manufacturing efficiency, agility, and reliability, and to accelerate the site’s transformation and integration agenda. Champion AI and advanced analytics for predictive maintenance, yield optimization, and proactive deviation management. Partner with BMS Digital and IT teams to pilot and scale enterprise digital initiatives, ensuring the workforce is trained and adaptable to new digital tools. - **Capital Projects & Operational Excellence**: Spearhead the planning and execution of major capital projects and technical upgrades at the Devens campus, integrating modular facility design, single-use technologies, and automation to increase flexibility and throughput for both business units. Oversee operational readiness for new facilities and equipment – from commissioning to validation and ramp-up. Continuously improve operational processes through a Lean and Six Sigma approach, driving productivity improvements, cost reduction, and waste elimination while protecting product quality and supply consistency. - **Talent & People Leadership:** Foster a high-performance, inclusive culture that attracts, develops, and retains top talent across both business units. Lead and mentor the site’s multi-disciplinary leadership team, ensuring all functional areas work toward common goals. Build a future-ready workforce with strong technical expertise in biologics and/or cell therapy and digital proficiency. Act as a role model for BMS’s values and leadership behaviors, promoting cross-functional collaboration and a culture of innovation, especially through the integration period. - **Financial & Business Accountability:** Manage the site’s P&L and financial performance for GBU Biologics operations, and oversee the shared campus services budget supporting both business units. Develop and oversee annual operating budgets and long-range financial plans, setting ambitious yet achievable targets. Rigorously track the return on investment (ROI) for capital projects, digital innovations, and integration initiatives, ensuring robust financial controls and forecasting. - **External Engagement & Stakeholder Management:** Serve as the key liaison between the Devens campus and external stakeholders, including government officials, regulatory agencies, industry associations, and the local community. Proactively engage with health authorities to build trust and ensure open communication. Champion BMS’s reputation in the community by supporting corporate social responsibility initiatives and upholding high standards of environmental stewardship and ethical operation. **Qualifications & Experience** - **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biochemistry, or a related field is required. An advanced degree (M.S., Ph.D., or MBA) is strongly preferred, especially with specialization in biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences, or business management. - **Experience:** Approximately 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical manufacturing, with significant leadership in large-scale biologics drug substance operations. Experience introducing and scaling up new modalities from late-stage development into full commercial production is highly desirable; experience with cell therapy or other advanced/complex therapy manufacturing is a strong plus. A track record of leading large-scale organizational transformations or business unit integrations (e.g., site consolidations, combining business units, network integrations) is required. - **Technical & Compliance Knowledge:** Deep knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, EMA, and other global health authorities) is essential, as is familiarity with EHS regulations and best practices for biologics and cell therapy manufacturing environments. Proven experience hosting or leading regulatory inspections and interacting with regulatory agencies is expected. Experience with large capital project planning and execution, including facility expansions or introduction of new production lines, is required, as well as strong understanding of financial management processes and P&L responsibility for a manufacturing site or business unit. - **Digital & AI-Driven Transformation:** Demonstrated expertise leading innovative, digitally and AI-driven transformations, including AI/ML implementation in manufacturing operations, digital twins and/or simulation technologies, predictive analytics, automation, and robotics. A proven ability to reimagine ways of working through emerging technology, and to build the organizational capability needed to sustain a digitally enabled site. - **Leadership:** Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional, multicultural teams and develop well-integrated, high-performing organizations across multiple business units. Excellent leadership qualities are needed, including strategic thinking, results-driven decision making, and the ability to influence across executive levels and functions. Exceptional communication skills and stakeholder management capabilities (including engagement with external partners, government officials, and regulatory bodies) are critical. The ideal candidate will have experience managing multi-site or large, complex sites and a strong grasp of the legal, cultural, and organizational nuances of leading in a global, matrixed environment. The role demands a leader who exemplifies a true enterprise mindset — prioritizing the success of the broader campus, business units, and BMS network above any single function — with high accountability for performance, scientific and technical curiosity, a passion for innovation and digital advancement, and the ability to inspire and transform organizational culture through complex, multi-year change. - **Enterprise Mindset & Change Leadership:** Proven track record leading complex, multi-year organizational transformations and business unit integrations, with the judgment to sequence change, manage ambiguity, and sustain safety, quality, and supply performance through disruption. Skilled at building unified governance and culture across previously separate organizations, aligning stakeholders around a shared campus vision, and balancing enterprise priorities against individual business unit needs. You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Supplemental Instruction (SI) is an academic support program that targets historically difficult courses. SI sessions are regularly scheduled, out-of-class review sessions for all students enrolled in a targeted course. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Work in-person in the designated CACE rooms at Lamond-Riggs, providing academic support (supplemental instruction, tutoring, etc.) to students. Report immediately to the Coordinator of the Center for Academic and Career Excellence when critical issues arise. Attend and participate in SI Leader group meetings as scheduled. Adhere to the policies and procedures of the University and the Center for Academic and Career Excellence. Demonstrate professionalism, responsibility, punctuality, and academic integrity. Maintain privacy and confidentiality of student information, including course progress and performance. Helping faculty and staff to facilitate weekend workshops Helping to promote C.A.C.E. at in-building events Other duties as assigned. REQUIRED COMPETENCIES Must have high competency in NO LESS than two subjects (ex: Accounting and Eng/Writing) A SI leader must demonstrate an ability to quickly establish rapport and communicate well with students. A SI leader must have completed the course(s) in which they wish to tutor, earning an A. Excellent interpersonal communication skills and ease in relating to people from varying educational, cultural, and social backgrounds. Excellent level of responsibility, reliability, and punctuality. Model appropriate professional attitude and behaviors toward faculty, staff, and students. STANDARDS & EXPECTATIONS: Expectations of the job: Work consists of a variety of complex interrelated tasks. The Incumbent is expected to function with considerable independence on all assignments and to use initiative and seasoned judgment in arriving at sound conclusions and recommendations. Recurring contacts are made with students, staff members, faculty, administrators, and the public, as well as with staff at the College. Contacts are established to open channels of communication and acquire information for decision-making and dissemination to others. Normal physical dexterity is required. The work is generally performed in an office setting. Development and Counseling: Employee is expected to participate in activities that will help in the development of his/her career and help in the performance of the job. An employee may seek counseling from the immediate supervisor. Training: Training is available to help improve the skill and knowledge level, and for updates on the latest techniques, methods, and theories that are used in the industry. Knowledge of UDC Rules and Regulations: The position requires a solid understanding of the policies and procedures of the Board of Trustees, the University, as well as applicable Federal and D.C. government laws. The university provides all the training required by OSHA to ensure employee safety. The University of the District of Columbia is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). We are seeking a **Robotics GNC Intern / Co-op** to join our GNC team in developing the sensing, localization, and control software for a novel hull-crawling marine robot. You will work hands-on with real robot hardware, sensors, and field data to help turn prototype autonomy software into a reliable system that can operate outside of the lab. Your work may include characterizing sensors, analyzing vehicle data, improving localization and control algorithms, building simulation and test infrastructure, and validating software through lab and field testing. CRABI is building autonomous robots that live aboard commercial ships and clean their hulls while they are underway. Marine biofouling creates enormous hydrodynamic drag, forcing ships to burn more fuel to maintain speed. By keeping hulls continuously clean, our robots can eliminate a major source of wasted energy across the global fleet—reducing fuel consumption, operating costs, and ultimately maritime CO2 emissions by more than 100 million tons per year. Doing that requires robots that can reliably navigate and operate on the hull of a moving ship, underwater, for long periods without human intervention. Our GNC team owns the software that turns noisy sensors and imperfect hardware into a robot that knows where it is, knows how it is moving, and can safely execute its mission. As an intern or co-op, you will work directly alongside our GNC engineers and the broader CRABI engineering team. You will have meaningful ownership over the systems you work on and will be expected to test your work on real hardware, analyze the results, and iterate quickly. This role is a particularly good fit for someone who enjoys the intersection of software, sensors, physics, and physical machines. The internship/co-op requires a strong safety mindset when performing lab and field testing. **Job Responsibilities:** - Develop and test localization, state estimation, navigation, and control software for an autonomous marine robot. - Work with real sensor data to characterize noise, drift, bias, latency, and other behaviors that affect vehicle performance. - Apply first-principles and physics-based modeling to understand sensor and vehicle behavior and improve estimation and control performance. - Build data analysis and visualization tools that turn robot logs into actionable engineering insights. - Develop automated tests and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) infrastructure to validate GNC software before deployment. - Define, conduct, and participate in tuning and testing of robotic systems in the lab and on the vehicle. - Investigate failures using logs, telemetry, experiments, and hardware debugging, then implement and validate fixes. - Collaborate with mechanical, electrical, firmware, and test engineers to integrate localization and control software with vehicle hardware. - Participate in occasional field testing and travel, including testing on and around marine vessels. **Required Qualifications:** - Currently pursuing a degree in robotics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a related technical field. - Familiarity with robotics fundamentals including state estimation, navigation, controls, or motion planning. - Experience programming in Python and/or C++. - Experience working in Linux and debugging software systems. - Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2 and common robotics development tools. - Experience analyzing time-series data using filtering, signal processing, statistics, or similar techniques. - Experience with software testing, simulation, or integration testing. - Familiarity with version control using Git. - Comfortable working hands-on with physical hardware and debugging problems that cross the boundary between software, sensors, electronics, and mechanics. **Preferred Qualifications:** - Experience integrating sensors into a robot, vehicle, UAV, or other physical system. - Experience with sensor fusion, Kalman filtering, inertial navigation, wheel odometry, SLAM, or related estimation techniques. - Experience with ROS 2 tools such as Gazebo, RViz, Foxglove, rosbag, or similar simulation and data-analysis tools. - Experience developing Software-in-the-Loop (SIL), Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL), or automated test systems. - Experience debugging complex robotic systems by analyzing logs and experimental data. - Ability to take a partially defined robotics problem, clarify the requirements, implement a solution, and validate it experimentally. - Experience with wheeled robot guidance, localization, or control. - Experience with marine robotics, field robotics, autonomous vehicles, aerospace systems, or other hardware operating in difficult environments. - Significant hands-on experience on a student engineering team such as FSAE Driverless, rocketry, UAVs, BattleBots/BattleBots-style robotics, or similar. ### **Export Control Requirement** CRABI Robotics designs equipment subject to the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), and this position requires immediate, unrestricted access to technical information controlled under ECCN 8A002/8E001. Under the EAR, sharing that information with certain foreign nationals requires a license from the U.S. Department of Commerce. Because the position requires access from the first day of employment, CRABI does not generally seek export licenses for this position. Accordingly, applicants for this position must be either (a) a U.S. person — a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident, or an individual granted asylum or refugee status — or (b) a national of a country for which the EAR does not require a license for this technology. This tool identifies whether your experience appears to meet, partially meet, or not meet each stated requirement, and it provides supporting evidence from your application for every assessment it makes. *What the AI does not do:* The AI does not make hiring decisions. Perform system clean-up, data validation, and ongoing maintenance to ensure master data, planning assumptions, product attributes, lead times, and supply parameters are reliable. - Assist with the creation, testing, implementation, and documentation of supply planning projects, tools, reports, and process improvements. - Partner with Raw Materials, Product Development, Production, and vendor teams to validate material readiness, sourcing details, production timelines, and supply constraints. - Assist with what-if analyses to assess the impact of changes in demand, assortment, sourcing, capacity, MOQ, lead times, or delivery dates. - Basic understanding of supply chain concepts, including demand forecasting, bills of materials, production lead times, MOQ, capacity, inventory, and seasonal planning. - Demonstrated interest in systems, data quality, process improvement, and project implementation. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and global partners. - Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt in a fast-paced, seasonal environment. - role: Associate Director of Site Operations - Care Campus
description: About the Role The Skid Row Care Campus is a comprehensive, low-barrier service center providing individuals experiencing homelessness with access to hygiene facilities, case management, health and behavioral health services, and connections to housing and other essential resources. The Campus offers a safe, welcoming, and trauma-informed environment that promotes dignity, stability, and pathways to long-term housing. The Associate Director of Site Operations is a senior operational leader responsible for the day-to-day readiness and coordination of the Care Campus. The position oversees Safety, Hygiene Services, and other assigned operational functions and directly leads the managers responsible for those areas. This role ensures that Campus operations are appropriately staffed, coordinated, supplied, and prepared to support safe, reliable, participant-centered services. Key areas of accountability include staffing and coverage, participant flow, Safety and Hygiene operations, emergency preparedness, incident response, facilities coordination, third-party security coordination, and continuity of operations. Key Responsibilities Campus Operations & Readiness Lead the day-to-day coordination of assigned Campus operations and maintain visibility into staffing, participant volume, service demand, site conditions, safety concerns, and other operational factors. Ensure effective opening, operating, shift-transition, and closing procedures across operational areas. Resolve significant cross-functional operational issues and maintain continuity of essential services during staffing shortages, facility disruptions, emergencies, and other unexpected situations. Identify operational barriers that affect participant access, safety, service delivery, or employee effectiveness and drive timely solutions. People Leadership & Workforce Management Provide direct supervision, coaching, development, and performance management to operational managers. Establish clear expectations and accountability for staffing, scheduling, attendance, call-offs, timekeeping, training, performance, and routine employee relations. Monitor vacancies, overtime, turnover, attendance trends, and other workforce indicators that may affect service delivery. Establish staffing and contingency systems that support reliable operations seven days per week, including periods of high call-offs, vacancies, emergencies, and increased participant volume. Ensure shift leaders understand their authority and escalation responsibilities when senior leadership is not on site. Safety & Emergency Operations Provide leadership oversight of the Care Campus Safety function and Safety management. Ensure appropriate Safety staffing, deployment, de-escalation practices, incident response, documentation, communication, and leadership coverage. Promote a trauma-informed approach to safety that protects participants, employees, visitors, and property while maintaining participant dignity. Serve as a key operational leader during medical emergencies, overdoses, behavioral health crises, fire, earthquake, utility outages, workplace violence, security incidents, and major service disruptions. Review significant incidents and trends and ensure appropriate corrective action, operational follow-up, and preparedness. Hygiene Services & Participant Flow Provide leadership oversight of Hygiene Services and ensure shower, restroom, and laundry services are appropriately staffed, supplied, safe, sanitary, accessible, and effectively managed. Monitor service capacity, wait times, participant flow, sanitation, and operational barriers affecting access. Coordinate operational strategies across waiting areas, common spaces, hygiene areas, entrances, exits, and other high-volume locations. Ensure operational practices support respectful, trauma-informed, participant-centered engagement and effective connections to program services when needs are identified. Facilities, Security & Infrastructure Serve as the primary site-level liaison with organizational Operations and Facilities leadership regarding building and infrastructure needs. Coordinate operational planning around repairs, inspections, utilities, equipment, maintenance, vendors, and facility disruptions. Develop temporary operating plans when physical spaces, building systems, equipment, or utilities are unavailable. Coordinate with organizational Operations regarding third-party security, including site protocols, emergency procedures, handoffs, performance concerns, and emerging coverage needs. Performance, Compliance & Continuous Improvement Monitor operational indicators related to staffing, service availability, incidents, safety, hygiene utilization, and other assigned areas. Maintain accurate operational documentation and support funder monitoring, audits, site reviews, corrective-action plans, and compliance activities. Use staffing information, incident trends, participant feedback, manager input, and operational observations to identify recurring risks and improve systems. Partner across Programs, Facilities, Human Resources, Compliance, Finance, Contracts, IT, Data, Safety, and other functions to resolve complex operational issues. What You'll Bring Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, human services, nonprofit management, operations management, or a related field preferred. At least five years of progressively responsible experience in operations, homeless services, social services, healthcare, residential services, facilities-based programs, or a related environment. At least three years of supervisory or management experience , including responsibility for managers, supervisors, or large frontline teams. Experience overseeing complex operations in a high-volume, extended-hours, 24/7, residential, shelter, healthcare, hospitality, or comparable environment strongly preferred. Experience managing large frontline teams and complex staffing and scheduling needs strongly preferred. Experience with safety operations, emergency response, incident management, facilities coordination, and vendor management preferred. Strong operational leadership, workforce-management, organizational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Ability to establish clear systems, expectations, accountability, procedures, and escalation pathways. Ability to balance operational effectiveness and safety with participant dignity, trauma-informed practices, and participant-centered services. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Digital Communications Intern - R Street Institute
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. The [R Street Institute](https://www.rstreet.org/) seeks a Digital Communications Intern to support its digital communications, multimedia, and online engagement efforts. This role will assist with social media, graphic design, video production, website publishing, digital marketing, and analytics. The ideal candidate is a versatile digital generalist who can take a piece of content, such as an article, video, podcast, or event, and help turn it into a strong package of digital products across multiple platforms. This internship can be completed remotely or in person in our Washington, D.C. office. ### Responsibilities - Draft social media copy for R Street research, events, videos, podcasts, and media appearances. - Assist with editing short-form and long-form video content, including captions, clips, and other platform-specific content. - Create and edit branded graphics, thumbnails, and other social media assets. - Publish and update articles, videos, podcasts, event pages, and staff bios in WordPress. - Assist with social media, website, and video analytics and reporting. - Help organize digital assets, content calendars, and shared files. - Proofread public-facing content for accuracy, formatting, links, and branding consistency. ### Qualifications - Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills. - Excellent attention to detail. - Familiarity with major social media platforms. - Experience creating visual and multimedia content, particularly video and graphics. - A portfolio or examples of previous video, graphic design, or other digital content work are highly encouraged. - Comfort appearing on camera and participating in video content when appropriate. Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. This is not a shadowing internship. You will own real workstreams: hiring pipeline hygiene, investor and partner communication drafts, vendor and manufacturing coordination, event and content execution. If you need a lot of structure to know what to do next, this isn't the right fit. If you can take a half-formed task and come back with a plan, it is. **Scope of responsibilities** CEO/Chief of Staff support - Draft first passes on memos, investor update sections, and partner communications that get edited, not originated from scratch. - Own scheduling logistics and meeting prep for key external conversations. We'll ask what you built and what broke. - Comfort with unglamorous work. Chasing a vendor invoice and drafting an investor update in the same afternoon. - Sharp writing. Overview Automotive Technician (Entry-Level / Mechanic) Employment Type: Full-Time Pay Range: $20-$27/ hour consisting of hourly + flag rate About Sun Auto Tire & Service Plaza Tire Service is part of the Sun Auto Network. Sun Auto Tire & Service is a growing family of trusted automotive service and tire brands united by one purpose: helping customers stay safely and confidently on the road. Our recent employee research confirmed what makes Sun Auto different – a values driven culture, a strong sense of belonging, pride in doing quality work, and real opportunities to learn and build a career. As we continue to grow, we’re committed to providing consistent support, clear communication, and to building strong teams so every teammate has the tools, training, and trust to do their best work. Why This Role Matters Ready to grow your automotive career in a shop that invests in training, teamwork, and quality work? As a Junior Automotive Technician , you'll perform inspections, maintenance, and basic-to-intermediate repairs while sharpening your diagnostic skills alongside experienced technicians. It's a great fit if you have automotive training, hands-on shop experience, or strong mechanical aptitude and you're ready to move beyond basic maintenance into a more advanced role. What We Offer Competitive pay, including bonus or commission opportunities Paid training and hands-on development Medical, dental, and vision benefits Paid time off Employee discounts Career advancement opportunities, including growth toward Automotive Technician, Senior Technician, Lead Technician, and other technical leadership roles What You’ll Do Perform Multi-Point and Digital Vehicle Inspections, accurately documenting findings, measurements, and photos to company standards. Complete maintenance and entry-level repairs—oil and fluid services, filters, batteries, tires, brakes, and basic cooling, starting, and charging services. Handle tire mounting/dismounting, balancing, rotations, steering and suspension wear-item replacement, and fluid flushes with appropriate oversight. Perform basic diagnostics with guidance (noise/vibration, brakes, starting/charging, code retrieval, and scan data), and escalate complex driveability, electrical, intermittent, or safety-critical concerns to a senior or lead technician. Follow repair procedures—including torque specifications, bleed procedures, and post-repair checks—and request verification when required by policy or experience level. Conduct State Safety and Emission Inspections in applicable locations, ethically and in line with all company and state guidelines. Communicate findings, needed approvals, and repair status to Store Managers and Service Advisors, and document recommendations in the customer record to support clear communication. Keep a clean, safe work area; properly use and care for tools, equipment, and vehicles; follow all safety, PPE, and environmental/hazardous-waste requirements; and report hazards or equipment concerns. Collaborate with the team, accept coaching, participate in ongoing training, and complete other duties as assigned. Work a flexible schedule, including weekends as needed. What We’re Looking For Required: The right candidate is mechanically inclined, coachable, safety-focused, and ready to continue building automotive repair skills in a structured shop environment. 0–2 years of automotive experience in a shop environment, or equivalent technical training, performing maintenance and basic repairs. Ability to follow written procedures, torque specifications, and safety standards. Willingness to ask for help, accept coaching, and escalate concerns when appropriate. Basic proficiency with shop technology, including Digital Vehicle Inspection/Multi-Point Inspection tools, scan tools for code retrieval, and computerized systems for documentation. Ability to possess and utilize basic tools required to perform the functions of the role successfully. Valid driver’s license and successful completion of a Motor Vehicle Records check. State Inspector License, in applicable locations, or ability to obtain within 30 days of hire if required by the store. Ability to work a flexible schedule, including weekends as needed. Must be 18 years of age or older. Preferred: Technical or vocational school training. ASE certification or willingness to obtain certification. Brake service and/or alignment experience, where applicable. High school diploma or equivalent. Growth & Development We want you to grow with us. In this role, you'll build your inspection, maintenance, repair, and troubleshooting skills with hands-on coaching from experienced technicians—and gain the training and certifications to keep moving up. Many of our teammates use this role as a launchpad into more advanced technical and leadership positions. Your path could look like: Junior Technician → Automotive Technician → Senior Technician → Lead Technician → and beyond into technical training or field leadership. Work Environment & Physical Requirements Automotive shop environment with exposure to moderate to loud noise, dust, exhaust fumes, lubricants, petroleum products, vapors, and caustic materials. Temperature variations may include extreme heat and/or extreme cold. Ability to stand up to eight hours per day and walk to access various areas of the building. Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, and crouch regularly, with full range of motion in arms and hands. Ability to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds regularly and up to 70 pounds frequently. Vision sufficient to detect color, depth, and refocus; use of safety goggles or other PPE as required. Ability to communicate with customers, service advisors, managers, and shop teammates. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities. Ready to Apply? If you're ready to build your skills and grow with a team that has your back, we'd love to meet you. Click Apply to get started—most applications take just a few minutes. Equal Opportunity Employer Sun Auto Tire & Service is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. It is our policy to consider for employment all individuals regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

description: ### About TEGNA TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news. **2027 TEGNA Summer News Internship Program** **Your Future Starts Here** At TEGNA, making news isn’t legacy — it’s leadership. This isn’t old-school TV. We’re setting the pace for a sustainable, streaming-first future of journalism. We’re hiring bold, creative interns who embrace cutting-edge tech to deliver high-impact journalism that makes a difference. This 10-week paid internship runs **May 31** **– August 6, 2027**, at select TEGNA stations nationwide. Many interns launch full-time TEGNA careers right after the program. **What You’ll Do** - Pitch and research stories that matter - Create content for streaming, digital, social, and TV - Work alongside reporters, producers, anchors, and meteorologists—sometimes in the field - Jump in on special projects that shape local coverage **How This Internship Skyrockets Your Career** - **Hands-On Work** – Real assignments for your demo reel - **Career Growth** – Development sessions to fast-track your skills - **Networking** – Learn from some of the nation’s top media pros - **Paid Opportunity** – Earn money while making an impact in a fast-paced newsroom - The standard compensation rate is $15.00 per hour unless a higher state or local minimum wage overrides it. Notable exceptions include: - Denver, CO - $19.84 per hour - Sacramento, CA - $17.40 per hour - San Diego, CA - $17.75 per hour - Seattle, WA - $21.30 per hour - Spokane, WA - $17.13 per hour **What We’re Looking For** - Current college **juniors** or **seniors** with a **3.0 GPA** or higher - Studying **journalism**, communications, or a related major - Passion for one of these **three career paths**: - **TV news producing** - **TV news reporting** - **TV meteorology** - Experience writing, editing, fact-checking, and using digital/social tools - Strong communicator who never misses deadlines This internship **is not** for sports or film. It’s for **hard-news journalists** and **meteorologists** ready to disrupt the industry and deliver information in new ways that meet audiences where they are. **A Final Note** Our summer internship program is **highly competitive**. We review every application personally, but only selected candidates will be contacted for interviews. - **Rolling applications** — most 2027 interns hired by the end of 2026 - **Decisions by email** — expect updates by Jan/Feb 2027 - **Summer Only** — Our internships are in the summer, not fall or spring Pay Range $15—$15 USD ### Benefits: TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance. Job Summary: The Police Academy Trainee is an entry-level, non-sworn position for individuals preparing to become sworn police officers with the Harvard University Police Department. Incumbents are sponsored by HUPD to attend and successfully complete the Municipal Police Training Committee (MPTC) Recruit Officer Course (ROC) at an MPTC authorized police academy, and to obtain certification from the Massachusetts Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) Commission. Under close supervision, the Trainee participates in and completes all academy training requirements and department pre- and post-academy training. Upon successful completion of the academy, meeting all MPTC standards, POST certification requirements, and HUPD/Harvard University standards, the Trainee may be appointed as a sworn Police Officer, subject to available positions and satisfactory performance. During the Academy, trainees earn $30 per hour. After graduating and becoming sworn officers, you'll join the Harvard University Police Association (HUPA) and be paid according to our tiered pay structure. Job-Specific Responsibilities: Academy & Field Training Attend, participate in, and successfully complete the MPTC Recruit Officer Course at an MPTC authorized academy, including classroom instruction, practical skills, scenario-based training, firearms training, and physical fitness. () Meet or exceed all training standards, testing benchmarks, and performance evaluations required by MPTC and the hosting academy, including academic, firearms, defensive tactics, emergency driving, and physical fitness standards. () Comply with all academy rules, regulations, policies, and codes of conduct. () Participate in HUPD pre-academy orientation and post-academy Field Training Officer (FTO) program, as directed. Compliance with POST Requirements Satisfy all baseline requirements for initial certification as a law enforcement officer by the Massachusetts Peace Officer Standards and Training Commission, including successful completion of an approved basic training program and meeting standards of good moral character and fitness for employment. () Maintain eligibility for POST certification throughout the academy and onboarding process, including adherence to all ethical, legal, and professional standards. Department & University Responsibilities Represent Harvard University and HUPD professionally, demonstrating courtesy, integrity, discretion, and respect for the diverse community served. Participate in additional in-service, remedial, or specialized training as assigned. Maintain required documentation, logs, and reports related to training, testing, and certifications. Comply with all HUPD policies, Harvard University policies, and applicable local, state, and federal laws. Perform related duties as assigned or required to support department operations and public safety initiatives. Working Conditions: Work is performed in a variety of settings, including classroom, training facilities, firing ranges, driving courses, and outdoor environments in all weather conditions. Subject to extended periods of standing, walking, running, and physical exertion during training. Exposure to realistic training scenarios that may involve simulated weapons, loud noises, and stressful situations. Must be willing to wear department-issued uniforms and equipment, including a ballistic vest and a duty belt, and eventually carry a firearm upon appointment as a sworn officer. Basic Qualifications: Legal & General Requirements Must be at least 21 years of age by the start date of the police academy (or by date specified by the academy or HUPD policy). United States citizen. High school diploma or GED required. An associate’s or bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, social/behavioral sciences, or a related field is strongly preferred and may be required or prioritized consistent with HUPD/Harvard hiring standards. Valid driver’s license (Massachusetts preferred or ability to obtain MA license prior to appointment). Ability to obtain and maintain a Massachusetts License to Carry Firearms (LTC) in accordance with state law and University/department policy. Ability to work any shift (days, evenings, nights), weekends, holidays, and mandatory overtime, as required. Additional Qualifications and Skills: MPTC Requirements (Academy Eligibility) Must meet all Municipal Police Training Committee eligibility requirements for enrollment in the full-time Recruit Officer Course, including: ( ) Sponsorship/employment by HUPD. Successful completion of all pre-admission physical fitness, medical, and psychological screening required by MPTC and the academy. ( ) Successful completion of any required entrance examination(s), interviews, and background review as required by MPTC or the hosting academy. Ability and commitment to complete approximately 800 hours of academy curriculum in accordance with M.G.L. c. 41 §96B and MPTC standards. ( ) POST Requirements (Certification Eligibility) Must meet baseline requirements for certification as a law enforcement officer by the Massachusetts POST Commission, including: ( ) Successful completion of an MPTC-approved basic training program (e.g., Recruit Officer Course). No disqualifying criminal convictions or prior POST decertifications or revocations in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction. Demonstrated good moral character and fitness for employment as determined by a comprehensive background investigation and other screening tools. Commitment to complying with ongoing training and recertification requirements established by POST. Harvard University / HUPD Standards Successful completion of a comprehensive background investigation, which may include but is not limited to: Criminal history check (state and national). Driving record. Verification of prior employment, education, and military service (if applicable). Review of social media and online presence as permitted by law and policy. Personal and professional reference checks. Successful completion of pre-employment medical examination, psychological evaluation, and drug/alcohol screening, as required by Harvard University and HUPD policy. Must meet and maintain Harvard University’s standards of conduct and ethics, including strict confidentiality, integrity, and adherence to University policies on discrimination, harassment, conflict of interest, and use of information systems. Demonstrated ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds and to support Harvard’s commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. This role will work closely with Crown leadership and the company’s third-party IT service provider. Troubleshoot common hardware, software, application, account, access, and connectivity issues. Track recurring issues and identify opportunities to improve IT support processes. Escalate infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, and other advanced technical issues to the appropriate external provider or authorized internal resources. Maintain accurate records of company issued computers, mobile devices, peripherals, and other IT assets. Support related IT onboarding, employee transfers, and offboarding activities. Prepare and configure equipment for new employees and ensure devices are properly recovered during separations. Troubleshoot Microsoft accounts, applications, configurations, licensing, and access issues. Assist with user and device administration within authorized Microsoft environments. Support employees using Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, SharePoint, and other commonly used Microsoft applications. Assist with employee access to approved business applications and systems. Network & Connectivity Support Troubleshoot Wi Fi and Ethernet connectivity issues. Troubleshoot shared folder and network drive access. Map and maintain network drives as appropriate. Perform basic network troubleshooting and diagnostics. Identify, document, and communicate recurring connectivity issues. Coordinate with the company’s third-party IT provider on network infrastructure matters requiring escalation. Support scanners, monitors, docking stations, conference room technology, and other office peripherals. Assist with setup and troubleshooting of meeting room and audiovisual equipment. Assist with implementation of technology projects involving the external IT provider. Monitor escalated issues to help ensure they are appropriately assigned and resolved within expected timeframes. Maintain accurate records of hardware, software, devices, telecommunications assignments, and other IT assets. Assist with development and maintenance of IT policies, procedures, and user guidance. Provide basic employee technology training and support materials as needed. Participate in technology projects, upgrades, migrations, and deployments. role: Summer 2027 Legal Intern, Voting Rights Project
location: Hybrid-New York City or Washington D.C.
description: ## **About the Role** The ACLU seeks a **Summer** **Legal** Intern in the **Voting Rights Project**of the ACLU’s National office in **New York City or Washington D.C.**This position may be remote or hybrid. **Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated legal students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.** **The Team:** The ACLU Voting Rights Project was established in 1965 – the same year that the historic Voting Rights Act (VRA) was enacted – and has litigated more than 400 cases since that time. Its mission is to build and defend an accessible, inclusive, and equitable democracy free from racial discrimination. We have three guiding principles: (1) all Americans should be eligible to vote; (2) voting should be free and easy; and (3) all people should count equally. The Project is litigation-focused, with active cases across the country, though it helps support legislative advocacy work and public education. The Voting Rights Project’s recent docket has included more than 40 lawsuits to protect voters during the 2020 and 2024 elections; a pair of recent cases in the Supreme Court challenging the last administration’s discriminatory census policies: *Department of Commerce v. New York* (successfully challenging an attempt to add a citizenship question to the 2020 Census) and *Trump v. New York* (challenging the exclusion of undocumented immigrants from the population count used to apportion the House of Representatives); challenges to voter purges and documentary proof of citizenship laws; challenges to other new legislation restricting voting rights in states like Georgia, Montana, and Texas; and challenges to unfair redistricting plans in states like Georgia, Alabama, Louisiana, Arkansas, South Carolina, and Mississippi. The Project also helps support voting rights litigation brought by ACLU affiliates across the country. **What You’ll Do:** Interns provide critical support to our team in litigation and other forms of advocacy. In the recent past, interns have served as integral members on our teams doing election protection work and litigating redistricting and voter suppression cases; pushing back against the addition of a citizenship question on the 2020 Census; working to prevent the Florida legislature from imposing financial barriers that would undermine voter-approved Amendment 4, which re-enfranchised many citizens with felony convictions; and helping to investigate and initiate redistricting litigation. **Your Day to Day:** Interns will gain valuable experience by working with the team on a wide variety of issues. Responsibilities for interns may include, but are not limited to, the following: - Conduct legal research and analysis to support new and active litigation projects; - Aid in drafting of legal memoranda, pleadings, affidavits, motions, and briefs; - Draft and edit public education and non-litigation advocacy materials; - Provide support and assistance to ACLU affiliates and cooperating attorneys; - Potential to work closely with clients and participate in outreach with impacted communities, discovery, and trial practice. **What You’ll Bring:** The internship is open to students who are in law school who have completed their 1L year or are in an LLM program. Interns should possess the following: - Excellent research skills, including conducting internet and legal database research; - Excellent communication skills, both verbal and writing; - Attention to detail and excellent organizing and time-management skills; - Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; - The initiative to see projects through to completion; - Demonstrated commitment to public interest law, civil liberties, and racial justice; - Demonstrated ability to conduct complex legal analysis and fact finding. **Preferred Qualifications:** - Demonstrated interest in voting rights work - Familiarity with or previous experience working on voting rights issues ## **Future ACLU'ers Will:** - Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU - Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives - Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflicts ## **Internship Logistics** - **Location**: Our internship program offers a limited number of remote or hybrid intern positions. This internship can be **remote or hybrid based in our New York office.** - **Time Commitment**: This internship is full-time (35 hrs/wk) for a duration of 10 consecutive weeks. - **Internship Duration**: This internship has a start date of **May 24 or June 7.** - **Stipend:** A stipend is available for those students who are lawfully authorized to work. Students who receive outside funding are eligible for a partial stipend to bring their total funding up to the level of the ACLU’s stipend amount for the summer. Legal interns receive a stipend amount of $24/hour (stipends are taxed) **Priority Application Deadline:** **October 28, 2026.** While there is a priority deadline, our project is committed to reviewing all applications on a rolling basis until the closing of posting. **Application Materials** Your cover letter should discuss your qualifications and your commitment to racial and social justice. If you are selected for an interview, we may request a legal writing sample. You may optionally submit a writing sample alongside your cover letter. ## **Why the ACLU** For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people. ## **Our Commitment to Accessibility, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion** Accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. *The ACLU is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need assistance applying online, please complete the* [Accommodation Request Form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=6XZWc5QkD0q_MUveoekZhpx9FkPMtDFAmz3e2gWC_wNUOTVFRTRINjdRT0FLSTVPUUU3N0NXQ0dDTS4u&route=shorturl) *If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.* ***In order to be considered for this position, all candidates must formally submit an application.**The ACLU does not accept unsolicited calls or emails from candidates regarding their application status.***

role: Spring 2027 Legal Intern, Voting Rights Project
location: Hybrid-New York City or Washington D.C.
description: ## **About the Role** The ACLU seeks a **Spring** **Legal** Intern in the **Voting Rights Project**of the ACLU’s National office in **New York City or Washington D.C.**This position may be remote or hybrid. This internship is course credit only. **Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated legal students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.** **The Team:** The ACLU Voting Rights Project was established in 1965 – the same year that the historic Voting Rights Act (VRA) was enacted – and has litigated more than 400 cases since that time. Its mission is to build and defend an accessible, inclusive, and equitable democracy free from racial discrimination. We have three guiding principles: (1) all Americans should be eligible to vote; (2) voting should be free and easy; and (3) all people should count equally. The Project is litigation-focused, with active cases across the country, though it helps support legislative advocacy work and public education. The Voting Rights Project’s recent docket has included more than 40 lawsuits to protect voters during the 2020 and 2024 elections; a pair of recent cases in the Supreme Court challenging the last administration’s discriminatory census policies: *Department of Commerce v. New York* (successfully challenging an attempt to add a citizenship question to the 2020 Census) and *Trump v. New York* (challenging the exclusion of undocumented immigrants from the population count used to apportion the House of Representatives); challenges to voter purges and documentary proof of citizenship laws; challenges to other new legislation restricting voting rights in states like Georgia, Montana, and Texas; and challenges to unfair redistricting plans in states like Georgia, Alabama, Louisiana, Arkansas, South Carolina, and Mississippi. The Project also helps support voting rights litigation brought by ACLU affiliates across the country. **What You’ll Do:** Interns provide critical support to our team in litigation and other forms of advocacy. In the recent past, interns have served as integral members on our teams doing election protection work and litigating redistricting and voter suppression cases; pushing back against the addition of a citizenship question on the 2020 Census; working to prevent the Florida legislature from imposing financial barriers that would undermine voter-approved Amendment 4, which re-enfranchised many citizens with felony convictions; and helping to investigate and initiate redistricting litigation. **Your Day to Day:** Interns will gain valuable experience by working with the team on a wide variety of issues. Responsibilities for interns may include, but are not limited to, the following: - Conduct legal research and analysis to support new and active litigation projects; - Aid in drafting of legal memoranda, pleadings, affidavits, motions, and briefs; - Draft and edit public education and non-litigation advocacy materials; - Provide support and assistance to ACLU affiliates and cooperating attorneys; - Potential to work closely with clients and participate in outreach with impacted communities, discovery, and trial practice. **What You’ll Bring:** The internship is open to students who are in law school who have completed their 1L year or are in an LLM program. Interns should possess the following: - Excellent research skills, including conducting internet and legal database research; - Excellent communication skills, both verbal and writing; - Attention to detail and excellent organizing and time-management skills; - Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; - The initiative to see projects through to completion; - Demonstrated commitment to public interest law, civil liberties, and racial justice; - Demonstrated ability to conduct complex legal analysis and fact finding. **Preferred Qualifications:** - Demonstrated interest in voting rights work - Familiarity with or previous experience working on voting rights issues ## **Future ACLU'ers Will:** - Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU - Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives - Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflicts ## **Internship Logistics** - **Location**: Our internship program offers a limited number of remote or hybrid intern positions. This internship can be **remote or hybrid** based in our **New York, NY or Washington DC office.** - **Time Commitment**: This is a part-time internship requiring a commitment of 10/15/20 hours per week for 12 consecutive weeks. - **Internship Duration**: This internship has a start date of **January 11 or January 25.** - **Stipend**: This internship is being offered for course credit only. This internship must be tied to the intern’s formal education program by integrated coursework or the receipt of academic credit. **Priority Application Deadline:** **October 28, 2026.** While there is a priority deadline, our project is committed to reviewing all applications on a rolling basis until the closing of posting. **Application Materials** Your cover letter should discuss your qualifications and your commitment to racial and social justice. If you are selected for an interview, we may request a legal writing sample. You may optionally submit a writing sample alongside your cover letter. ## **Why the ACLU** For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people. ## **Our Commitment to Accessibility, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion** Accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. *The ACLU is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need assistance applying online, please complete the* [Accommodation Request Form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=6XZWc5QkD0q_MUveoekZhpx9FkPMtDFAmz3e2gWC_wNUOTVFRTRINjdRT0FLSTVPUUU3N0NXQ0dDTS4u&route=shorturl) *If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.* ***In order to be considered for this position, all candidates must formally submit an application.**The ACLU does not accept unsolicited calls or emails from candidates regarding their application status.*** ## ACLU’s internship program is supported in part by the Arnie Miller Fund for the Next Generation: [The Arnie Miller Fund For The Next Generation | American Civil Liberties Union](https://www.aclu.org/the-arnie-miller-fund-for-the-next-generation).

role: Manager II, Program Management - Late-Stage Development
description: Hi Tarsan! Thanks for your interest in this position.
