## **About Peec AI** Peec AI is the analytics platform for AI search. People increasingly discover products and make buying decisions through ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Google's AI Overviews instead of traditional search, and most brands have no idea where they show up in those answers. Peec gives marketing, SEO, and growth teams the data to see exactly that: how visible their brand is across AI platforms, how they compare to competitors, and where to win. We are defining this category, and the market is moving with us. Peec is a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, that went from $0 to $15M ARR in 18 months, with a 100+ person team across our Berlin HQ and our New York office. ## **About The Role** We're looking for a GTM Intern based in our New York office to support our sales and revenue teams as we scale Peec AI's customer base in the US. In this role, you'll work closely with the sales team on deal execution, sales content, and CRM operations while helping improve the systems and automations that power our revenue engine. You'll gain hands-on exposure to modern B2B SaaS sales, from outreach and pipeline management to revenue operations and automation, making this an ideal role for someone eager to learn quickly and help build a fast-growing startup's go-to-market presence in New York. ## **What You'll Do** - Support the sales team in closing deals and managing key client relationships - Develop sales content, from outreach sequences to pitch decks and case studies - Design and implement automations across our sales stack to improve efficiency and tracking - Contribute to revenue operations by analyzing metrics, improving CRM hygiene, and streamlining data flows - Jump into new challenges, learn fast, and help make things happen ## **What We're Looking For** - Currently studying, on a gap semester, or recently graduated, and available to start immediately full-time in New York for 3–6 months - Strong interest in B2B SaaS, startups, and revenue growth - Exceptional communication skills, written and verbal: you're comfortable reaching out to people and building relationships - Analytical mindset and structured approach to problem-solving - Solid grasp of technology and excitement to work hands-on with cutting-edge AI and automation tools - Self-starter with a bias for action, eager to learn, and comfortable with ambiguity - Low-ego team player who's easy to work with and doesn't shy away from rolling up their sleeves for operational tasks ## **Bonus Points** - Experience with tools like HubSpot, Clay, Lemlist, Apollo, Notion, or n8n - Exposure to sales operations, CRM management, or data-driven growth - Have built your own startup or cool projects you're proud of ## **What We Offer** - A rolling internship program with flexible start dates (minimum 3-month duration) - A high-impact internship at one of the fastest-growing Series A startups in AI, as part of the team building our New York office from the ground up - Real ownership and visibility across the sales and revenue organization - Regular team events and off-sites - Dinner on us every evening, plus Uber rides home when working late - A collaborative, high-energy in-office work environment in NYC **EEOC Statement** Peec AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. description: We are excited to announce an open call for talented interns to join Oklo's dynamic team! Below are multiple positions across various disciplines that may be available, offering the chance to work on innovative projects for Summer 2027. If you're passionate about solving complex challenges, thrive in a collaborative environment, and are eager to contribute to groundbreaking solutions, we encourage you to apply. ## **Requirements** Oklo interns are required to: - Relocate or be available to work out of Santa Clara CA where Oklo Headquarters is located for the duration of the internship or out of one of our satellite locations in Denver, CO, Brooklyn, NY, Idaho Falls, ID, or Washington D.C. - Be available to work 30-40 hours per week between June 7, 2027 - August 20, 2027 (depending on the scope of work) - Be currently enrolled or recently (2027) graduated with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree from an accredited university ## **Intern Position Descriptions** ***Core Thermal Hydraulics Intern*** The CTH Intern will develop intermediate fidelity (IF) subchannel and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for applications in sodium fast reactors (SFRs). The project will involve comparisons between simulation results and experimental data. The exact topic will depend on interest and company needs but could cover fluid-structure interaction, turbulence model development, uncertainty quantification, or surrogate modeling. - **Required Qualifications** - Coursework in fluid mechanics and heat transfer - Experience with 3-D CFD and meshing workflows - Proficiency in Python - Clear technical communication and documentation skills - **Bonus Qualifications** - Experience with advanced 3-D CFD concepts (large eddy simulation, fluid-structure interaction) - Familiarity with high-performance computing workflows and tools - Experience with MOOSE - Familiarity with statistics and reduced order modeling ***Materials Intern*** Working with members of Oklo’s Materials Team, will help with the selection and qualification of materials for use in nuclear reactor systems. Typical work duties include computational model development and implementation, engineering analysis, documentation, and interfacing with our fuel fabrication and engineering teams. - **Key Responsibilities** - Analyzing material performance across expected operating conditions - Developing new analysis methods to predict material behavior in service - Performing engineering analyses, including assessments of thermal performance, mechanical performance, safety performance, manufacturability, and cost. - Collaborating cross-functionally to provide technical feedback to quick-iterating computational teams. - Authoring technical reports using modern documentation tools and techniques - **Required **Qualifications**** - Experience working with and developing material behavior models - Experience with material characterization (material testing, metallography) - Background in nuclear, chemical, materials engineering, or equivalent - Motivated learner who is adept at efficiently summarizing literature - **Bonus Qualifications** - Experience with engineering simulation software, such as ANSYS or COMSOL - Coding or data analysis experience (e.g., Python or similar tools) ***Mechanical Analyst Intern*** This intern will contribute to the evaluation and optimization of mechanical components that are critical to Oklo’s advanced power plant designs. This position offers hands-on experience in applying engineering fundamentals, performing structural analysis, and integrating results into design iterations. - **Key Responsibilities** - Apply first-principles mechanics and strength of materials to support analysis of structural components - Assist in summarizing mechanical analysis results for design teams, highlighting key findings such as peak stresses, margins of safety, and potential design revisions - Support the development of technical documentation, ensuring clear and concise communication of assumptions, methods, and results - Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and testing teams to help inform design improvements - **Required **Qualifications**** - Working toward a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline - Strong foundation in mechanics of materials, dynamics, and heat transfer - Exposure to FEA tools (e.g., Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL, or similar) through coursework or projects - Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or another programming language for basic data analysis or workflow automation - Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly document and present technical findings - **Bonus Qualifications** - Prior research or project experience involving creep, fatigue, or thermal-mechanical problems - Familiarity with engineering codes and standards (e.g., ASME, AISC, or similar) - Experience using Git or another version control system ***Instrumentation and Controls Intern*** This intern will contribute to the development, integration, and testing of measurement and control systems that support advanced reactor operation and power generation. This position provides hands-on exposure to sensors, automation, and control strategies, while giving interns the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges. - **Key Responsibilities** - Assist in developing and testing sensors, instrumentation, and actuators under real design constraints - Help design and implement control algorithms for equipment and processes - Support the integration of I&C components into reactor systems and analysis workflows - Contribute to documenting methods, results, and system designs in a clear and professional manner - Collaborate with design and analysis teams to provide feedback that supports rapid iteration and improvement - **Required **Qualifications**** - Working toward a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field - Familiarity with measurement techniques, data acquisition, and signal processing - Exposure to control theory and feedback systems through coursework or projects - Basic programming skills in Python (or similar) for data analysis and automation - Strong communication skills and an eagerness to learn in a collaborative environment - **Bonus Qualifications** - Experience with circuit design (analog or digital) from labs, research, or projects - Exposure to communication protocols and digital networks - Familiarity with Git version control ***Neutronics Methodologies Intern*** This intern will assist in updating and streamlining neutronic methodologies to align with the latest format and standards. They will ensure that the methodologies match the way the code base builds the model, verifying consistency across both. This position also involves identifying and documenting gaps or discrepancies in the review process for future improvements. - **Key Responsibilities** - Update and optimize neutronic methodologies to the latest format and standards. - Ensure methodologies align with the way the code base builds the model. - Identify and document any gaps or discrepancies in the current processes. - Collaborate with team members to ensure consistency and accuracy in modeling procedures. - **Required **Qualifications**** - Proficient in Python for scripting and automation. - Familiar with AsciiDoc for documentation and formatting. - Strong background in nuclear engineering and neutronics. - Attention to detail with an ability to identify gaps in methodologies and processes. ***Process Intern*** This intern will support the design and analysis of fluid and power systems that are essential to Oklo’s advanced reactors. This position provides hands-on experience with system modeling, equipment evaluation, and prototyping, offering interns a chance to apply classroom knowledge to real-world energy systems. - **Key Responsibilities** - Assist in designing fluid and process systems, including piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and heat exchangers - Support definition of process equipment specifications, performance criteria, and operating conditions - Contribute to prototype setup and testing activities for iterative system design and validation - Help prepare technical documentation to support system layout, fabrication, installation, and operation - Collaborate with engineers on analyses to evaluate performance and inform design refinements - Document results and methods in a clear and professional manner for use across design and regulatory teams - **Required **Qualifications**** - Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline - Background in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer through coursework or projects - Familiarity with process or system modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, Aspen, or similar) - Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail - Ability to clearly communicate technical findings through reports or presentations - **Bonus Qualifications** - Experience with lab work, prototyping, or experimental systems - Exposure to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) or process design coursework - Familiarity with pumps, heat exchangers, or thermal-fluid systems from research or internships ***Prototyping/Manufacturing Intern*** The prototyping engineering intern will be a part of the prototyping and visualization team. - **Key Responsibilities** - Assist in machining and general fabrication of prototypes and test setups - Work with engineers to develop and execute testing procedures for mechanical systems - Support assembly, troubleshooting, and optimization of electro-mechanical systems - Conduct inspections and quality control on fabricated components - Document test results, process improvements, and technical findings - Collaborate with the engineering team to improve designs and manufacturing processes - Maintain a safe and organized workspace - **Required qualifications** - Mechanical, manufacturing, electrical, nuclear, chemical, or similar engineering student graduating with bachelors, masters, or PhD within the following year - Hands-on experience with mechanical fabrication, machining, or assembly - Good understanding of mechanical design, materials, and manufacturing processes - Familiarity with mechanical measurement tools (calipers, micrometers, etc.) - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and schematics - Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently and in a team environment - Good communication and technical documentation skills - **Bonus qualifications** - Experience with manual or CNC machining - Exposure to electronics, sensors, and control systems (mechatronics experience) - Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or similar) - Experience with welding, 3D printing, or other prototyping techniques - Understanding of fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, or materials science - Experience with data acquisition systems and programming (Python, LabVIEW, or MATLAB) ***Business Operations Intern*** This role provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in business operations, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. This role is ideal for someone looking to grow their operational skill set in core business operational functions and is passionate about contributing to initiatives that drive efficiency while supporting key compliance functions across the organization. - **Key Responsibilities** - Assist with day-to-day business operations, including process documentation, workflow optimization, and project coordination. - Collect, organize, and analyze operational and financial data to generate insights and support decision-making. - Prepare reports, presentations, and dashboards for internal stakeholders. - Collaborate with cross-functional teams (finance, HR, marketing, product, etc.) to support operational initiatives. - Conduct research on industry trends, competitors, and best practices to support strategic planning. - Identify and recommend opportunities for process improvements and increased efficiency. - Provide administrative and logistical support for team projects and meetings. - **Required **Qualifications**** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Economics, or a related field. - Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) or Google Workspace. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills. - Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. - Attention to detail and eagerness to learn. ## **Competencies** We are looking for interns that are: - Passionate about making advanced fission a reality - Willing and able to learn quickly - Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us - Willing to think differently and do things in new ways - Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment - Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before - Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems - An excellent writer who can write in modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well! - Able to communicate technical content and results verbally ### **Who you are:** A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that. Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals. A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team. An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator. Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day. Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward. ## **About Oklo's Intern compensation:** Oklo offers housing assistance, $35 - $44 per hour (compensation is determined based on education, skills, and experience), 1-on-1 mentorship, hands-on training, and the opportunity to engage in fun team-building activities as well as interactive workshops, enhancing both professional and personal growth. **Due to the nature of Oklo's work, only U.S. citizens can be considered for these positions.** --- **About Oklo Inc.:** Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories. **#CHOP: Oklo’s Values** **Collaboration**: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes. **Humility**: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition. **Ownership**: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy. **Pathfinding**: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity. Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. ### **Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer** Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does **not** contact you from an official Oklo email address. All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come **exclusively** from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### **Antenna Intern (Summer 2027)** Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Antenna Intern, you will work closely with mechanical, thermal, and payload system engineers to design, build and test antenna systems for ongoing and next-generation satellite payloads. **Role** - Leverage cutting-edge design tools to realize high-performance communications antenna systems with on-orbit flexibility to meet evolving customer demand. - Work with vendors to design and procure antenna and RF components and validate their performance through anechoic chamber testing. - Co-design antenna components and systems in conjunction with other technical disciplines, including Mechanical/Structural/Thermal/Payload Systems. **Requirements** - Fundamental understanding of electromagnetics, including antenna fundamentals, impedance matching, transmission lines, and circuit matching. - Experience measuring components using vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, and signal sources. - Demonstrated ability to solve engineering challenges in innovative and creative ways. - Capable of using industry-standard design tools such as CST, HFSS, or TICRA and scripting to solve engineering problems using Matlab or Python. **Bonus** - Experience with 3D printing (Direct Metal Laser Sintering and Fused Deposition Modeling). - Experience with link budget and system calculations including EIRP, noise figure, and G/T. - Experience designing waveguide components (OMT, MUX, diplexer, filters, polarizers, etc). - Experience with reflectors. The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29—$29 USD **U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required** (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. Across the country, young people are standing up and demanding a safer future for their communities—demanding a future free from gun violence. Since 2018, GIFFORDS has supported these brave activists through our Courage Fellowship program, which provides a select group of young people the opportunity to refine their advocacy skills and work together to reduce gun violence. Over the course of the program, Courage Fellows between the ages of 18 and 24 will be placed at the heart of the gun violence prevention discussion. They will engage in an array of activities that focus on advocacy and effective organizing , from learning about the issue firsthand from gun policy experts to lobbying legislators at their state capitol. The program will consist of three in-person trainings and four virtual trainings with GIFFORDS staff. Between these trainings, participants will work on a community engagement project of their choosing, with the support of GIFFORDS staff and resources. Colorado is a state with a history of both high-profile gun violence tragedies and meaningful legislative victories. After the state passed gun safety laws in 2013, a local gun rights group led a successful recall effort that flipped the state senate to Republican control and fostered a deep fear among lawmakers that kept many from supporting new gun violence prevention bills. When GIFFORDS began investing resources in Colorado in 2018 with the goal of creating a strong gun safety coalition, many viewed the issue as too politically risky. Since then, we’ve worked to counter that narrative and ensure that gun safety remains a top priority for our elected officials. We helped beat candidates endorsed by gun-rights groups in 2018 and 2020—backing champions like State Senator Tom Sullivan, an Aurora theater shooting survivor—and showed that gun violence prevention is not just good policy, but a winning political issue. Today, with a robust network of local leaders and engaged communities in spite of persistent opposition from extremist groups, Colorado continues to be a prime example of how we can drive meaningful change in the statehouse and at the ballot box. GIFFORDS is dedicated to doing the tough work that needs to be done to save lives from gun violence in Colorado. You can be a part of that. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the 2026/27 class of Colorado Courage Fellows is Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 12 am MT. Our application is now live. If you have technical difficulties or questions, please email couragefellows@ . Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. The primary program components for the Colorado Courage Fellowship include: An orientation meeting on Saturday, October 17, 2026 . A three-day training in Denver from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, 2026 . Virtual Training #1 on Saturday, January 16, 2027 . Virtual Training #2 on Saturday, February 6, 2027 . A two-day lobbying training and legislator meeting in Denver from Wednesday, February 10, to Thursday, February 11, 2027 . Virtual Training #3 on Saturday, February 27, 2027 . A three-day graduation in Denver from Friday, March 12, to Sunday, March 14, 2027 . Regular check-ins and mentorship opportunities with GIFFORDS staff. The creation and implementation of a community engagement project with support from GIFFORDS. Courage Fellowship Program Details Throughout the program, Courage Fellows will: Learn from nationally recognized leaders in the gun violence prevention and greater progressive movements. Network with other young activists in Colorado, including past Courage Fellows. Develop and implement a gun violence prevention project in their community. Build critical team-building, communication, organizing, and advocacy skills. Meet with lawmakers to discuss the importance of gun violence prevention legislation and advocacy. What is the community engagement project? The purpose of the take-home, community engagement project is for Courage Fellows to put the skills they learn in the first training to use in their own communities. The ideal project will be substantive, engaging, and locally focused. Fellows will brainstorm project ideas, subject to approval by GIFFORDS staff, throughout their first training. Past projects have included: Voter registration drives Press conferences Town halls with local elected officials Art installations Who Should Apply? We’re looking for the next generation of leaders in the gun violence prevention movement. The ideal candidate will: Have strong ties to Colorado and plan on remaining in Colorado for the foreseeable future. Have a demonstrated interest in politics, community organizing, activism, or volunteerism. Be eager to learn new skills and open to different points of view. Be passionate about fighting gun violence and willing to work with others towards this shared goal. Applicants do not need to be extensively involved in the gun violence prevention movement already—we are looking to build a diverse class of Courage Fellows with varying backgrounds and experiences. Candidate Requirements Willing to travel throughout Colorado for all listed trainings (all program-related costs, including food, travel, and hotel costs, will be covered by GIFFORDS). Able to attend the entirety of all trainings. Ready to join our Courage Fellowship Ambassador Program after the initial program ends, which includes: Representing and attending at least two GIFFORDS community, legislative, and media events per year. Mentoring incoming Courage Fellows. Planning or co-leading at least one event or advocacy initiative per year. Participating in quarterly check-ins with GIFFORDS staff. Contributing to communications through blogs, op-eds, or social media. GIFFORDS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an environment that celebrates diversity, equity and inclusion. People of color, trans individuals, gender non-conforming individuals, women, people with differing abilities, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.

About FIRE The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression’s mission is to defend and sustain the individual rights of all Americans to free speech and free thought — the most essential qualities of liberty. FIRE educates Americans about the importance of these inalienable rights, promotes a culture of respect for these rights, and provides the means to preserve them. Overview The Arthur D. Hellman Fellowship in First Amendment Litigation is FIRE’s premier summer opportunity for law students committed to defending free expression. This 10-week, paid opportunity offers an $8,000 stipend and runs from June through August. Fellows work at FIRE’s Philadelphia or Washington, D.C. offices, contributing directly to cutting-edge litigation that protects freedom of speech, expression, and thought. The position will run from June 1st, 2027 to August 6th, 2027. The fellowship serves as a pipeline to connect talented law students with FIRE’s long-term mission. Hellman Fellows will build a long-term relationship with FIRE with the possibility of returning to work with us as full-time employees, joining our Legal Network where they can take their own cases pro bono, authoring supporting amicus briefs, or serving as our local counsel. Hellman Fellows will work at FIRE's Philadelphia or D.C. office. Hellman Fellows work closely with FIRE’s First Amendment litigators on substantive projects that advance our strategic litigation. Fellows are trained in essential skills of public-interest practice — including legal research and writing, client interaction, and media relations — and are expected to make meaningful contributions to active cases. After the completion of the program, Fellows in good standing with FIRE will be inducted into FIRE's Alumni Association, a group dedicated to former FIRE interns, fellows, clerks, and full-time staffers. Qualifications FIRE seeks rising 2Ls and 3Ls with excellent academic credentials and a demonstrated passion for civil liberties and public-interest litigation. Successful applicants are collaborative, detail-oriented, and deeply committed to the principles of free expression. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. FIRE is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. As part of FIRE's hiring process, all candidates receiving a conditional offer of employment will be required to undergo a background check as permitted by and in compliance with federal, state and local law.

Across the country, young people are standing up and demanding a safer future for their communities—demanding a future free from gun violence. Since 2018, GIFFORDS has supported these brave activists through our Courage Fellowship program, which provides a select group of young people the opportunity to refine their advocacy skills and work together to reduce gun violence. Over the course of the program, Courage Fellows between the ages of 18 and 24 will be placed at the heart of the gun violence prevention discussion. They will engage in an array of activities that focus on advocacy and effective organizing , from learning about the issue firsthand from gun policy experts to lobbying legislators at their state capitol. The program will consist of three in-person trainings and four virtual trainings with GIFFORDS staff. Between these trainings, participants will work on a community engagement project of their choosing, with the support of GIFFORDS staff and resources. Colorado is a state with a history of both high-profile gun violence tragedies and meaningful legislative victories. After the state passed gun safety laws in 2013, a local gun rights group led a successful recall effort that flipped the state senate to Republican control and fostered a deep fear among lawmakers that kept many from supporting new gun violence prevention bills. When GIFFORDS began investing resources in Colorado in 2018 with the goal of creating a strong gun safety coalition, many viewed the issue as too politically risky. Since then, we’ve worked to counter that narrative and ensure that gun safety remains a top priority for our elected officials. We helped beat candidates endorsed by gun-rights groups in 2018 and 2020—backing champions like State Senator Tom Sullivan, an Aurora theater shooting survivor—and showed that gun violence prevention is not just good policy, but a winning political issue. Today, with a robust network of local leaders and engaged communities in spite of persistent opposition from extremist groups, Colorado continues to be a prime example of how we can drive meaningful change in the statehouse and at the ballot box. GIFFORDS is dedicated to doing the tough work that needs to be done to save lives from gun violence in Colorado. You can be a part of that. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the 2026/27 class of Colorado Courage Fellows is Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 12 am MT. Our application is now live. If you have technical difficulties or questions, please email couragefellows@ . Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. The primary program components for the Colorado Courage Fellowship include: An orientation meeting on Saturday, October 17, 2026 . A three-day training in Denver from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, 2026 . Virtual Training #1 on Saturday, January 16, 2027 . Virtual Training #2 on Saturday, February 6, 2027 . A two-day lobbying training and legislator meeting in Denver from Wednesday, February 10, to Thursday, February 11, 2027 . Virtual Training #3 on Saturday, February 27, 2027 . A three-day graduation in Denver from Friday, March 12, to Sunday, March 14, 2027 . Regular check-ins and mentorship opportunities with GIFFORDS staff. The creation and implementation of a community engagement project with support from GIFFORDS. Courage Fellowship Program Details Throughout the program, Courage Fellows will: Learn from nationally recognized leaders in the gun violence prevention and greater progressive movements. Network with other young activists in Colorado, including past Courage Fellows. Develop and implement a gun violence prevention project in their community. Build critical team-building, communication, organizing, and advocacy skills. Meet with lawmakers to discuss the importance of gun violence prevention legislation and advocacy. What is the community engagement project? The purpose of the take-home, community engagement project is for Courage Fellows to put the skills they learn in the first training to use in their own communities. The ideal project will be substantive, engaging, and locally focused. Fellows will brainstorm project ideas, subject to approval by GIFFORDS staff, throughout their first training. Past projects have included: Voter registration drives Press conferences Town halls with local elected officials Art installations Who Should Apply? We’re looking for the next generation of leaders in the gun violence prevention movement. The ideal candidate will: Have strong ties to Colorado and plan on remaining in Colorado for the foreseeable future. Have a demonstrated interest in politics, community organizing, activism, or volunteerism. Be eager to learn new skills and open to different points of view. Be passionate about fighting gun violence and willing to work with others towards this shared goal. Applicants do not need to be extensively involved in the gun violence prevention movement already—we are looking to build a diverse class of Courage Fellows with varying backgrounds and experiences. Candidate Requirements Willing to travel throughout Colorado for all listed trainings (all program-related costs, including food, travel, and hotel costs, will be covered by GIFFORDS). Able to attend the entirety of all trainings. Ready to join our Courage Fellowship Ambassador Program after the initial program ends, which includes: Representing and attending at least two GIFFORDS community, legislative, and media events per year. Mentoring incoming Courage Fellows. Planning or co-leading at least one event or advocacy initiative per year. Participating in quarterly check-ins with GIFFORDS staff. Contributing to communications through blogs, op-eds, or social media. GIFFORDS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an environment that celebrates diversity, equity and inclusion. People of color, trans individuals, gender non-conforming individuals, women, people with differing abilities, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.

Overview FIRE’s Summer Legal Internship provides law students with an unparalleled opportunity to contribute to the nation’s leading defender of free expression. This 10-week, paid program offers an $8,000 stipend and runs from June through August. Legal interns work from FIRE’s Philadelphia or Washington, D.C. offices, contributing directly to advocacy and policy projects that shape the national conversation on free speech. The position will run from June 1st, 2027 to August 6th, 2027. Summer Legal Interns are placed in one of FIRE’s non-litigation advocacy departments, where they support ongoing efforts to defend free expression and academic freedom: Campus Rights Advocacy: Investigate free speech violations on college campuses, help draft public-facing commentary, conduct legal research, and participate in voluntary learning sessions on substantive First Amendment law. Public Advocacy: Research and respond to threats to free expression beyond the campus, draft advocacy materials, and assist in shaping FIRE’s public commentary. Policy Reform: Draft and edit policy analyses for college administrators, research emerging issues in higher education policy, and help advance reforms to improve protections for student and faculty expression. Legislative & Policy: Conduct legal research on public policy affecting expressive rights, draft internal bill analyses and public commentary, and monitor legislative developments. In addition, interns may assist in drafting memos and correspondence, conducting research projects to identify new advocacy targets, and contributing to FIRE’s Newsdesk . Interns also participate in seminars with FIRE leadership and civil liberties experts, gaining deeper insight into free expression issues and public-interest advocacy. After the completion of the program, Fellows in good standing with FIRE will be inducted into FIRE's Alumni Association, a group dedicated to former FIRE interns, fellows, clerks, and full-time staffers. Qualifications FIRE seeks rising 2Ls and 3Ls with strong academic credentials and a demonstrated interest in civil liberties and public-interest law. Successful applicants will be detail-oriented, collaborative, and passionate about advancing FIRE’s mission to defend freedom of speech, expression, and thought. Application Information FIRE seeks rising 2Ls and 3Ls with excellent academic credentials and a demonstrated passion for civil liberties and public-interest litigation. Successful applicants are collaborative, detail-oriented, and deeply committed to the principles of free expression. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. FIRE is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. As part of FIRE's hiring process, all candidates receiving a conditional offer of employment will be required to undergo a background check as permitted by and in compliance with federal, state and local law.

description: University of the District of Columbia Job Classification Description Job Title: Student Library Employee for Library and Media Services FLSA: Job Series/Salary Plan/Grade: Union Status: Job Code: GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE JOB FOR LIBRARY SERVICES STUDENT EMPLOYEE: The Student Library Employee for Library Services assists the Library Technician in managing the Circulation Desk by assisting patrons in the use of the UDC library catalog to identify, locate, retrieve, and request books and other materials within our collection or at one of our Washington Research Library Consortium member institutions (WRLC). The Student Library Employee for Library Services also serves as a valuable resource to students, faculty, staff, and guest patrons as the initial contact for all services related to the Learning Resources Division, Library Services. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Understands and performs all tasks related to Circulation, including charging, discharging, and renewing library materials, registering patrons. Sorts books and other items according to procedure and returns them to shelves, files, or other designated storage areas. Delivers and retrieves items throughout the library by hand or using pushcart. Sorts and shelves books. Removes damaged books from collection. Checks materials in and our using the circulation process. Monitors the daily operation of the online circulation system. Maintains statistics on circulation activity. GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE JOB FOR LIBRARY MEDIA SERVICES STUDENT EMPLOYEE: The Library Media Student Employee, under the general guidance of the Media Technician and the supervision of the Information Technology Specialist Supervisor will perform work in the Media Access Services department to provide technical support and assistance to patrons. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Assists patrons with a variety of media equipment such as, but not limited to, audio and video recording/playback equipment, projectors, and laptop/desktop computers. Charges and discharges materials utilizing our own system. Help with delivery of equipment, setup, and pickup of media equipment used in classrooms and auditoriums spaces. Assists with maintaining inventory of the unit materials and supplies. Assist in weeding collections. MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS: Currently matriculating UDC student. Strong communication and organizational skills. Computer proficient, including Microsoft Office and standard office equipment. REQUIRED COMPETENCIES: Knowledge of Microsoft Office and standard office equipment. Excellent communication, organizational, and project management skills and the ability to deliver excellent customer service. STANDARDS & EXPECTATIONS: Expectations of the job: The successful candidate will have demonstrated the ability to work effectively, independently, and collaboratively in a diverse, collegial, changing environment. The candidate will possess excellent interpersonal, communication, leadership, and project management skills. Recurring contacts are made with faculty, administrators, staff members, students, and the general public, as well as with staff of other WRLC member institutions. Normal physical dexterity is required. The work is generally performed in an office setting. Knowledge of UDC Rules and Regulations: The university provides all training required by OSHA to ensure employee safety. The University of the District of Columbia is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Note: The University reserves the right to change or reassign job duties as provided in policy and negotiated agreements.

The Construction Intern supports the project team by observing and assisting with day-to-day activities in the field and office. This role is designed to introduce students or early-career candidates to the construction industry, providing exposure to safety practices, field documentation, and project coordination under the guidance of the Superintendent and project engineering team. The Construction Intern gains hands-on learning experience while contributing to real project tasks. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS, DUTIES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES The following statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and skills required of personnel so classified. Field Exposure & Quality Control Observe and assist with field layout activities, learning how dimensional control is verified against drawings and specifications Shadow quality control inspections of installed work, gaining exposure to how deficiencies are identified and documented Help track and follow up on punch list items under supervision, learning the closeout process from identification to resolution Observe material verification and quantity tracking processes to understand how deliveries are checked against project needs Documentation and Reporting Assist with daily field reports, photo logs, and general site documentation to build familiarity with recordkeeping standards Help maintain material and equipment tracking logs, learning how procurement and logistics are managed on an active site Shadow the project team on RFI and submittal tracking, gaining an understanding of how field questions and material approvals move through the process Support as-built documentation and drawing markups under the guidance of field staff Safety Participate in daily safety huddles and toolbox talks to understand how safety communication happens on site Learn to identify and report safety observations and hazards, developing an eye for site risks under supervision Observe PPE compliance checks and general safety protocol enforcement across the jobsite Communication & Coordination Attend project meetings and assist with meeting minutes to gain exposure to how project decisions and updates are communicated Shadow coordination efforts between the field team, subcontractors, and office staff to understand how information flows across a project Observe how site logistics (laydown areas, access routes, trade sequencing) are planned and adjusted in real time GENERAL BACKGROUND AND MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Education/Experience Currently pursuing an Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field Strong interest in learning about the construction industry, strong attention to detail, and eagerness to learn Willingness to work on an active construction site in varying weather conditions Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to learn Procore, Bluebeam, Microsoft Project, and other software programs Safety Requirement Willingness to comply with company and OSHA safety requirements Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) including hard hat, safety vest, safety glasses, gloves, steel toe boots, and other specialized equipment as jobs require. Current certifications for First Aid and CPR or willingness to obtain Physical Demands and Work Environment The Field Engineer regularly splits time between an office environment and active construction sites. The employee must be able to perform duties in each setting as project needs require: Walk across uneven terrain and active construction areas during site visits Climb ladders, scaffolding, and permanent and temporary stairways as needed Stand or walk for extended periods and navigate partially completed structures Bend, kneel, crouch, and lift materials or equipment that weigh up to 40 pounds Work outdoors in varying weather conditions and be exposed to construction noise, dust and vibration Sit for extended periods and use a computer, phone, and other office equipment Occasionally stand, walk, bend, reach, and lift office materials, weighing up to 25 pounds Review documents and construction drawings and communication in person, by phone, or virtually Specialty project locations (such as industrial facilities, healthcare environments, or restricted sites) may involve additional safety requirements or environmental conditions WORK AUTHORIZATION Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Holt Brothers Construction does not provide sponsorship for employment visas and will not consider applicants who require sponsorship now or in the future.

About G2 G2 Capital Advisors ( ) is a multi-product and sector-focused investment bank headquartered in Back Bay, Boston. G2 was formed on the premise that lower middle market advisory firms could do more to help clients navigate operational or financial challenges and the complexity of capital markets transactions. As part of GA Group (backed by Oaktree), G2 brings additional scale and resources to support middle-market companies. What sets us apart? G2 is not your typical investment bank or restructuring firm: we are a group of former business operators with unique industry experience and financial advisory bankers who help our clients achieve their strategic and financial goals. We are always in search of entrepreneurial, talented, driven, and intellectually curious team members to join our team in achieving success for our clients. About the Co-op Program: G2's Insolvency & Fiduciary Services (IFS) Co-op program provides students with an in-depth understanding of our IFS practice, which helps clients navigate the day-to-day ambiguity of distress situations, while working toward the overall goal of preserving value, maximizing economic recovery, and reducing risk. Opportunities to regularly collaborate and forge relationships with team members, subject matter experts in the industry, and our G2 Leadership Team are endless through your exposure to deal work and ongoing training. You'll have an immediate impact on projects and initiatives from day one, arming you with an even more diverse background for success in your professional career! Program Timing: Spring cycle (beginning in January 2027) Location: G2 Capital Advisors operates in a hybrid work model with 4 days per week in the office, in Boston. Hourly Requirement : Candidates selected for the program will be required to provide at least 40 hours weekly and be available between the normal business hours of 9:00am - 5:00pm EST. What You'll Do: Support a wide range of operational, accounting, and strategic tasks and manage associated deadlines Perform in-depth market research that supports G2's IF&S clients Collaborate in the development of marketing collateral for distressed sale processes Proactively & efficiently solve problems in complex & time-sensitive work situations Provide timely communication to internal and external stakeholders on engagements as and when required Manage competing timelines and priorities accordingly on engagements Work collaboratively with team members toward a shared goal What We Look For: Currently enrolled in a 4 or 5-year academic institution with an outstanding academic record (3.5 GPA minimum) Demonstrated ability to exhibit strong attention to detail, business acumen, business writing, and work ethic Proactive, self-starter in nature; adept at working in a fast-paced environment Demonstrated research experience and proven ability with Microsoft Office products (Excel, PPT, etc.) Strong understanding of the three financial statements Familiarity with financial analysis and financial modeling Can manage multiple priorities effectively; manages up and across to proactively keep others up-to-date on progress and challenges All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment at G2 without regard to race; creed; color; religion; national origin; sex; age; disability; sexual orientation; gender identity or expression; genetic predisposition or carrier status; veteran, marital, or citizenship status; or any other status protected by law.

role: Plastics Application Development & Technical Service Co-Op - 2027
description: Job Summary The Application Development & Technical Service (ADTS) Co-op will collaborate with local ADTS teams within SEM to participate in engineering activities. The Co-op will be located at a different location during each of their rotations to get broad exposure to Avient’s technologies and businesses. Activities will include both in-house application development testing and internal mold trials, as well as collaborating with External ADTS engineers to travel to customer facilities for product validation. The Application Development & Technical Service (ADTS) Engineer will be responsible for recommending appropriate Engineered Thermoplastics (ETP’s) for customer applications and optimizing customer processes, while also providing education/training on how to design applications and tooling. The candidate will also participate in the resolution of customer complaints, as needed. ADTS Engineer may also be responsible for developing testing plans and procedures, data analysis, and communication of results for new applications and product launches. Essential Functions Support application evaluation and material selection Attend process trials of new and existing products Troubleshoot processing problems at existing customers Engage customers on quality issues as well as process and technology questions Create product part or mold design and processing/troubleshooting literature for each product line Construct presentations and provide processing and design training to the customer Interpret and analyze customer part drawings, mold filling simulation, elemental analysis, etc. Additional support as needed to internal customers – Sales, Product Management, Technology, Manufacturing. Familiarization of current and legacy product portfolio. Other duties as assigned. Education and Experience Bachelors Student in Plastics Engineering or related Engineering field required. 1+ year’s related experience (including internship/co-op experience) preferred Injection molding, extrusion, blow molding, thermoforming experience a plus Qualifications Strong injection molding and/or extrusion processing skills. Knowledge of other processing methods a plus Strong mold and part design skills Capability to think outside the box and work on cutting edge concepts Proficiency with SolidWorks and Moldflow (or similar software) Proficiency with Finite Element Analysis Software Understanding of plastics materials and compounding processes Performs work with speed and accuracy. Adheres to internal Avient policies and rules. Interprets Technical Data sheets (TDS) / Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and provide proper instruction Strong communication skills required, both oral and written (technical and non-technical) Able to present ideas and results in a logical manner Receptive to ideas and feedback Responds to emails/calls and provides detailed reports in appropriate fashion and timeframe. Understands project purpose and commitment required. Able to present ideas and results in a logical manner. Can effectively communicate technical information with other functions that are non-technical. Works seamlessly with others without difficulty. Bi-lingual with Spanish is a plus

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### Electrical Reliability Intern (Winter 2027) Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. #### **Role** - Perform reliability analyses on satellite systems - Work with the reliability design team to analyze flight hardware - Support DFMEA efforts - Write code to help evaluate performance and automate testing of satellite hardware #### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a B.S. in electrical or computer engineering (or equivalent technical degree) - Interest in learning about, designing, and working with electronics systems - A passion for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development - Demonstrated ability to personally design, build, and test hardware from scratch - US Citizenship or Green Card - Don't meet them all? Not a problem. Please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria. #### **Bonus** - Experience with agentic AI systems - Experience with SPICE-based simulators (LTSpice, PSPICE, ADS, etc) - Familiarity with standard EE lab bench (power supply, oscilloscope, multimeter, etc) - Experience with Python The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29—$29 USD **U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required** (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we invite all people to join our team and bring their unique perspectives to make us stronger. #### **Astranis SMS Terms of Service** 1. **Recruiting Updates:** By opting in, you agree to receive SMS updates, interview coordination, and recruiting communications from Astranis Space Technologies Corp. 2. **Opt-Out:** You can cancel this service at any time by replying **STOP**. role: Staff Recruiter, Early Career and Interns
location: McCarran, NV; San Francisco, California, United States
description: **About Redwood Materials** **Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.** **Position Summary** Redwood Materials is building the domestic supply chain for battery materials, and our early careers program is where many of the engineers, scientists, and operators who will run it get their start. This role owns that program end to end: strategy, budget, university partnerships, hiring manager enablement, the intern experience, and conversion to full-time. It sits within the Talent Acquisition team and works closely with Engineering, Operations, R&D, and the broader People team. The program runs well today. We are looking for someone to scale it across our Nevada and South Carolina sites, tighten conversion, and grow it into a broader early-careers strategy covering co-op and new-grad hiring. **Essential Duties and Responsibilities** - Set the annual intern headcount plan with Finance, HR Business Partners, and org leaders across Engineering, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and corporate functions, and own the program budget and operating calendar - Run the full intern lifecycle from sourcing and offers through onboarding, relocation, mid-point reviews, final presentations, and conversion decisions - Build and own the target school strategy and relationships with University of Nevada, Reno (UNR), Truckee Meadows Community College (TMCC), Clemson University, and the national engineering programs that feed our sites, including campus and virtual recruiting events - Train intern managers on scoping projects, giving feedback, and making conversion calls, and run calibration so intern performance and offer decisions are consistent across sites - Design and deliver the summer program, including onboarding, site tours, executive speaker series, cohort projects, and the final showcase, and act on intern and manager feedback - Own program metrics including offer acceptance, conversion rate, school yield, cost per hire, and retention of converted interns, and report on program health to Talent Acquisition and People leadership - Partner with Legal on work authorization guidelines for interns, with HR Operations on Greenhouse and Workday workflows, and with Communications on student-facing employer brand content, and extend the program into co-op and new-grad tracks **Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities** - Experience owning an internship or early-careers program end to end, ideally at a company that hires engineers into manufacturing, hardware, energy, automotive, or industrial environments - Track record of growing or rebuilding a program rather than maintaining one - Belvedere Trading is a leading proprietary trading firm proudly headquartered in downtown Chicago. Our traders work hard to provide liquidity to the market through their market-making activities and are the masters of a diverse set of commodities, interest rates, exchange-traded funds (ETF), and equity index options. From the beginning, we began iteratively investing in our proprietary technology and committing to building our systems from the ground up. Our trading models and software systems are continually re-engineered, optimized, and maintained to stay on top of the industry. Our People Team department focuses on delivering employee-first solutions to the business. We go all-out to understand and support our team member's needs, leverage data to gain insights and trends, and advance our human-capital-related applications for efficiency and consistency. We look for passionate team members that excel and their contribution is critical to our continued success. The People Team is comprised of Employee Experience, People Operations, Talent, and People & Development. These groups work closely together to bring in the best talent for Team Belvedere and from day one, make sure that all team members have all the tools they need to succeed and develop through their tenure. We believe university and early career hiring helps our company look at problems in alternative ways, integrate fresh perspectives, and innovate. We're currently looking for an Early Career Talent Partner to own hiring for our Trading Department, building the pipeline of quantitative traders and trading-adjacent talent that keeps Belvedere competitive. This role will be responsible for attracting and hiring high-potential colleagues, developing quality relationships with student groups and academic programs that feed into our industry, and building a strong employer brand among the communities that produce top trading talent. You will own have stakeholder relationships with Trading leadership and strategically partner with the business to drive hiring and lead best practices in trading talent acquisition for interns, graduates, and those early in their professional careers. ### What you'll do - Execute the early career recruitment strategy for the Trading Department and influence future campus recruiting cycles, including undergraduate and graduate-student recruitment - Represent Belvedere at collegiate trading competitions, poker tournaments, and industry networking events using these events as a primary sourcing and brand-building channel for quant trading talent - Foster and maintain relationships with campus trading groups, investment clubs, and quant/finance student organizations, positioning Belvedere as a destination employer within those communities - Build and deepen pipelines with academic programs that feed directly into our industry (such as financial mathematics, financial engineering, quantitative/quant research, applied math, and statistics programs) including faculty, program-director relationships, and alumni groups - Full-cycle campus recruiting for Trading roles: managing a high-volume candidate pipeline from initial application through Super Day and offer stage, in partnership with our People Operations team on engagement and onboarding, including candidates with extended non-compete periods - Partner with Trading hiring managers to understand evolving skill and market needs (quantitative reasoning, probability, market intuition) and translate them into sourcing strategy and candidate evaluation criteria - Represent Belvedere during campus visits and virtual open houses, presenting our internship programs and early trading talent development paths - Retroactively analyze engagement efforts to understand the return on strategic partnerships (competitions, clubs, academic programs) and the success of new engagements, out of the box engagement ideas area embraced - Provide a high-touch candidate and hiring manager experience by articulating our core values in ways that resonate with a quantitative, trading-focused candidate pool - Evaluate and measure recruiting results and identify areas for process and performance improvement, systematization, and automation ### What you'll need - 2+ years recruitment experience, preferably with intern, entry-level and early career talent pools in fintech, professional services, and financial firms - Ability to manage full-cycle recruiting process including resume review, phone screens, interview scheduling and facilitation, and offer calls - Demonstrated success recruiting at multiple universities in highly competitive markets, ideally within quantitative trading, prop trading, or finance - Comfort engaging with quantitative and markets-adjacent concepts (probability, statistics, game theory) enough to speak credibly to trading competition organizers, quant faculty, and student trading groups - Excellent oral and written communication skills - Ability to travel as needed during peak campus recruiting periods in the fall and spring, including to trading competitions and conferences - Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities/projects, meet deadlines, and facilitate change with a sense of urgency - Proven analytical, organizational, and decision-making skills with demonstrated negotiation skills and influencing positive outcomes - Eager to take on new tasks/responsibilities and passion for candidate experience, operational excellence, and continuous development - Experience coordinating and participating in both in-person and virtual recruiting events/activities - Comfortable working with and presenting recruitment data and market data, reporting, and analytics - Bachelor's Degree required

location: New York City, New York, United States
description: ## **About Flexport:** At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us. ## **Build the operational and technical skill set that runs global trade** At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. We're shaping the future of a $10T industry with technology and people who understand it end to end. The Rotational Development Program (RDP) exists because that combination — real supply chain fluency plus the ability to build and automate — doesn't exist at scale in the market today. So we're building it ourselves. This is an 18-month program, not a rotation for rotation's sake. Every assignment is live, revenue-generating work. Every participant leaves with a certification in AI and low-code tooling running alongside their operational and commercial training. And every graduate places into a role with real scope: primarily Account Management, with paths into Automation Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering/Consulting, Sales Engineering, or a traditional Ops/Sales/Customs track. ## **What you'll do** You'll rotate through three functions, six months each, with AI/low-code curriculum running continuously across all three: - **Gateway Ops (Air or Ocean).** Own the shipment lifecycle. Execute bookings, manage exceptions, and hold data integrity to Flexport's standard. Build your first automation and reporting skills through structured coursework running in parallel. - **Customs.** Become a global trade expert by navigating the complex world of customs regulations to ensure goods comply with international laws. Simultaneously, move into applied technical work: SQL, workflow automation, Lean process improvement, etc. - **Sales / Account Management.** Take on go-to-market work and build client-facing skills, operating with more independence. Your capstone: identify a real business problem in the function you're sitting in and build the tooling or process fix that solves it. This internship provides an opportunity to gain hands-on consulting experience while working alongside industry experts on real client engagements. As an intern, you will function in a role similar to a full-time Analyst, contributing directly to project teams and client deliverables. Gather, organize, and analyze qualitative and quantitative data. - Support the development of strategic recommendations based on research findings and market insights. - Identify trends and draw meaningful conclusions from complex information. - Academic concentration in Life Sciences, Public Health, Economics, Business, Healthcare, Pharmacy, or a related field. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills. - Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, and Word. - Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. - Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. - Interest in healthcare, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, consulting, or market access. ### Preferred - Previous internship, research, or leadership experience. - Experience analyzing data and presenting findings. - Familiarity with the U.S. healthcare system or pharmaceutical industry. - Demonstrated intellectual curiosity and willingness to learn. ## Why Join Precision AQ? - Gain hands-on experience working on real client engagements. - Learn from experienced consultants and industry leaders. - Build research, analytical, and presentation skills. - Develop an understanding of healthcare market access and commercialization strategy. - Expand your professional network through a structured internship program. - Explore potential full-time career opportunities following graduation. We've built the framework: a 5-stage adoption model, a validated self-assessment tool, a live results dashboard, and stage-by-stage deep-dives showing teams exactly how to move from individual AI skills to full-scale, cross-team adoption. Now we need someone to help teams actually climb that ladder. This intern will work directly with marketing leadership to turn the adoption roadmap into measurable progress — helping teams move from experimenting individually with AI to embedding it in daily workflows, and eventually contributing to tools that work across functions. This is a hands-on role, with close support from Marketing leadership. We're looking for someone who's energized rather than unsettled by open-ended problems, who can observe a vague signal ("this team seems stuck") and turn it into a concrete hypothesis and test. Contribute to building out session materials for the 12-session AI fluency curriculum - Help coordinate rollout logistics and gather feedback for iteration **Qualifications:** **Required** - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Demonstrated interest in AI tools and workflows — coursework, personal projects, or hands-on use count - Organized, self-directed, and comfortable working across multiple workstreams and keeping projects on track with guidance from a manager - Analytical mindset — comfortable interpreting assessment data and summarizing insights and recommendations for leadership - Currently pursuing a degree in marketing, business, communications, or a related field - Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. This has the potential to enable a wide range of therapeutic editing strategies that Beam is using to advance a diversified portfolio of base editing programs. Beam is a values-driven organization committed to its people, cutting-edge science, and a vision of providing life-long cures to patients suffering from serious diseases. **Position Overview:** Beam is seeking a highly talented and motivated engineering or science student interested in a career in biopharmaceutical manufacturing to join our Technical Operations team from January through June 2027 as a co-op. The Technical Operations co-op will be responsible for supporting the cross-functional validation teams that demonstrate newly developed gene editing equipment and manufacturing processes work as intended by Beam and as required by government agencies (including FDA) for the benefit of patients. Support activities will include learning about and obtaining scientific/ technical information related to manufacturing equipment and processes to ensure integrity of data included in Technical Operations protocols and reports. As a part of these cross-functional teams, the candidate will have the opportunity to interact with various functions involved with supporting the biopharmaceutical manufacturing industry, including R&D (process and analytical development), Manufacturing, Manufacturing Sciences and Technology (MSAT), Quality (both Quality Control and Quality Assurance), Supply Chain, and Procurement to help the candidate explore potential career options in the biopharmaceutical manufacturing industry. **Responsibilities:** - Develop an understanding of Beam’s gene editing manufacturing equipment, technologies, and processes supporting both hematology and liver programs. - Review and verify technical and scientific data included in risk assessments, protocols, and reports to ensure accuracy, completeness, and data integrity in support of project timelines and milestones. - Communicate findings, recommendations, and any identified issues from verification activities to cross-functional teams through written summaries, presentations, and verbal updates, supporting timely resolution and project milestones. - Support the evaluation and documentation of manufacturing process data, ensuring records are accurate, attributable, legible, and compliant, while identifying potential issues and recommending solutions. **Qualifications:** -
