role: January 2027 BES Fellowship for Founding School Leaders - Workforce Development Schools in Atlanta
description: **Fellowship for Founding School Leaders- Atlanta** BES seeks a Fellow for our Fellowship program to serve as a founding school leader in Atlanta. This BES Fellowship offers highly motivated leaders committed to transforming education the rigorous, multi-year training needed to design, found, and lead a high-achieving school that meets the unique needs of its community. BES welcomes applicants from the Atlanta region for new public charter schools and aligned with authorizer priorities, with particular interest in leaders aiming to found schools in the Gwinnett county area. For regions with significant charter presence, applicants will be required to make a strong case for how a new proposed charter school will be viable and meet the needs of the community. **Who We Are**Strong schools are built by strong leaders, which is why BES identifies and prepares exceptional individuals to transform education in their communities. From school founders and executive directors to operations leaders, deans, and curriculum directors, we train leaders to build schools, to ensure their schools excel, and to sustain their results over time. The BES Fellowship and selection process fosters an equitable, inclusive, and empowering experience for Fellows. For over two decades, BES Fellows have founded over 220 schools and are currently serving more than 73,000 students, with many BES-trained leaders consistently driving student achievement beyond district and state averages and helping to close the opportunity gap. **What You’ll Do** The BES Fellowship for founding school leaders includes approximately one year of training for Build Track Fellows followed by three years of Follow On Support to support leaders in building a high-performing, locally responsive school. For a comprehensive description of our Fellowship, please visit [our website.](https://bes.org/fellowship/) An overview is provided below. Fellows in Atlanta begin with an intensive training year, where they engage in over 300 hours of coursework on school design, leadership, governance, and community engagement, as well as diversity, equity, and inclusion. Fellows also conduct in-depth studies of effective schools across the nation and complete residencies at high-performing schools, all while developing a charter application and establishing a founding board. In year two, the planning year, Fellows partner with a BES coach to refine their project management and leadership skills, hire founding staff, recruit students, and solidify their school vision. This dedicated coaching and cohort-based training, known as Follow On Support, helps Fellows bridge the transition from founder to school leader, preparing them to launch a strong, sustainable school. During years three and four, the first two operational years, leaders put their vision into action, welcoming their inaugural class, coaching teachers, and using data to drive academic success. By the second year of operation, they deepen the academic focus, serving a growing population of students, and build leadership capacity to support future growth, all while fostering an empowered, mission-aligned team. In year three of operation and beyond, BES Fellow-founded schools can opt-in to other [leadership and professional development opportunities](https://bes.org/programs/) from BES to support their school and strengthen their leadership bench. **What You Bring** - **The ability to lead, manage and motivate:** You have demonstrated the ability to lead and manage a team towards results, and you are committed to serving as a school leader in the community for at least 10 years. - **Self awareness and humility:** You possess a growth mindset and have a continuous desire to improve. You are eager to give, take, and implement feedback with humility and in real time. - **Commitment to community:** You have experience in the community you are proposing for your school and bring strong organizational partnerships. You can articulate how you will gain and factor in community input. - **Diversity, equity and inclusion in action**: Your school model will primarily serve students from under-sourced communities and bring an anti-racist lens to the work. You have had success with similar populations of students and been responsive to community needs. - **Commitment to excellence for all students**: You have a clear vision for your school and can discuss key elements of the school in a detailed, compelling, and direct manner. You hold yourself accountable for results and believe that all students can achieve at high levels. **Qualifications** - Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s or Professional degree preferred - Minimum 8 years of professional experience, with instructional or instructional leadership experience required - At least 2 years managing and supervising adults in a PreK-12 setting required, 2 years of school leadership experience preferred - Commitment to serving as a school leader in the proposed community for at least 10 years required - Ability to establish and activate local connections to support school enrollment - Strong preference for candidates with at least 2-3 years of experience living or working in the proposed school region, especially those with strong ties to the community - Clear, compelling rationale for the proposed school location - Experience in career-connected learning and/or existing workforce partnerships preferred **Compensation and Benefits** - This is a contract role with a $110,000 grant during the first year of the program (the Fellowship training year) - Healthcare reimbursement of up to $6,000 for an individual healthcare plan or up to $8,000 for a family plan - Travel and accommodations for training and during school study travel - Reimbursement for up to $5,000 in moving expenses - Reimbursements for school design expenses, design team expenses, or professional development (amount dependent on track) - The opportunity to apply for BES start-up fund awards and/or those provided exclusively to Fellows by our partners **Additional Information** The BES Fellowship training year runs from January 2027 through December 2027, during which time BES Fellows will receive disbursements from their $110,000 grant. While grant disbursements will end in December 2027 (or typically 12 months after beginning the Fellowship), the authorization process in certain regions can sometimes extend beyond that time. Note that the beginning and end date for the Atlanta Fellowship will depend on the local counties’ authorization timeline AND a candidate’s readiness. BES Fellows will continue to receive coaching and guidance from BES through this phase to help them navigate the entirety of the authorization process. In addition, BES will work with Fellows affected by this timeline to identify additional funding opportunities for Fellows, wherever possible. Please note that Fellows may begin assignments prior to Fellowship orientation. **To Apply**Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. As such, applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible in order to secure limited spots in our available regions. Before applying, please review our [Applicant Toolkit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gS4Bp1MJqpaYYMks7LVPjORcUS3tacKa2x-e50JrjWw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.v97uvu8prgy1), which includes guidance and resources to support you through the application process. If you are interested in founding a school in a region other than Atlanta please note that additional regions will be announced as they become available. **In the meantime, please consider these next steps:** - Subscribe to receive updates on new regions [here](https://bes.org/contact/). - Complete [this interest form](https://40h7f1.share-na2.hsforms.com/232tkk4c5SeGpY-fiqo3D3w) to share where you hope to found a school. - [Connect with our team](https://bes.org/fellowship-more-info/) with questions about the Fellowship or selection process. *It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.*

ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation. We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government. We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust. ABOUT THE UNIT Public Affairs Division The Public Affairs division engages New Yorkers, informs them about elections, and boosts their participation in the democratic process. We make election information accessible and relevant, increase engagement with underrepresented communities, and cultivate a team that reflects our core values of purpose, curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. The division includes Marketing and Digital Communications, Community Engagement, Language Access, and Public Relations. Our division’s work includes publishing the citywide Voter Guide, running the official citywide Debates Program, and managing the voter engagement initiative, NYC Votes. Community Engagement Unit The Community Engagement unit works to build partnerships across the city to disseminate voting information, deliver accessible voter education, and conduct direct to voter outreach. Through relationships with community-based organizations as well as on-the-ground voter outreach, this team creates pathways for all New Yorkers to gain trustworthy and accessible information and education around voting and democracy. JOB DESCRIPTION NYC Votes aims to increase civic participation among New Yorkers through Community Education and Outreach efforts, with a particular focus on reaching priority audiences, including voters under 30, voters with disabilities, voters impacted by the criminal legal system, and voters who speak languages other than English. Although we're seeking three interns to join the Partnerships & Outreach team, this posting is focused on our one Community Outreach Intern. One Community Outreach Intern will report to the Senior Outreach Manager and support outreach efforts in low-turnout neighborhoods across New York City, with a focus on engaging communities that speak languages other than English (LOTE). This intern will support the research, preparation, implementation, and evaluation of outreach events; contribute creative outreach tactics, and lead strategy development for maximizing our impact and reach in priority communities. The interns will also support the Partnerships and Outreach team in building and maintaining strong internal systems to organize and track partnership development. This includes maintaining team databases, documenting outreach efforts, and supporting data entry. The responsibilities and tasks to be completed in this role include, but are not limited to: - Supporting the team’s efforts to build relationships with key stakeholders, such as City-agencies, CBOs, schools, and college campuses, to increase voter turnout. The Community Outreach intern will be expected to travel independently to deliver NYC Votes civic engagement curriculum to priority audiences. - Understanding, tracking, and meeting community needs through the provision of resources and materials, education delivery, event execution, among other engagement and education approaches. - Identify organizations that work in our priority neighborhoods and/or serve one or more of our priority communities, including voters under 30, voters with disabilities, and systems-impacted voters. - Research legislation and public policy relevant to our priority communities; compile this research and present at the end of summer. - Support the development and delivery of outreach programming for priority audiences, including voters under 30, voters with disabilities, voters who speak languages other than English, and voters impacted by the criminal legal system. - Work with staff to design and implement a capstone project, a signature outreach event tailored to a high-need priority neighborhood, incorporating community input and creative civic engagement tactics. ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs) We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. We believe in the power of diverse perspectives and the unique blend of lived experiences, non-traditional education pathways, practical know-how, and a variety of skills and abilities that each candidate brings to the table. If you're ready to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply and be part of our dynamic team. Knowledge - Major in relevant field such as: Political Science, Community Organizing, English, Journalism, Ethnic or Cultural Studies, Social Work, Public Administration, etc. - Understanding or experience with New York City institutions such as libraries, public schools, criminal legal system, etc. - Interest in New York City politics and/or social justice. Skills - Strong organization skills and attention to detail. - Proficiency with Microsoft Suite. - Strong written and oral communication skills. - Strong active listening skills and ability to respond in real time to the concerns and needs of the public. Abilities - Willingness to ask questions and learn on the job. - Experience with public speaking and community education. - Strong facilitation skills, as this intern will be responsible for independently leading workshops and trainings for New Yorkers. Other Characteristics - Adaptable and effective collaborator. - Ability to learn through receiving and implementing feedback. - Willingness to engage in conversation that challenge assumptions and pre-conceived notions of different groups in a way that leads toward culturally competent approach. - Ability to work evenings and/or weekends, as needed. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS While completing the application, candidates are invited to provide a cover letter via “attachment” or the “Message to the Hiring Team” field on SmartRecruiters. Please indicate in your cover letter if you’re interested in the community outreach position or the community education position. description: **About Us** SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. **Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja**, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. **AI at SharkNinja** At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in. **Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience:** Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast. Are you the person who finds the error everyone else already signed off on? Do you want to understand how a product gets from a factory to a shelf on another continent — and who decides how many to send? Are you excited by the challenge of making a fast-growing global company run better? If so, we invite you to learn more about Business Operations & Corporate Functions Co-op opportunities at SharkNinja. This is a single application for business operations, commercial, finance, and corporate function early talent roles across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our sales and retail analytics, strategic planning, global expansion, supply chain, finance, People & Culture, communications, and legal functions. Whichever team you join, you’ll work on the systems and decisions that keep a global consumer business moving. You might be building the dashboard a sales team runs its week on, modeling how many units a new product will sell in three countries, repositioning inventory after an S&OP meeting, reconciling what a product actually costs to make, localizing a launch for a market you’ve never visited, recruiting the next co-op cohort, or researching the regulation that shapes how we handle consumer data. If you’re analytical, organized, curious, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you! **Teams that you can be connected to through this posting include:** - Sales - Retail Excellence Systems & Analytics - Strategic Planning & Operations - APAC NPD Commercial Readiness - Geo Expansion - Supply Planning - Finance - People & Culture (Early Talent, Talent Acceleration, Employer Brand) - Corporate Communications - Legal **Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:** - Work on the analysis, planning, and process behind real commercial decisions across Shark and Ninja - Build the reports, dashboards, models, and trackers that leaders actually make calls from - Turn messy data into a clear recommendation — and then defend it in the room - Partner across sales, marketing, supply chain, finance, product, and regional teams, often across time zones - Find the inefficiency nobody has gotten around to fixing, and fix it - Present your findings and recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders and senior leaders - Learn how a global consumer business actually operates — its systems, approvals, cadences, and speed - Own a meaningful project end to end and present your contributions to SharkNinja leaders Depending on the team, your day-to-day may include: **Sales, Retail Excellence & Analytics** - Preparing sales reports, dashboards, and account presentations that track performance and surface actionable insights - Analyzing sales data and market trends across retail partners to identify growth opportunities and support account planning - Building and maintaining dashboards on sales performance, inventory, and retail KPIs using Excel, Tableau, Power BI, and SQL - Developing automated reporting solutions that improve operational efficiency and data accuracy - Supporting retailer-facing customer meetings — preparation, agendas, briefing documents, logistics, and follow-ups - Maintaining the national sales team’s resource hub and helping create digital learning content such as training modules, video tutorials, and interactive guides - Facilitating communication between internal departments and key accounts, and researching industry trends, competitors, and consumer preferences - Supporting retail initiatives that improve sell-through, shelf presence, and consumer experience **Strategic Planning, Global Expansion & Supply** - Identifying and implementing process improvements across departments and geographies for standardization, efficiency, and cost reduction - Supporting a portfolio of transformation projects — stakeholder analysis, communication strategies, training programs, and KPI reporting to executive leadership - Monitoring retailer-level sell-through, connecting insights to forecast accuracy and supply needs, and building market share projections and high/medium/low forecast scenarios by country - Analyzing how promotions, media investments, and product placements affect forecast accuracy and category momentum - Tracking APAC program timelines and critical launch schedules, owning artwork and translation requirements, and routing local market insights back to the US team - Supporting localized products, packaging, and marketing for LATAM and EMEA, and coordinating product sample orders for Geo Expansion distributor partners - Purchase order management and SKU replenishment, inventory portfolio reviews, DC inventory balancing, and master data maintenance - Participating in weekly S&OP meetings and repositioning inventory levels based on the outputs **Finance** - Maintaining and validating standard costing assumptions including factory costs, freight, amortization, overhead, royalties, and duties - Analyzing cost changes driven by raw materials, labor, foreign exchange, and engineering adjustments across product lines - Partnering with Inventory Accounting to reconcile purchase price variances and support inventory valuation analysis - Participating in month-end close with a focus on purchases and inventory reconciliation - Building standardized reporting templates and supporting automation of SharkNinja’s product costing systems - Taking on ad hoc financial analysis, standard cost maintenance, and global margin analysis **People & Culture, Communications & Legal** - Supporting full-cycle early talent recruiting — job postings, resume reviews, interview coordination, and candidate communications — and tracking recruiting metrics in systems such as Workday or Greenhouse - Planning and attending campus events, building university partnerships, and designing recruitment marketing assets in Canva for LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram, and the Careers site - Supporting onboarding, leadership development, and learning programs, and building digital content, toolkits, program calendars, and participant communications - Drafting internal and external communications and helping tell employee and company stories across channels - Conducting legal and regulatory research on frameworks such as CSRD, ISSB, GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA, and supporting privacy impact assessments and ESG reporting - Reviewing and organizing documentation for disclosures, policies, and corporate governance initiatives **ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:** - Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s or PhD program or has graduated from such a program within the past year— Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Supply Chain or Operations, Analytics or Statistics, International Business, Marketing, Human Resources or Organizational Behavior, Communications, Pre-Law, or similar - Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week onsite-hybrid schedule - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the judgment to turn data into a recommendation rather than just a chart - High accuracy and attention to detail with large datasets, financial figures, and operational records - Strong organizational skills — you can hold several workstreams and deadlines at once without dropping the details - Clear, professional written and verbal communication with stakeholders at every level, including presentations to management - Proactive and self-motivated: you take ownership, flag issues early, and follow through - Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities in a fast-moving environment - Collaborative and cross-functional by instinct, including across time zones and regions - Advanced Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP, modeling) and confidence in PowerPoint - Discretion and professionalism with confidential financial, employee, and legal information - Prior internship, campus leadership, research, or case competition experience is a strong asset **Any of the following are a plus — we don’t expect all of them:** - Data and BI tools: Tableau, Power BI, or SQL - Financial modeling and reporting tools - Sales enablement and CRM systems such as Showpad, Salesforce, or LMS platforms - Applicant tracking systems such as Workday or Greenhouse, and Canva for digital and printed assets - Familiarity with supply chain concepts — S&OP, purchase order management, inventory planning, and DC operations - Understanding of retail fundamentals such as incrementality, cannibalization, and market share dynamics - Project management or change management coursework or experience - Applying AI and automation to business process improvement - Coursework in data ethics, cybersecurity, or global privacy frameworks; privacy tools such as OneTrust - Consumer packaged goods (CPG) or consumer products experience - Language fluency, particularly Spanish or Portuguese, to support LATAM and international markets ***This evergreen job post is for upcoming Business Operations & Corporate Functions Co-ops at SharkNinja. We’re continuously seeking exceptional candidates who aspire to make a positive impact on people’s lives. Your application will be thoroughly reviewed for potential future opportunities within our team. We encourage you to explore all relevant current openings and apply accordingly.*** **Salary and Other Compensation:** The hourly salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more. Hourly Pay Range $26—$35 USD **Our Culture** At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. **Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset** drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home. **What We Offer** We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. **We empower your personal and professional growth** with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. **When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community.** Together, we won’t just launch products—**we’ll disrupt entire markets.** At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA. Learn more about us: [Life At SharkNinja](https://www.instagram.com/sharkninja/) [**Outrageously Extraordinary**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLmRfBxyGu_mKl9SF12lM1NAIx-z07uLNQ) **SharkNinja Candidate Privacy Notice** - For candidates based in **all regions**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/candidate-privacy-notice.html). - For candidates based in **China**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-china.html). - For candidates based in **Vietnam**, please refer to this [Candidate Privacy Notice](https://www.sharkninja.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice-vietnam.html). *We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other class protected by legislation, and local law. SharkNinja will consider reasonable accommodations consistent with legislation, and local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact SharkNinja People & Culture at [accommodations@sharkninja.com](mailto:accommodations@sharkninja.com)*

description: # **Chart Your Journey at Secretariat** From a collaborative culture to teammates who will always be by your side, find a career that will grow with you. Deliver your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT THE FIRM** Secretariat is a consulting firm that helps companies, law firms, and organizations solve complex business problems—often when there is a dispute, investigation, major project challenge, or high-stakes decision involved. At Secretariat, you’ll work on some of the most important legal, risk, and regulatory challenges facing businesses around the world. From your first day, you’ll be part of a fast-growing team of smart, curious, and driven people who enjoy solving complex problems. You’ll learn by working alongside experienced professionals and contributing to projects for leading law firms, global companies, and major institutions. Our teams collaborate across offices and disciplines, bringing energy, fresh thinking, and commitment to every client challenge. We invest in your growth through hands-on experience, mentorship, professional development, recognition, and a culture that values diverse perspectives. Start your career where your work matters. Make your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT OUR ECONOMICS TEAM** Secretariat’s Economics team helps clients understand the numbers behind major business and legal questions. As part of our casework, our team members may analyze the impact of a merger on competition, estimate company losses in a dispute due to patent infringement or stolen trade secrets, determine employee fair compensation, or study the effect of market rules and regulations on businesses. Much of our work supports complex litigation, regulatory investigations, and business disputes, where our economists analyze evidence and help explain economic issues to courts, regulators, and decision-makers. **RESPONSIBILITIES** Launch your career by putting your classroom skills to work on real cases, real data, and real business challenges. As an Intern, you will use your curiosity, analytical mindset, and communication skills to help clients navigate high-stakes decisions while learning directly from experienced experts in economics, intellectual property, finance, and litigation consulting. Interns play an active role on project teams, working under the supervision of experienced case managers and alongside recent graduates and PhD economists to address complex business challenges. This opportunity is ideal for students who enjoy asking “why,” digging into data, solving puzzles, researching new industries, and writing reports that turn complex information into a clear story. The skills you develop as an Intern can support a wide range of career paths in consulting, economics, finance, analytics, and beyond. If you are excited by economics, finance, math, data, or coding—and want a role where you can grow quickly, contribute early, and see the impact of your work—Secretariat is the place to build that momentum. What you’ll get to do: - Dive into real-world data to uncover what is happening in companies, markets, and industries - Support quantitative analysis, including gathering, processing, and analyzing data, and conduct qualitative market and industry research - Explore business issues that go beyond the textbook by researching companies, competitors, and industries - Turn numbers, research, and analysis into insights that clients and legal teams can act on - Create clear visuals and presentations that bring complex ideas to life - Build hands-on experience with tools like Excel, R, Stata, or Python **QUALIFICATIONS** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, data science or a related field - Expected graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 - Minimum GPA of 3.5 - Comfortable using Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and experience with Stata, Python, or R - Enjoys solving problems, thinking logically, and using analysis to support recommendations - Has experience working with data through coursework, projects, research, internships, or other hands-on activities - Brings curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to learn new tools, topics, and ways of thinking - Pays close attention to details, stays organized, and takes pride in producing high-quality work - Works well independently while also enjoying collaboration with teammates, mentors, and project leaders - Communicates clearly in writing and conversation, especially when explaining research, data, or ideas - Is authorized to work in the U.S. without needing sponsorship now or in the future Interested in joining us? Please submit your resume/CV, a cover letter, a writing sample and all applicable transcripts. At Secretariat, we believe in pay transparency and equity. Compensation for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, and location. Further details will be provided during the hiring process. Pay Transparency $20—$30 USD ## A rewarding career above all There are a lot of fine consulting firms out there. But when everything is on the line, it takes a unique combination of skill and savvy to succeed under pressure. Our culture and people are driven by passion, pride, and performance. Passion for the clients we serve, the work we deliver, and the communities we live in. Pride in our cohesive team recognized for excellence and trusted to perform in the most challenging situations. And our track record of outstanding performance across all of our disciplines speaks for itself. [Our people](https://secretariat-intl.com/people/) are motivated to be the best in everything they do – from our approach to making the complex simple to the way we mentor our up-and-coming talent to become trusted experts early in their careers. To learn how Secretariat collects, uses, and protects your personal information during the recruitment process, please review our [Privacy Policy](#)

We are currently looking to hire a Finance Intern based on West Jordan, UT! As a Finance Intern, you will support the Plant Finance team through financial analysis, reporting, and process improvement initiatives. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to gain an understanding of manufacturing operations, assist with research and analysis projects, and translate operational activities into meaningful financial insights. This role provides hands-on experience in plant finance while supporting business objectives and continuous improvement efforts. Key Responsibilities As a key member of our team, you will play an important role in driving our mission forward. The following responsibilities outline the core expectations and contributions for this position: Supporting Plant Finance day-to-day activities through data collection, analysis, reporting, and administration support. Conducting research, analysis, and continuous improvement projects aligned with department and plant objectives. Partnering with cross-functional teams to understand manufacturing processes and their impact on plant financial performance. Analyzing operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement. Preparing reports, presentations, and recommendations to support business decision-making. Presenting project findings, financial analysis, and solution proposals to team members and plant leadership. Participating in job shadowing and learning opportunities across multiple departments to gain knowledge of plant operations. Maintaining accurate records and reporting documentation while adhering to company policies and procedures. Collaborating with team members to support department initiatives and special projects. Performing other duties as assigned. Physical Demands Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods throughout the workday. Ability to use a computer, keyboard, and other office equipment for prolonged periods. Ability to occasionally bend, reach, stoop, and lift or carry up to 25 pounds. Ability to move throughout the office and manufacturing environments safely. Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and electronically. Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) when entering manufacturing areas. Work Environment Work in both office and manufacturing plant environments. Regular exposure to active production operations, including forklift traffic and material handling activities. May be exposed to loud noise level, wet floors, condensation, agricultural odors, and varying temperatures within the facility. May be exposed to chemicals, heavy machinery, steam pipelines, and other manufacturing-related hazards while following established safety procedures. Must comply with all safety, food safety, quality, and company policies while working in a manufacturing environment. Engagement in our Integrated Work Systems Ensure adherence to plant standards and procedures (including but not limited to GMP, AIB, FDA, IWS, Quality, Safety, Finance, ISO, HOPE, Danone Behaviors, Daily Direction Setting, Driving OE). About You The ideal candidate will bring a combination of education, experience, and skills that enable them to excel in this position. Previous internship, project, leadership, or campus organization experience preferred. Experience with data analysis, financial modeling, or reporting tools preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, with advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel preferred. Basic understanding of accounting, finance, and business principles. Interest in manufacturing operations and plant finance processes. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret data and identify trends. Effective written communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports and presentations. Strong verbal communication and presentation skills with the ability to communicate across all levels of the organization. Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Ability to collaborate effectively within cross-functional teams. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while meeting deadlines and objectives. Demonstrate initiative, curiosity, and a continuous improvement mindset. Ability to learn new systems, processes, and business concepts quickly. Ability to analyze complex information and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Ability to adapt to a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Position Description: Assist in day-to-day supervised activities related to the development of a construction project to build foundational knowledge in construction management, business and project financial management, project safety protocols, subcontractor relationships, quality control, and project coordination and lifecycle. Where applicable, your assignment will support learning that applies to earning educational credits. Essential Duties Key Responsibilities: Depending on business need and location, the Intern/Co-Op will be supervised and assigned to work at an active construction project site, in a department located at a main office working in one of our many construction specialties. Support project team with meeting coordination, material tracking, file management, document control, and progress reporting. Comprehend and follow project site signage and supervisor instructions as directed. Provide progress reports to supervisor and be receptive to learning about construction management. Relate and apply knowledge acquired in the academic setting to work activities. Maintain professional relationships with employees, customers, clients, and subcontractors. Participate in training, meetings, and orientation. Comply with safety protocols, follow safety expectations, and wear appropriate PPE (Personal Protection Equipment). Other activities, duties, and responsibilities as assigned. Based on the assignment, the following activities may be performed (longer-term assignments may gain more in-depth experience and exposure): Assist with project start-up activities and provide support to Project Engineer, Project Superintendent, and/or Project Manager. Assist with collection and review of information and approvals for processing shop drawings, submittals, and Requests for Information (RFIs). Assist with preparation and distribution of information for contract requirements to appropriate parties. Assist with preparation of estimates for changes in work from subcontractors. Attend project site visits to observe and document construction field activities. Assist with preparation of and conduct correspondence and communication as directed to Architects, Engineers, vendors, and subcontractors in connection with performing their assigned trades. Assist with communication to Trades and subcontractors to understand and track job schedules. Assist with monitoring contractor compliance with Turner’s safety program, as directed. Assist with preparation of quantity take-offs and studies for project items using either traditional or computer-aided programs, learning and discussing details necessary to complete project. Request and distribute subcontractor proposals relative to their scope of work to assemble proposals for delivery system. Assist with project close out preparations.

Position Description: Assist in activities associated with safety and loss control while working on construction project or office location. Essential Duties Key Responsibilities: • Assist with implementing Building L.I.F.E. (Living Injury Free Everyday) and project safety program while working on construction project or office location and under direction by supervisor. • Assist with identifying and reporting safety violations or unsafe practices, with emphasis on situations of imminent danger to life or property. • Assist with coordination of safety duties for safety committees, preplanning meetings, and tool box meetings. • Assist with coordination of training at safety meetings, tool box meetings, and orientations. • Assist with reviewing subcontractor safety programs for completeness and compliance with company policies, • Assist with promoting safe work practices and safe working conditions in accordance with company, Federal, State and Local regulations, and owner/contractual requirements. • Assist with administration of drug screening program (e.g., pre-employment, post-accident, random, cause) aligned with company and/or client requirements. • Assist with preconstruction meetings and conducting research. Position Description: Participate in a structured Intern Program designed to apply academic knowledge to real-world business scenarios. Build foundational knowledge in Operational Finance, including training on accounting fundamentals, project finance concepts, and financial systems. Support day-to-day financial management activities across key accounting functions including Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, General Ledger, Reconciliation, and Special Services. Contribute to data collection, reporting, and analysis efforts while assisting with process improvements related to budgeting, cost tracking, variance analysis, and operational performance metrics. Gain exposure to emerging technologies, including use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data tools in finance to support analysis, improve efficiency, and enhance reporting processes. Where applicable this assignment will support learning that applies to earning educational credits. Intern may be assigned to a single construction project on a construction job site or to an office location supporting multiple projects. This opportunity is available during summer. Essential Duties Key Responsibilities: • Engage with full participation and immersion of Intern Program, take ownership to fulfill learning requirements and assigned responsibilities, while coordinating with supervisors to effectively prioritize work, manage time, and ensure successful completion of program and project deliverables. • Learn, understand, and apply Turner financial accounting processes, including construction accounting principles, earnings, and revenue recognition, with guidance from your supervisor. • Follow company and Finance policies related to financial reporting, confidentiality, and data governance. • Learn and develop skills related to effective communication, conflict resolution, taking direction, and teamwork. Maintain professional relationships with colleagues, clients, and business partners. • Participate in training sessions, meetings, project site visits, and other learning opportunities provided through Intern Program. • Review billing details against client contractual requirements for accuracy, review contracts and invoice backup for accurate accounts receivable. • Assist with validating coding of project costs and comparing invoices and expenses to project cost coding structures. • Support Shared Services Organization (SSO) with invoice processing tasks, verify subcontractor and vendor accounts status, including lien waivers and recoded costs to support accurate month-end work-in-place reporting. • Assist with analyzing budgets and reallocating costs through preparation of journal entries and in support of month-end close process. Assist with monitoring project cash flow, including billings, collections, and payments, and prepare payments held reports to support team communication and visibility. • Support under and overbilling analysis and participate in team meetings to support communication of project status. • Gain exposure to Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled tools and data analytics techniques to support financial analysis, reporting, and process efficiencies. • Contribute to process improvement initiatives, identify opportunities to use AI technology and automation to standardize financial workflows, templates, and reports. • Prepare ad hoc analyses and presentations to support financial reviews and management requests. • Share periodic progress updates with your supervisor and engage in feedback conversations to support learning and professional growth. • Other activities, duties, and responsibilities as assigned.

Job Summary The main objective of the peer coaching position are to help recruit, engage and retain students with a background in foster care and ensure they are accessing and utilizing resources/benefits available due to their status as a former foster youth, with particular attention to state tuition and fee waiver utilization. Peer coaches will work directly with identified students as they become familiar with Blinn's College's campus resources and any benefits or services for which they may be eligible. Peer coaches will engage students with experience in foster care by directly reaching out to students and provide individual support as appropriate. Peer coaches will work directly with and be supervised by the LPC Liaison in the Disability Services Office. Peer coaches will work directly with the Education Reach for Texas staff to learn, practice and document use of peer coaching as a model as part of a pilot program to increase engagement and access to campus and community resources. Principal Accountabilities Ability to follow through on assigned tasks and work independently. Attend all scheduled meetings Applicants should be familiar with campus processes including but not limited to meeting with academic advisors, class registration and accessing campus resources. Provide outreach and engagement to students at Blinn identified as having lived experience in the foster care system. Practice utilization of a peer coaching model being piloted for the project. Assist in assessment of students needs an eligibility for other services and benefits and connect students to resources as appropriate with the support of the institutions higher education foster care liaison. Track all touchpoints and other data related to the project and report on a regular basis to grant staff. Attend all in person and online trainings and professional development related to the peer coaching model and Education Reach for Texas annual conference and webinars. Maintain a simple budget of money to engage with students and programming.

role: 2027 Applied Science Internship - Automated Reasoning - United States, PhD Student Science Recruiting, Automated Reasoning
description: This role sits within Amazon's Automated Reasoning and Formal Verification research horizon. Shape the Future of Cloud Computing. Are you a graduate student passionate about Automated Reasoning and its real-world applications? Join our team of innovators and embark on a journey to revolutionize cloud computing through innovative automated reasoning techniques. Our tools are called billions of times daily, powering the backbone of Amazon's products and services. We are changing the way computer systems are developed and operated, raising the bar for security, durability, availability, and quality. Applied Scientists in Automated Reasoning develop and apply formal methods, automated reasoning techniques, and neurosymbolic approaches to ensure the security, reliability, and correctness of Amazon and AWS services and customer applications. Application areas span cloud infrastructure verification, cryptographic assurance, AI safety, and formal guarantees for generative AI systems. Methods range from interactive theorem proving and constraint solving to neuro-inspired proof search. As an Applied Science Intern, you will have the opportunity to work alongside our scientists and contribute to projects. From distributed proof search and SAT/SMT solvers to program analysis, synthesis, and verification, you will tackle complex challenges at the intersection of theory and practice. Key job responsibilities We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in: Theorem Proving, Boolean Satisfiability Solvers, Bounded Model Checking, Deductive Verification, Programming/Scripting Languages, Abstract Interpretation, Automated Reasoning, Static/Program Analysis, Program Synthesis. Contribute to the design and implementation of algorithms and formal methods for automated reasoning, including constraint solving, model checking, static analysis, theorem proving, and program synthesis, within a guided research framework. Explore and apply generative AI and machine learning techniques to enhance automated reasoning, including learning-based heuristics for search, neural approaches to symbolic reasoning, and methods for verifying the correctness of AI-generated code. Contribute to automated reasoning techniques for generative AI and agentic coding systems, including methods that apply formal guarantees to large language model outputs. Contribute to the scientific community through publications at peer-reviewed conferences and journals. Leverage AI-powered tools where applicable to accelerate research, experimentation, and prototyping. Critically review and validate outputs from AI tools and automated systems. The ideal intern must have the ability to communicate research findings clearly to diverse audiences.

## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** Base designs its own hardware, builds it in its own factory, installs it at homes, and sells the power. That vertical integration is our advantage, and it means the suppliers we choose and the deals we strike directly shape our cost and speed. As a GSM Intern, you will own sourcing for a set of assigned parts, run the RFQ process end to end, and negotiate cost and terms directly with suppliers. This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to source, suppliers to negotiate with, and quotes that carry real weight in our build cost. The work sits between Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Finance, and suits someone who thinks in systems, is comfortable acting on incomplete information, and likes building durable, repeatable sourcing processes. ## **What You’ll Do** - Own sourcing for a set of assigned parts: build and run RFQs, compare supplier quotes on cost, lead time, and capacity, and make the call on award. - Negotiate price, payment terms, and lead time directly with suppliers, and track savings against the prior baseline. - Build supplier cost models — bottoms-up where you can — so you can tell a fair quote from a padded one. - Support qualification of new suppliers and second sources for critical components: gather quotes, samples, and capability data for the team’s decision. - Track supplier performance — cost, delivery, and quality — and flag risk before it hits the production line. ## **What You’ll Bring** - Working toward a degree in supply chain, industrial engineering, operations, mechanical engineering, business, or another quantitative field — or on a comparable path. - Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort working with large, messy datasets. SQL, Python, or scripting is a plus. - Genuine interest in how physical products get built. Exposure to an MRP or ERP system (Odoo, SAP, NetSuite) is a plus, not a requirement. - Clear, direct written communication — you will send RFQs, quote comparisons, and escalations to suppliers and internal teams. - Bias to action and follow-through. You close loops without being asked twice. - Available to work in person in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship. ## **About the Team** Global Supply Management owns every part that goes into a Base battery and its associated systems. This includes sourcing, planning, and getting it to the line on time. We are ramping in-house manufacturing of our own battery product while qualifying second sources for critical components, which means the plan changes often and the cost of being wrong is a stopped line. Sourcing is where that pressure lands first: the team decides who we buy from and on what terms, and builds the leverage and systems that make those calls repeatable. *Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.* ## **Our Values** - **First Principles Thinking:** Question assumptions. Principles > rules. - **Operate at Base Pace:** Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing. - **Give & Get Feedback:** Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset. - **Everyone’s an Owner:** Follow through on commitments and own results. - **Strong Opinions, Loosely Held:** Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information. - **Committed to the Mission:** Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in. - **Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit:** Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things. ## **Do the best work of your life at Base.**

## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** We're looking for an Accounting Intern to get hands-on experience across the core of what our accounting team does day to day. You'll support month-end close, help keep the books accurate, and get exposure to how accounts payable, accounts receivable, reconciliations, and reporting actually work at a fast-growing company — not just the theory from a textbook. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants real reps on the fundamentals: journal entries, reconciliations, and the discipline of making sure every number ties out. You'll also have room to bring fresh thinking to how we work — using AI tools to speed up manual tasks and automate reconciliations, and helping develop and enhance our monthly reporting processes. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About You and The Role** The Technical Writing team builds and maintains a dependable documentation system that supports safe, effective work across Zipline’s products and operations. We partner with engineering, operations, and support to translate complex technical and operational information into clear manuals, procedures, guides, references, onboarding materials, and troubleshooting content. Our work spans the full documentation lifecycle, from understanding user needs and how systems operate to organizing, editing, reviewing, and publishing content. We set a high bar for accuracy, clarity, consistency, usability, and timeliness while making it easier for people to find the right information at the right time. ### What You'll Do - Documentation Quality: Help review and improve manuals, procedures, guides, and other content for clarity, accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and usability. - Training and Guide Refresh: Update materials to reflect current product behavior, use timeless language, and broaden content for the audiences and products it serves. - Information Architecture: Improve site navigation and content structure around user tasks and workflows so readers can reach the right information more easily. - Troubleshooting Guide Structure: Reorganize troubleshooting pages so context, prerequisites, and supporting information lead clearly into step-by-step guidance. - Contributor Onboarding: Simplify onboarding documentation by clarifying prerequisites, setup, contribution guidelines, review expectations, and the path from a proposed change to published content. - Technical Understanding: Read technical source material, ask questions about how systems and processes operate, and help identify documentation gaps or opportunities for improvement. - Review and Collaboration: Work with technical writers, engineers, and operations partners to validate accuracy, check clarity and page flow, and incorporate feedback. ### What You'll Bring - Educational Background: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in English, Rhetoric and Composition, Technical or Professional Writing, Journalism, Communications, Information Science, Computer Science, or a related field. - Writing and Editing: Strong editing and writing skills, with the ability to make documentation accurate, clear, specific, complete, and concise. - Technical Communication: Ability to explain technical concepts to people with different levels of technical familiarity. - Technical Curiosity: Interest in learning how software, hardware, and operational systems work, and willingness to learn from technical source material. - Organization and Information Design: Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to structure complex information, evaluate priorities, and manage multiple documentation tasks. - Logical and Creative Thinking: Ability to think logically and creatively about how information should be structured for different audiences and tasks. - Collaboration and Independence: Collaborative, self-directed, and comfortable receiving feedback while making progress on defined projects **Bonus Qualifications:** - Experience with version-controlled documentation workflows or content management systems. - Experience creating documentation for software, hardware, operations, or other complex technical domains. - Experience using AI tools to draft, edit, or review content, with an interest in developing responsible editorial workflows. - Interest in robotics, aviation, logistics, service operations, or other technical products. ### What Else You Need to Know The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48". Walking · For short distances for short durations · Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location. Sitting Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table Lifting · Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck. · Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'. · Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high. Carrying · Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves. · Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store. · Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray. · During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties. Pushing · To move trays which are placed on dollies. · A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push. · Trays may also be pulled. Climbing · Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance. · During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required. Stooping/Bending · Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station. · Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station. · Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day. · Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients. **About Us** Curi Capital, founded in 2005, is a rapidly growing national registered investment advisory firm (RIA) based in Chicago. We are committed to building meaningful relationships and making a difference in our clients’ financial wellness. Our mission is focused on enriching the lives of our teammates, clients, partners, and the communities in which we live and work. Curi Capital is perennially ranked among Barron’s Top 100 Independent Registered Investment Advisors globally. Our values—Accountability, Curiosity, Teamwork, Inclusion, and Service Commitment—are at the core of our culture. **Program** **Duration:** 10 Weeks, Paid | **Eligible:** College Juniors **Build Real Experience at a Top-Ranked RIA** Our Wealth Management Internship Program gives college juniors a genuine look at how a wealth management firm operates, working alongside the advisors and leaders who guide clients through some of the most important financial decisions of their lives. **What You'll Actually Do** From day one, you'll be exposed to all aspects of our Client Advisory business unit, working on real projects with real stakes. Over 10 weeks, you'll: - Partner with your team on meaningful projects and research that inform actual client and business decisions - Sit in on client and prospect meetings, seeing firsthand how our advisors build trust and deliver recommendations - Get hands-on exposure to planning, portfolio construction, and the technical work behind the scenes that most students never see until years into their careers - Communicate directly with clients, vendors, and internal teams, sharpening the professional instincts you'll rely on for the rest of your career By the end of the summer, you won't just have a line on your resume. You'll have a genuine, firsthand understanding of what a career in wealth management actually looks like, and the clarity to know where your own skills and interests fit best. **Who Thrives Here** We're looking for students who are naturally curious, driven, and ready to bring energy to a team environment. You're a strong fit if you: - Are pursuing a degree in Finance, Trust and Wealth Management, or general business - Have taken on a leadership role in a club, organization, or job, and know how to own a responsibility - Bring sharp analytical thinking and genuine curiosity about financial markets and business strategy - Communicate clearly and confidently, whether in a client meeting, a team huddle, or a written summary - Are organized enough to juggle multiple projects and self-motivated enough to run with ambiguity - Have a solid handle on Microsoft Office, especially Outlook, Word, and Excel - Take confidentiality and integrity seriously, because our clients expect high integrity from each and every member of the team - Give examples of how you demonstrate accountability, curiosity, teamwork, inclusion, service commitment **Why Curi Capital** Unlike an internship at a large brokerage or investment bank, you won't be just another intern for the marketing materials. You'll engage with employees across several departments in the firm, building a network and a perspective that most students don't get until much later in their careers. This is a place where curiosity is rewarded, questions are welcomed, and at the end of the internship, you'll showcase what you learned throughout the program to your mentor and leadership. If you're ready to spend your summer doing work that matters, at a firm that's proud to be recognized among the best in the industry, we want to hear from you. **Compensation and work schedule** $10,000 stipend for a 10-week program. The schedule is Monday – Thursday 9am – 4pm, and Friday 9am – 3pm local time. The base salary will be commensurate with an individual's work experience and educational background. US Pay Range $10,000—$10,000 USD ### **Our Vision:** To be the trusted partner in medicine, business, and life. ### **Our Mission:** By providing valued advice and support, we help strengthen care, mitigate risk, and build financial futures to enhance the lives of those we serve. ### **Our Values:** - **Accountability:** *We are driven to act, work with integrity, and deliver results.* - **Curiosity:***We ask and listen, stay curious, and are eager to learn.* - **Teamwork**: *We build strong relationships, celebrate success, and partner for greater impact.* - **Inclusion:** *We respect, recognize, and encourage the differences that make us stronger—we are better together* *Built On;* - **Service Commitment:** *We demonstrate an unwavering commitment to our clients, business partners, teammates, and communities.* **Our Benefits** Curi Capital offers eligible team members and their dependents comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance. Other benefits for eligible team members include education assistance, annual bonus opportunity, 401(k) with employer match, short-term and long-term disability, flexible time off, and 13 paid holidays annually. **Mission**Cowboy Space Corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. We are tackling one of humanity's most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects — from orbit to Earth. **Background**Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport. Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases. Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. Inspired by his father's work with NASA Langley Research Center, Baiju earned his B.S. in Physics and M.S. in Mathematics at Stanford before co-founding Robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million Americans access the financial system. Cowboy Space Corporation has raised ~$365 million from Index Ventures, Interlagos, Construct Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and others. This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Cowboy Space Corporation's team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA, and is based in San Carlos, CA. If you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you. **About the Role** We're looking for a Mechanical/Aerospace Engineering Intern to join our team in Kent, Washington for Summer 2027. This is a hands-on opportunity to work alongside experienced spacecraft engineers on the mechanical systems that make our orbital solar power satellites possible — from structural design and thermal management to assembly, integration, and test. You'll contribute to real hardware that is on the path to flight, not a simulated project, while learning directly from engineers who have built spacecraft at SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis, and NASA. **Responsibilities** - Support the design and analysis of structural, mechanical, or thermal subsystems using CAD tools and engineering analysis methods - Assist in developing and executing test plans for mechanical hardware, including structural, vibration, thermal, or deployment testing - Participate in the build, integration, and assembly of flight or engineering development hardware in the lab - Analyze test data and generate technical reports summarizing findings, anomalies, and design recommendations - Collaborate cross-functionally with electrical, software, and systems engineering teams to resolve integration issues - Support fabrication and machine shop activities, including reviewing drawings and coordinating with machinists or vendors - Help maintain engineering documentation, including drawings, test procedures, and design change requests - Present findings and progress updates to the engineering team throughout the internship **Basic Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field - Coursework or hands-on project experience in mechanical design, structural analysis, or thermal systems (e.g., senior design, formula/rocketry/robotics teams, research lab work) - Proficiency with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, CATIA, or similar) - Strong fundamentals in statics, dynamics, materials, and/or thermodynamics - Demonstrated ability to work hands-on with hardware, not just simulation or theory - Strong ownership mentality, comfort with ambiguity, and ability to work effectively in a fast-paced startup environment - Available to work on-site in Kent, WA for the full duration of the Summer 2027 internship **Preferred Qualifications** - Experience with spacecraft, aerospace structures, or other flight hardware programs (internship, co-op, or extracurricular project team) - Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) tools (e.g., ANSYS, Nastran) - Exposure to machining, fabrication, or hands-on prototyping **Compensation** (Quarter-long internship) — Paid $1,800 weekly Daily lunch in the office and a fully stocked kitchen with beverages and snacks **ITAR Requirements** Export Control Requirement: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Are you working toward your BCBA and looking for a practicum experience that actually supports your growth? Centria’s Elevate Program is a full-time, paid practicum opportunity where you'll earn supervision hours, mentorship, and support across all hours, all while building real clinical experience with children and families. As part of the Elevate team, you’ll work as a Behavior Technician (BT) or Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) and progress through a structured, three-stage pathway, **Emerge**, **Empower**, **Ascend**, with built-in milestones, wage increases, and personalized support. **Compensation**: $19- $24 base pay with $2 per hour increases at each stage, plus full benefits. ### **What Centria Offers:** - **Fieldwork That Pays Off** – Every hour paid, both restricted and unrestricted fieldwork, while working within a role that grows with you. - **Structured Growth, Built In** – Follow Elevate’s three-stage model with clearly defined milestones, clinical competencies, and stage-based wage increases. - **Real Clinical Experience** – Provide 1:1 ABA therapy in home, center, or school settings, gaining hands-on experience across six key domains. - **Assent-Based ABA at Its Best** – Learn from leaders in Practical Functional Assessment, Skills-Based Treatment, and compassionate, client-led care. - **Mentorship That Matters** – Receive regular 1:1 and group supervision from experienced BCBAs and connect with a supportive network of mentors and peers. - **Clear Path to BCBA** – Graduate from the Elevate program into a BCBA role with post-certification tuition reimbursement (up to $20,000), career ladders, and internal promotions. - **Perks That Matter** – Full benefits (medical, dental, vision), paid time off, 401(k) with company match, tuition reimbursement, exclusive Elevate gear, and milestone recognition. ### **Your Role & Impact as a BCBA** - Lead ABA therapy delivery within a collaborative, in-center environment - Participate in small-group and 1:1 supervision with experienced BCBAs - Learn clinical best practices across six core domains: assessment, intervention, communication, documentation, program design, and ethics - Attend professional development sessions and apply learnings in real time - Progress through Elevate's structured stages and earn milestone rewards - Collaborate with a team that values compassion, client assent, and data-driven care ### **What You’ll Need** - Active enrollment in (or completion of) a master’s-level ABA program (verified before start date), or a completed master’s degree with enrollment in (or completion of) an ABA course sequence. - Strong desire to grow into a BCBA role within a values-driven care model - Ability to work full-time, including availability for afternoon and early evening hours **At Centria, you’re not just a BCBA - you’re a clinical leader, a mentor, and a changemaker. If you’re ready to grow your career without sacrificing your values, apply today and join a team that invests in your clinical excellence!** *Centria is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.*
