ISW Internship Program Overview ISW is offering in-person, remote, and hybrid internships for Spring 2027. Instructions to apply for the scholarship are below. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is committed to training the next generation of national security leaders through its innovative educational programs. ISW seeks motivated and experienced college students or recent graduates to join our intern team. ISW offers internships across diverse research portfolios and departments, including Russia, China, and Iran's Axis of Resistance. ISW also offers internships in Geospatial Intelligence and National Security Technologies, our Cognitive Warfare Task Force, and in Communications. Why Work for ISW? ISW believes that ground realities must drive the formulation of strategy and policy. In pursuit of this principle, ISW conducts detailed open-source intelligence analysis to provide timely and accurate information on current conflicts and security threats directly to policymakers and warfighters. Interns at ISW have an unparalleled opportunity to analyze conflicts in ways that directly inform policymakers on some of the most pressing issues facing American national security. Our interns work directly with analysts. They receive classroom education, regular leadership engagement, and a chance to work with cutting-edge technologies employed in business and the intelligence community. Interns have the opportunity to stand at the front lines of military research and policy development, tackling the latest crises in the headlines. The ISW Internship Program is one of three core education programs housed within The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders, launched to identify, educate, and develop the future cadre of leaders committed to America’s national security. ISW views interns as an integral component of its team. ISW has worked with interns to draft, edit, and publish their own research under the mentorship of senior analysts. It has also hired many interns onto its staff. Korean Peninsula Intelligence Analysis Internship : ISW is a leading source of innovative analysis and intelligence on global conflicts that threaten American national security. ISW publishes regular research reports and graphics to inform US and international policy-makers, warfighters, and journalists in Washington, DC, as well as the general public. Interns provide critical assistance to our analysts and receive hands-on training from their supervisors as well as a formal development program taught by our leadership. Interns will be trained to use innovative technologies to conduct open-source collection and analysis in a fast-paced environment. Interns will conduct the daily collection and analysis of open-source information in native language sources and contribute to the weekly Korean Peninsula Update (KPU) under the guidance of ISW researchers, in partnership with the Center for Defense of Taiwan (CDOT) at the American Enterprise Institute. In addition, interns collaborate with the wider research team to generate longer-term intelligence products; assist with editing, documenting, and compiling materials for publications; and support the planning, preparation, and execution of public events and private briefings held by ISW. This is a full-time internship (five days per week), but part-time work will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Qualifications Candidates must be motivated and organized college students or recent graduates with demonstrated expertise in a related field. Candidates must possess excellent writing, editing, and oral communication skills. Candidates should preferably possess strong critical language capabilities in Korean; language capabilities in Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, Russian, and other regional languages are a plus. Candidates must display the ability to conduct complex tasks in a timely and efficient manner. Candidates should be self-motivated, independent, creative, and capable of working in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Candidates must show commitment to—and interest in—the core mission and values of ISW. Spring 2027 Internship Program Dates: ISW internships starts on January 12, 2027. The program will run until May 14. Interns must both be authorized to work in the United States and be physically present in the United States during their internship tenure. Working remotely outside of the United States is not authorized. If you attend a US university on a student visa, you must be eligible for and obtain a CPT authorization before beginning at ISW. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Instructions: Please upload your resume, cover letter, and writing sample. Your cover letter and writing sample should be no longer than five pages combined; the writing sample can be excerpted from a longer paper. ISW will work with students to gain academic credit for internships where applicable. ISW Scholarship Application The Institute for the Study of War will offer intern candidates up to a $1,000 monthly living stipend as part of a scholarship program.* To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Candidates will be assessed based on the following criteria: Ability to contribute as a member of one of ISW’s research, operations, business development, or external relations teams; and Financial need, such that an unpaid internship would not be possible without assistance. Within the scholarship application, candidates should upload a 2- to 3-page cover letter which answers each of the following questions. (This should be a different cover letter than the one used for the internship application itself.) Which ISW internship is your top choice? Why do you believe you are qualified? What do you believe to be the most pressing national security problem the US faces today? What solution(s) would you propose? Where do you see yourself in your future career? How will an ISW internship help you get there? Why have you chosen to apply for this supplemental scholarship? Are you currently receiving federal financial aid and/or need-based aid from your university? Feel free to describe using as much detail as you are comfortable. *Please note that the up to $1,000 monthly scholarship is classified as taxable income. Questions? Email for more information.

role: Middle East Intelligence Analysis Internship Spring 2027
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description: ISW Internship Program Overview ISW is offering in-person, remote, and hybrid internships for Spring 2027. Instructions to apply for the scholarship are below. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is committed to training the next generation of national security leaders through its innovative educational programs. ISW seeks motivated and experienced college students or recent graduates to join our intern team. ISW offers internships across diverse research portfolios and departments, including Russia, China, and Iran's Axis of Resistance. ISW also offers internships in Geospatial Intelligence and National Security Technologies, our Cognitive Warfare Task Force, and in Communications. Why Work for ISW? ISW believes that ground realities must drive the formulation of strategy and policy. In pursuit of this principle, ISW conducts detailed open-source intelligence analysis to provide timely and accurate information on current conflicts and security threats directly to policymakers and warfighters. Interns at ISW have an unparalleled opportunity to analyze conflicts in ways that directly inform policymakers on some of the most pressing issues facing American national security. Our interns work directly with analysts. They receive classroom education, regular leadership engagement, and a chance to work with cutting-edge technologies employed in business and the intelligence community. Interns have the opportunity to stand at the front lines of military research and policy development, tackling the latest crises in the headlines. The ISW Internship Program is one of three core education programs housed within The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders, launched to identify, educate, and develop the future cadre of leaders committed to America’s national security. ISW views interns as an integral component of its team. ISW has worked with interns to draft, edit, and publish their own research under the mentorship of senior analysts. It has also hired many interns onto its staff. Middle East Intelligence Analysis Internship : ISW is a leading source of innovative analysis and intelligence on global conflicts that threaten American national security. ISW publishes regular research reports and graphics to inform US and international policy-makers, warfighters, and journalists in Washington, DC, as well as the general public. Interns provide critical assistance to our analysts and receive hands-on training from their supervisors as well as a formal development program taught by our leadership. Interns will be trained to use innovative technologies to conduct open-source collection and analysis in a fast-paced environment. Interns will conduct the daily collection and analysis of open-source information in native language sources and contribute to long-term research projects on Iran’s Axis of Resistance, Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen under the guidance of ISW researchers for the Middle East research portfolio that works in partnership with the Critical Threats Project (CTP) at the American Enterprise Institute. In addition, interns collaborate with the wider research team to generate the Middle East portfolio’s intelligence products, such as the daily Iran Update; assist with editing, documenting, and compiling materials for publications; and support the planning, preparation, and execution of public events and private briefings held by ISW. This is a full-time internship (five days per week), but part-time work will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Qualifications Candidates must be motivated and organized college students or recent graduates with demonstrated expertise in a related field. Candidates must possess excellent writing, editing, and oral communication skills. Candidates should preferably possess strong critical language capabilities in Arabic, Hebrew, Turkish, Kurdish, or Farsi; or a programming language such as Python. Candidates must display the ability to conduct complex tasks in a timely and efficient manner. Candidates should be self-motivated, independent, creative, and capable of working in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Candidates must show commitment to—and interest in—the core mission and values of ISW. Spring 2027 Internship Program Dates: ISW internships starts on January 12, 2027. The program will run until May 14. Interns must both be authorized to work in the United States and be physically present in the United States during their internship tenure. Working remotely outside of the United States is not authorized. If you attend a US university on a student visa, you must be eligible for and obtain a CPT authorization before beginning at ISW. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Instructions: Please upload your resume, cover letter, and writing sample. Your cover letter and writing sample should be no longer than five pages combined; the writing sample can be excerpted from a longer paper. ISW will work with students to gain academic credit for internships where applicable. ISW Scholarship Application The Institute for the Study of War will offer intern candidates up to a $1,000 monthly living stipend as part of a scholarship program.* To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Candidates will be assessed based on the following criteria: Ability to contribute as a member of one of ISW’s research, operations, business development, or external relations teams; and Financial need, such that an unpaid internship would not be possible without assistance. Within the scholarship application, candidates should upload a 2- to 3-page cover letter which answers each of the following questions. (This should be a different cover letter than the one used for the internship application itself.) Which ISW internship is your top choice? Why do you believe you are qualified? What do you believe to be the most pressing national security problem the US faces today? What solution(s) would you propose? Where do you see yourself in your future career? How will an ISW internship help you get there? Why have you chosen to apply for this supplemental scholarship? Are you currently receiving federal financial aid and/or need-based aid from your university? Feel free to describe using as much detail as you are comfortable. *Please note that the up to $1,000 monthly scholarship is classified as taxable income. Questions? Email for more information.

The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. ### **About the Role** As a Technical Support Engineering Intern, you won't be grabbing coffee or shadowing others. Our interns are at the forefront of our team, tackling real-world challenges alongside our full-time engineers. Based at our San Mateo HQ, you'll work with cutting-edge, cloud-managed IoT technology, helping our enterprise clients with everything from troubleshooting to system design. You will assist in producing quantitative signals, impact models, and analyze Talos unique trading datasets to support improvements of the trading products and beyond. You will work alongside experienced team members, including product owners, quantitative analysts, and managers who will provide guidance and mentorship. This role offers excellent exposure to quantitative trading technology and will provide hands-on experience with financial markets data analysis. description: # About Us Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our AI, Data, and Analytics teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process. - Data Engineering Intern - AI & Analytics - Data Engineering Intern - AI/ML - Data Engineering Intern - Analytics - Software Engineering Intern - AI & Machine Learning - Software Engineering Intern - AI Platform - Software Engineering Intern - DevOps - Software Engineering Intern - Execution Apps - Software Engineering Intern - Fleet Applications - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle and Fleet Apps - Systems Analytics Engineering Intern - Connectivity and Telematics ## Role Summary Software-defined vehicles generate enormous amounts of data, from vehicle telemetry to manufacturing and fleet operations. As a Data Engineering intern, you will help turn that data into usable, reliable infrastructure and analytics, working on data pipelines, machine learning platforms, or the software and analytics supporting fleet and manufacturing applications. Specific project areas vary by team and may include: - Developing SQL and Python based data transformation and pipeline code - Building and maintaining ELT pipelines and analytics workflows on Databricks or similar platforms - Supporting machine learning model development, evaluation, or deployment infrastructure - Contributing to software for fleet management or manufacturing execution applications that depend on reliable data - Building automated data quality tests and integrating with CI/CD workflows ## Responsibilities - Design, build, or maintain data pipelines, analytics workflows, or ML supporting infrastructure - Write Python and SQL code to process, transform, and validate data - Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, or software engineers to meet data or platform needs - Contribute to automated testing for data quality and pipeline reliability - Document your work and share progress with your team throughout the internship ## Qualifications Minimum: - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university - Proficient in Python and SQL Preferred: - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Data Science, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship - Coursework or project experience with data engineering, analytics, or machine learning - Familiarity with cloud data platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, or Google BigQuery - Exposure to data transformation tools such as dbt, or infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform - Interest in applying data skills to vehicle, fleet, or manufacturing use cases ## **Total Rewards** We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements. In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. role: Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Controls (January - August 2027)
description: # About Us Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world. The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. Candidates should be available for a full-time commitment from January 11, 2027 to August 13, 2027. This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Vehicle Controls teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process. - Engineering Intern - Electrical Systems - Software Engineering Intern - Charging - Software Engineering Intern - Controls Test and Automation - Software Engineering Intern - Embedded Software - Software Engineering Intern - Embedded Software Programming - Software Engineering Intern - Energy Storage and Distribution - Software Engineering Intern - Functional Safety - Software Engineering Intern - High Voltage Charging - Software Engineering Intern - Mechanisms - Software Engineering Intern - Systems Architecture - Software Engineering Intern - Systems Engineering, Propulsion - Software Engineering Intern - Test Automation - Software Engineering Intern - Test Automation and Lighting - Software Engineering Intern - Thermal Controls - Software Engineering Intern - Unit Testing and Automation - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Dynamics Controls - Systems Engineering Intern - Homologation ## Role Summary When software-defined vehicles accelerate, manage battery temperature during fast charge, activate body controls, respond to steering input, or detect a system fault, the embedded software making that possible was built by a vehicle controls team. As a Vehicle Controls intern, you will work on embedded software or controls algorithms for one of several vehicle domains, including propulsion and dynamics, energy storage and charging, thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, functional safety, or systems engineering and test automation supporting these domains. Specific project areas vary by team and may include: - Implementing and validating embedded software for battery management, charging, or energy distribution systems - Developing controls software for thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, or lighting - Contributing to vehicle dynamics or propulsion controls algorithms - Supporting functional safety analysis and requirements for safety critical vehicle software - Building and running automated tests in Unit, Software in the Loop, or Hardware in the Loop environments - Working on systems engineering tasks such as requirements definition, architecture, or homologation ## Responsibilities - Design, implement, and test embedded software or controls algorithms for an assigned vehicle domain - Write production quality code in C or C++, with Python used for test tooling - Collaborate with systems engineers and test engineers to validate features before deployment - Support test execution in SIL, HIL, or bench environments and help debug issues that arise - Communicate progress and technical tradeoffs to your team throughout the internship ## Qualifications Minimum: - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university - Proficiency in C or C++, with some exposure to Python Preferred: - Actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship - Coursework or project experience with embedded systems, control theory, or real time operating systems - Familiarity with automotive communication protocols such as CAN, LIN, or Automotive Ethernet - Exposure to MATLAB and Simulink for controls modeling - Interest or coursework in functional safety concepts such as ISO 26262 ## **Total Rewards** We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements. In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. [**Learn more about our global benefit programs**](https://rvtech.mybenefits.life/)**.** External candidates can apply for this role through the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies careers site ([**](https://rivianvw.tech/#careers)). Field Engineers play a key role in ensuring that work meets the required quality standards by conducting inspections and implementing quality control measures. - **Participation in Project Meetings:** Regular participation in both daily and weekly project meetings is necessary to stay updated on project progress, discuss issues, and coordinate activities with other team members. - **Document Management:** Ensuring that Field Superintendents and Foremen have access to up-to-date contract documents, drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, and shop drawings is crucial for keeping the project on track. - **Issue Reporting:** Field Engineers promptly report any field issues to the Project Engineer and Field Superintendent. This allows for swift problem resolution and minimizes delays. - **Quantity Tracking:** Field Engineers are responsible for tracking and reporting the quantities of installed materials and equipment on a weekly basis. This is essential for project cost control and progress assessment. - **Equipment and Material Management:** Managing the storage and maintenance of equipment and materials on-site is necessary to ensure that resources are readily available and in good condition. - **Record Drawings and As-Builts:** Maintaining accurate record drawings and as-builts as per contract requirements is important for future reference and documentation. - **Permit Document Maintenance:** Field Engineers may be responsible for managing permit documents, such as those related to dust control and stormwater pollution prevention (SWPPP). - **Project Progress Photos:** Gathering weekly project progress photos can help document the project's development and provide visual updates to project stakeholders. - **Training and Mentoring:** Field Engineers often play a role in, sharing their knowledge and expertise to help develop the next generation of professionals. - **Stakeholder Relations:** Building rapport with owners, clients, engineers, and trade partners is important. Field Engineers must also ensure that the project complies with all contractual obligations and requirements. **Qualifications** - Applicant must be currently enrolled in a four-year Construction Management or Engineering program. - Ability to assume responsibility, interface and effectively communicate with others - Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) - Positive and teachable attitude **Safety Level** This is a safety sensitive position, and all applicable policies including drug test and background check will apply. - The inherent responsibilities of your role may include physical working conditions. In order to safely and successfully perform job duties you must be able to: - Potentially lift up to 50 pounds - Potentially need to do repeated pushing, pulling, carrying, reaching (or working above shoulder), walking, standing, sitting, stooping, kneeling, bending, and climbing - Potentially operate a motor vehicle, crane, tractor, etc. - We reserve the right to continually monitor your ability to safely and successfully complete these inherent physical responsibilities and take action as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Americans with Disability Act (ADA) This internship will provide you with exposure to the construction and project management industry, allowing you to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world situations. You will gain hands-on experience, work with experienced professionals, and contribute to the success of our projects. We look forward to your active participation and contributions to our team during this internship program. description: AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Arlington on November 18-19, 2026. This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027. The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer from 6-8 pm, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines. On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Arlington office. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities. AECOM is seeking an Electrical Engineering Intern to be based in Arlington, VA . This position is expected to begin in Spring/Summer 2027. Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. Interns work with cutting-edge technology, learn industry best practices, and collaborate with experienced professionals in a globally recognized firm. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. Additionally, AECOM’s dedication to innovation and sustainability enables interns to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape communities and the built environment. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to: Build analytic and design skills. Conduct engineering design under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Create designs, calculations, sketches, diagrams, schematic drawings, and final working drawings under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Collect and analyzes data under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Uses computer software as a tool for solving basic engineering problems. Perform work in accordance with agreed upon budget and schedule under supervision. Design and document normal, standby and emergency power distribution systems. Design and document normal and emergency lighting systems for interior and exterior applications. Perform calculations to support designs. Work through all project design phases including construction administration. Work on varying project types and sizes including laboratories, educational facilities, office spaces, mission critical facilities, and cultural facilities. Work in a team environment. Minimum Requirements: Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or related field and must have completed at least two of years of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s degree and plan to continue with the Master’s degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Recent graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship. Due to the nature of the work, U.S. Citizenship is required. Preferred Qualifications: Use AutoCAD and/or Revit for creating construction documents, sketches, etc. Knowledge of SKM and/or ETAP to perform electrical studies. Knowledge of AGi32 software to perform lighting calculations. Experience of design work for new construction and renovation projects. Prior internship experience utilizing drafting, surveying, and/or construction administration skills. Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. This position requires a hybrid work schedule which includes office work in Arlington, VA. The selected candidate must be available to work in Arlington, VA. description: ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more. ## Turn what you've learned into real leadership experience. Maybe you studied supply chain, logistics, operations, business, or engineering. Maybe you got your first exposure to the field through an internship, co-op, part-time job, or project and realized you want to build a career in operations. Now you're ready to do more than observe the operation. You're ready to **lead one**. ShipMonk is looking for early-career talent to join our Fort Worth fulfillment operation as an **Operations Supervisor**. This isn't a program where you spend your first year watching from the sidelines. You'll learn our business while taking on real frontline leadership responsibility — leading approximately 25–30 associates, managing performance, working with operational data, solving problems, and helping your department improve. ## Why start your operations career at ShipMonk? You can learn the fundamentals of supply chain in a classroom or internship. Leading an operation teaches you what happens when the forecast changes, volume spikes, labor doesn't match the plan, a process breaks, or your team needs you to make a decision. At ShipMonk, you'll build hands-on experience in: - Frontline people leadership - Fulfillment and distribution operations - Labor planning and allocation - Productivity and throughput management - Inventory and quality - Safety and compliance - Operational KPIs and data analysis - Root-cause problem solving - Continuous improvement - Cross-functional leadership And you'll do it in an environment where we believe in developing our people and **promoting from within whenever we can**. Strong performers have opportunities to take on more responsibility and continue building their careers as ShipMonk grows. ## What you'll do - Lead, coach, and develop approximately 25–30 warehouse associates - Run shift huddles and set clear daily priorities for your team - Monitor productivity, throughput, quality, accuracy, attendance, and safety - Learn how to allocate labor based on volume and operational priorities - Use data to understand performance and identify root causes - Coach associates and provide clear, timely feedback - Partner with Operations leaders and teams across HR, Safety, Quality, and Engineering - Help onboard and train new associates - Identify opportunities to eliminate waste and improve processes - Maintain a safe, organized, and compliant work area - Learn the operation from the floor up while progressively taking greater ownership ## What we're looking for We're especially interested in early-career candidates who have: - An interest in building a career in **operations, supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, or people leadership** - Exposure to a professional or operational environment through an **internship, co-op, part-time job, project, or other relevant experience** - Demonstrated leadership potential through work experience, campus organizations, athletics, volunteer leadership, military experience, or other team environments - Comfort working with data and metrics to understand performance and solve problems - Strong communication and interpersonal skills - A willingness to spend the majority of the shift on the fulfillment floor working directly with your team - Flexibility to work days, nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs - Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs. **Nice to have** - A degree, current enrollment, or coursework in **Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, Engineering, or a related field** - Internship or co-op experience in supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, distribution, manufacturing, transportation, or operations - Coursework or project experience involving operations management, supply chain analytics, Lean, Six Sigma, process improvement, or data analysis - Previous experience leading a team, project, student organization, athletic team, or other group **A college degree and prior full-time warehouse supervisory experience are not required.** We're looking for leadership potential, relevant exposure, and someone who wants to build a career in operations. ## What success looks like **In your first 30 days:** You're learning the operation, getting to know your team, understanding the KPIs that drive your department, and spending significant time learning directly on the floor. **In 90 days:** You're increasingly accountable for your team's performance, using data to identify problems, coaching associates, and beginning to identify opportunities to improve your operation. **In year one:** You understand how people, labor, inventory, technology, and process come together to run a high-volume fulfillment operation. You've built real frontline leadership experience and demonstrated your ability to continue taking on more at ShipMonk. ## Work Location This is an on-site role based at ShipMonk's Fort Worth fulfillment center: **ShipMonk TX1** 2601 NE 33rd St. Fort Worth, TX 76111 **About ShipMonk** ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL; we're a **growth partner for merchants**. We provide cutting-edge technology and a network of owned and operated fulfillment centers that empower high-growth ecommerce and DTC brands to stress less and grow more. With over 2,500 employees across five countries, we're on a mission to revolutionize fulfillment by providing everything from the fastest click-to-delivery and real-time inventory to custom solutions—all with a **merchant**-**first** mindset. **Why ShipMonk?** We believe in building for the long term, and our success is powered by five key differentiators that help us become true partners to our merchants. - **Global Fulfillment Network:** Our 12+ owned and operated fulfillment centers span the US, Canada, the U.K., and Mainland Europe. We never outsource, ensuring quality and consistency. ● **Proprietary Technology:** We've eliminated the need for tribal knowledge with our AI-powered platform. It provides a real-time, unified view of inventory and orders, giving our merchants the control and visibility they need to succeed. ● **Unrivaled Support:** We provide hands-on, "mom and pop" support with a global reach. Our dedicated teams are on-site at every fulfillment center, ready to jump into action. ● **Transparent Pricing**: We believe in honest, long-term partnerships. Our all- inclusive pricing means predictable costs, with no hidden fees or surprises. ● **Committed to the Future:** We invest over $10 million annually in research and development to ensure our technology and services continually evolve, helping merchants plant roots with a partner who is here to stay. **Our Core Values** Our values are the heart of our culture. We're looking for individuals who embody these principles every day. - **Merchant-first:** We handle the logistics so our merchants can focus on what they do best—growing their business. - **People make ShipMonk:** We believe in our team and invest in our people. - **Own it:** We take ownership of our work, our mistakes, and our successes. - **Get sh\*t done:** We're a fast-paced, high-growth company that values action and results. - **Change the score:**We challenge the status quo, constantly innovating and improving. ShipMonk is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We are a global community of different cultures, voices, and experiences. We celebrate what makes us unique and connect through what we share, in an authentic and safe environment. Together we shape the future, and each other. role: Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern - Spring/Summer/Fall 2027
description: Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. ### **About the Role:** As a Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern at Hermeus, you will support the planning, development, and execution of flight operations and airworthiness activities for the Quarterhorse aircraft. This role is ideal for an engineering student with practical aviation experience who is interested in the cross functional intersection of flight operations, flight test, safety, and airworthiness. You will contribute to professional technical deliverables supporting military and civil airworthiness packages, assist with risk assessments and data analysis, and support strategic planning that will advance longer-term program objectives. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who can take ownership of complex, ambiguous problems; develop a path forward; and communicate clearly across internal and external teams. This internship offers direct exposure to the unique challenges of operating and certifying high-performance experimental aircraft in a fast-paced development environment. Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April) Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August) Fall: Around 16 weeks (September - December) ### Responsibilities: - Support the development of airworthiness, flight operations, and safety documentation for experimental aircraft operations. - Assist in preparing professional technical deliverables for military and civil airworthiness packages. - Support operational-risk analysis, including hazard identification, risk tracking, and management of operational constraints and mitigations. - Apply engineering fundamentals and statistical methods to assess operational data, characterize risk, and support envelope an operational expansion. - Collaborate with engineering, flight test, operations, and program teams to collect technical inputs and ensure airworthiness artifacts are accurate, complete, and traceable. - Independently identify and effectively communicate gaps, inefficiencies, and upcoming needs in flight operations and airworthiness processes. - Support longer-range planning by identifying work that advances programmatic milestones and airworthiness objectives well ahead of formal tasking. ### Requirements: - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related STEM discipline. Undergraduate candidates should be in their junior or senior year of study; graduate students are also encouraged to apply. - Demonstrated interest in aviation, flight test, flight operations, or airworthiness. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop clear, professional technical documentation. - Strong mathematical and analytical skills, including the ability to organize, interpret, and draw conclusions from engineering or test data. - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment with shifting priorities. - Demonstrated initiative and comfort working through ambiguous technical or operational problems without a fully defined path. - Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to safe operations. - GPA of 3.0 or above. ### Preferred Skills and Experience: - Manned or unmanned aircraft pilot experience or comparable flight experience. - Experience with experimental aircraft, flight test, aircraft maintenance, aviation safety, or airworthiness activities. - Experience designing, building, testing, or operating vehicles through internships, academic work, student teams, military service, or personal projects. - Familiarity with risk-management methods, safety assessments, reliability analysis, statistical analysis, or data-analysis tools. - Exposure to civil or military aviation regulations, certification processes, flight authorizations, or airworthiness documentation. - Experience developing technical reports, engineering analyses, test procedures, or operational documentation. - A strong desire to learn, seek feedback, and take on progressively greater responsibility.

This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities. AECOM is seeking an Entry-Level Civil Engineer to be based in Piscataway, NJ. This position is expected to begin in Spring/Summer 2027. We take on the most complex challenges and pioneer innovative, iconic solutions that push the limits of what’s possible – the world’s longest cable-stayed bridge, record-breaking sports events, the largest greenfield port development megaproject, life-sustaining and disaster recovery programs, and the tallest tower in the Western Hemisphere. AECOM’s Transportation business line partners with clients around the world to build, modernize and expand transportation projects that carry all of our communities into the future — safely and reliably. We use our extensive knowledge in planning, designing, and managing transportation systems — as well as restoring and replacing aging infrastructure — to help our public and private clients find smarter, more advanced ways to move people across cities, countries and continents. Our integrated approach and social responsibility have earned us the trust of local municipalities, government agencies, commercial clients and public-private partnerships. Our expertise and global reach enable us to deliver high-quality solutions for our clients that pave the way for long-lasting benefits to society. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to: Builds analytic and design skills. Conducts engineering design under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Collects and analyzes data under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Uses computer software as a tool for solving basic engineering problems. Performs work in accordance with agreed-upon budget and schedule under supervision. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or in another related field or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education. Citrus Health Group is a new type of agency that brings an empathetic patient focus to the new product commercialization process. Citrus creates hand-picked teams that provide clients with scientific, clinical, pharmacologic, evidence-generation, pricing and reimbursement, market access, affordability, and patient support expertise and experience in their time of need. Client teams are built with talented experts who function as a fluid, agile, and highly energized team. We are passionate about science; our focus is to effectively communicate science in compelling and engaging ways to drive true value and enable patients to gain access to new medicines. We do so with the highest level of integrity and respect for the ethical nature of our business. We invite you to join our talented team of dedicated professionals, working closely together to provide the services our clients need, at the time they need them. We are driven by one word, RESPECT. We respect each other, we respect our clients, and we respect the professionals we work with on behalf of our clients. We value every team member and strive for an inclusive and collaborative culture that fosters the best in everyone. **About the Opportunity** The Medical Communications Postdoctoral Fellowship is a one-year program where participants will develop an understanding of the medical communications industry, and the types of services provided by an agency to its pharmaceutical and biotech client teams. During this program, fellows will have the ability to gain core competency experience by developing various types of scientific communications while working cross-functionally with internal partners [Account, Creative, and Medical Strategy] along with external client stakeholders. As such, this is an ideal opportunity for individuals with minimal or no prior medical communications experience. By the end of the program, fellows will have a clear understanding of the key competencies and responsibilities of the Medical Writing role, and well as the Scientific Director role. Additionally, fellows will gain familiarity with industry guidelines and will learn Good Publication Practices, and have the ability to apply those to key learnings while developing highly visible projects. **Ideal Candidate** The ideal candidate for this fellowship program has: - **Advanced Degree (PharmD\*, MD, PhD or DVM).** \*Pharmacist licensure is not required. - Physically located in Eastern or Central time zones (preferable) and is able to work our standard operating hours 9am - 5pm (approximately), Monday thru Friday. - Ongoing eligibility to work for any employer in the US; Citrus is unable to provide work sponsorships at this time. Residents of Canada are able to apply. - Proficiency in Microsoft Suite. - Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team. - Effective attention to detail and accuracy and ability to confirm writing to prescribed style format. - High level of integrity, confidentiality and accountability. - Ability to think analytically and to effectively plan, prioritize, and execute. - Expert verbal and written communication skills. **Benefits** Fellows receive a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability insurance, 401k matching and technology stipends. **Application Procedures** We are accepting applicants for our Spring 2027 cohort. Applicants must include an up-to-date Curriculum Vitae and Letter of Intent. Applicants may also include any letters of recommendation and/or writing samples; however this is not required. The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) protects public health and the environment by supplying clean drinking water, collecting and treating wastewater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP delivers more than 1.1 billion gallons per day of the highest quality drinking water to 8.5 million NYC residents and more than 1 million people in Upstate New York, and has a wastewater conveyance and treatment system capable of processing over 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater per day to protect the environment and the city’s surrounding waterways. The primary responsibilities of the Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations (BWSO) are: the operation, maintenance and protection of the City’s drinking water and wastewater collection (sewer) systems; the protection of adjacent waterways; and the development and protection of the Department’s Capital Water and Sewer Design Program. The Bureau also approves and inspects water and sewer connections performed by licensed plumbers and/or authorized contractors. In addition, the Bureau has overall responsibility for the approval and inspection of all public and private construction projects which could impact on the City’s water or sewer systems. The Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations is seeking to hire an Environmental Engineer Intern within the Division of Capital Program Management (CPM) for Distribution & Drainage section. The selected candidate will provide engineering support for stormwater management, drainage infrastructure, sewer systems, environmental compliance, and related water quality and resiliency projects. Responsibilities will include assisting with engineering analyses, data collection and evaluation, preparation of technical reports, review of design documents, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders. The employee will support the evaluation of drainage and sewer system through field investigations, hydraulic/environmental data review and modeling, GIS mapping, and engineering calculations. The position will assist senior engineers with: - Collecting, organizing, and analyzing environmental, hydraulic, and infrastructure-related data. - Supporting stormwater management and drainage improvement projects. - Reviewing drainage plans, reports, calculations, and technical documentation. - Performing basic engineering analyses and calculations. - Preparing spreadsheets, maps, figures, presentations, and technical reports. - Using engineering software, databases, GIS applications, and agency data management tools. - Participating in field visits to observe infrastructure conditions, collect information, and support project assessments. - Coordinating with DEP units, consultants, contractors, and other agencies as needed. The position provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in environmental engineering, stormwater management, drainage systems, and infrastructure planning while working under the guidance of experienced engineers. **ALL APPLICANTS MUST HAVE TAKEN CIVIL SERVICE EXAM NO. 6118 FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEER INTERN, TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION. ** Appointments are subject to OMB approval. For additional information about DEP, visit Recruitment Contact: DEP is an equal opportunity employer with a strong commitment to the diversity of our organization and workforce. Your voluntary response to the NYCAPS on-line application section for referral information will assist us tremendously in our ability to track the success of our outreach and recruitment efforts. Please be sure to indicate your source of referral to this job. NOTE: This position is open to qualified persons with a disability who are eligible for the 55-a Program and also meet the education and experience requirements as listed in the job posting notice. Please indicate on your resume or cover letter that you would like to be considered for the position under the 55-a Program. This position is also open to non 55-a Program candidates who meet the education and experience requirements as listed in the job posting notice. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Real Estate & Development Team** The Real Estate & Development team identifies, secures, and entitles the sites that power Zipline’s network. We source markets, lead site selection and due diligence (zoning, utilities, environmental), negotiate LOIs/leases and land agreements, and drive entitlements and permitting with municipalities and partner real estate teams. We align stakeholders, manage budgets and schedules, and deliver permitted, ready-to-build locations—spanning test sites and regional hubs—before handing off to construction. By turning candidate properties into drone delivery sites at speed, we enable Zipline to scale into new regions and deliver life-changing logistics where they’re needed most. ### **The Role** As a Real Estate & Development Intern based in our San Francisco office, you will help expand the physical infrastructure that makes Zipline’s delivery system possible. You will support projects from early site identification through approvals and development, helping turn promising locations into operational sites that serve customers and communities. Along the way, you will tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of aviation, real estate, technology, and the built environment. You will work alongside and learn from experienced partners across Real Estate, Engineering, Operations, Government Affairs, and Communications. Your work will contribute directly to Zipline’s mission by helping bring fast, reliable delivery to more people in more places. ### **What You'll Do** - Support market screening and site selection by evaluating zoning, land-use requirements, setbacks, utilities, easements, environmental conditions, and airspace considerations. - Assess potential sites for feasibility and risk, identifying permitting hurdles, title issues, infrastructure constraints, and other factors that could affect development. - Partner with Engineering and Operations to translate technical requirements into practical site criteria, scopes of work, site plans, and permit-ready materials. - Learn how projects move through local approval processes by working with city planners, zoning officials, building departments, and external consultants. - Coordinate with landlords, brokers, and real estate partners to evaluate site readiness and support negotiations, including letters of intent, leases, and required exhibits. - Prepare comparative site analyses, deal memos, and recommendation summaries that help cross-functional teams make informed investment and development decisions. - Build project-management skills by maintaining timelines, budget estimates, and entitlement trackers, communicating progress to stakeholders, and preparing complete handoff packages for downstream teams. ### **What You'll Bring** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in real estate, urban planning, engineering, construction management, architecture, geography, environmental studies, business, public policy, or a related field. - Demonstrated interest in real estate development, site acquisition, infrastructure, permitting, or the built environment through coursework, projects, internships, or other relevant experience. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate information from multiple sources, identify potential risks, and form a clear recommendation. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the judgment to work professionally with cross-functional teammates, consultants, property owners, and public-agency stakeholders. - Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assignments, maintain accurate project information, and follow through on deadlines. - Comfort learning new tools and working with maps, spreadsheets, plans, schedules, and project documentation; prior experience with specialized real estate, design, or construction software is not required. ### **What Else You Should Know** *Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September.* *The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.* *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

## About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. ## About the Role: As an Engineering Intern at Vercel, you will be an important part of our engineering team, working on real projects that will impact our products and customers. You will be mentored by experienced engineers and will be given opportunities to grow and learn. ## ## What You Will Do: Work will vary by team - but your general scope will include, but not be limited to: - Own an end-to-end project: scope it with your manager, build it, ship it, and see it in customers' hands. - Write and review production code alongside the engineers who maintain it. - Debug real systems under real conditions - trace an issue through the stack and fix the root cause. - Communicate your progress clearly, including when you're blocked. ## ## About You: - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, graduating December 2027 or May 2028. - Strong knowledge and capability with JavaScript and/or TypeScript. Experience with Go or Rust is a bonus. - You dig into problems rather than around them - you want to know *why* something broke. - You move work forward on your own. You surface blockers early instead of waiting to be asked. - You communicate well in writing. Much of how we work is asynchronous and written down. - Fluent with AI tooling and clear-eyed about it. You use it to move faster, and you can still explain, defend, and debug everything you ship. - Based in San Francisco, willing and able to commute Mon/Tues/Fri. ## ## **Benefits & Compensation:** - Competitive compensation package, including equity. - Inclusive Healthcare Package. - Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills. - Flexible Time Off. - We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed. The San Francisco, CA base pay range for this role is $110,000 - $132,000. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location. Compensation outside of San Francisco may be adjusted based on employee location. The total compensation package may include benefits, equity-based compensation, and eligibility for a company bonus or variable pay program depending on the role. Your recruiter can share more details during the hiring process. ## **Disclosures:** - **Privacy:** Please review our [Job Applicant Privacy Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/job-applicant-privacy-notice) for more information on how we handle your data. - **Equal Opportunity:**Vercel is committed to fostering and empowering an inclusive community within our organization. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Vercel encourages everyone to apply for our available positions, even if they don't necessarily check every box on the job description.

About the role Go Fish is seeking a motivated, curious, and collaborative emerging designer to join our team through an immediate Design Apprenticeship. As a Design Apprentice, you will work alongside Art Directors, Designers, Strategists, and Copywriters to help create thoughtful, high-impact work for a diverse range of clients. You will gain hands-on experience across brand, digital, print, paid media, and social, while building the craft, confidence, and professional judgment to grow as a designer. This is a hands-on opportunity to learn within a collaborative agency environment. You will contribute to real client work, receive guidance from experienced creative leaders, and develop your skills through feedback, mentorship, and day-to-day practice. You will learn how strategic thinking, visual design, writing, and production come together to create cohesive brand experiences across channels. What you'll do Support Art Directors and Designers in concepting and producing strategic client deliverables across brand identity, UI/UX, print, paid media, and organic social. Create and adapt visual assets that are thoughtful, polished, on-brand, and appropriate for their intended channel. Collaborate with Strategy and Copywriting teams to bring visual and written storytelling together in clear, compelling brand narratives. Participate in creative brainstorms, research, concept development, and design reviews. Support the creative team with internal marketing materials and other strategic projects as needed. Organize files, prepare production-ready assets, and help maintain a high standard of accuracy and quality throughout the design process. Explore approved AI-assisted tools and emerging technologies to support research, ideation, concept exploration, moodboarding, and efficient production workflows. Skills and Experience You'll Bring and Develop Design Craft and Tools A portfolio that demonstrates strong visual thinking and a foundation in graphic design, visual communication, marketing, or related work. Working proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud, especially Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign. A foundational understanding of typography, color, layout, visual hierarchy, and core design principles. Interest in working across a range of formats, including brand identity, digital design, social media, print, and campaign creative. Familiarity with AI-assisted creative workflows, such as using ChatGPT or Claude for research and ideation, and appropriate tools for visual exploration and moodboarding. An ability to evaluate AI-generated outputs critically and use these tools responsibly, with respect for client confidentiality, intellectual property, accessibility, and brand standards. Collaboration and Growth Currently pursuing, recently completed, or able to demonstrate equivalent experience in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Marketing, Communications, or a related field. Curiosity, initiative, and a genuine desire to develop your design craft. A collaborative, thoughtful approach to feedback and a willingness to ask questions. Strong organizational skills and close attention to detail. The ability to manage multiple tasks, communicate progress clearly, and seek support when needed. description: We’re looking for Software Engineering Interns to help build and scale the systems that power Datadog’s observability and security platform. Interns contribute directly to real-world engineering challenges across backend, frontend, infrastructure, data engineering, and developer tooling while working alongside experienced engineers and mentors. You’ll help design, build, and improve systems that process and analyze massive volumes of metrics, logs, and application data in real time. Whether you’re interested in distributed systems, Kubernetes, AI-powered products like Bits AI, or developer platform tooling, you’ll work on meaningful projects that deliver impact to customers at global scale. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. **What You’ll Do:** - Contribute to production systems that process and analyze large-scale observability and application data in real time - Build and improve distributed systems across backend infrastructure, developer platforms, and cloud-native services - Help identify and solve performance, reliability, and scalability challenges in critical services supporting Datadog’s growing customer base - Own and deliver technical projects from design through deployment with support from experienced engineers and mentors - Develop technical expertise through hands-on experience with technologies such as Kubernetes, distributed systems, and cloud-native infrastructure - Collaborate with fellow interns, mentors, and engineers while building software that delivers impact at global scale **Who You Are:** - Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or have equivalent practical experience - Targeting a **2028** full-time start date - Demonstrate strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and software design - Comfortable coding in one or more programming languages and excited to use AI-assisted tools to enhance software development and problem solving - Have experience using AI coding tools or a strong interest in learning how to use them effectively, while exploring how AI can improve engineering practices and products - Available to work full-time from the Datadog New York or Boston office during the internship program dates: - May 24 - Aug 20, 2027 - May 24 - Aug 27, 2027 - June 7 - Sep 3, 2027 Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply. **Benefits and Growth:** - Work on meaningful technical challenges alongside engineers across the globe - Participate in mentorship and buddy programs designed to support learning and development - Join an in-person intern cohort and expand your network through engineering talks, social events, and community engagement opportunities throughout your internship - Receive relocation support and travel benefits where applicable - Enjoy office perks including snacks, drinks, and catered lunches on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday *Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.* *This job is available in various departments within our company; to conform to US export control regulations, some of these roles may require candidates to be eligible for any required authorizations from the US government.* **If possible, please apply using your personal email address instead of your university email address.** Students can sign up for a [free Datadog Pro account](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/datadog-github-student-developer-pack/) to learn more about our platform and products. #LI-Hybrid Datadog offers a competitive salary for this role and may include additional compensation elements. description: Overview Join the Loretto family and begin training to start your career path today as a Certified Home Health Aide in our Syracuse, Jamesville or Community positions! Considering a rewarding career in healthcare? No Experience Required! NEW Higher Wages! We will provide free classroom training! Upon completion of training and state certification, your pay rate will increase to the s tarting rate of $21.52/hr Our training classes run monthly and require a full time commitment to complete a 4 week training class, including classroom and clinical hours from 7:00am - 4:30pm. Part Time and Full Time positions are available once you have graduated and received your certification. Placement into the positions are determined prior to being acceptance into the training program Our Certified Home Health Aides work at one of our Assisted Living Facilities or PACE CNY Home Care program in the Syracuse area. Some Home Health Aide positions require working in the community, visiting participants in their home, while others are located at 1 building, therefore, your own vehicle is not always required. Our Syracuse locations are located on a bus route, however, the following locations are not easily accessible by the bus route, include North Syracuse, Jamesville and Baldwinsville. Responsibilities WHAT CAN LORETTO OFFER ME? A dedicated, caring and passionate Loretto family, ready to support you and provide opportunity! A fun environment, including recognition events and opportunities to learn and advance your career within the healthcare industry. Healthcare benefits for qualifying full time and part time employees upon hire! Upon successful completion of the program, a stipend for uniforms will be given yearly WHAT DOES A HOME HEALTH AIDE DO? As a Certified Home Health Aide (HHA) , supporting the mission of Loretto, will include the following responsibilities: Provide health care tasks to serve Loretto residents, including, personal hygiene services, housekeeping tasks, and other related support services essential to the residents’ health Work with Loretto’s clinical team to record and report changes regarding the resident’s physical condition, behavior, or appearance Perform light housekeeping duties including cooking, dusting, vacuuming, mopping, & sweeping Assist with bathing, dressing and grooming Assist with transfer and ambulation including the use of a cane, walker, and wheelchair Qualifications Must have a high school diploma or GED that can be verified. Must be 18 years of age. Must have reliable transportation to get to and from training classes and then your work location after completion of the program. Ability to pass medication competency tests including a written exam and Medication Administration Test/Cart Quiz. Possess the emotional and mental maturity and stability to care for the frail elderly and other disabled or compromised clients in their “home” environment; ability to deal tactfully with clients, families, other support persons and members of the health care team. Able to follow guidelines established by Loretto’s Customer Service as presented at Loretto Orientation. Ability to plan, prioritize, organize work tasks and carry out ongoing care plan. Ability to be flexible in regards to clients care needs INDBSJ Benefits/Compensation Pay Range $16.00 - $16.00 / hour Excellent medical, dental, prescription and vision insurance Disability coverage Tuition Reimbursement Program 401(k) Retirement/Pension Plans Discounted Gym Membership Paid Time-Off Accrual Fun events for employees Convenient locations with free parking Employee Coaches - to help you achieve life goals Diaper Assistance Program Opportunity for career growth and movement within 19 sites

role: (CHHA) Certified Home Health Aide Trainee - Community Openings
description: Overview Join the Loretto family and begin training to start your career path today as a Certified Home Health Aide in our Syracuse, Jamesville or Community positions! Considering a rewarding career in healthcare? No Experience Required! NEW Higher Wages! We will provide free classroom training! Upon completion of training and state certification, your pay rate will increase to the s tarting rate of $21.52/hr Our training classes run monthly and require a full time commitment to complete a 4 week training class, including classroom and clinical hours from 7:00am - 4:30pm. Part Time and Full Time positions are available once you have graduated and received your certification. Placement into the positions are determined prior to being acceptance into the training program Our Certified Home Health Aides work at one of our Assisted Living Facilities or PACE CNY Home Care program in the Syracuse area. Some Home Health Aide positions require working in the community, visiting participants in their home, while others are located at 1 building, therefore, your own vehicle is not always required. Our Syracuse locations are located on a bus route, however, the following locations are not easily accessible by the bus route, include North Syracuse, Jamesville and Baldwinsville. Responsibilities WHAT CAN LORETTO OFFER ME? A dedicated, caring and passionate Loretto family, ready to support you and provide opportunity! A fun environment, including recognition events and opportunities to learn and advance your career within the healthcare industry. Healthcare benefits for qualifying full time and part time employees upon hire! Upon successful completion of the program, a stipend for uniforms will be given yearly WHAT DOES A HOME HEALTH AIDE DO? As a Certified Home Health Aide (HHA) , supporting the mission of Loretto, will include the following responsibilities: Provide health care tasks to serve Loretto residents, including, personal hygiene services, housekeeping tasks, and other related support services essential to the residents’ health Work with Loretto’s clinical team to record and report changes regarding the resident’s physical condition, behavior, or appearance Perform light housekeeping duties including cooking, dusting, vacuuming, mopping, & sweeping Assist with bathing, dressing and grooming Assist with transfer and ambulation including the use of a cane, walker, and wheelchair Qualifications Must have a high school diploma or GED that can be verified. Must be 18 years of age. Must have reliable transportation to get to and from training classes and then your work location after completion of the program. Ability to pass medication competency tests including a written exam and Medication Administration Test/Cart Quiz. Possess the emotional and mental maturity and stability to care for the frail elderly and other disabled or compromised clients in their “home” environment; ability to deal tactfully with clients, families, other support persons and members of the health care team. Able to follow guidelines established by Loretto’s Customer Service as presented at Loretto Orientation. Ability to plan, prioritize, organize work tasks and carry out ongoing care plan. Ability to be flexible in regards to clients care needs INDBSJ Benefits/Compensation Pay Range $16.00 - $16.00 / hour Excellent medical, dental, prescription and vision insurance Disability coverage Tuition Reimbursement Program 401(k) Retirement/Pension Plans Discounted Gym Membership Paid Time-Off Accrual Fun events for employees Convenient locations with free parking Employee Coaches - to help you achieve life goals Diaper Assistance Program Opportunity for career growth and movement within 19 sites
