Student Support Services-TRIO (SSS), a federally funded U.S. Department of Education TRIO Program, is seeking a dynamic, self-motivated individual to step into the role of Student Success Splst and join our team. SSS provides comprehensive and sensitive support to college participants, focusing on educational, social, and cultural experiences to enhance graduation rates for low-income, first-generation, and students with disabilities. On occasion, weekend and evening hours will be required. Our mission: The mission of Student Support Services-TRIO is to increase the college retention and graduation rates of program partici­pants at the University of New Mexico Main Campus. The SSS program draws upon a holistic framework where committed participants receive individualized support by ad­dressing their educational and personal needs. The ideal candidate is passionate about helping students navigate through the university systems and is a proactive problem-solver, adept at working collaboratively in a fast-paced office environment. They embody a student-centered, holistic approach and are deeply committed to student success. They will be responsible for providing ongoing academic advising and provide support to participants’ individual needs and career exploration. They will assist in the development and delivery of outreach efforts for program promotion and assist in attracting and retaining qualified applicants to the SSS program. Duties and Responsibilities: Works directly with SSS program students one-on-one or in a group setting providing holistic-proactive advisement, financial aid/scholarship advisement, advocacy and program services. Assists with outreach and retention activities designed to attract, retain, and serve SSS students. Supports activity logistics, communications and outreach that promotes an inclusive climate for the SSS population; foster a supportive climate and students’ sense of belonging. Assists in the preparation, logistics, and delivery of workshops (academic success, time management, study skills, financial literacy, FAFSA applications, career development, etc.), presentations, and orientations promoting student success. Receives guidance, training, and mentoring from professional personnel in planning and carrying out activities and assignments; engages in directed professional development. Maintains and documents records; assists with data collection to generate reports. Performs miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned to fulfill the SSS grant objectives and goals. This position is multifaceted and impacts many key performance initiatives the university promotes to ensure that students are successful at UNM. As a result, the ability and willingness to collaborate with other departments, academic units, internal/external donors, and other university stakeholders is essential.

### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. #### **About the Marketing Team** The Marketing team helps people discover, try, and continue using Zipline. We work across lifecycle, merchandising, and growth to create campaigns and customer experiences that support awareness, conversion, retention, and repeat usage. Our team partners closely with Product, Creative, Commercial, Analytics, Engineering, and Operations to bring campaigns and experiments to life. This is a fast-moving, cross-functional team where creativity, customer empathy, and analytical thinking come together to support Zipline’s growth. #### **The Role** Zipline is looking for a Marketing Operations & Project Management Intern to help our marketing and creative teams bring ideas to life. You’ll help organize incoming requests, track project timelines, and make it easier for teams to see what needs to happen next. You’ll work alongside experienced marketers and creative partners on campaigns, launches, and brand projects. This is a hands-on opportunity to learn how work moves from an initial request to a finished customer experience, while helping the team stay organized along the way. **What You'll Do** - Help maintain project plans and trackers so owners, deadlines, and next steps are clear. - Gather information for new marketing requests and help ensure each project has a clear goal, list of deliverables, and timeline. - Follow up with team members on project updates and flag missing information or possible delays early. - Prepare meeting agendas and follow through with owners to keep decisions and action items moving. - Help coordinate meetings, kick offs, reviews and approvals for creative work across marketing teams. - Organize project files, templates, and process guides so information is easy to find. - Support campaign and production logistics, such as tracking deliverables, vendor details, and launch checklists, with guidance from the team. - Look for simple ways to make recurring work easier and help document improvements. #### **What You'll Bring** - Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree, ideally with an interest in marketing, communications, business, consumer products, or a related field. Candidates must have completed at least the second year of their undergraduate studies. - Interest in marketing, creative work, operations, or project management. - Strong organization skills and attention to detail. - Clear, thoughtful communication and comfort following up with people across teams. - Ability to manage several assignments, ask questions, and raise concerns when priorities or deadlines are unclear. - A willingness to learn new tools and improve how work gets done. - Experience with a project management tool is helpful, but not required. We care more about your curiosity, follow-through, and ability to bring clarity to a busy team. #### What Success Looks Like - Team members can quickly see the status, owner, and next step for the projects you support. - Meetings have clear agendas, and decisions lead to completed actions. - Missing details and potential delays are surfaced early. - Project information is accurate, organized, and easy to find. - You leave the internship with practical experience helping marketing and creative projects move from planning to launch. #### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns (May/June - August/September).* *Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.* The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. What you'll do A Protect Life Michigan (PLM) Campus Activist (CA) carries out the mission of PLM by working directly with campus groups and pro-life students. The Campus Activist's purpose is to develop pro-life students into leaders in the pro-life movement and to change pro-choice minds on abortion by leading outreach efforts on college campuses. The Campus Activist will work with their fellow Campus Activists and their student-run boards at their assigned college, and execute any strategic adjustments made by managers and select team members. Campus Activists report to a Campus Activist Supervisor or a Campus Activist Lead. This position can be filled by a part-time or full-time candidate. If the CA is currently attending college, they typically work 11-15 hours per week. This role is primarily in-person at the assigned college, with some work-from-home days, and requires the candidate to support raise their salary and ministry expenses; please read more details in the Salary & Benefits section below. For your first semester on campus, you may be paired with an experienced Campus Activist to receive on-the-job training. Please note that your training location may be further away from the campus with which you are working. Duties & Responsibilities: Recruit: The Campus Activist will encourage pro-life students to join the campus group. Examples of this include: Plan and lead recruitment events like tabling, clipboarding, and socials Build trusting relationships with students Create a strong culture of pro-life community Equip: The Campus Activist will seek to equip pro-life students to better communicate the pro-life message in a loving and persuasive way. Examples of this include: Plan and facilitate weekly club meetings, utilizing materials provided by PLM Foster student identities as social reformers Answer apologetics questions from students Deploy: The Campus Activist will motivate pro-life students to participate in outreach events and to take their next step as an activist. Examples of this include: Plan and lead various outreach events on campus, including both immensely effective “high barrier” outreaches (conversational, utilizes abortion victim photography, etc.) and “low barrier” outreaches (chalking, stickering, etc.) which act as a stepping stone for more cautious students Meet with students one-on-one to convict them of the importance and effectiveness of our strategy Embolden students to participate in our summer internship program and to pursue long-term work in the pro-life movement Qualifications Commitment to the pro-life movement and the mission of Protect Life Michigan. Ability to commit to joining the team for one school year Passionate and positive view of support raising and/or fundraising. Support raising is necessary for this role. A positive view of support raising is part of PLM’s culture. Ability to effectively communicate in person, and in writing, including public speaking. A positive attitude, attention to detail, and ability to organize effectively. Valid driver’s license and the ability to travel. Lives within 30 minutes of at least one of the universities in the region. Flexible work schedule, and the ability to work nights/weekends as necessary. Proficiency in Google Applications. Must be a self-starter with the ability to work independently and productively. Experience in a campus pro-life group is preferred. Must be able to pass a background check. Salary/Benefits Salary and benefits are determined by the needs of the individual, commensurate with education and experience. Benefits include: After completing 1 year of work, eligibility for employer-matched Simple IRA. Ample professional development opportunities. Ample paid vacation time, holidays, and sick days. Semi-flexible schedule to be set with the employee and supervisor Ability to work from home. Support Raising Protect Life Michigan is a support-raising organization. The salary and all expenses associated with this position will be fundraised by the candidate . Protect Life Michigan will provide training and coaching in order to help the candidate reach full support and will pay the candidate while they raise support. We have an excellent track record of helping job candidates reach full support: 85% of our candidates have reached full support within 2-3 months. You will complete support raising prep work over the first 1-3 weeks, then you will attend a support raising bootcamp around week 4 of your employment with PLM. Subsequently, you will spend the next 6-13 weeks support raising before beginning your job duties. All applicants must be supportive of this approach and open to engaging in it. The compensation range is $14-20 per hour, depending on location. role: Student Worker - Residence Hall-Front Desk Assistant
description: Job Summary The Front Desk Assistant is a student position within the Department of Housing and Residence Life. Front Desk Assistants are responsible for providing professional front desk, administrative, and customer service support within the residence halls. Front Desk Assistants assist the Residence Hall Director and/or Assistant Residence Hall Director with the effective administration and daily operation of the residence hall. This includes staffing the front desk, assisting residents and guests, monitoring building access, responding appropriately to questions and concerns, and completing related administrative tasks. Front Desk Assistants are expected to maintain a professional, mature, and responsible demeanor at all times. They must exercise sound judgment, demonstrate strong communication and customer service skills, maintain confidentiality, and consistently follow and support Blinn College and Housing and Residence Life policies and procedures. Front Desk Assistants are scheduled to provide coverage during designated front desk hours, with shifts scheduled between 5:00 PM and 11:00 PM. Employees are expected to report to all assigned shifts on time and remain attentive and engaged throughout their scheduled work hours. Principal Accountabilities Front Desk Assistants are responsible for confirming that students live in the residence hall by checking student IDs and signing in all guests. They monitor the building entrance to ensure that only authorized residents and approved guests enter the student living areas. Front Desk Assistants help maintain a safe and welcoming residence hall environment 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through scheduled desk coverage. Assistants must be punctual and report to all assigned shifts on time. Front Desk Assistant shifts are scheduled between 5:00 PM and 11:00 PM, and employees must have availability to work during these hours. Check in all guests at the front desk. Verify residents and provide keys only for their assigned room when completing lockouts. Update FOB access as needed. Know emergency procedures and when it is appropriate to contact the RA on duty, Residence Hall Director, and/or Campus Police. Follow all fire alarm system and emergency evacuation procedures appropriately. Assist with all residence hall opening and closing responsibilities and assist with check-in and checkout procedures throughout the year. This includes reviewing room inventory forms, Personal Data Sheets, and other paperwork as residents check in and check out. Troubleshoot problems that occur with front desk operations. Maintain a clean and organized front desk and lobby area. Complete paperwork and administrative assignments in a timely manner, including but not limited to equipment checkouts and room inventory forms. Read and maintain the desk log, which is used to sign in and out of the desk, inventory lockout and equipment keys, and track other equipment and desk supplies. Respond to emergency exit door alarms, monitor security cameras, and greet students and guests entering the building. Confront policy violations that occur in the desk area and complete incident reports accurately and in a timely manner, immediately when possible. Report maintenance and custodial issues online or to the Residence Hall Director on call and show residents how to submit maintenance and custodial work requests online. Assist residents with lockout keys and other key-related issues. Serve as an information source to residents and parents regarding college and community services. Respect and maintain student and staff confidentiality, except in situations that may pose a danger to individuals or the greater community. Maintain a positive and open attitude when interacting with staff members, supervisors, Campus Police, residents, and visitors. Front Desk Assistants should model strong leadership characteristics, including responsibility, a positive attitude, fairness, enthusiasm, flexibility, commitment, integrity, good time management, communication skills, and a willingness to learn and work as part of a team. Perform other duties as assigned.

role: Cloud Hardware Development Engineer Intern, Annapurna Labs - 2027
description: At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you. What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus. About the team Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon at Amazon - including Graviton (our server processors), Trainium and Inferentia (our machine learning training and inference accelerators), and the Nitro system that powers modern EC2. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). As a Cloud Hardware Development Engineer Intern, you'll write the software that turns custom silicon into products used by millions. Annapurna has hardware teams across a range of systems and disciplines, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include: - Board and system design for ML servers and accelerator platforms - Firmware and low-level software development (BMC, device firmware) - Hardware bring-up, validation, and post-silicon testing - High-speed interconnect and signal integrity - System-level integration across compute, networking, and storage Once you join, we partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your project is something you're genuinely excited to work on. As a Cloud HDE Intern, you'll contribute to real hardware development work, which may include: - Supporting the design, bring-up, and validation of hardware systems and subsystems - Developing firmware or low-level software that interfaces directly with hardware - Debugging hardware-software integration issues in the lab using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and other bench equipment - Writing and running tests to validate hardware functionality, performance, and reliability - Collaborating with ASIC, systems, and software teams to take hardware from design through deployment - Documenting your work and presenting findings to the team You'll be paired with a mentor and manager who will scope your project, support your growth, and set you up to deliver meaningful, measurable impact by the end of your internship.

The Engineering Apprentice I shall be a member of a project engineering team responsible for completing assigned tasks within the allotted schedule and cost constraints. The Engineering Apprentice shall report directly to the Manager of the Engineering Department who is responsible for managing the engineering and design schedules and supervising team members. The Engineering Apprentice shall be fully capable and willing to perform all tasks assigned by the Management of the Engineering Department. The Engineering Apprentice shall be the single person on the Engineering and Design Team who is responsible and accountable for all aspects related to the structural and physical substation design of the project. The engineer is expected to be knowlegable in all aspects of substation design, including structural steel, foundations, rigid and flexible bus design, substation layout, electrical clearance and safety requirements, and equipment functions and their purpose. The engineer assigned to perform the structural calculations on a project is expected to follow his/her project throughout the design process, supporting the design team and providing technical advice. The engineer shall provide guidance, direction, instruction, and leadership to the design team pertaining to technical issues. The main objectives for the Engineering Apprentice shall be 0 Errors, 0 Missed Commitments, and efficient production. ### CORE COMPETENCIES: - Customer Focus - Decision Quality - Business Insight - Drives Results - Collaborates - Communicates Effectively - Courage - Instills Trust - Manages Ambiguity ### ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - The Engineering Apprentice shall be capable of applying engineering principles, judgment, and knowledge to develop innovative and cost saving solutions for all DIS-TRAN projects. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be responsible for producing accurate and organized structural calculations, for customer review, sizing all structural elements for structures to be fabricated as well as providing reactions for foundation design. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be fully knowledgeable of DIS-TRAN design standards including all applicable building codes and standards relating to physical and structural substation design. - The Engineering Apprentice shall produce efficient steel designs that meet all requirements of building codes, customer specifications, and equipment operational requirements. The engineer is expected to and be responsible for ensuring that all reasonable efforts are made to keep steel designs within the quoted steel cost. - The Engineering Apprentice shall work hand-in-hand with Structural Design Coordinators to efficiently create accurate structural models to feed the design process. The engineer is responsible for thoroughly checking all structural models before calculations are submitted for a project. - The Engineering Apprentice shall have adequate Inventor knowledge to be able to create simple structural models and all drawings that go in the structural calculation books. - The Engineering Apprentice shall have a thorough knowledge of all electrical clearance requirements, and assure they are met. - The Engineering Apprentice shall have a thorough knowledge of the function and operation of all substation equipment. Applying this knowledge is critical to producing adequate structure designs. - The Engineering Apprentice shall have a working knowledge of all engineering software used by DIS-TRAN. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be capable of reviewing/checking the bus design and structural layout for all projects. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be able to produce foundation designs and foundation construction drawings. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be responsible for following the project throughout the design process, support the design team on technical matters, and ensure that their design intent is maintained. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be responsible for helping, including working with project management, to resolve or remove any impediments to the successful completion of the project. - The Engineering Apprentice shall be responsible for knowing and understanding the specifications and/or customer requests – communicating any items that may be easily missed to the design team. It is expected that the engineer remains in touch with the design team on a periodic basis while the work is ongoing. - The Engineering Apprentice shall proactively schedule any team meetings that may be necessary due to multitudes of customer changes, piecemealed information, a sense of team confusion, conflicting specifications, progress getting off track, etc. Also, the engineer shall help make any decisions necessary to keep all parts/aspects of the project moving forward. - The Engineering Apprentice shall schedule any necessary check points for drawing and/or drawing package review to ensure the highest quality possible (ex. scheduling a checking session {possibly over lunch} to review the entire drawings package for an EPC job to ensure all changes or modifications along the way were incorporated). ### EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: - Must have a degree in Civil Engineering or a related field from an accredited university or equivalent experience. - PE preferred. - Strong background in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint required. - Excellent communication, organization, and writing skills are a must.

Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. Our first robot, LeLamp, explores a new category of consumer robotics where everyday objects become interactive and help us reshape our attachment to technology. Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments. **What to expect** We’re looking for a designer who thinks deeply about how objects make people feel and wants to shape what LeLamp looks like, how it interacts with people, and what it communicates just by sitting on a table. This isn’t about styling around existing hardware, it’s about defining the visual and physical language of a new kind of object without precedent. You’ll work closely with the CEO and founding team to take the robot’s exterior form from early sketches through physical samples to shipped products. **In this role, you will:** - Lead the exterior design of LeLamp across product generations, and maintain consistency as the product platform evolves. - Develop the product’s visual language, form, materials, and emotional presence. - Sketch and present design directions that communicate personality, not just geometry. - Translate concepts into production-ready 3D models with mechanical engineers. - Define CMF specs (materials, colors, finishes) and maintain documentation. - Review prototypes and cosmetic samples against design intent. - Contribute to how the robot is presented visually, including packaging, photography, art direction, and first-impression experience. - Own Class-A surfacing for injection molded and fabricated exterior parts, and ensuring surfaces remain DFM-ready without compromising design quality. - Prepare visual references, annotated models, and finish sample boards to support design reviews. **You may be a good fit if you:** - Have 3+ years in industrial or product design (consumer hardware or robotics). - Have a strong portfolio showing proportion, detail, and emotional sensitivity. - Have taken products from concept to production. - Are fluent in Rhino, Alias, Fusion, or similar tools. - Are comfortable designing without clear precedents. - Have Class-A surfacing experience. - Have worked with CMF specs and injection molding vendors. - Understand DFM constraints (draft, parting lines, textures). - Have a sharp eye for cosmetic quality and can articulate the difference between acceptable and not. - Care how products feel in everyday life, not just how they render. **We are looking for people who:** - Care deeply about how everyday objects fit into people's lives and homes. - Can hold creative direction steady across a long, messy development process without losing the thread. - Move quickly and can iterate through physical samples and vendor feedback without losing design direction. - Take ownership over the aesthetic quality of the product, even in stages of the process they don't directly control. - Work well in small, collaborative teams where the industrial designer and mechanical engineer are often the same conversation. - Think about the full arc from concept to shipped unit and hold the thread throughout. The early team becomes the DNA of the company. We set ourselves and others to a high standard, and we respond with kindness when things get hard but keep everyone accountable. This requires us to be curious, creative, and diverse in our thinking and approach. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hold back unless they meet 100% of the criteria - we don’t want that to be the reason we miss out on great talent.

### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. #### **About The Embedded Team** Zipline designs and operates the world’s largest drone delivery service providing access to critical medical supplies. Leading the way in drone delivery often means exceeding the capabilities of what’s available off the shelf, and as a result we need to engineer the majority of our system in-house. Doubling down on the reliability of our systems by writing embedded applications and drivers close to the hardware is a critical path to delivering to people whose lives will be meaningfully affected by smarter, more equitable access! We trust our team, so we’ll trust you. We’ll help you (and you’ll help us) find an area of technical ownership that you can dive deep into to define system requirements, develop creative and simple solutions, and prove with testing and data that your system meets the rigors and edge-cases of real-world deployment. We are a team that is constantly learning to improve our systems, and ourselves, and we can’t wait for you to join us! Among our current challenges: - Design and develop a software platform for the new P2 Zip and the world’s cutest Droid delivery and dock system - Scale our flight and distribution center software to allow upwards exponentially more deliveries per day - Prototype, test, and refine next generation flight and ground systems working alongside our mechanical and electrical engineering teams - Develop safe software architecture that will be deployed across the world - Develop perception solutions for any weather and any real world environment - Achieve safety and reliability goals beyond the current state of the art #### **The Role** Do you love tinkering with mechanical and electrical devices and watching your code come to life? Does writing safety-critical low-level software intrigue you? Do you see your projects through from start to finish, regardless of what you’re working on? Zipline is looking for interns to join our Embedded Systems team to advance our autonomous aircraft and ground systems. In this role, you will work alongside cross-functional partners to develop solutions to some of our trickiest problems. A lot goes into flying vital supplies autonomously, but doing so reliably and at scale is an even bigger challenge. From deploying embedded software to devices across the world, fault response and handling, launching & landing, all the way to integration with our customer’s physical & software systems, you will work with and learn from not only some of the most impressive embedded engineers in the field, but from a huge variety of our amazing Zipline team! **What You'll Do** - Embedded interns own a variety of big problems integral to our system! Examples of previous projects included: - Building an RF radio test setup to validate antenna performance of the flight compute at the production end-of-line. Responsibilities include owning the entire system—from RF signal injection, testing, and validation, to developing manufacturing software test suites, integrating with Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL), and leveraging simulation to model and measure worst-case scenarios. - Develop firmware for a real-time coprocessor that manages high-frequency signals and I/O expansion for the Linux camera subsystem. Own the overall system design, contribute to board design revisions, and validate signal integrity, jitter, and clock alignment. - Building a high data rate voltage and current telemetry system that runs continuously in our RTOS using ADCs, I2C devices and GPIO interrupts. Testing this feature rigorously, deploying it to production globally, building data analysis tools to verify that the feature is working properly, and using this data to root-cause tricky failures to improve the reliability of our systems. - Rapidly iterating on the concept of a new perception system, integrating compute modules and sensor prototypes to fly a proof of concept ASAP and de-risk key aspects of the approach. - Working with operations teams to identify ways to improve our ground systems behavior to enable faster aircraft launch and landing. Prioritizing changes by obtaining engineering leadership buy-in, and implementing them by using a variety of bench-top and real flight-test methods to verify the code. Ultimately, rolling out the update to global operations! #### **What You'll Bring** - Must have at least completed the second year of your Undergraduate studies. Masters and PhD students are also eligible - Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Computer Engineering - You've designed, built and/or deployed electromechanical systems or robots, inside or outside the classroom - You’re comfortable working in one of C, C++, Python, or Rust, and have developed software for a real time operating system or embedded Linux - You are comfortable getting feedback so that you can learn to write code that is efficient, easy-to-read, well-tested, has friendly APIs, and incurs minimal technical debt - You’re familiar with basic electrical engineering concepts, such as reading schematics, debugging with an oscilloscope, and communication protocols (CAN, SPI, UART, etc) - You've had experience writing low level drivers for sensors and actuators, reading datasheets, and debugging hardware systems - Bonus for having experience with embedded camera interfaces (MIPI, GMSL2, etc.), ISP tuning, and camera sensor bringup #### **What Else You Should Know** *Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September).* *The hourly rate for this internship is $54 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.* *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. role: Junior Bioinformatics Scientist, Bureau of the Public Health Laboratory
description: The Division of Disease Control's mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. PHL is committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns. The NYC Public Health Laboratory seeks a qualified City Research Scientist II to serve as a Junior Bioinformatics Scientist. DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Assist with conducting bioinformatics analyses for sequencing data that support public health efforts Assist with developing or improving tools related to pathogen identification, outbreak tracking, mapping drug resistance determinants, variant analysis, genome annotation and phylogenetics, genomics data visualization. Assist with strengthening the application of genomic tools to support public health diagnostic testing for pathogens from clinical and environmental samples (e.g., wastewater). Conducting literature reviews and stay up to date with cutting edge scientific and epidemiological research and tools. Assist with mentoring and cross-training staff or research fellows at PHL. Collaborating with other team members and partners on genomics data management (e.g., SQL data bases, public repository uploads, other datasets). Participating in agency wide WGS journal club and genomic data exchange working groups. Developing tools (e.g., dashboards) or strategies (e.g., Docker-based pipelines) to improve accessibility of bioinformatics analyses to no bioinformaticians (e.g., epidemiologists, virologists, microbiologists). Drafting written protocols and maintain accurate records of software tools design. Writing original manuscripts for publication based on data analyses and product development. Maintaining quality assurance and control of HTS data generated by PHL to ensure reproducibility and accuracy of downstream bioinformatics analyses. This includes writing and designing SOPs and validation/verification protocols. Using best practices for code development, and documentation. Participating in presentations and workshops with Quality Management (QM) at PHL to improve understanding and tracking of sequencing data and analyses quality control measures, data security and data management using resources from APHL, ASM, and others. PREFERRED SKILLS: Strong skills in Linux command line and BASH shell scripting. Proficient in R, Python, C, Java, or other programming languages. Experience in SQL. Experience in utilizing multi-core server resources, automating processes, containerization, and workflow languages. Experience with common tools for Next Generation Sequencing Analysis (NGSA), including reference-based analysis and de novo sequencing analysis (knowledge of open source and commercial microbial NGS analysis pipelines) and genome annotation. Demonstrated work in public health genomics research. MS or PhD degree in the biological sciences, evolutionary biology, genomics, or related fields. Strong analytical and organizational skills; Excellent oral, inter-personal and written communication skills. **About The Weather Company:** The Weather Company is the world’s leading weather provider, helping people and businesses make more informed decisions and take action in the face of weather. Together with advanced technology and AI, The Weather Company’s high-volume weather data, insights, advertising, and media solutions across the open web help people, businesses, and brands around the world prepare for and harness the power of weather in a scalable, privacy-forward way. The world’s most accurate forecaster globally, the company reaches hundreds of enterprise clients and more than 360 million monthly active users via its digital properties from The Weather Channel () and Weather Underground (). **AI is part of how we work:**Human judgment, expertise, and creativity remain essential and are amplified by AI. We expect everyone in this role to use AI thoughtfully and proactively to accelerate their performance, improve the quality of their work, and explore new possibilities. We are looking for people who are curious, adaptable, and excited to help shape an AI-enabled culture that delivers better outcomes for our customers and our company. **Job brief:** The Weather Company is hiring a **Weather Science Intern** for a 12-month term on our Consumer Weather Science team. This is a hands-on role for a science-minded builder: someone who knows weather, likes to code, is energized by AI tooling, and thinks like a product person. You will work alongside meteorologists, engineers, and product managers to improve real consumer weather experiences used by millions of people, across a portfolio that spans experiments, flagship app features, and the Project Synoptic forecasting platform, with **Storm Radar** as one of your focal projects. This is not a fetch-coffee internship and it is not a summer project that gets shelved in August. You will own real work, get mentored by a senior science and product team, and build the exact skills (agentic AI, product engineering, applied meteorology) that the weather industry is moving toward. We designed the role as a runway: prove yourself over the year and there is a clear path to a full-time offer. **The impact you'll make:** - **Contribute across the Consumer Weather Science portfolio.** Help build and improve consumer weather experiences that span topics like severe weather, snow, pollen, wildfire, and outdoor and seasonal activities, from experiments to flagship app features. - **Make Storm Radar better for the people who actually use it (a focal project).** Partner with our Storm Radar product lead to pressure-test the product against real “in-field” moments: the user standing outside deciding whether to seek shelter, keep driving, or resume the game. Look hard at latency (does the newest radar arrive fast enough to matter) and global coverage (does it hold up outside the US), and turn what you find into clear product feedback. - **Prototype with modern AI tooling.** Build small, working prototypes of new consumer experiences and internal tools using our stack: Python, LLM and agentic workflows, and a modern web stack (Next.js, React, TypeScript) on AWS and Vercel. You will ship fast, learn by doing, and get real code review and mentorship. - **Do science-grounded analysis.** Pull, clean, and analyze weather data (radar, model output, observations) to answer product questions across the portfolio and confirm that features are meteorologically sound. You will turn analysis into decision ready findings the team can act on. **What you've accomplished:** - Current graduate student or recent graduate in **atmospheric science, meteorology, or a closely** **related quantitative field** (Graduate students preferred; strong senior undergraduates considered). - Genuine curiosity about weather and a track record of teaching yourself things (personal projects, research, forecasting, competitions). - Comfort with **Python** and real interest in **AI and agentic tooling.** You do not need to be an expert. We care about aptitude and appetite to learn. - A **product and business instinct**: you care about how real users experience a product, not just the model behind it. - Bonus, not required: any exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript, React/Next.js, Git, AWS, Mapbox/GIS, or weather-data formats (radar, GRIB, NetCDF, NWS/METAR APIs). - Able to commit to the full ~12-month term (roughly 30 hours/week in the summer and 10 hours/week during the school year) and to work hybrid from a TWC hub (Atlanta preferred; New York or Andover also work). **Pay Rate:** $35.00/hr (Undergraduate) – $50.00/hr (Graduate) *The hourly pay offered will take into account internal equity and may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region of work premises, academic level (undergraduate vs. graduate), job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, among other factors.* **TWCo Benefits/Perks:** - Hybrid work model - An opportunity to work for a global and industry-leading technology company - Impactful work in a collaborative environment

Our robots take on the tedious, hazardous, and ergonomically demanding work that has kept manufacturing dependent on a shrinking skilled workforce, delivering superhuman performance. Robotics has a demo problem. GMR doesn't. Our systems are in active production today, adapting autonomously to real geometries, real materials, and real process variation without reprogramming. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale. As the **AI Research Intern: Foundation Models**, you will join the Special Projects: AI team, a cross-functional group responsible for designing, building, and operationalizing AI capabilities across GMR’s products and customer deployments. The team operates end-to-end from problem formulation and data strategy to model development, simulation, deployment, and long-term performance monitoring collaborating closely with robotics software, solutions engineering, applications, process engineering, hardware, and deployment teams. The team’s mandate is to ensure that AI systems scale across processes, customers, and sites, and perform reliably on real robots in real factories, today, not just in controlled demonstrations. ***PLEASE NOTE: This is an immediate start of a full-time, onsite internship position.*** **What to Expect** - Work with the Special Projects AI team to work on next generation of foundation models that power GrayMatter Robotics Solutions (FSI) - Take on real, complex, ambiguous problems and work through them on accelerated timelines, largely independently - Develop foundation models for high precision manufacturing applications with multi-modal data beyond Vision or Force alone - Validate models through rigorous testing on real world industrial robots and actual production parts - Own the entire project lifecycle: data curation, simulation, model training, evaluation and robot deployment - Write maintainable, production quality code for internal R&D **Export Control Requirements** In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158. **What You’ll Bring** - Currently remotely pursuing a PhD in Robotics, AI, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related fields - Research experience in Foundation Models for robot manipulation applications - Proficiency in Python and at least one deep learning framework: PyTorch is preferred - Strong working knowledge and deep understanding of current World Models and Foundation Model Research - Demonstrated experience working with simulation environments and/or physics-based modeling for robotics (e.g. Isaac Lab or MuJoCo) - Experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or policy optimization for robotic manipulation or process control - Experience with robotics middleware and tooling (e.g., ROS/ROS2) and deployment on real robotic hardware - A publication track record in venues such as ICRA, CoRL, RSS, IROS, RA-L, or T-RO, balanced with a strong bias toward real-world production impact **Nice to Have’s** - Experience with VLA/VLM training - # Software Engineer — New Graduate ## About Us At Prophet Security, we’re not just building a platform that automates complex security tasks—we’re building a company where every team member directly impacts customer success. You’ll work closely with our customers, understand their needs, and see firsthand how your work makes a difference. Prophet Security’s founding team brings more than 30 years of cybersecurity experience from leading companies, including Abnormal Security, Expel, Mandiant, McAfee, Oracle, Red Canary, Red Hat, Riverbed, and Symantec. We are focused on disrupting the $400 billion security labor market by building the future of automated security operations. We’re seeking recent and upcoming graduates to join our engineering team. If you’re excited to build impactful products, grow alongside experienced engineers, and take meaningful ownership at a fast-growing startup, we encourage you to apply. ## What Our Platform Does Our platform analyzes security alerts, develops and executes investigation plans, and produces detailed findings and actionable recommendations. Security analysts review these investigations and provide context and feedback, which are continuously incorporated into future automation. ## The Impact You’ll Have As a New Graduate Software Engineer, you’ll help build and evolve the core backend systems that power Prophet’s platform. Working alongside experienced engineers and experts in product, machine learning, and cybersecurity, you’ll contribute to services that ingest, process, and reason over large volumes of security data. Example projects may include: - **Integrations at scale:** Building extensible frameworks for integrations with third-party security systems, including SIEMs, EDR/XDR platforms, identity providers, and cloud and SaaS logs. - **Proof-of-Value pipelines:** Developing performant, reliable backends that enable fast customer onboarding and compelling proof-of-value experiences, from data ingestion to actionable insights. - **Security data platforms:** Designing storage, indexing, and access patterns for highly dimensional, time-oriented security data used in real-time analysis and historical investigations. - **AI-powered security workflows:** Developing and evaluating agents and automation that help security teams investigate threats more quickly and effectively. You’ll write production code, participate in technical design, collaborate across teams, and take ownership of projects from development through deployment. You’ll receive guidance and mentorship while gaining the independence to solve meaningful technical and customer problems. **Our technology stack:** AI-powered agents, data synthesis and correlation, security-tool integrations, Python, Go, React, and TypeScript. ## Qualifications - Recently completed or currently completing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. - Experience with one or more relevant programming languages, such as Python or Go, through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects. - Understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts, including data structures, algorithms, testing, and system design. - Demonstrated experience building software through academic, internship, research, open-source, or personal projects. - Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail. - Clear written and verbal communication skills. - Ability to collaborate effectively and learn in a fast-moving environment. - Passion for building high-quality products and solving customer problems. Experience with backend services, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, or machine learning is helpful but not required. ## Our Culture Our employees are our greatest asset. We provide competitive benefits, meaningful equity participation, and a fun, inspiring environment in which to learn, create, and collaborate. - **Customer Centricity:** We place customers at the center of our decisions and strive to exceed their expectations. - **Practicality over Perfection:** We favor effective solutions, thoughtful tradeoffs, and agile decision-making. - **Strive for Excellence:** We hold ourselves to high standards and continuously improve. - **Transparent Communication:** We encourage open, honest dialogue and build trust through collaboration. - **Unwavering Resilience:** We persist through challenges and remain focused on achieving our goals. - **Have Fun:** We balance hard work with creativity, enjoyment, and a positive team environment. ## Equal Opportunity Prophet Security is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse, global talent pool and the collaboration that results from an inclusive team. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected characteristic. Our hiring decisions are based exclusively on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** We are seeking a highly motivated and organized Hardware Technical Program Management (TPM) Intern to join our Hardware team. This role is critical in supporting our engineering builds by ensuring the timely and accurate management and tracking of hardware parts and materials, as well as helping to keep the build process running smoothly. As an intern, you will contribute directly to the efficiency and success of our hardware development cycles, working closely with engineers and cross-functional teams. **What You’ll Do** - Manage and track the inventory of hardware parts and materials required for various engineering builds. - Track build issues and help unblock problems, acting as a critical liaison between engineering and external teams. - Coordinate with the Hardware Engineering and Procurement teams to ensure parts are ordered and delivered on schedule to meet build timelines. - Implement and maintain a systematic tracking process for all components, from initial order through to deployment in the build. - Identify and flag potential material shortages or delays, proactively communicating risks to the engineering team. - Support continuous improvement efforts for the parts management and inventory control processes to increase efficiency. **What You'll Bring** - Hands-on experience bringing next-gen battery into production. - Strong organizational and interpersonal skills to coordinate across multiple teams and stakeholders. *Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. ## **Junior Quantitative Researcher** ## About the role Deeter Analytics is a privately held investment research and trading firm managing its own capital across public markets. After years of discretionary success, we think we have some unique ways of seeing the market, and we pair sharp human judgment with modern AI to act on them. A lot of what we trade starts as a hunch at the desk: a pattern that keeps showing up, a relationship that feels like it should hold, a setup someone wants to trust but doesn't yet. We're hiring a Junior Quantitative Researcher to turn those hunches into evidence, and evidence into signals the desk actually uses. You'll take questions from the traders, test them honestly against the data, and come back in plain language: what holds, what doesn't, how strong, since when, and where it breaks. This is not a systematic seat: your models won't trade on their own, and you won't be one factor in an anonymous alpha pool. Your work is done when a trader understands it, trusts it, and acts on it. It's an entry point into a serious seat: as your signals prove out, they get more weight in the book, and you get more scope. The role is full-time and fully remote, US-based, overlapping the desk on US market hours. ## What you'll own • **The question queue.** Desk hunches in, answers out. You scope the question, run the study, and come back sometimes same-day with what the data says, at the depth the question deserves. • **The signal shelf.** A growing library of signals and screens the desk trades around (earnings and event setups, positioning and flow extremes, regime and factor context) each with a documented edge, known failure modes, and live tracking against expectation. You retire what decays. • **The evidence standard.** Event studies, conditioning analyses, base rates, and walk-forward checks that hold up: point-in-time data, no leakage, no survivorship, costs counted, multiple-testing restraint. A backtest here is a way to kill an idea, not to sell it. • **The quant read.** The recurring numbers layer under the desk's picture of the market (regime, factor moves, breadth, positioning) feeding the morning picture rather than duplicating it. • **The research data.** Clean, point-in-time datasets (prices, fundamentals, earnings calendars, options and positioning) organized so every number you've ever reported traces back to code and data. • **AI leverage.** Use modern AI tools to test more ideas, read more literature, and write cleaner code than one person otherwise could, and verify what they give you. ## Who you are We hire for demonstrated judgment and how you think, not for pedigree. This is a junior seat, so we don't expect a markets résumé — the best evidence usually comes from wherever you've already done rigorous quantitative work. We look for signs that you are: • **Rigorous where it counts.** You think in base rates, sample sizes, and conditioning; you know what autocorrelation, overlapping windows, and fat tails do to naive statistics, and you'd rather report a small honest edge than a large fragile one. • **Hypothesis-driven.** You start from a mechanism (why would this work, who's on the other side, why hasn't it been arbitraged away) and let the data disappoint you, not the other way around. • **A translator.** Your finished product is a chart and a paragraph a non-quant acts on. If the desk can't understand it, it isn't done. • **Comfortable finding nothing.** "There's nothing there" is a result you deliver without flinching: a clean negative saves the desk real money, and you never dress noise up as signal to give someone the answer they wanted. • **Genuinely curious about markets.** You want to know why prices move. You don't need professional markets experience, you need to care about the answer. • **Low ego and coachable.** You take feedback well, update quickly when the facts change, and care more about the answer than the credit. ## How you work • **At desk speed, without cutting corners.** A rough answer today often beats a perfect answer next week; a deep study is worth a month when the stakes justify it. You know which question is which, and you label your answers accordingly. • **Kill your own results first.** Before anyone else sees a number, you've gone hunting for the leak, the regime dependence, and the artifact that would explain it away. • **Reproducible by default.** Versioned data and code; any signal or study can be re-run months later and give the same answer. • **Signal over noise.** You surface the few things that matter, track what you've shipped, and say so plainly when something stops working. • **AI-native.** Fluent with modern AI tools for research, coding, and literature triage, and disciplined about checking their output. • **Self-directed.** You thrive working remotely with low guardrails, managing your own time and flagging what needs attention without being asked. ## Core skills • **Statistics and probability.** Regression and its failure modes, hypothesis testing, bootstrap and resampling, thinking clearly about uncertainty in small and messy samples. • **Python data stack.** pandas, NumPy, SQL, and plotting that makes a point; notebooks that read top to bottom, graduating to scripts when a study becomes a signal. • **Backtest and event-study hygiene.** Point-in-time discipline, survivorship and look-ahead awareness, transaction-cost sanity, walk-forward validation, restraint about how many things you tested. • **Market data.** Comfort with prices, returns, fundamentals, and earnings calendars; options or positioning data a plus. • **ML as a tool, not an identity.** Regularized regression and gradient boosting when they beat something simpler, interpretability first. This is a statistics-first seat, not a deep-learning one. • **Crisp communication.** Compressing a study into exactly what a trader needs to know, now. ## What we offer • A seat inside a live trading operation, with a direct line to the traders who act on your evidence. • Fast feedback: when a signal proves out, you watch it get used — and you'll know precisely what your work changed. • A well-capitalized firm with a distinctive approach to markets. • A deliberate growth path: own the question queue first, then take on a bigger slice of the research agenda as you prove out. • A small, low-ego, fully remote team. • Compensation: $120k - $170k + bonus.

The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) protects and enhances the daily economic lives of New Yorkers to create thriving communities. DCWP licenses nearly 45,000 businesses in more than 40 industries and enforces key consumer protection and workplace laws that apply to countless more. By supporting businesses through equitable enforcement and access to resources, DCWP protects the marketplace from predatory practices and strives to create a culture of compliance. DCWP empowers consumers and working families by providing the tools and resources they need to achieve financial health and work-life balance. DCWP also conducts research and advocates for public policy that furthers its work to support New York City’s communities. For more information about DCWP and its work, call 311 or visit DCWP at NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), sign up for its newsletter, or follow on its social media sites, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube. Within DCWP, the Office of Financial Empowerment (OFE) focuses on initiatives that support New Yorkers and communities with low incomes in building wealth and improving their financial health. OFE is the first local government initiative in the country with the mission to educate, empower, and protect New Yorkers and neighborhoods with low incomes so they can build assets and make the most of their financial resources. OFE uses data and research, policy, partnerships, and convenings to advance its mission. Using this model, OFE is able to develop, offer, and advocate for innovative programs and products for all New Yorkers. To further its mission, OFE launched in January 2026, the Financial Literacy for Youth Initiative with the mission to connect NYC Public School students and their families to financial and consumer education programming to help them learn how to spend and save money so that they have a head start on being financially empowered adults. The City has committed funding to this initiative which will be overseen by DCWP, in collaboration with NYC Public Schools, to offer every student access to quality financial and consumer education by 2030. OFE designed the Financial Literacy for Youth Initiative with the goal to cultivate financially savvy youth by collaborating with educators, banking experts, and community partners to provide hands-on financial empowerment and consumer protection programming and services to youth and their families, while providing real-life professional development opportunities in school. This initiative launched in January 2026 with Financial Educators in 15 districts to lead the charge and deliver core programming, including 2Gen financial and consumer education workshops for both students and their families; on-site financial counseling; build school districts and schools capacity to integrate financial literacy inside and outside classrooms, and promotion of the Financial Education Resource Hub. OFE is seeking a Graduate Intern to join the Financial Counseling and Coaching team, with the primary responsibility of supporting the implementation of this new youth financial empowerment initiative. The Graduate Intern is, ideally, a graduate student studying instructional design and learning technology, and will work closely with the Senior Program Officer and Program Officer responsible for leading the implementation of the initiative, supporting the creation of the 2Gen financial education workshops for students and parents/caregivers and their alignment with NYS Education’s 2026 change to require personal finance education in all grade levels. The Graduate Intern will collaborate with other stakeholders, such as the DCWP External Affairs & Communications Division, NYC Public Schools, and OFE’s contracted providers, through the implementation of a youth initiative with the mission to cultivate financially savvy youth by providing hands-on financial empowerment and consumer protection services and real-life professional development opportunities in school. The Graduate Intern is an organized project manager with a strong commitment to supporting New Yorkers and communities with low incomes in building wealth and improving their financial health and a passion for financial education. The Graduate Intern will report to the Senior Program Officer for Financial Counseling and Coaching Programs. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: - Assisting the Senior Program Officer with research on youth financial education and/or youth financial empowerment programs to inform the design and implementation of financial empowerment services focusing on youth and their families – including developing metrics, assessment tools, touchpoints for service integration, and operational strategy; - Supporting the Senior Program Officer in liaising with the DCWP External Affairs & Communications Division, NYC Public Schools, and MWBE vendors to coordinate and monitor the design and develop age-appropriate, engaging workshop curriculum materials on financial literacy topics (e.g., budgeting, savings, banking, credit, paying for college education, and consumer protection) and ensure that workshop content is culturally-relevant, inclusive, and accessible to diverse student populations. - Liaising and coordinating with the DCWP External Affairs and Communications Division and Division of Technology and Strategic Solutions, as well as MWBE vendors, to recommend instructional design models to guide the creation of digital and in-person learning experiences. - Under the supervision of the Senior Program Officer, and in coordination with the Policy and Research team, developing formative and summative assessment tools (e.g., pre/post surveys, quizzes, reflective prompts) to measure knowledge gains and shifts in attitudes or behaviors. - Working with OFE's Policy and Research team to understand and document the success of programs and assist with data analysis to inform iterative improvements to content and delivery methods and provide timely updates to OFE and DCWP leadership; - Maintaining clear documentation of curriculum frameworks, learning objectives, digital tools used, and impact metrics. - Providing general administrative assistance, including drafting, proofreading, and/or editing a range of materials, including but not limited to reports, program documents, and presentations. Support and contribute to broader team projects as needed as a Financial Counseling and Coaching team member. The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high-quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP's water supply system is comprised of 19 reservoirs and 3 controlled lakes throughout the system’s 2,000 square mile watershed that extends 125 miles north and west of the City. The Bureau of Environmental Planning and Analysis (BEPA) is responsible for the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) planning and implementation for the City including permitting and enforcement for the construction/post construction program. The Stormwater Permitting Section is responsible for implementing 15 RCNY Chapter 19.1 and the construction /post-construction requirements of the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System permit issued to the City by NYS Department of Environmental Conservation. Professional engineers, registered landscape architects and other professionals that have knowledge in design and implementation of designs for the prevention of pollution related to stormwater runoff prepare and submit stormwater pollution prevention plans. Under the updated MS4 Permit, the City has reduced the soil disturbance threshold of projects requiring review and approval in the MS4 areas to 20,000 square feet. In addition, the City will enforce the same rules in the combined sewer service area in an effort to reduce the occurrence of combined sewer overflows. That addition with the MS4 area reduction is expected to increase the number of applications. BEPA is seeking to hire Environmental Engineering Interns for the Stormwater Permitting section located in Queens, NY. Under supervision, selected candidates will review construction plans for compliance with the rules and regulations for the management of stormwater from construction sites and maintenance of post construction stormwater management practices (SMPs), inspect sites for compliance with approved plans and in response to complaints from public. Applications will include documents, drawings and supporting calculations to demonstrate compliance with the code; the reviewer must be able to read and understand documents drawing and supporting calculations to determine compliance. The reviewer will inspect sites before, during and after construction and must be able to read design plans and locate proposed practices in the field. The reviewer may be required to witness soil testing for compliance with standards and specifications. Specific work areas where staff will be engaged include, but are not necessarily limited to, review of plans, calculations and supporting documentation for stormwater pollution prevention plans, witnessing soil tests, inspecting sites prior to construction, and inspecting stormwater management practices during and after construction. Environmental Engineering Interns will be responsible for the following. - Demonstrates the ability to read and understand engineering plans and drawings - Understands requirements of the SWPPP. Understands applicable rules and codes. Is able to complete calculations to check designs. - Reviews applications for compliance with rules - Responds to complaints - Inspects construction sites for compliance with approved plans - Inspect stormwater management practices (SMPs) for compliance with permit - Communicates questions and concerns on applications and inspections ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING INTE - 20616 A baccalaureate degree in environmental, fire protection, chemical, mechanical, petroleum, aeronautical, or materials engineering from an accredited college; or A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college in environmental, fire protection, chemical, mechanical, petroleum, aeronautical, or materials engineering technology and two years of full-time satisfactory experience in environmental engineering work. **Who We Are** GITAI is a vertically integrated space and defense company building the next generation of hardware for low-Earth-orbit missions. At our core is the space robotics technology that has defined GITAI from the beginning. A small, highly capable engineering team applies that foundation across satellite buses, in-orbit servicing robotics, and mission hardware for applications such as Earth observation. Today, a major focus of our work is supporting U.S. national security missions, particularly through proliferated LEO satellite constellations and other next-generation space systems. We design, build, integrate, and test much of our hardware in-house. Electrical, mechanical, software, manufacturing, integration, and test teams work closely together, allowing a small team to own complete systems rather than isolated components. This vertical integration helps us move quickly, learn directly from hardware, and shorten the path from architecture to a working system. We are still early. The systems, the company, and the market are all being built at the same time. Requirements change, technical problems are often ambiguous, and many answers do not yet exist. We are looking for exceptional engineers and operators who want broad ownership, can work across disciplines, and are willing to stay close to the hardware until the mission succeeds. **Your Mission** As an Early Career Electrical Engineer at GITAI, you will design, build, and test board-level electrical hardware for spacecraft, robotic systems, and space defense programs. This is a hands-on PCB design and avionics hardware role. You will work across the full hardware lifecycle, including schematic capture, PCB layout, fabrication, assembly, board bring-up, debugging, and system integration. We do not expect you to already know how to build space hardware. No prior space, aerospace, or defense experience is required. Strong candidates may come from university engineering teams, research labs, internships, robotics, automotive, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment, consumer electronics, or other hardware environments. What matters is that you have already spent meaningful time designing real electronics and turning those designs into working hardware. You will work closely with experienced electrical, mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and systems engineers. You will be given real ownership early. The problems will not always be well defined, and the design that looks right on paper will sometimes fail on the bench. You will be expected to learn quickly, debug methodically, and keep the hardware moving. **What You’ll Drive** - Design schematics and PCB layouts for spacecraft and robotic systems. - Take PCBAs from design release through fabrication, assembly, bring-up, and test. - Debug board-level hardware and drive issues to root cause. - Work with mechanical, firmware/software, and manufacturing engineers to integrate hardware into complete systems. - Support hardware testing, failure investigation, and design iteration. **What We’re Looking For** - 2+ years of hands-on PCB design experience using Altium or a similar ECAD tool. - Experience taking at least one PCB from schematic and layout through fabrication, bring-up, and test. - Hands-on PCBA debugging experience using standard lab equipment. - Practical knowledge of PCB fabrication, assembly, and DFM. - Strong fundamentals in board-level electrical design. - No prior aerospace, space, or defense industry experience required. **Location & Employment Details** - Location: Torrance, CA (onsite).
