# **Campus Director — AoPS Academy Cambridge** ## **Build a Campus Where Motivated Students Thrive** Some students are happiest when the work is hard, the questions are deep, and the people around them share their enthusiasm for learning. AoPS Academy exists for those students. As Campus Director of AoPS Academy Cambridge campus, you will lead a community built around intellectual curiosity and meaningful mathematical challenge. You will bring together exceptional teachers, motivated students, and families who believe young people are capable of far more than they are often asked to do. You will set the tone for the campus, champion AoPS’s academic mission, and help make the Cambridge Campus a place where students feel known, inspired, and excited to stretch themselves. ## **About AoPS Academy** AoPS Academy is part of Art of Problem Solving (AoPS), a global leader in advanced K–12 math education. Since 1993, AoPS has helped discover, inspire, and train the next generation of great problem solvers — students who are energized by challenge, motivated to stretch their thinking, and eager to explore complex ideas. AoPS Academy brings this approach to small, live classrooms, both in person and online. We offer advanced courses in math, science, and language arts for students in Grades 1–12, creating local communities where intellectual exploration meets rigorous challenges. Our students learn from accomplished instructors and alongside peers who share their enthusiasm for learning. Since opening our first Academy in 2016, we have grown to more than 20 campuses nationwide, and we are continuing to expand. ## **The Opportunity** The AoPS Academy Campus Director at our Cambridge campus leads a vibrant, dynamic enrichment program where each day brings new opportunities to engage students, mentor instructors, and solve meaningful challenges. In addition to being the academic leader of the campus, you will lead a team to engage with families of both current and prospective students, growing campus enrollments, and ensuring a thriving learning community. This might be the right job for you if you thrive in a dynamic environment, enjoy solving problems creatively while guiding others to do the same, and have the academic vision and leadership capability to grow a problem solving culture among staff, students, and their families. If you’re passionate about cultivating critical thinking, challenging students to solve complex math problems, and inspiring a love of deep learning, we want to hear from you! ## **What You Will Lead** ### **Create an Exceptional Academic Community** - Establish a campus culture where academically advanced students are challenged, supported, and excited to learn. - Ensure every class challenges and engages our most advanced learners, reflecting AoPS’s commitment to deep understanding, active participation, and rigorous problem-solving. - Teach AoPS courses and remain closely connected to the student and instructor experience. - Build a culture of instructional excellence in which all instructors continue to grow as educators and ambassadors of the AoPS approach, and exceptionally talented teachers who can engage and challenge our most advanced students are recognized and celebrated. - Maintain the highest standards of academic quality and service to families. ### **Build and Inspire a Strong Team** - Recruit, hire, train, evaluate, and retain outstanding full-time and part-time staff. - Give team members clear expectations, meaningful feedback, and opportunities to develop. - Build a collaborative culture in which people take ownership, solve problems, and remain focused on the company mission. ### **Help More Families Discover and Stay with AoPS** - Build trusted relationships with current and prospective students and families. - Help families understand what makes AoPS different and determine whether our programs are the right fit for their children. - Lead efforts to grow enrollment and retain students by delivering an experience families find academically meaningful and personally welcoming. - Develop mission-aligned partnerships with local organizations. Attend and host events that strengthen the local advanced math learning community. ### **Turn Vision into a Thriving Campus** - Take ownership of the campus’s reputation in academic and customer service excellence, and ensure its long-term success. - Execute campus playbooks to deliver the most mission-aligned experience possible. - Use your frontline experience to anticipate future needs, plan thoughtfully, and partner with regional and national leadership to address challenges and opportunities as they emerge. ## **Qualifications** ### **Required** - Bachelor’s degree - Teaching experience and highly aligned with AoPS pedagogy - Deep understanding of the needs of students advanced in mathematics - Strong leadership and commitment to academic excellence ### **Preferred** - Advanced degree in math or a related field - Teaching experience with advanced learners in elementary or secondary schools - Familiarity with math and other academic competitions - Leadership experience, preferably in an academically enriching environment - Experience with student recruitment, marketing, community engagement, or enrollment growth We recognize that exceptional candidates do not always follow identical professional paths. We encourage you to apply if the mission resonates with you and your experience has prepared you to lead an ambitious educational community. ## **Work Schedule** AoPS Academy is an after-school program, so most classes and many campus responsibilities take place during evenings and weekends. Campus Directors therefore work a nontraditional schedule during the school year and should be present during the hours when students, families, and instructors are most active. Summer operations typically follow a more traditional Monday-through-Friday schedule. ## **Why Join AoPS** **Meaningful impact:** Work directly with motivated students and passionate educators while advancing a mission centered on developing the great problem solvers of the next generation. **An intellectually ambitious culture:** Join an organization of builders, educators, and lifelong learners who care deeply about ideas, academic quality, and continual improvement. **A chance to build:** Shape the culture, reputation, and future of a growing AoPS Academy campus. **Benefits**: Multiple options for Medical, Dental and Vision plans **Future Planning:** 401(k) retirement plan with company matching **Quality of Life:** PTO Plan and supportive leadership **Ease of Transition:** Relocation bonus for candidates living outside the greater area ## **Location and Compensation** **Location:** Cambridge, MA **Hiring range:** $129,275 – 133,463 **Please note that in order to be considered for this position you must be legally authorized to work in the US. We are unable to offer sponsorship, including STEM-OPT and H-1B.**

High School Diploma or equivalent Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills Comfortable making outbound phone calls and engaging with new people Positive attitude and willingness to learn Experience using Microsoft office including Word, Outlook, and Excel Time management and task prioritization Commitment and understanding of company policies and controls Strong work ethic with a high focus on being proactive Working towards a college degree with targeted graduation date in the next two years or less All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place! E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems. We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. **About the Role** Join our RF Product Development team as an intern supporting component and assembly prototyping, testing, and debugging activities. This role emphasizes software development skills to drive automation across ground-based RF test systems, data acquisition, and fault analysis workflows. **Key Responsibilities** - Support prototyping, integration, and bring-up of RF components and assemblies in a lab environment - Perform functional, performance, and environmental testing on RF hardware - Troubleshoot and debug RF circuits, assemblies, and test setups to isolate root causes of failures - Design and develop software/scripts to automate ground-based RF test systems and reduce manual test time - Program data acquisition routines to collect measurement data from RF test equipment (e.g., spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, signal generators, power meters) - Develop analysis routines/algorithms to process acquired data for fault detection and anomaly identification - Build and validate data pipelines that produce "proofed" (verified/cleaned) data streams to support calibration activities and fault resolution - Document test procedures, automation scripts, and analysis methods for repeatability and knowledge transfer - Collaborate with RF engineers, test engineers, and software developers to translate manual test processes into automated workflows - Assist in creating dashboards, reports, or visualizations to communicate test results and fault trends to engineering teams - Support calibration activities for RF test equipment and assemblies as needed **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field - Foundational knowledge of RF/microwave concepts (S-parameters, signal chains, impedance matching, etc.) - Programming experience in Python, MATLAB, C#, or similar languages - Familiarity with instrument control/automation frameworks (e.g., PyVISA, SCPI commands, LabVIEW, VISA/GPIB interfaces) - Basic understanding of data analysis techniques (statistical analysis, signal processing, or similar) - Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail - Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a lab environment **Preferred Qualifications** - Experience with RF test equipment (VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power sensors) - Exposure to automated test equipment (ATE) systems or test executive software (e.g., TestStand) - Experience with fault detection algorithms, anomaly detection, or machine learning basics - Familiarity with version control (Git) and software development best practices - Coursework or project experience in RF/microwave engineering, embedded systems, or signal processing - Experience with databases or data pipeline tools for managing test data **Other Requirements** - U.S. Citizenship may be required due to export control/ITAR regulations (add/remove based on your organization's needs) - Ability to work on-site in a laboratory setting - Must be enrolled in an accredited university program for the duration of the internship

***Have you ever enjoyed Arnold®, Brownberry® or Oroweat® bread? A Thomas’® English muffin or bagel? Or perhaps snacked on a Sara Lee®, Entenmann’s® or Marinela® cake or donut? If the answer is yes, then you know Bimbo Bakeries USA!*** ***More than 20,000 associates in bakeries, sales centers, offices and on sales routes work to ensure our consumers have the freshest products at every meal. In addition to competitive pay and benefits, we provide a safe and inclusive work environment that appreciates diversity, promotes development and allows our associates to be their authentic selves.*** **Come join the largest baking company in the world and our family of 20,000 associates nationwide!** **Top Reasons to Work at Bimbo Bakeries USA:** · Salary Range: $63,500 - $82,500 · Comprehensive Benefits Package · Vehicle Reimbursement Program · Annual Bonus Eligibility · 401k & Company Match · On the Job Training with Advancement Opportunities #LI-JS1 The **Route to Readiness: MSL Development Program** is a structured six-month development experience designed to prepare high-potential and early-career talent for future Market Sales Leader opportunities within Bimbo Bakeries USA. This program provides immersive exposure to sales operations, customer execution, route operations, frontline leadership, and key cross-functional business areas. Participants will build critical business knowledge, leadership skills, and operational expertise that support long-term career growth. Through a combination of structured learning, field experiences, and practical application, participants will gain experience in Direct Store Delivery (DSD) operations, sales execution, merchandising, customer support, coaching fundamentals, and business planning over a 6-month rotation. The program also offers insight into how teams across the organization collaborate to deliver results, preparing participants for future opportunities as a Market Sales Leader. ## **Position Summary:** As a participant in the **Route to Readiness: MSL Development Program**, you will gain valuable experience working alongside sales leaders, field teams, customers, and cross-functional business partners. This role supports market growth and customer execution through Direct Store Delivery operations, merchandising excellence, relationship building, sales execution, coaching exposure, and operational excellence. The program is designed to strengthen Bimbo Bakeries USA's talent pipeline by developing future MSL candidates before opportunities become available. Participants will contribute to real business priorities while building the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to support successful transition into a future Market Sales Leader role. **Key Job Responsibilities:** - Successfully complete all requirements of the Route to Readiness: MSL Development Program, including assessments, development milestones, and readiness evaluations. - Engage in structured learning, field-based experiences, customer interactions, and targeted development opportunities designed to build business and leadership capability. - Support route sales execution through merchandising, inventory management, product freshness, and adherence to operational standards. - Develop productive relationships with customers, route operators, frontline associates, cross-functional partners, and key business partners. - Gain practical exposure to frontline leadership, including coaching practices, performance management, and team engagement. - Utilize sales tools, business reporting, customer insights, and performance metrics to support decision-making and execution. - Contribute to market planning, customer service initiatives, and execution priorities that drive business results. - Partner with cross-functional teams, including Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Revenue Growth Management, Customer Teams, Marketing, and Innovation, to understand how the organization delivers results. - Participate in field-based projects and continuous improvement initiatives that support operational and sales effectiveness. **Key Behavioral Competencies:** - Demonstrates curiosity and a strong desire to learn the sales organization, customer landscape, and field operations. - Thrives in both independent and collaborative work environments while navigating changing business priorities. - Leverages data and insights to evaluate performance, identify opportunities, and support informed decision-making. - Adapts effectively to evolving customer needs, market conditions, business objectives, and technology. - Communicates clearly and professionally with customers, sales associates, route operators, leaders, and cross-functional partners. - Builds credibility through accountability, consistency, and with a consumer and servant-focused mindset. - Embraces feedback as an opportunity for continuous learning and development. - Takes initiative, has urgency, and demonstrates ownership when addressing challenges and advancing business priorities. - Influences others by translating data and insights into clear, compelling business stories. **Key Leadership Competencies:** - Gains the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity. - Builds strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals. - Consistently achieves results, even under tough circumstances. - Makes good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward. - Take ownership of individual development, execution excellence, and program commitments. - Exhibits leadership potential through the ability to coach, influence, and positively impact others in a field environment. **Education and Work History:** - Recent graduate or graduated within the past 24 months with a bachelor's degree in business, marketing, or related field. - A GPA of 3.0 is preferred - Demonstrated leadership experience through academic, professional, military, volunteer, or community involvement. - Demonstrates an interest in Consumer-Packaged Goods, Direct Store Delivery, customer service, retail execution, and field operations. - Strong motivation to build customer relationships, support market execution, and achieve business results. - Ability to learn and apply sales tools, customer insights, performance data, and operational processes. - Computer skills and proficiency are required, including Microsoft Office Suite or similar systems. - Account management, retail, merchandising, sales, operations, or leadership experience is a plus. - Must have a valid driver’s license and able to obtain and maintain a DOT medical card. **Physical Demands:** - The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. - Reasonable accommodations may be requested to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. - This role does require travel to various North American locations that will be determined by the program and functional leader. - Must be 21 years of age or older. - A valid driver’s license is required and must be able to obtain and retain a DOT medical card. - Use various forms of transportation for extended periods of time periodically. - Ability to communicate effectively with customers and internal partners. Able to use a variety of communication methods frequently. - Must be able to work in all weather conditions. - Must be able to lift 25-50 pounds regularly, as well as routinely enter and exit a delivery vehicle. - Must be able to climb, push/pull, bend, stoop, and kneel for extended periods, as well as perform frequent reaching, walking, and use of fingers. The physical and mental demands described in each job posting are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential functions of each job. **Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.** From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide. **We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on.** By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future. **We’re a Series B startup backed by** **Lachy Groom,** **Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel**. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy. **The Opportunity** As part of our second cohort of engineering interns, you'll work as a valued member of our team building features that directly impact farmers across America. This is an exciting opportunity to gain real-world development experience while contributing to sustainable agriculture, with mentorship from experienced engineers who are invested in your growth.​ **We’re looking for someone who we can count on to…** - Own: Build and ship real product features that customers use, while helping improve our infrastructure alongside experienced engineers. - Learn: Gain experience in engineering best practices, agile development, and working across teams while discovering how agritech and climate solutions help farmers succeed. - Grow: Understand the basics of agricultural finance, farm operations, and sustainability practices through hands-on project work. - Contribute: Help identify ways to improve our development process and codebase while learning full-stack development. **Within the first few weeks you’ll** - Learn how to use Ambrook’s tech stack to deliver a standalone feature to our customers - Contribute to Engineering team meetings and review code from peers. - Analyze Ambrook’s use of best practices and share a technical note with our team about where we have opportunities to improve. **By the end of your internship you’ll…** - Collaborate with the team as the owner for a full-stack feature built into our core product. As the engineering owner, you’ll break down your project into granular pieces and practice good project management hygiene, triaging and prioritizing new issues that come in. - Collaborate with our Product team to influence prioritization of feature ideas and requests with insights from our audience. - Embed yourself deeply in understanding the state of farm finance, building a strong intuition about customer needs and audience segmentation. **About you** - Currently pursuing B.S. (or higher) in Computer Science or a related field. Expected graduation: Winter 2027 - Spring/Summer 2028 - Available to work full-time in our NYC office for 12-16 weeks between May - August 2027 - Excited to build software that makes natural resource industries like agriculture more sustainable and profitable. - Comfortable taking on ambiguous problems and creating elegant technical solutions - Exhibits strong computer science fundamentals and an eagerness to learn - Bonus: Experience with Typescript, React, React Native, and/or Next.js. - Bonus: Track record of building and shipping complex software projects - Bonus: Experience in agriculture **Our tech stack** - Next.js / React application written in Typescript - Hosted on Google Cloud - Firestore & Google Cloud Storage & Postgres for data storage - BigQuery & Data Studio for data insights **What makes this internship special** - Make a real difference: Build features that help farmers adopt sustainable practices and grow their businesses - Experience life at a high growth startup: see the complete product development cycle, from design to deployment in a fast-paced environment - Get personalized mentorship: Work directly with senior engineers who are invested in your growth - ## Job Description **About Kraft Heinz** Kraft Heinz is a global food company with a delicious heritage. With iconic and emerging food and beverage brands around the world, we deliver the best taste, fun and quality to every meal table we touch. We’re on a mission to disrupt not only our own business, but the global food industry. A consumer obsession and unexpected partnerships fuel our progress as we drive innovation across every part of our company. Around the world, our people are connected by a culture of ownership, agility and endless curiosity. We also believe in being good humans, who are working to improve our company, communities, and planet. We’re proud of where we’ve been – and even more thrilled about where we’re headed – as we nourish the world and lead the future of food. **R&D – The Creators:** Our R&D teams create high-quality products that push the boundaries of what’s possible. Innovation is what gets them up in the morning! **Job Description – Packaging Co-op Program** The Kraft Heinz Company is looking for **Undergraduate** students who want to have an all-inclusive Co-Op experience and learn all about the food and beverage industry. As a Kraft Heinz Packaging Co-Op, you are hand-selected by our Packaging Leadership team to participate in a roughly 6-month immersive program. Instead of going on coffee runs and making copies, you’ll be seated at the table making critical decisions that will influence not only your team, but the overall achievement of Kraft Heinz’s mission. During your program, you will join a cohort of other ambitious co-ops to learn directly from Kraft Heinz leaders, own your projects with tangible business results, and be immersed in ongoing learning opportunities and social events. At the program's conclusion, you will have the opportunity to present your project and results to the North American R&D Leadership Team. Our program’s goal is to build a pipeline for our direct-hire pool after graduation. **Dates:** Spring Cohort: January – June Fall Cohort: July – December **Co-Op Goals and Responsibilities:** - Successfully complete real projects across different commercialization stages (initiation, development and/or launch). The projects will vary in complexity levels and give exposure to different packaging formats and materials - Form recommendations throughout projects by developing hypotheses, planning and executing test/trial procedures, analyzing data, and reporting results to cross-functional teams - Projects may be rooted in innovation, renovation, sustainability, productivity, operational efficiency, and/or quality improvement initiatives. - Potential for travel to manufacturing facilities, supplier locations, and offsite trainings - Actively pursue technical and business knowledge to understand the big picture of how the project impacts the business (understanding the ‘why’) **Example Project Types:** We are dedicated to providing an experience that allows for the co-ops to experience life at Kraft Heinz by giving them projects that are critical to their team’s success. Project examples include: - Qualification of new materials, molds, etc. - New primary and/or secondary packaging design, testing, and implementation - Development of packaging designs for customer-specific initiatives - Develop and execute testing procedures to evaluate product/package performance **You should join us at our table if:** - You will be enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree in Packaging Science, Packaging Engineering and other related majors (i.e., Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Applied Engineering, etc.) during the co-op program - Will be in your **Junior or Senior year** of your degree program during the co-op program - Interested in gaining experience in the food or consumer products industry - Ability to work in office, lab, and manufacturing environments - Strong verbal and written communication skills - Highly motivated with a sense of urgency - Demonstrate a desire for constant learning - Willing to travel up to 30% depending on business needs **Program Location(s)** Glenview, IL or Warrendale, PA R&D Centers (Location preferences will be discussed during the interview process) **Housing:** All co-ops will be provided furnished housing at a subsidized rate for the duration of their program. **Total Compensation:** $24,000 **Office Collaboration & Hybrid Work Environment** We believe our office environment fuels our collaboration, connection & community as an organization and allows our employees to grow toward greatness. **About the company** General Matter enriches uranium. We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. #### **The Role** Does aggressively tackling cross disciplinary projects from early conceptual stages through to full field deployment sound like the way you want to spend your time? Do you eliminate circular discussions by running a test or use your hands-on skills to build a prototype instead of scheduling another meeting? At Zipline, your work is intended for the field, where customers are counting on it every day, so there is no time for ambiguous communication or unrealistic expectations. We need dedicated engineers to burn down risk and improve reliability in our system like their life depends on it– because others' lives do. If you thrive working with a fast-paced and driven team that focuses on only the most important goals, eliminates blockers, and executes with extreme practicality, keep reading! Materials Engineers at Zipline go deep in their area of ownership, become experts in the problem domain, and prove with testing that their system meets the rigors and edge-cases of real-world deployment. We are composed of teams that are involved with everything from the earliest designs of a new system, to creating test and validation strategies, root-causing issues with existing systems, and much more. **What You'll Do** - Materials interns can own a variety of big problems integral to our system! You can expect to: - Perform materials characterization using tools such as section/mount/polish, optical microscopy, SEM/EDS, hardness testing, and mechanical testing. - Support failure investigations by examining physical evidence, developing hypotheses, and identifying material or processdriven failure mechanisms. - Evaluate the effects of manufacturing processes, surface condition, coatings, joining, and environmental exposure on component performance. - Qualify material, supplier, or process changes through structured testing and data analysis. - Analyze experimental data using Python, MATLAB, JMP, or similar tools and communicate conclusions through clear plots, images, and technical documentation. - Develop or improve test methods, fixtures, procedures, and characterization workflows. - Work cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, reliability, supplier quality, and test engineers to turn materials evidence into engineering decisions. - Document your work so that others can easily understand key decisions made #### **What You'll Bring** The most critical skill we’ve seen in prior entry-level candidates is robust experience designing and actually building multiple mechanical systems outside of the classroom. This is the component of your application we’re most excited about, so please ensure that you’ve included this work in your application. Examples of things previous interns have built include submarines, solar cars in the Australian outback, electric boats and airplanes, rockets, etc. - You’ll bring strong fundamentals in materials science and mechanical behavior for identifying material or process driven failure mechanisms. - You have hands-on experience through research, internships, or projects involving materials characterization, mechanical testing, manufacturing, or failure analysis. - You have experience analyzing data and clearly communicating technical conclusions. - You must have completed at least the second year of your Undergraduate studies in Materials Science & Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, or a related technical field. - Masters and PhD students are also eligible. - You’re comfortable working independently in a laboratory environment and troubleshooting experiments. - You're quick to change direction when you realize you’ve made a mistake OR could achieve the same goal in a simpler way - You bias to action and communicate consistently with your team to ensure everyone is focused on meeting the project goals on time - You can anticipate, plan and schedule your own work - You bring a “can do” attitude, because we have a lot of vital work to get done and only work with people who are invested in solving critical problems #### **What Else You Should Know** *Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host this intern from January to August/September.* *The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.* *Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.* Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. Using simulation, we can rapidly explore a vast array of designs to optimize future products, and we can find ways to squeeze more performance out of our existing products. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. #### **About the Sales Operations Team** Sales Operations partners with Zipline’s commercial teams to turn strategy into repeatable execution. We build the systems, data, and operating rhythms that help sales teams prioritize the right accounts, manage pipeline, and act on insights. Our work spans CRM governance, account research, pipeline reporting, process improvement, sales enablement, and cross-functional go-to-market initiatives. #### **The Role** As a Sales Operations Analyst Intern, you will help strengthen the infrastructure behind Zipline’s growing commercial organization. You will work on projects that make sales data more useful, processes more scalable, and decisions easier to make. You may support pipeline analysis, account and territory planning, CRM improvements, prospecting operations, and reporting. You will collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and other business partners while learning how a high-growth company builds and scales its go-to-market engine. **What You'll Do** - Audit, standardize, and enrich CRM records to improve data quality and trust in reporting. - Support recurring pipeline, forecast, and funnel reporting; identify trends in stage movement, aging, coverage, and conversion. - Build account lists, market maps, and research briefs that help sales teams prioritize prospects and whitespace opportunities. - Document and improve sales processes, including lead routing, handoffs, opportunity stages, and follow-up workflows. - Coordinate cross-functional Sales Operations initiatives by tracking milestones, owners, risks, and next steps. - Create practical dashboards, analysis, playbooks, and enablement materials for sales and leadership stakeholders. - Identify repetitive work and help evaluate automation or AI-enabled ways to improve speed, consistency, and quality. #### **What You'll Bring** - You must have completed at least two years of undergraduate degree in business, economics, analytics, marketing, operations, engineering, or a related field. Candidates who are currently pursuing or have completed a bachelor’s, master’s, or MBA degree are eligible. - Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with an ability to work carefully with data and details. - Curiosity about how sales organizations operate and a willingness to ask questions, investigate problems, and learn new tools. - Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn analysis into a concise recommendation. - Comfort managing multiple workstreams in a fast-moving and sometimes ambiguous environment. - Experience with spreadsheets, CRM systems, reporting tools, or process documentation is helpful but not required. - HubSpot Admin experience is a plus. #### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from (January 2027 - April 2027).* *Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.* The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

description: Advanced DV Engineering Intern About the role Astera Labs is seeking an Advanced Design Verification Engineering Intern to help validate complex ASIC and system designs before silicon is available. You will work with design verification engineers to develop tests, improve verification environments, analyze coverage, debug failures, and apply simulation and formal methods to assess whether designs meet their specifications. This internship is intended for a student who is ready to go beyond running existing tests and contribute to verification strategy, reusable infrastructure, and difficult debug problems. You will own a scoped project with guidance from experienced engineers and deliver verification work in a usable state. What you will do Translate architectural, microarchitectural, interface, and product requirements into verification scenarios, test plans, coverage goals, and checkers. Develop and maintain SystemVerilog and UVM testbench components, sequences, tests, monitors, scoreboards, functional coverage, and end-of-test checks. Add directed, constrained-random, error-injection, compliance, stress, and corner-case tests for blocks, subsystems, or top-level functionality. Configure and run simulations and regressions using project submission flows, manifests, plusargs, firmware images, and test definitions. Debug failures by correlating logs, UVM messages, assertions, register reports, firmware output, and Verdi or DVE waveforms. Triage regression failures, distinguish design issues from testbench or environment issues, reproduce failures, and communicate actionable root-cause analysis. Analyze functional and code coverage, identify untested scenarios or coverage gaps, and propose targeted tests or verification improvements. Write, review, and debug SystemVerilog assertions and coverage properties that capture design intent and interface behavior. Support formal verification flows such as design compile, reset analysis, automatic property extraction, dead-code analysis, and formal property verification. Create or improve Python, Tcl, or other automation that simplifies test generation, regression execution, result parsing, coverage analysis, or failure triage. Collaborate with RTL design, firmware, emulation, physical design, and systems engineers to clarify assumptions and close verification issues. Document test intent, debug findings, coverage status, known limitations, and handoff information; present the completed project and recommendations. What you bring Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field. Coursework, research, or project experience in digital logic, computer architecture, ASIC/FPGA design, verification, embedded systems, or hardware/software integration. Programming or verification experience with SystemVerilog, Verilog, C, C++, Python, or a comparable language. Familiarity with digital design concepts, simulation, testbenches, interfaces, clocks, resets, registers, and debugging from waveforms or logs. Familiarity with Linux development environments, Git, command-line tools, and technical documentation. Ability to reason from a specification, investigate failures systematically, and communicate clear technical conclusions. Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across engineering functions. Preferred qualifications Experience with UVM components, sequences, virtual sequences, agents, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, or functional coverage. Familiarity with SystemVerilog Assertions, constrained-random testing, coverage-driven verification, error injection, or compliance testing. Exposure to verification IP and protocols such as PCIe, CXL, AXI, or other high-speed and control interfaces. Experience with Verdi, DVE, VCS, Questa, Xcelium, VC Formal, or comparable simulation and formal tools. Familiarity with formal concepts such as assumptions, assertions, covers, counterexamples, reset analysis, dead-code analysis, or automatic property extraction. Experience managing regressions, parsing results, debugging intermittent failures, or running jobs on a compute cluster or CI system. role: Program Manager, Alternative Investments Fellowship Program (AIFP)
location: New York, New York, United States
description: Title: Program Manager, Alternative Investments Fellowship Program (AIFP) Department: SEO Career & Alternative Investments Report to: Senior Resident, AIFP Compensation: $70,500 - $83,000 FLSA: Exempt Employee Type: Full-Time, Regular Location: New York, NY Work Arrangement: Hybrid - 3 days/week in the SEO office at 55 Exchange Place, New York, NY 10005 ABOUT SEO Founded in 1963 during the Civil Rights Movement, SEO closes educational and career opportunity gaps for 7,000 ambitious young people annually. POSITION OVERVIEW The Program Manager, Alternative Investments supports the Associate Director, Alternative Investments and Senior Resident, AIFP in the day-to-day coordination and execution of SEO's Alternative Investments programming for the Alternative Investment Fellowship Program (AIFP). At times, this position may work with the Project Manager for the other programs in the Alternatives Investments portfolio, including Level Up: Alternative Investments and Investment Academy to encourage pipeline development and joint activities. While the Program Manager will have exposure to participants and contribute to their development journey, the core of the work centers on keeping programs running smoothly — managing logistics, tracking deliverables, coordinating across coaches and vendors, maintaining program data, and supporting the Senior Resident and Associate Director in executing against strategic priorities. This role serves as an operational backbone for the Alternative Investments Fellowship Program, ensuring that programming is well-organized, information flows effectively across stakeholders, and nothing falls through the cracks. Program Coordination & Operations (40%) Support the end-to-end coordination of AIFP programming, including scheduling, logistics, communications, and event execution for workshops, bootcamps, roadshows, partner-led sessions, and other program touchpoint. Maintain and update program calendars, participant trackers, coach schedules, and operational documentation to ensure the Associate Director and the broader team have accurate, real-time visibility into program status and upcoming deliverables. Assist in coordinating logistics for the SEO Alternative Investments Conference and other marquee program events, supporting planning activities and on-site execution. Assist in sourcing and coordinating with vendors, third-party training providers, and external coaches, managing scheduling and follow-through to ensure programming is delivered on time and to standard. Support the coordination of partner-led events, including materials preparation, firm communications, and post-event follow-up, in collaboration with the Partnerships and Events teams. Serve as a consistent point of contact for program participants on logistical and administrative matters, directing substantive coaching and advising questions to the appropriate team member or coach. Project Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration (30%) Support the Associate Director in managing work streams across the Alternative Investments portfolio, tracking progress against program milestones, flagging risks or delays, and helping to keep deliverables on schedule. Liaise with the Pathways team to coordinate participant readiness updates, ensure timely information-sharing about candidate pipeline status, and support the matching and placement process for AIFP participants. Coordinate with the Program Manager supporting Level Up: Alternative Investments and Investment Academy to support the pipeline for alternative investments roles, ensuring scheduling and logistics are aligned. Collaborate with coaches and AIFP mentors supporting the Alternative Investments programs — coordinating their schedules, managing session logistics, and tracking participation and completion — to ensure coaching is well-integrated and consistently delivered across the portfolio. Assist in the development and maintenance of program curriculum materials, sourcing publicly available resources and coordinating with third-party training providers as directed by the Associate Director and Senior Resident. Draft written content for participant communications, program marketing materials, newsletters, and engagement updates. Participant Engagement Support (15%) Support the onboarding of new AIFP participants, including communicating program expectations, distributing materials, and tracking completion of intake requirements. Assist in the fellow and participant selection process for AIFP, coordinating application logistics, scheduling interviews, and managing candidate pipeline tracking in collaboration with the Associate Director and Senior Resident Facilitate participant engagement touchpoints — including information sessions, check-ins, and group workshops — as directed, with a focus on connecting participants to the right resources, coaches, and program opportunities at each stage of their development. Data Management & Reporting (15%) Maintain program data across tracking systems and databases, ensuring participant records, engagement logs, coach activity, and outcome data are current and accurate. Support the preparation of regular program performance updates and reporting for the Associate Director and Senior Resident, compiling data on participants engaged, coaching sessions completed, and placement and conversion outcomes across the Alternative Investments portfolio. Track key program metrics — including AIFP fellows class formation, participant engagement rates, and placement rates — and flag data gaps or discrepancies to the Associate Director and Senior Resident for resolution. Respond to ad hoc data and reporting requests from the Associate Director, Senior Resident and other program team members with accuracy and appropriate urgency. Perform other assigned duties in support of SEO Career & Alternative Investments program goals and the overall mission of the organization. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year institution required. 3–5 years of professional experience in program coordination, project management, operations, or a related field; experience in nonprofit, education, or financial services a plus. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production. Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data. The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. About Flexport: At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. Demonstrated leadership experience — this can come from campus organizations, athletics, ROTC/military, student government, internships, or part-time or summer jobs. Must be able to work on a secure mezzanine at a height of up to 40 feet (applies to buildings with mezzanines). description: About Gusto At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy. AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.Submit your interest to join our Sales team! Gusto is seeking sales professionals who thrive in a fast-paced, consultative environment and are interested in being considered for future start dates in 2026. If you’d like to be considered for future opportunities with our team, please complete the form below and upload your resume. While start dates are still being determined for 2026, we’d love to connect! Does this sound like you? Apply below! About the Role: Gusto is seeking motivated, customer-centric professionals interested in being considered for future sales and onboarding opportunities in 2026. These roles are ideal for early-career sales talent who thrive in a fast-paced, consultative environment and are passionate about helping small businesses succeed. As a member of our Sales or Onboarding teams, you’ll own customer experience from first conversation through successful adoption—helping small businesses select Gusto and navigate their first steps with us. You’ll handle inbound calls and chats while potentially engaging in some outbound outreach to prospective or current customers. Through empathy, problem-solving, and advisory selling, you’ll make an immediate impact on how our customers experience Gusto from day one. Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: Handle high-volume inbound calls, chats, and emails from customers or partners at various stages of their journey—from discovery to onboarding. Serve as a trusted advisor, helping small businesses or accounting partners select the right Gusto solutions for their needs. Support customers through the onboarding process to ensure a smooth and successful start. Demonstrate strong product knowledge and a commitment to ethical, customer-first selling. Maintain accurate notes and pipeline details in Salesforce to ensure excellent follow-through. Positions available in the future range levels. Here’s what we're looking for: 1–3 years of experience in a sales or customer service role. Experience working in high-volume environments that include inbound and outbound calling. Proven success achieving or exceeding goals and maintaining strong customer relationships. A passion for consultative, solution-oriented selling and helping small businesses succeed. Comfortable using Salesforce or similar CRM systems. This posting represents a general talent pipeline that spans multiple levels within our Sales team. Final compensation will be determined based on the specific role, level, and experience alignment. The estimated compensation range for these roles is $20.00–$28.00 per hour. At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate. Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale. Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees. Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve. Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. The Lyft Rider Science team is seeking an Applied Scientist intern to develop next-generation user simulation methods using state of the art AI methods. The goal of this project is to develop and validate LLM-based Rider Agents that can serve as behavioral proxies for real riders, and study when agent simulations can provide reliable signal about rider responses to product interventions before online experimentation. You will build agent-based simulation systems grounded in real rider context and behavioral data, evaluate their fidelity against observed rider behavior and historical experiments, and study where these simulations can accelerate product iteration and experimentation. This role combines LLM engineering, agent-based modeling, machine learning, and causal inference with direct applications to real-world rider products. The expected outcome is to build a working Rider Agent simulation prototype, establish an evaluation framework for measuring simulation fidelity and validate the framework using historical rider experiments. Responsibilities: Develop LLM-based Rider Agents that represent heterogeneous rider contexts, preferences, histories, and behaviors Build agent-based simulation environments for evaluating rider interactions with different product experiences and interventions Build evaluation pipelines to assess realism, robustness, and mechanism plausibility of simulated behavior against human data or established theory Analyze emergent behaviors and interaction dynamics in simulated populations under different user segment and marketplace conditions Conduct experiments and ablation studies on agent behavior, interaction dynamics, and simulation validity Apply the simulation framework to real Rider product problems and assess its usefulness for hypothesis generation, product iteration, and pre-experiment evaluation Communicate technical findings and recommendations to science, engineering, and product partners Experience: Currently pursuing a PhD degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related technical field, with a graduation date between December 2027 and Summer 2028 (required) Proficiency with Python and working in a production coding environment Hands-on experience with large language models or agent-based systems Strong foundation in machine learning and empirical model evaluation Ability to independently develop prototypes and work through open-ended technical problems Strong verbal and written communication skills, and ability to collaborate and communicate with others to solve a problem Familiarity with A/B testing, causal inference, or experimental design Bonus Points: Experience building production level ML inference, simulation, or evaluation pipelines Prior research experience with LLM agents, generative user simulation, or agent-based modeling Background in computational social science or behavioral modeling Experience evaluating AI systems against human behavioral data, qualitative studies, or controlled experiments Familiarity with prompting, tool use, memory, planning, or coordination in LLM-based agents Publication record in relevant venues such as NeurIPS, ICLR,
